28.15: "Then, with the most careful workmanship, make a chestpiece that will be used to determine God's will. Use the same materials as you did for the ephod: fine linen cloth embroidered with gold thread and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
28.16: This chestpiece will be made of two folds of cloth, forming a pouch nine inches square.
28.17: Four rows of gemstones will be attached to it. The first row will contain a red carnelian, a chrysolite, and an emerald.
28.18: The second row will contain a turquoise, a sapphire, and a white moonstone.
28.19: The third row will contain a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst.
28.20: The fourth row will contain a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. All these stones will be set in gold.
28.21: Each stone will represent one of the tribes of Israel, and the name of that tribe will be engraved on it as though it were a seal.
28.22: "To attach the chestpiece to the ephod, make braided cords of pure gold.
28.23: Then make two gold rings and attach them to the top corners of the chestpiece.
28.24: The two gold cords will go through the rings on the chestpiece,
28.25: and the ends of the cords will be tied to the gold settings on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod.
28.26: Then make two more gold rings, and attach them to the two lower inside corners of the chestpiece next to the ephod.
28.27: And make two more gold rings and attach them to the ephod near the sash.
28.28: Then attach the bottom rings of the chestpiece to the rings on the ephod with blue cords. This will hold the chestpiece securely to the ephod above the beautiful sash.
28.29: In this way, Aaron will carry the names of the tribes of Israel on the chestpiece over his heart when he goes into the presence of the LORD in the Holy Place. Thus, the LORD will be reminded of his people continually.
28.30: Insert into the pocket of the chestpiece the Urim and Thummim, to be carried over Aaron's heart when he goes into the LORD's presence. Thus, Aaron will always carry the objects used to determine the LORD's will for his people whenever he goes in before the LORD.
28.31: "Make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth,
28.32: with an opening for Aaron's head in the middle of it. The opening will be reinforced by a woven collar so it will not tear.
28.33: Make pomegranates out of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and attach them to the hem of the robe, with gold bells between them.
28.34: The gold bells and pomegranates are to alternate all the way around the hem.
28.35: Aaron will wear this robe whenever he enters the Holy Place to minister to the LORD, and the bells will tinkle as he goes in and out of the LORD's presence. If he wears it, he will not die.
28.36: "Next make a medallion of pure gold. Using the techniques of an engraver, inscribe it with these words: SET APART AS HOLY TO THE LORD.
28.37: This medallion will be attached to the front of Aaron's turban by means of a blue cord.
28.38: Aaron will wear it on his forehead, thus bearing the guilt connected with any errors regarding the sacred offerings of the people of Israel. He must always wear it so the LORD will accept the people.
28.39: "Weave Aaron's patterned tunic from fine linen cloth. Fashion the turban out of this linen as well. Also make him an embroidered sash.
28.40: "Then for Aaron's sons, make tunics, sashes, and headdresses to give them dignity and respect.
28.41: Clothe Aaron and his sons with these garments, and then anoint and ordain them. Set them apart as holy so they can serve as my priests.
28.42: Also make linen underclothes for them, to be worn next to their bodies, reaching from waist to thigh.
28.43: These must be worn whenever Aaron and his sons enter the Tabernacle or approach the altar in the Holy Place to perform their duties. Thus they will not incur guilt and die. This law is permanent for Aaron and his descendants.

29.1: "This is the ceremony for the dedication of Aaron and his sons as priests: Take a young bull and two rams with no physical defects.
29.2: Then using fine wheat flour and no yeast, make loaves of bread, thin cakes mixed with olive oil, and wafers with oil poured over them.
29.3: Place these various kinds of bread in a single basket, and present them at the entrance of the Tabernacle, along with the young bull and the two rams.
29.4: "Present Aaron and his sons at the entrance of the Tabernacle, and wash them with water.
29.5: Then put Aaron's tunic on him, along with the embroidered robe of the ephod, the ephod itself, the chestpiece, and the sash.
29.6: And place on his head the turban with the gold medallion.
29.7: Then take the anointing oil and pour it over his head.
29.8: Next present his sons, and dress them in their tunics
29.9: with their woven sashes and their headdresses. They will then be priests forever. In this way, you will ordain Aaron and his sons.
29.10: "Then bring the young bull to the entrance of the Tabernacle, and Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.
29.11: You will then slaughter it in the LORD's presence at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
29.12: Smear some of its blood on the horns of the altar with your finger, and pour out the rest at the base of the altar.
29.13: Take all the fat that covers the internal organs, also the long lobe of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and burn them on the altar.
29.14: Then take the carcass (including the skin and the dung) outside the camp, and burn it as a sin offering.
29.15: "Next Aaron and his sons must lay their hands on the head of one of the rams
29.16: as it is slaughtered. Its blood will be collected and sprinkled on the sides of the altar.
29.17: Cut up the ram and wash off the internal organs and the legs. Set them alongside the head and the other pieces of the body,
29.18: and burn them all on the altar. This is a burnt offering to the LORD, which is very pleasing to him.
29.19: "Now take the other ram and have Aaron and his sons lay their hands on its head
29.20: as it is slaughtered. Collect the blood and place some of it on the tip of the right earlobes of Aaron and his sons. Also put it on their right thumbs and the big toes of their right feet. Sprinkle the rest of the blood on the sides of the altar.
29.21: Then take some of the blood from the altar and mix it with some of the anointing oil. Sprinkle it on Aaron and his sons and on their clothes. In this way, they and their clothing will be set apart as holy to the LORD.
29.22: "Since this is the ram for the ordination of Aaron and his sons, take the fat of the ram, including the fat tail and the fat that covers the internal organs. Also, take the long lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.
29.23: Then take one loaf of bread, one cake mixed with olive oil, and one wafer from the basket of yeastless bread that was placed before the LORD.
29.24: Put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons to be lifted up as a special gift to the LORD.
29.25: Afterward take the bread from their hands, and burn it on the altar as a burnt offering that will be pleasing to the LORD.
29.26: Then take the breast of Aaron's ordination ram, and lift it up in the LORD's presence as a special gift to him. Afterward keep it for yourself.
29.27: "Set aside as holy the parts of the ordination ram that belong to Aaron and his sons. This includes the breast and the thigh that were lifted up before the LORD in the ordination ceremony.
29.28: In the future, whenever the people of Israel offer up peace offerings or thanksgiving offerings to the LORD, these parts will be the regular share of Aaron and his descendants.
29.29: "Aaron's sacred garments must be preserved for his descendants who will succeed him, so they can be anointed and ordained in them.
29.30: Whoever is the next high priest after Aaron will wear these clothes for seven days before beginning to minister in the Tabernacle and the Holy Place.
29.31: "Take the ram used in the ordination ceremony, and boil its meat in a sacred place.
29.32: Aaron and his sons are to eat this meat, along with the bread in the basket, at the Tabernacle entrance.
29.33: They alone may eat the meat and bread used for their atonement in the ordination ceremony. The ordinary people may not eat them, for these things are set apart and holy.
29.34: If any of the ordination meat or bread remains until the morning, it must be burned. It may not be eaten, for it is holy.
29.35: "This is how you will ordain Aaron and his sons to their offices. The ordination ceremony will go on for seven days.
29.36: Each day you must sacrifice a young bull as an offering for the atonement of sin. Afterward make an offering to cleanse the altar. Purify the altar by making atonement for it; make it holy by anointing it with oil.
29.37: Make atonement for the altar every day for seven days. After that, the altar will be exceedingly holy, and whatever touches it will become holy.
29.38: "This is what you are to offer on the altar. Offer two one-year-old lambs each day,
29.39: one in the morning and the other in the evening.
29.40: With one of them, offer two quarts of fine flour mixed with one quart of olive oil; also, offer one quart of wine as a drink offering.
29.41: Offer the other lamb in the evening, along with the same offerings of flour and wine as in the morning. It will be a fragrant offering to the LORD, an offering made by fire.
29.42: "This is to be a daily burnt offering given from generation to generation. Offer it in the LORD's presence at the Tabernacle entrance, where I will meet you and speak with you.
29.43: I will meet the people of Israel there, and the Tabernacle will be sanctified by my glorious presence.
29.44: Yes, I will make the Tabernacle and the altar most holy, and I will set apart Aaron and his sons as holy, that they may be my priests.
29.45: I will live among the people of Israel and be their God,
29.46: and they will know that I am the LORD their God. I am the one who brought them out of Egypt so that I could live among them. I am the LORD their God.

30.1: "Then make a small altar out of acacia wood for burning incense.
30.2: It must be eighteen inches square and three feet high, with horns at the corners carved from the same piece of wood as the altar.
30.3: Overlay the top, sides, and horns of the altar with pure gold, and run a gold molding around the entire altar.
30.4: Beneath the molding, on opposite sides of the altar, attach two gold rings to support the carrying poles.
30.5: The poles are to be made of acacia wood and overlaid with gold.
30.6: Place the incense altar just outside the inner curtain, opposite the Ark's cover--the place of atonement--that rests on the Ark of the Covenant. I will meet with you there.
30.7: "Every morning when Aaron trims the lamps, he must burn fragrant incense on the altar.
30.8: And each evening when he tends to the lamps, he must again burn incense in the LORD's presence. This must be done from generation to generation.
30.9: Do not offer any unholy incense on this altar, or any burnt offerings, grain offerings, or drink offerings.
30.10: "Once a year Aaron must purify the altar by placing on its horns the blood from the offering made for the atonement of sin. This will be a regular, annual event from generation to generation, for this is the LORD's supremely holy altar."
30.11: And the LORD said to Moses,
30.12: "Whenever you take a census of the people of Israel, each man who is counted must pay a ransom for himself to the LORD. Then there will be no plagues among the people as you count them.
30.13: His payment to the LORD will be one-fifth of an ounce of silver.
30.14: All who have reached their twentieth birthday must give this offering to the LORD.
30.15: When this offering is given to the LORD to make atonement for yourselves, the rich must not give more, and the poor must not give less.
30.16: Use this money for the care of the Tabernacle. It will bring you, the Israelites, to the LORD's attention, and it will make atonement for your lives."
30.17: And the LORD said to Moses,
30.18: "Make a large bronze washbasin with a bronze pedestal. Put it between the Tabernacle and the altar, and fill it with water.
30.19: Aaron and his sons will wash their hands and feet there
30.20: before they go into the Tabernacle to appear before the LORD and before they approach the altar to burn offerings to the LORD. They must always wash before ministering in these ways, or they will die.
30.21: This is a permanent law for Aaron and his descendants, to be kept from generation to generation."
30.22: Then the LORD said to Moses,
30.23: "Collect choice spices--12 1/2 pounds of pure myrrh, 6 1/4 pounds each of cinnamon and of sweet cane,
30.24: 12 1/2 pounds of cassia, and one gallon of olive oil.
30.25: Blend these ingredients into a holy anointing oil.
30.26: Use this scented oil to anoint the Tabernacle, the Ark of the Covenant,
30.27: the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and all its accessories, the incense altar,
30.28: the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the large washbasin with its pedestal.
30.29: Sanctify them to make them entirely holy. After this, whatever touches them will become holy.
30.30: Use this oil also to anoint Aaron and his sons, sanctifying them so they can minister before me as priests.
30.31: And say to the people of Israel, `This will always be my holy anointing oil.
30.32: It must never be poured on the body of an ordinary person, and you must never make any of it for yourselves. It is holy, and you must treat it as holy.
30.33: Anyone who blends scented oil like it or puts any of it on someone who is not a priest will be cut off from the community.'"
30.34: These were the LORD's instructions to Moses concerning the incense: "Gather sweet spices--resin droplets, mollusk scent, galbanum, and pure frankincense--weighing out the same amounts of each.
30.35: Using the usual techniques of the incense maker, refine it to produce a pure and holy incense.
30.36: Beat some of it very fine and put some of it in front of the Ark of the Covenant, where I will meet with you in the Tabernacle. This incense is most holy.
30.37: Never make this incense for yourselves. It is reserved for the LORD, and you must treat it as holy.
30.38: Those who make it for their own enjoyment will be cut off from the community."

31.1: The LORD also said to Moses,
31.2: "Look, I have chosen Bezalel son of Uri, grandson of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
31.3: I have filled him with the Spirit of God, giving him great wisdom, intelligence, and skill in all kinds of crafts.
31.4: He is able to create beautiful objects from gold, silver, and bronze.
31.5: He is skilled in cutting and setting gemstones and in carving wood. Yes, he is a master at every craft!
31.6: "And I have appointed Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, to be his assistant. Moreover, I have given special skill to all the naturally talented craftsmen so they can make all the things I have instructed you to make:
31.7: the Tabernacle itself; the Ark of the Covenant; the Ark's cover--the place of atonement; all the furnishings of the Tabernacle;
31.8: the table and all its utensils; the gold lampstand with all its accessories; the incense altar;
31.9: the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils; the washbasin and its pedestal;
31.10: the beautifully stitched, holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments for his sons to wear as they minister as priests;
31.11: the anointing oil; and the special incense for the Holy Place. They must follow exactly all the instructions I have given you."
31.12: The LORD then gave these further instructions to Moses:
31.13: "Tell the people of Israel to keep my Sabbath day, for the Sabbath is a sign of the covenant between me and you forever. It helps you to remember that I am the LORD, who makes you holy.
31.14: Yes, keep the Sabbath day, for it is holy. Anyone who desecrates it must die; anyone who works on that day will be cut off from the community.
31.15: Work six days only, but the seventh day must be a day of total rest. I repeat: Because the LORD considers it a holy day, anyone who works on the Sabbath must be put to death.
31.16: The people of Israel must keep the Sabbath day forever.
31.17: It is a permanent sign of my covenant with them. For in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, but he rested on the seventh day and was refreshed."
31.18: Then as the LORD finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two stone tablets inscribed with the terms of the covenant, written by the finger of God.

32.1: When Moses failed to come back down the mountain right away, the people went to Aaron. "Look," they said, "make us some gods who can lead us. This man Moses, who brought us here from Egypt, has disappeared. We don't know what has happened to him."
32.2: So Aaron said, "Tell your wives and sons and daughters to take off their gold earrings, and then bring them to me."
32.3: All the people obeyed Aaron and brought him their gold earrings.
32.4: Then Aaron took the gold, melted it down, and molded and tooled it into the shape of a calf. The people exclaimed, "O Israel, these are the gods who brought you out of Egypt!"
32.5: When Aaron saw how excited the people were about it, he built an altar in front of the calf and announced, "Tomorrow there will be a festival to the LORD!"
32.6: So the people got up early the next morning to sacrifice burnt offerings and peace offerings. After this, they celebrated with feasting and drinking, and indulged themselves in pagan revelry.
32.7: Then the LORD told Moses, "Quick! Go down the mountain! The people you brought from Egypt have defiled themselves.
32.8: They have already turned from the way I commanded them to live. They have made an idol shaped like a calf, and they have worshiped and sacrificed to it. They are saying, `These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you out of Egypt.'"
32.9: Then the LORD said, "I have seen how stubborn and rebellious these people are.
32.10: Now leave me alone so my anger can blaze against them and destroy them all. Then I will make you, Moses, into a great nation instead of them."
32.11: But Moses pleaded with the LORD his God not to do it. "O LORD!" he exclaimed. "Why are you so angry with your own people whom you brought from the land of Egypt with such great power and mighty acts?
32.12: The Egyptians will say, `God tricked them into coming to the mountains so he could kill them and wipe them from the face of the earth.' Turn away from your fierce anger. Change your mind about this terrible disaster you are planning against your people!
32.13: Remember your covenant with your servants--Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. You swore by your own self, `I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars of heaven. Yes, I will give them all of this land that I have promised to your descendants, and they will possess it forever.'"
32.14: So the LORD withdrew his threat and didn't bring against his people the disaster he had threatened.
32.15: Then Moses turned and went down the mountain. He held in his hands the two stone tablets inscribed with the terms of the covenant. They were inscribed on both sides, front and back.
32.16: These stone tablets were God's work; the words on them were written by God himself.
32.17: When Joshua heard the noise of the people shouting below them, he exclaimed to Moses, "It sounds as if there is a war in the camp!"
32.18: But Moses replied, "No, it's neither a cry of victory nor a cry of defeat. It is the sound of a celebration."
32.19: When they came near the camp, Moses saw the calf and the dancing. In terrible anger, he threw the stone tablets to the ground, smashing them at the foot of the mountain.
32.20: He took the calf they had made and melted it in the fire. And when the metal had cooled, he ground it into powder and mixed it with water. Then he made the people drink it.
32.21: After that, he turned to Aaron. "What did the people do to you?" he demanded. "How did they ever make you bring such terrible sin upon them?"
32.22: "Don't get upset, sir," Aaron replied. "You yourself know these people and what a wicked bunch they are.
32.23: They said to me, `Make us some gods to lead us, for something has happened to this man Moses, who led us out of Egypt.'
32.24: So I told them, `Bring me your gold earrings.' When they brought them to me, I threw them into the fire--and out came this calf!"
32.25: When Moses saw that Aaron had let the people get completely out of control--and much to the amusement of their enemies--
32.26: he stood at the entrance to the camp and shouted, "All of you who are on the LORD's side, come over here and join me." And all the Levites came.
32.27: He told them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Strap on your swords! Go back and forth from one end of the camp to the other, killing even your brothers, friends, and neighbors."
32.28: The Levites obeyed Moses, and about three thousand people died that day.
32.29: Then Moses told the Levites, "Today you have been ordained for the service of the LORD, for you obeyed him even though it meant killing your own sons and brothers. Because of this, he will now give you a great blessing."
32.30: The next day Moses said to the people, "You have committed a terrible sin, but I will return to the LORD on the mountain. Perhaps I will be able to obtain forgiveness for you."
32.31: So Moses returned to the LORD and said, "Alas, these people have committed a terrible sin. They have made gods of gold for themselves.
32.32: But now, please forgive their sin--and if not, then blot me out of the record you are keeping."
32.33: The LORD replied to Moses, "I will blot out whoever has sinned against me.
32.34: Now go, lead the people to the place I told you about. Look! My angel will lead the way before you! But when I call the people to account, I will certainly punish them for their sins."
32.35: And the LORD sent a great plague upon the people because they had worshiped the calf Aaron had made.

33.1: The LORD said to Moses, "Now that you have brought these people out of Egypt, lead them to the land I solemnly promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I told them long ago that I would give this land to their descendants.
33.2: And I will send an angel before you to drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
33.3: Theirs is a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not travel along with you, for you are a stubborn, unruly people. If I did, I would be tempted to destroy you along the way."
33.4: When the people heard these stern words, they went into mourning and refused to wear their jewelry and ornaments.
33.5: For the LORD had told Moses to tell them, "You are an unruly, stubborn people. If I were there among you for even a moment, I would destroy you. Remove your jewelry and ornaments until I decide what to do with you."
33.6: So from the time they left Mount Sinai, the Israelites wore no more jewelry.
33.7: It was Moses' custom to set up the tent known as the Tent of Meeting far outside the camp. Everyone who wanted to consult with the LORD would go there.
33.8: Whenever Moses went out to the Tent of Meeting, all the people would get up and stand in their tent entrances. They would all watch Moses until he disappeared inside.
33.9: As he went into the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and hover at the entrance while the LORD spoke with Moses.
33.10: Then all the people would stand and bow low at their tent entrances.
33.11: Inside the Tent of Meeting, the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. Afterward Moses would return to the camp, but the young man who assisted him, Joshua son of Nun, stayed behind in the Tent of Meeting.
33.12: Moses said to the LORD, "You have been telling me, `Take these people up to the Promised Land.' But you haven't told me whom you will send with me. You call me by name and tell me I have found favor with you.
33.13: Please, if this is really so, show me your intentions so I will understand you more fully and do exactly what you want me to do. Besides, don't forget that this nation is your very own people."
33.14: And the LORD replied, "I will personally go with you, Moses. I will give you rest--everything will be fine for you."
33.15: Then Moses said, "If you don't go with us personally, don't let us move a step from this place.
33.16: If you don't go with us, how will anyone ever know that your people and I have found favor with you? How else will they know we are special and distinct from all other people on the earth?"
33.17: And the LORD replied to Moses, "I will indeed do what you have asked, for you have found favor with me, and you are my friend."
33.18: Then Moses had one more request. "Please let me see your glorious presence," he said.
33.19: The LORD replied, "I will make all my goodness pass before you, and I will call out my name, `the LORD,' to you. I will show kindness to anyone I choose, and I will show mercy to anyone I choose.
33.20: But you may not look directly at my face, for no one may see me and live."
33.21: The LORD continued, "Stand here on this rock beside me.
33.22: As my glorious presence passes by, I will put you in the cleft of the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed.
33.23: Then I will remove my hand, and you will see me from behind. But my face will not be seen."

34.1: The LORD told Moses, "Prepare two stone tablets like the first ones. I will write on them the same words that were on the tablets you smashed.
34.2: Be ready in the morning to come up Mount Sinai and present yourself to me there on the top of the mountain.
34.3: No one else may come with you. In fact, no one is allowed anywhere on the mountain. Do not even let the flocks or herds graze near the mountain."
34.4: So Moses cut two tablets of stone like the first ones. Early in the morning he climbed Mount Sinai as the LORD had told him, carrying the two stone tablets in his hands.
34.5: Then the LORD came down in a pillar of cloud and called out his own name, "the LORD," as Moses stood there in his presence.
34.6: He passed in front of Moses and said, "I am the LORD, I am the LORD, the merciful and gracious God. I am slow to anger and rich in unfailing love and faithfulness.
34.7: I show this unfailing love to many thousands by forgiving every kind of sin and rebellion. Even so I do not leave sin unpunished, but I punish the children for the sins of their parents to the third and fourth generations."
34.8: Moses immediately fell to the ground and worshiped.
34.9: And he said, "If it is true that I have found favor in your sight, O Lord, then please go with us. Yes, this is an unruly and stubborn people, but please pardon our iniquity and our sins. Accept us as your own special possession."
34.10: The LORD replied, "All right. This is the covenant I am going to make with you. I will perform wonders that have never been done before anywhere in all the earth or in any nation. And all the people around you will see the power of the LORD--the awesome power I will display through you.
34.11: Your responsibility is to obey all the commands I am giving you today. Then I will surely drive out all those who stand in your way--the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
34.12: "Be very careful never to make treaties with the people in the land where you are going. If you do, you soon will be following their evil ways.
34.13: Instead, you must break down their pagan altars, smash the sacred pillars they worship, and cut down their carved images.
34.14: You must worship no other gods, but only the LORD, for he is a God who is passionate about his relationship with you.
34.15: "Do not make treaties of any kind with the people living in the land. They are spiritual prostitutes, committing adultery against me by sacrificing to their gods. If you make peace with them, they will invite you to go with them to worship their gods, and you are likely to do it.
34.16: And you will accept their daughters, who worship other gods, as wives for your sons. Then they will cause your sons to commit adultery against me by worshiping other gods.
34.17: You must make no gods for yourselves at all.
34.18: "Be sure to celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days, just as I instructed you, at the appointed time each year in early spring, for that was when you left Egypt.
34.19: "Every firstborn male belongs to me--of both cattle and sheep.
34.20: A firstborn male donkey may be redeemed from the LORD by presenting a lamb in its place. But if you decide not to make the exchange, you must kill the donkey by breaking its neck. However, you must redeem every firstborn son. No one is allowed to appear before me without a gift.
34.21: "Six days are set aside for work, but on the Sabbath day you must rest, even during the seasons of plowing and harvest.
34.22: And you must remember to celebrate the Festival of Harvest with the first crop of the wheat harvest, and celebrate the Festival of the Final Harvest at the end of the harvest season.
34.23: Three times each year all the men of Israel must appear before the Sovereign LORD, the God of Israel.
34.24: No one will attack and conquer your land when you go to appear before the LORD your God those three times each year. I will drive out the nations that stand in your way and will enlarge your boundaries.
34.25: "You must not offer bread made with yeast as a sacrifice to me. And none of the meat of the Passover lamb may be kept over until the following morning.
34.26: You must bring the best of the first of each year's crop to the house of the LORD your God. "You must not cook a young goat in its mother's milk."
34.27: And the LORD said to Moses, "Write down all these instructions, for they represent the terms of my covenant with you and with Israel."
34.28: Moses was up on the mountain with the LORD forty days and forty nights. In all that time he neither ate nor drank. At that time he wrote the terms of the covenant--the Ten Commandments--on the stone tablets.
34.29: When Moses came down the mountain carrying the stone tablets inscribed with the terms of the covenant, he wasn't aware that his face glowed because he had spoken to the LORD face to face.
34.30: And when Aaron and the people of Israel saw the radiance of Moses' face, they were afraid to come near him.
34.31: But Moses called to them and asked Aaron and the community leaders to come over and talk with him.
34.32: Then all the people came, and Moses gave them the instructions the LORD had given him on Mount Sinai.
34.33: When Moses had finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.
34.34: But whenever he went into the Tent of Meeting to speak with the LORD, he removed the veil until he came out again. Then he would give the people whatever instructions the LORD had given him,
34.35: and the people would see his face aglow. Afterward he would put the veil on again until he returned to speak with the LORD.

35.1: Now Moses called a meeting of all the people and told them, "You must obey these instructions from the LORD.
35.2: Each week, work for six days only. The seventh day is a day of total rest, a holy day that belongs to the LORD. Anyone who works on that day will die.
35.3: Do not even light fires in your homes on that day."
35.4: Then Moses said to all the people, "This is what the LORD has commanded.
35.5: Everyone is invited to bring these offerings to the LORD: gold, silver, and bronze;
35.6: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen; goat hair for cloth;
35.7: tanned ram skins and fine goatskin leather; acacia wood;
35.8: olive oil for the lamps; spices for the anointing oil and the fragrant incense;
35.9: onyx stones, and other stones to be set in the ephod and the chestpiece.
35.10: "Come, all of you who are gifted craftsmen. Construct everything that the LORD has commanded:
35.11: the entire Tabernacle, including the sacred tent and its coverings, the clasps, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases;
35.12: the Ark and its poles; the Ark's cover--the place of atonement; the inner curtain to enclose the Ark in the Most Holy Place;
35.13: the table, its carrying poles, and all of its utensils; the Bread of the Presence;
35.14: the lampstand and its accessories; the lamp cups and the oil for lighting;
35.15: the incense altar and its carrying poles; the anointing oil and fragrant incense; the curtain for the entrance of the Tabernacle;
35.16: the altar of burnt offering; the bronze grating of the altar and its carrying poles and utensils; the large washbasin with its pedestal;
35.17: the curtains for the walls of the courtyard; the posts and their bases; the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard;
35.18: the tent pegs of the Tabernacle and courtyard and their cords;
35.19: the beautifully stitched clothing for the priests to wear while ministering in the Holy Place; the sacred garments for Aaron and his sons to wear while officiating as priests."
35.20: So all the people left Moses and went to their tents to prepare their gifts.
35.21: If their hearts were stirred and they desired to do so, they brought to the LORD their offerings of materials for the Tabernacle and its furnishings and for the holy garments.
35.22: Both men and women came, all whose hearts were willing. Some brought to the LORD their offerings of gold--medallions, earrings, rings from their fingers, and necklaces. They presented gold objects of every kind to the LORD.
35.23: Others brought blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, fine linen, or goat hair for cloth. Some gave tanned ram skins or fine goatskin leather.
35.24: Others brought silver and bronze objects as their offering to the LORD. And those who had acacia wood brought it.
35.25: All the women who were skilled in sewing and spinning prepared blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen cloth, and they brought them in.
35.26: All the women who were willing used their skills to spin and weave the goat hair into cloth.
35.27: The leaders brought onyx stones and the other gemstones to be used for the ephod and the chestpiece.
35.28: They also brought spices and olive oil for the light, the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense.
35.29: So the people of Israel--every man and woman who wanted to help in the work the LORD had given them through Moses--brought their offerings to the LORD.
35.30: And Moses told them, "The LORD has chosen Bezalel son of Uri, grandson of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
35.31: The LORD has filled Bezalel with the Spirit of God, giving him great wisdom, intelligence, and skill in all kinds of crafts.
35.32: He is able to create beautiful objects from gold, silver, and bronze.
35.33: He is skilled in cutting and setting gemstones and in carving wood. In fact, he has every necessary skill.
35.34: And the LORD has given both him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, the ability to teach their skills to others.
35.35: The LORD has given them special skills as jewelers, designers, weavers, and embroiderers in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn on fine linen cloth. They excel in all the crafts needed for the work.

36.1: "Bezalel, Oholiab, and the other craftsmen whom the LORD has gifted with wisdom, skill, and intelligence will construct and furnish the Tabernacle, just as the LORD has commanded."
36.2: So Moses told Bezalel and Oholiab to begin the work, along with all those who were specially gifted by the LORD.
36.3: Moses gave them the materials donated by the people for the completion of the sanctuary. Additional gifts were brought each morning.
36.4: But finally the craftsmen left their work to meet with Moses.
36.5: "We have more than enough materials on hand now to complete the job the LORD has given us to do!" they exclaimed.
36.6: So Moses gave the command, and this message was sent throughout the camp: "Bring no more materials! You have already given more than enough." So the people stopped bringing their offerings.
36.7: Their contributions were more than enough to complete the whole project.
36.8: The skilled weavers first made ten sheets from fine linen. One of the craftsmen then embroidered blue, purple, and scarlet cherubim into them.
36.9: Each sheet was exactly the same size--forty-two feet long and six feet wide.
36.10: Five of these sheets were joined together to make one set, and a second set was made of the other five.
36.11: Fifty blue loops were placed along the edge of the last sheet in each set.
36.12: The fifty loops along the edge of the first set of sheets matched the loops along the edge of the second set.
36.13: Then fifty gold clasps were made to connect the loops on the edge of each set. Thus the Tabernacle was joined together in one piece.
36.14: Above the Tabernacle, a roof covering was made from eleven sheets of cloth made from goat hair.
36.15: Each sheet was exactly the same size--forty-five feet long and six feet wide.
36.16: The craftsmen joined five of these sheets together to make one set, and the six remaining sheets were joined to make a second set.
36.17: Then they made fifty loops along the edge of the last sheet in each set.
36.18: They also made fifty small bronze clasps to couple the loops, so the two sets of sheets were firmly attached to each other. In this way, the roof covering was joined together in one piece.
36.19: Then they made two more layers for the roof covering. The first was made of tanned ram skins, and the second was made of fine goatskin leather.
36.20: For the framework of the Tabernacle, they made frames of acacia wood standing on end.
36.21: Each frame was 15 feet high and 2 1/4 feet wide.
36.22: There were two pegs on each frame so they could be joined to the next frame. All the frames were made this way.
36.23: They made twenty frames to support the south side,
36.24: along with forty silver bases, two for each frame.
36.25: They also made twenty frames for the north side of the Tabernacle,
36.26: along with forty silver bases, two for each frame.
36.27: The west side of the Tabernacle, which was its rear, was made from six frames,
36.28: plus an extra frame at each corner.
36.29: These corner frames were connected at the bottom and firmly attached at the top with a single ring, forming a single unit from top to bottom. They made two of these, one for each rear corner.
36.30: So for the west side they made a total of eight frames, along with sixteen silver bases, two for each frame.
36.31: Then they made five crossbars from acacia wood to tie the frames on the south side together.
36.32: They made another five for the north side and five for the west side.
36.33: The middle crossbar of the five was halfway up the frames, along each side, running from one end to the other.
36.34: The frames and crossbars were all overlaid with gold. The rings used to hold the crossbars were made of pure gold.
36.35: The inner curtain was made of fine linen cloth, and cherubim were skillfully embroidered into it with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
36.36: This curtain was then attached to four gold hooks set into four posts of acacia wood. The posts were overlaid with gold and set into four silver bases.
36.37: Then they made another curtain for the entrance to the sacred tent. It was made of fine linen cloth and embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
36.38: This curtain was connected by five hooks to five posts. The posts with their decorated tops and bands were overlaid with gold. The five bases were molded from bronze.

37.1: Next Bezalel made the Ark out of acacia wood. It was 3 3/4 feet long, 2 1/4 feet wide, and 2 1/4 feet high.
37.2: It was overlaid with pure gold inside and out, and it had a molding of gold all the way around.
37.3: Four gold rings were fastened to its four feet, two rings at each side.
37.4: Then he made poles from acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
37.5: He put the poles into the rings at the sides of the Ark to carry it.
37.6: Then, from pure gold, he made the Ark's cover--the place of atonement. It was 3 3/4 feet long and 2 1/4 feet wide.
37.7: He made two figures of cherubim out of hammered gold and placed them at the two ends of the atonement cover.
37.8: They were made so they were actually a part of the atonement cover--it was all one piece.
37.9: The cherubim faced each other as they looked down on the atonement cover, and their wings were stretched out above the atonement cover to protect it.
37.10: Then he made a table out of acacia wood, 3 feet long, 1 1/2 feet wide, and 2 1/4 feet high.
37.11: It was overlaid with pure gold, with a gold molding all around the edge.
37.12: A rim about 3 inches wide was attached along the edges of the table, and a gold molding ran around the rim.
37.13: Then he cast four rings of gold and attached them to the four table legs
37.14: next to the rim. These were made to hold the carrying poles in place.
37.15: He made the carrying poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
37.16: Next, using pure gold, he made the plates, dishes, bowls, and pitchers to be placed on the table. These utensils were to be used in pouring out drink offerings.
37.17: Then he made the lampstand, again using pure, hammered gold. Its base, center stem, lamp cups, blossoms, and buds were all of one piece.
37.18: The lampstand had six branches, three going out from each side of the center stem.
37.19: Each of the six branches held a cup shaped like an almond blossom, complete with buds and petals.
37.20: The center stem of the lampstand was also decorated with four almond blossoms.
37.21: One blossom was set beneath each pair of branches, where they extended from the center stem.
37.22: The decorations and branches were all one piece with the stem, and they were hammered from pure gold.
37.23: He also made the seven lamps, the lamp snuffers, and the trays, all of pure gold.
37.24: The entire lampstand, along with its accessories, was made from seventy-five pounds of pure gold.
37.25: The incense altar was made of acacia wood. It was eighteen inches square and three feet high, with its corner horns made from the same piece of wood as the altar itself.
37.26: He overlaid the top, sides, and horns of the altar with pure gold and ran a gold molding around the edge.
37.27: Two gold rings were placed on opposite sides, beneath the molding, to hold the carrying poles.
37.28: The carrying poles were made of acacia wood and were overlaid with gold.
37.29: Then he made the sacred oil, for anointing the priests, and the fragrant incense, using the techniques of the most skilled incense maker.

38.1: The altar for burning animal sacrifices also was constructed of acacia wood. It was 7 1/2 feet square at the top and 4 1/2 feet high.
38.2: There were four horns, one at each of the four corners, all of one piece with the rest. This altar was overlaid with bronze.
38.3: Then he made all the bronze utensils to be used with the altar--the ash buckets, shovels, basins, meat hooks, and firepans.
38.4: Next he made a bronze grating that rested on a ledge about halfway down into the firebox.
38.5: Four rings were cast for each side of the grating to support the carrying poles.
38.6: The carrying poles themselves were made of acacia wood and were overlaid with bronze.
38.7: These poles were inserted into the rings at the side of the altar. The altar was hollow and was made from planks.
38.8: The bronze washbasin and its bronze pedestal were cast from bronze mirrors donated by the women who served at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
38.9: Then he constructed the courtyard. The south wall was 150 feet long. It consisted of curtains made of fine linen.
38.10: There were twenty posts, each with its own bronze base, and there were silver hooks and rods to hold up the curtains.
38.11: The north wall was also 150 feet long, with twenty bronze posts and bases and with silver hooks and rods.
38.12: The west end was 75 feet wide. The walls were made from curtains supported by ten posts and bases and with silver hooks and rods.
38.13: The east end was also 75 feet wide.
38.14: The courtyard entrance was on the east side, flanked by two curtains. The curtain on the right side was 22 1/2 feet long and was supported by three posts set into three bases.
38.15: The curtain on the left side was also 22 1/2 feet long and was supported by three posts set into three bases.
38.16: All the curtains used in the courtyard walls were made of fine linen.
38.17: Each post had a bronze base, and all the hooks and rods were silver. The tops of the posts were overlaid with silver, and the rods to hold up the curtains were solid silver.
38.18: The curtain that covered the entrance to the courtyard was made of fine linen cloth and embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn. It was 30 feet long and 7 1/2 feet high, just like the curtains of the courtyard walls.
38.19: It was supported by four posts set into four bronze bases. The tops of the posts were overlaid with silver, and the hooks and rods were also made of silver.
38.20: All the tent pegs used in the Tabernacle and courtyard were made of bronze.
38.21: Here is an inventory of the materials used in building the Tabernacle of the Covenant. Moses directed the Levites to compile the figures, and Ithamar son of Aaron the priest served as recorder.
38.22: Bezalel son of Uri, grandson of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, was in charge of the whole project, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
38.23: He was assisted by Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, a craftsman expert at engraving, designing, and embroidering blue, purple, and scarlet yarn on fine linen cloth.
38.24: The people brought gifts of gold totaling about 2,200 pounds, all of which was used throughout the Tabernacle.
38.25: The amount of silver that was given was about 7,545 pounds.
38.26: It came from the tax of one-fifth of an ounce of silver collected from each of those registered in the census. This included all the men who were twenty years old or older, 603,550 in all.
38.27: The 100 bases for the frames of the sanctuary walls and for the posts supporting the inner curtain required 7,500 pounds of silver, about 75 pounds for each base.
38.28: The rest of the silver, about 45 pounds, was used to make the rods and hooks and to overlay the tops of the posts.
38.29: The people also brought 5,310 pounds of bronze,
38.30: which was used for casting the bases for the posts at the entrance to the Tabernacle, and for the bronze altar with its bronze grating and altar utensils.
38.31: Bronze was also used to make the bases for the posts that supported the curtains around the courtyard, the bases for the curtain at the entrance of the courtyard, and all the tent pegs used to hold the curtains of the courtyard in place.

39.1: For the priests, the craftsmen made beautiful garments of blue, purple, and scarlet cloth--clothing to be worn while ministering in the Holy Place. This same cloth was used for Aaron's sacred garments, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
39.2: The ephod was made from fine linen cloth and embroidered with gold thread and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
39.3: A skilled craftsman made gold thread by beating gold into thin sheets and cutting it into fine strips. He then embroidered it into the linen with the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
39.4: They made two shoulder-pieces for the ephod, which were attached to its corners so it could be tied down.
39.5: They also made an elaborate woven sash of the same materials: fine linen cloth; blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; and gold thread, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
39.6: The two onyx stones, attached to the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, were set in gold filigree. The stones were engraved with the names of the tribes of Israel, just as initials are engraved on a seal.
39.7: These stones served as reminders to the LORD concerning the people of Israel. All this was done just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
39.8: The chestpiece was made in the same style as the ephod, crafted from fine linen cloth and embroidered with gold thread and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
39.9: It was doubled over to form a pouch, nine inches square.
39.10: Four rows of gemstones were set across it. In the first row were a red carnelian, a chrysolite, and an emerald.
39.11: In the second row were a turquoise, a sapphire, and a white moonstone.
39.12: In the third row were a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst.
39.13: In the fourth row were a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. Each of these gemstones was set in gold.
39.14: The stones were engraved like a seal, each with the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
39.15: To attach the chestpiece to the ephod, they made braided cords of pure gold.
39.16: They also made two gold rings and attached them to the top corners of the chestpiece.
39.17: The two gold cords were put through the gold rings on the chestpiece,
39.18: and the ends of the cords were tied to the gold settings on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod.
39.19: Two more gold rings were attached to the lower inside corners of the chestpiece next to the ephod.
39.20: Then two gold rings were attached to the ephod near the sash.
39.21: Blue cords were used to attach the bottom rings of the chestpiece to the rings on the ephod. In this way, the chestpiece was held securely to the ephod above the beautiful sash. All this was done just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
39.22: The robe of the ephod was woven entirely of blue yarn,
39.23: with an opening for Aaron's head in the middle of it. The edge of this opening was reinforced with a woven collar, so it would not tear.
39.24: Pomegranates were attached to the bottom edge of the robe. These were finely crafted of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
39.25: Bells of pure gold were placed between the pomegranates along the hem of the robe,
39.26: with bells and pomegranates alternating all around the hem. This robe was to be worn when Aaron ministered to the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
39.27: Tunics were then made for Aaron and his sons from fine linen cloth.
39.28: The turban, the headdresses, and the underclothes were all made of this fine linen.
39.29: The sashes were made of fine linen cloth and embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
39.30: Finally, they made the sacred medallion of pure gold to be worn on the front of the turban. Using the techniques of an engraver, they inscribed it with these words: SET APART AS HOLY TO THE LORD.
39.31: This medallion was tied to the turban with a blue cord, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
39.32: And so at last the Tabernacle was finished. The Israelites had done everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
39.33: And they brought the entire Tabernacle to Moses: the sacred tent with all its furnishings, the clasps, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases;
39.34: the layers of tanned ram skins and fine goatskin leather; the inner curtain that enclosed the Most Holy Place;
39.35: the Ark of the Covenant and its carrying poles; the Ark's cover--the place of atonement;
39.36: the table and all its utensils; the Bread of the Presence;
39.37: the gold lampstand and its accessories; the lamp cups and the oil for lighting;
39.38: the gold altar; the anointing oil; the fragrant incense; the curtain for the entrance of the sacred tent;
39.39: the bronze altar; the bronze grating; its poles and utensils; the large washbasin and its pedestal;
39.40: the curtains for the walls of the courtyard and the posts and bases holding them up; the curtain at the courtyard entrance; the cords and tent pegs; all the articles used in the operation of the Tabernacle;
39.41: the beautifully crafted garments to be worn while ministering in the Holy Place--the holy garments for Aaron the priest and for his sons to wear while on duty.
39.42: So the people of Israel followed all of the LORD's instructions to Moses.
39.43: Moses inspected all their work and blessed them because it had been done as the LORD had commanded him.

40.1: The LORD now said to Moses,
40.2: "Set up the Tabernacle on the first day of the new year.
40.3: Place the Ark of the Covenant inside, and install the inner curtain to enclose the Ark within the Most Holy Place.
40.4: Then bring in the table, and arrange the utensils on it. And bring in the lampstand, and set up the lamps.
40.5: "Place the incense altar just outside the inner curtain, opposite the Ark of the Covenant. Set up the curtain made for the entrance of the Tabernacle.
40.6: Place the altar of burnt offering in front of the Tabernacle entrance.
40.7: Set the large washbasin between the Tabernacle and the altar and fill it with water.
40.8: Then set up the courtyard around the outside of the tent, and hang the curtain for the courtyard entrance.
40.9: "Take the anointing oil and sprinkle it on the Tabernacle and on all its furnishings to make them holy.
40.10: Sprinkle the anointing oil on the altar of burnt offering and its utensils, sanctifying them. Then the altar will become most holy.
40.11: Next anoint the large washbasin and its pedestal to make them holy.
40.12: "Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the Tabernacle, and wash them with water.
40.13: Clothe Aaron with the holy garments and anoint him, setting him apart to serve me as a priest.
40.14: Then bring his sons and dress them in their tunics.
40.15: Anoint them as you did their father, so they may serve me as priests. With this anointing, Aaron's descendants are set apart for the priesthood forever, from generation to generation."
40.16: Moses proceeded to do everything as the LORD had commanded him.
40.17: So the Tabernacle was set up on the first day of the new year.
40.18: Moses put it together by setting its frames into their bases and attaching the crossbars and raising the posts.
40.19: Then he spread the coverings over the Tabernacle framework and put on the roof layers, just as the LORD had commanded him.
40.20: He placed inside the Ark the stone tablets inscribed with the terms of the covenant, and then he attached the Ark's carrying poles. He also set the Ark's cover--the place of atonement--on top of it.
40.21: Then he brought the Ark of the Covenant into the Tabernacle and set up the inner curtain to shield it from view, just as the LORD had commanded.
40.22: Next he placed the table in the Tabernacle, along the north side of the Holy Place, just outside the inner curtain.
40.23: And he arranged the Bread of the Presence on the table that stands before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded.
40.24: He set the lampstand in the Tabernacle across from the table on the south side of the Holy Place.
40.25: Then he set up the lamps in the LORD's presence, just as the LORD had commanded.
40.26: He also placed the incense altar in the Tabernacle, in the Holy Place in front of the inner curtain.
40.27: On it he burned the fragrant incense made from sweet spices, just as the LORD had commanded.
40.28: He attached the curtain at the entrance of the Tabernacle,
40.29: and he placed the altar of burnt offering near the Tabernacle entrance. On it he offered a burnt offering and a grain offering, just as the LORD had commanded.
40.30: Next he placed the large washbasin between the Tabernacle and the altar. He filled it with water so the priests could use it to wash themselves.
40.31: Moses and Aaron and Aaron's sons washed their hands and feet in the basin.
40.32: Whenever they walked past the altar to enter the Tabernacle, they were to stop and wash, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
40.33: Then he hung the curtains forming the courtyard around the Tabernacle and the altar. And he set up the curtain at the entrance of the courtyard. So at last Moses finished the work.
40.34: Then the cloud covered the Tabernacle, and the glorious presence of the LORD filled it.
40.35: Moses was no longer able to enter the Tabernacle because the cloud had settled down over it, and the Tabernacle was filled with the awesome glory of the LORD.
40.36: Now whenever the cloud lifted from the Tabernacle and moved, the people of Israel would set out on their journey, following it.
40.37: But if the cloud stayed, they would stay until it moved again.
40.38: The cloud of the LORD rested on the Tabernacle during the day, and at night there was fire in the cloud so all the people of Israel could see it. This continued throughout all their journeys.

1.1: The LORD called to Moses from the Tabernacle and said to him,
1.2: "Give the following instructions to the Israelites: Whenever you present offerings to the LORD, you must bring animals from your flocks and herds.
1.3: "If your sacrifice for a whole burnt offering is from the herd, bring a bull with no physical defects to the entrance of the Tabernacle so it will be accepted by the LORD.
1.4: Lay your hand on its head so the LORD will accept it as your substitute, thus making atonement for you.
1.5: Then slaughter the animal in the LORD's presence, and Aaron's sons, the priests, will present the blood by sprinkling it against the sides of the altar that stands in front of the Tabernacle.
1.6: When the animal has been skinned and cut into pieces,
1.7: the sons of Aaron the priest will build a wood fire on the altar.
1.8: Aaron's sons will then put the pieces of the animal, including its head and fat, on the wood fire.
1.9: But the internal organs and legs must first be washed with water. Then the priests will burn the entire sacrifice on the altar. It is a whole burnt offering made by fire, very pleasing to the LORD.
1.10: "If your sacrifice for a whole burnt offering is from the flock, bring a male sheep or goat with no physical defects.
1.11: Slaughter the animal on the north side of the altar in the LORD's presence. Aaron's sons, the priests, will sprinkle its blood against the sides of the altar.
1.12: Then you must cut the animal in pieces, and the priests will lay the pieces of the sacrifice, including the head and fat, on top of the wood fire on the altar.
1.13: The internal organs and legs must first be washed with water. Then the priests will burn the entire sacrifice on the altar. It is a whole burnt offering made by fire, very pleasing to the LORD.
1.14: "If you bring a bird as a burnt offering to the LORD, choose either a turtledove or a young pigeon.
1.15: The priest will take the bird to the altar, twist off its head, and burn the head on the altar. He must then let its blood drain out against the sides of the altar.
1.16: The priest must remove the crop and the feathers and throw them to the east side of the altar among the ashes.
1.17: Then, grasping the bird by its wings, the priest will tear the bird apart, though not completely. Then he will burn it on top of the wood fire on the altar. It is a whole burnt offering made by fire, very pleasing to the LORD.

2.1: "When you bring a grain offering to the LORD, the offering must consist of choice flour. You are to pour olive oil on it and sprinkle it with incense.
2.2: Bring this offering to one of Aaron's sons, and he will take a handful of the flour mixed with olive oil, together with all the incense, and burn this token portion on the altar fire. It is an offering made by fire, very pleasing to the LORD.
2.3: The rest of the flour will be given to Aaron and his sons. It will be considered a most holy part of the offerings given to the LORD by fire.
2.4: "When you present some kind of baked bread as a grain offering, it must be made of choice flour mixed with olive oil but without any yeast. It may be presented in the form of cakes mixed with olive oil or wafers spread with olive oil.
2.5: If your grain offering is cooked on a griddle, it must be made of choice flour and olive oil, and it must contain no yeast.
2.6: Break it into pieces and pour oil on it; it is a kind of grain offering.
2.7: If your offering is prepared in a pan, it also must be made of choice flour and olive oil.
2.8: "No matter how a grain offering has been prepared before being offered to the LORD, bring it to the priests who will present it at the altar.
2.9: The priests will take a token portion of the grain offering and burn it on the altar as an offering made by fire, and it will be very pleasing to the LORD.
2.10: The rest of the grain offering will be given to Aaron and his sons as their food. It will be considered a most holy part of the offerings given to the LORD by fire.
2.11: "Do not use yeast in any of the grain offerings you present to the LORD, because no yeast or honey may be burned as an offering to the LORD by fire.
2.12: You may add yeast and honey to the offerings presented at harvesttime, but these must never be burned on the altar as an offering pleasing to the LORD.
2.13: Season all your grain offerings with salt, to remind you of God's covenant. Never forget to add salt to your grain offerings.
2.14: "If you present a grain offering to the LORD from the first portion of your harvest, bring kernels of new grain that have been roasted on a fire.
2.15: Since it is a grain offering, put olive oil on it and sprinkle it with incense.
2.16: The priests will take a token portion of the roasted grain mixed with olive oil, together with all the incense, and burn it as an offering given to the LORD by fire.

3.1: "If you want to present a peace offering from the herd, use either a bull or a cow. The animal you offer to the LORD must have no physical defects.
3.2: Lay your hand on the animal's head, and slaughter it at the entrance of the Tabernacle. Aaron's sons, the priests, will then sprinkle the animal's blood against the sides of the altar.
3.3: Part of this peace offering must be presented to the LORD as an offering made by fire. This includes the fat around the internal organs,
3.4: the two kidneys with the fat around them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which is to be removed with the kidneys.
3.5: The sons of Aaron will burn these on the altar on top of the burnt offering on the wood fire. It is an offering made by fire, very pleasing to the LORD.
3.6: "If you present a peace offering to the LORD from the flock, you may bring either a goat or a sheep. It may be either male or female, and it must have no physical defects.
3.7: If you bring a sheep as your gift, present it to the LORD
3.8: by laying your hand on its head and slaughtering it at the entrance of the Tabernacle. The sons of Aaron will then sprinkle the sheep's blood against the sides of the altar.
3.9: Part of this peace offering must be presented to the LORD as an offering made by fire. This includes the fat of the entire tail cut off near the backbone, the fat around the internal organs,
3.10: the two kidneys with the fat around them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which is to be removed with the kidneys.
3.11: The priest will burn them on the altar as food, an offering given to the LORD by fire.
3.12: "If you bring a goat as your offering to the LORD,
3.13: lay your hand on its head, and slaughter it at the entrance of the Tabernacle. Then the sons of Aaron will sprinkle the goat's blood against the sides of the altar.
3.14: Part of this offering must be presented to the LORD as an offering made by fire. This part includes the fat around the internal organs,
3.15: the two kidneys with the fat around them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which is to be removed with the kidneys.
3.16: The priest will burn them on the altar as food, an offering made by fire; these will be very pleasing to the LORD. Remember, all the fat belongs to the LORD.
3.17: "You must never eat any fat or blood. This is a permanent law for you and all your descendants, wherever they may live."

4.1: Then the LORD said to Moses,
4.2: "Give the Israelites the following instructions for dealing with those who sin unintentionally by doing anything forbidden by the LORD's commands.
4.3: "If the high priest sins, bringing guilt upon the entire community, he must bring to the LORD a young bull with no physical defects.
4.4: He must present the bull to the LORD at the entrance of the Tabernacle, lay his hand on the bull's head, and slaughter it there in the LORD's presence.
4.5: The priest on duty will then take some of the animal's blood into the Tabernacle,
4.6: dip his finger into the blood, and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD in front of the inner curtain of the Most Holy Place.
4.7: The priest will put some of the blood on the horns of the incense altar that stands in the LORD's presence in the Tabernacle. The rest of the bull's blood must be poured out at the base of the altar of burnt offerings at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
4.8: The priest must remove all the fat around the bull's internal organs,
4.9: the two kidneys with the fat around them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver.
4.10: Then he must burn them on the altar of burnt offerings, just as is done with the bull or cow sacrificed as a peace offering.
4.11: But the rest of the bull--its hide, meat, head, legs, internal organs, and dung--
4.12: must be carried away to a ceremonially clean place outside the camp, the place where the ashes are thrown. He will burn it all on a wood fire in the ash heap.
4.13: "If the entire Israelite community does something forbidden by the LORD and the matter escapes the community's notice, all the people will be guilty.
4.14: When they discover their sin, the leaders of the community must bring a young bull for a sin offering and present it at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
4.15: The leaders must then lay their hands on the bull's head and slaughter it there before the LORD.
4.16: The priest will bring some of its blood into the Tabernacle,
4.17: dip his finger into the blood, and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD in front of the inner curtain.
4.18: He will then put some of the blood on the horns of the incense altar that stands in the LORD's presence in the Tabernacle. The rest of the blood must then be poured out at the base of the altar of burnt offerings at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
4.19: The priest must remove all the animal's fat and burn it on the altar,
4.20: following the same procedure as with the sin offering for the priest. In this way, the priest will make atonement for the people, and they will be forgiven.
4.21: The priest must then take what is left of the bull outside the camp and burn it there, just as is done with the sin offering for the high priest. This is a sin offering for the entire community of Israel.
4.22: "If one of Israel's leaders does something forbidden by the LORD his God, he will be guilty even if he sinned unintentionally.
4.23: When he becomes aware of his sin, he must bring as his offering a male goat with no physical defects.
4.24: He is to lay his hand on the goat's head and slaughter it before the LORD at the place where burnt offerings are slaughtered. This will be his sin offering.
4.25: Then the priest will dip his finger into the blood of the sin offering, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offerings, and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
4.26: He must burn all the goat's fat on the altar, just as is done with the peace offering. In this way, the priest will make atonement for the leader's sin, and he will be forgiven.
4.27: "If any of the citizens of Israel do something forbidden by the LORD, they will be guilty even if they sinned unintentionally.
4.28: When they become aware of their sin, they must bring as their offering a female goat with no physical defects. It will be offered for their sin.
4.29: They are to lay a hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it at the place where burnt offerings are slaughtered.
4.30: The priest will then dip his finger into the blood, put the blood on the horns of the altar of burnt offerings, and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
4.31: Those who are guilty must remove all the goat's fat, just as is done with the peace offering. Then the priest will burn the fat on the altar, and it will be very pleasing to the LORD. In this way, the priest will make atonement for them, and they will be forgiven.
4.32: "If any of the people bring a sheep as their sin offering, it must be a female with no physical defects.
4.33: They are to lay a hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it at the place where the burnt offerings are slaughtered.
4.34: The priest will then dip his finger into the blood, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offerings, and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
4.35: Those who are guilty must remove all the sheep's fat, just as is done with a sheep presented as a peace offering. Then the priest will burn the fat on the altar on top of the offerings given to the LORD by fire. In this way, the priest will make atonement for them, and they will be forgiven.

5.1: "If any of the people are called to testify about something they have witnessed, but they refuse to testify, they will be held responsible and be subject to punishment.
5.2: "Or if they touch something that is ceremonially unclean, such as the dead body of an animal that is ceremonially unclean--whether a wild animal, a domesticated animal, or an animal that scurries along the ground--they will be considered ceremonially unclean and guilty, even if they are unaware of their defilement.
5.3: "Or if they come into contact with any source of human defilement, even if they don't realize they have been defiled, they will be considered guilty as soon as they become aware of it.
5.4: "Or if they make a rash vow of any kind, whether its purpose is for good or bad, they will be considered guilty even if they were not fully aware of what they were doing at the time.
5.5: "When any of the people become aware of their guilt in any of these ways, they must confess their sin
5.6: and bring to the LORD as their penalty a female from the flock, either a sheep or a goat. This will be a sin offering to remove their sin, and the priest will make atonement for them.
5.7: "If any of them cannot afford to bring a sheep, they must bring to the LORD two young turtledoves or two young pigeons as the penalty for their sin. One of the birds will be a sin offering, and the other will be a burnt offering.
5.8: They must bring them to the priest, who will offer one of the birds as the sin offering. The priest will wring its neck but without severing its head from the body.
5.9: Then he will sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering against the sides of the altar, and the rest will be drained out at the base of the altar.
5.10: The priest will offer the second bird as a whole burnt offering, following all the procedures that have been prescribed. In this way, the priest will make atonement for those who are guilty, and they will be forgiven.
5.11: "If any of the people cannot afford to bring young turtledoves or pigeons, they must bring two quarts of choice flour for their sin offering. Since it is a sin offering, they must not mix it with olive oil or put any incense on it.
5.12: They must take the flour to the priest, who will scoop out a handful as a token portion. He will burn this flour on the altar just like any other offering given to the LORD by fire. This will be their sin offering.
5.13: In this way, the priest will make atonement for those who are guilty, and they will be forgiven. The rest of the flour will belong to the priest, just as with the grain offering."
5.14: Then the LORD said to Moses,
5.15: "If any of the people sin by unintentionally defiling the LORD's sacred property, they must bring to the LORD a ram from the flock as their guilt offering. The animal must have no physical defects, and it must be of the proper value in silver as measured by the standard sanctuary shekel.
5.16: They must then make restitution for whatever holy things they have defiled by paying for the loss, plus an added penalty of 20 percent. When they give their payments to the priest, he will make atonement for them with the ram sacrificed as a guilt offering, and they will be forgiven.
5.17: "If any of them sin by doing something forbidden by the LORD, even if it is done unintentionally, they will be held responsible. When they become aware of their guilt,
5.18: they must bring to the priest a ram from the flock as a guilt offering. The animal must have no physical defects, and it must be of the proper value. In this way, the priest will make atonement for those who are guilty, and they will be forgiven.
5.19: This is a guilt offering, for they have been guilty of an offense against the LORD."

6.1: And the LORD said to Moses,
6.2: "Suppose some of the people sin against the LORD by falsely telling their neighbor that an item entrusted to their safekeeping has been lost or stolen. Or suppose they have been dishonest with regard to a security deposit, or they have taken something by theft or extortion.
6.3: Or suppose they find a lost item and lie about it, or they deny something while under oath, or they commit any other similar sin.
6.4: If they have sinned in any of these ways and are guilty, they must give back whatever they have taken by theft or extortion, whether a security deposit, or property entrusted to them, or a lost object that they claimed as their own,
6.5: or anything gained by swearing falsely. When they realize their guilt, they must restore the principal amount plus a penalty of 20 percent to the person they have harmed.
6.6: They must then bring a guilt offering to the priest, who will present it before the LORD. This offering must be a ram with no physical defects or the animal's equivalent value in silver.
6.7: The priest will then make atonement for them before the LORD, and they will be forgiven."
6.8: Then the LORD said to Moses,
6.9: "Give Aaron and his sons the following instructions regarding the whole burnt offering. The burnt offering must be left on the altar until the next morning, and the altar fire must be kept burning all night.
6.10: The next morning, after dressing in his special linen clothing and undergarments, the priest on duty must clean out the ashes of the burnt offering and put them beside the altar.
6.11: Then he must change back into his normal clothing and carry the ashes outside the camp to a place that is ceremonially clean.
6.12: Meanwhile, the fire on the altar must be kept burning; it must never go out. Each morning the priest will add fresh wood to the fire and arrange the daily whole burnt offering on it. He must then burn the fat of the peace offerings on top of this daily whole burnt offering.
6.13: Remember, the fire must be kept burning on the altar at all times. It must never go out.
6.14: "These are the instructions regarding the grain offering. Aaron's sons must present this offering to the LORD in front of the altar.
6.15: The priest on duty will take a handful of the choice flour that has been mixed with olive oil and sprinkled with incense. He will burn this token portion on the altar, and it will be very pleasing to the LORD.
6.16: After burning this handful, the rest of the flour will belong to Aaron and his sons for their food. It must, however, be baked without yeast and eaten in a sacred place within the courtyard of the Tabernacle.
6.17: Remember, this flour may never be prepared with yeast. I have given it to the priests as their share of the offerings presented to me by fire. Like the sin offering and the guilt offering, it is most holy.
6.18: Any of Aaron's male descendants, from generation to generation, may eat of the grain offering, because it is their regular share of the offerings given to the LORD by fire. Anyone or anything that touches this food will become holy."
6.19: And the LORD said to Moses,
6.20: "On the day Aaron and his sons are anointed, they must bring to the LORD a grain offering of two quarts of choice flour, half to be offered in the morning and half to be offered in the evening.
6.21: It must be cooked on a griddle with olive oil, and it must be well mixed and broken into pieces. You must present this grain offering, and it will be very pleasing to the LORD.
6.22: As the sons of the priests replace their fathers, they will be inducted into office by offering this same sacrifice on the day they are anointed. It is the LORD's regular share, and it must be completely burned up.
6.23: All such grain offerings of the priests must be entirely burned up. None of the flour may be eaten."
6.24: Then the LORD said to Moses,
6.25: "Give Aaron and his sons these further instructions regarding the sin offering. The animal given as a sin offering is most holy and must be slaughtered in the LORD's presence at the place where the burnt offerings are slaughtered.
6.26: The priest who offers the sacrifice may eat his portion in a sacred place within the courtyard of the Tabernacle.
6.27: Anything or anyone who touches the sacrificial meat will become holy, and if the sacrificial blood splatters anyone's clothing, it must be washed off in a sacred place.
6.28: If a clay pot is used to boil the sacrificial meat, it must be broken. If a bronze kettle is used, it must be scoured and rinsed thoroughly with water.
6.29: Only males from a priest's family may eat of this offering, for it is most holy.
6.30: If, however, the blood of a sin offering has been taken into the Tabernacle to make atonement in the Holy Place for the people's sins, none of that animal's meat may be eaten. It must be completely burned up.

7.1: "These are the instructions for the guilt offering, which is most holy.
7.2: The animal sacrificed as a guilt offering must be slaughtered where the burnt offerings are slaughtered, and its blood sprinkled against the sides of the altar.
7.3: The priest will then offer all its fat on the altar, including the fat from the tail, the fat around the internal organs,
7.4: the two kidneys with the fat around them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which is to be removed with the kidneys.
7.5: The priests will burn these parts on the altar as an offering to the LORD made by fire. It is a guilt offering.
7.6: All males from a priest's family may eat the meat, and it must be eaten in a sacred place, for it is most holy.
7.7: "For both the sin offering and the guilt offering, the meat of the sacrificed animal belongs to the priest in charge of the atonement ceremony.
7.8: In the case of the whole burnt offering, the hide of the sacrificed animal also belongs to the priest.
7.9: Any grain offering that has been baked in an oven, prepared in a pan, or cooked on a griddle belongs to the priest who presents it.
7.10: All other grain offerings, whether flour mixed with olive oil or dry flour, are to be shared among all the priests and their sons.
7.11: "These are the instructions regarding the different kinds of peace offerings that may be presented to the LORD.
7.12: If you present your peace offering as a thanksgiving offering, the usual animal sacrifice must be accompanied by various kinds of bread--loaves, wafers, and cakes--all made without yeast and soaked with olive oil.
7.13: This peace offering of thanksgiving must also be accompanied by loaves of yeast bread.
7.14: One of each kind of bread must be presented as a gift to the LORD. This bread will then belong to the priest who sprinkles the altar with blood from the sacrificed animal.
7.15: The animal's meat must be eaten on the same day it is offered. None of it may be saved for the next morning.
7.16: "However, if you bring an offering to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering, the meat may be eaten on that same day, and whatever is left over may be eaten on the second day.
7.17: But anything left over until the third day must be completely burned up.
7.18: If any of the meat from this peace offering is eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted by the LORD.
