23.38: These festivals must be observed in addition to the LORD's regular Sabbath days. And these offerings must be given in addition to your personal gifts, the offerings you make to accompany your vows, and any freewill offerings that you present to the LORD.
23.39: "Now, on the first day of the Festival of Shelters, after you have harvested all the produce of the land, you will begin to celebrate this seven-day festival to the LORD. Remember that the first day and closing eighth day of the festival will be days of total rest.
23.40: On the first day, gather fruit from citrus trees, and collect palm fronds and other leafy branches and willows that grow by the streams. Then rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.
23.41: You must observe this seven-day festival to the LORD every year. This is a permanent law for you, and it must be kept by all future generations.
23.42: During the seven festival days, all of you who are Israelites by birth must live in shelters.
23.43: This will remind each new generation of Israelites that their ancestors had to live in shelters when I rescued them from the land of Egypt. I, the LORD, am your God."
23.44: So Moses gave these instructions regarding the annual festivals of the LORD to the Israelites.

24.1: The LORD said to Moses,
24.2: "Command the people of Israel to provide you with pure olive oil for the lampstand, so it can be kept burning continually.
24.3: Aaron will set it up outside the inner curtain of the Most Holy Place in the Tabernacle and must arrange to have the lamps tended continually, from evening until morning, before the LORD. This is a permanent law for you, and it must be kept by all future generations.
24.4: The lamps on the pure gold lampstand must be tended continually in the LORD's presence.
24.5: "You must bake twelve loaves of bread from choice flour, using three quarts of flour for each loaf.
24.6: Place the bread in the LORD's presence on the pure gold table, and arrange the loaves in two rows, with six in each row.
24.7: Sprinkle some pure frankincense near each row. It will serve as a token offering, to be burned in place of the bread as an offering given to the LORD by fire.
24.8: Every Sabbath day this bread must be laid out before the LORD on behalf of the Israelites as a continual part of the covenant.
24.9: The loaves of bread belong to Aaron and his male descendants, who must eat them in a sacred place, for they represent a most holy portion of the offerings given to the LORD by fire."
24.10: One day a man who had an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father got into a fight with one of the Israelite men.
24.11: During the fight, this son of an Israelite woman blasphemed the LORD's name. So the man was brought to Moses for judgment. His mother's name was Shelomith. She was the daughter of Dibri of the tribe of Dan.
24.12: They put the man in custody until the LORD's will in the matter should become clear.
24.13: Then the LORD said to Moses,
24.14: "Take the blasphemer outside the camp, and tell all those who heard him to lay their hands on his head. Then let the entire community stone him to death.
24.15: Say to the people of Israel: Those who blaspheme God will suffer the consequences of their guilt and be punished.
24.16: Anyone who blasphemes the LORD's name must be stoned to death by the whole community of Israel. Any Israelite or foreigner among you who blasphemes the LORD's name will surely die.
24.17: "Anyone who takes another person's life must be put to death.
24.18: "Anyone who kills another person's animal must pay it back in full--a live animal for the animal that was killed.
24.19: "Anyone who injures another person must be dealt with according to the injury inflicted--
24.20: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. Whatever anyone does to hurt another person must be paid back in kind.
24.21: "Whoever kills an animal must make full restitution, but whoever kills another person must be put to death.
24.22: "These same regulations apply to Israelites by birth and foreigners who live among you. I, the LORD, am your God."
24.23: After Moses gave all these instructions to the Israelites, they led the blasphemer outside the camp and stoned him to death, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

25.1: While Moses was on Mount Sinai, the LORD said to him,
25.2: "Give these instructions to the Israelites: When you have entered the land I am giving you as an inheritance, the land itself must observe a Sabbath to the LORD every seventh year.
25.3: For six years you may plant your fields and prune your vineyards and harvest your crops,
25.4: but during the seventh year the land will enjoy a Sabbath year of rest to the LORD. Do not plant your crops or prune your vineyards during that entire year.
25.5: And don't store away the crops that grow naturally or process the grapes that grow on your unpruned vines. The land is to have a year of total rest.
25.6: But you, your male and female slaves, your hired servants, and any foreigners who live with you may eat the produce that grows naturally during the Sabbath year.
25.7: And your livestock and the wild animals will also be allowed to eat of the land's bounty.
25.8: "In addition, you must count off seven Sabbath years, seven years times seven, adding up to forty-nine years in all.
25.9: Then on the Day of Atonement of the fiftieth year, blow the trumpets loud and long throughout the land.
25.10: This year will be set apart as holy, a time to proclaim release for all who live there. It will be a jubilee year for you, when each of you returns to the lands that belonged to your ancestors and rejoins your clan.
25.11: Yes, the fiftieth year will be a jubilee for you. During that year, do not plant any seeds or store away any of the crops that grow naturally, and do not process the grapes that grow on your unpruned vines.
25.12: It will be a jubilee year for you, and you must observe it as a special and holy time. You may, however, eat the produce that grows naturally in the fields that year.
25.13: In the Year of Jubilee each of you must return to the lands that belonged to your ancestors.
25.14: "When you make an agreement with a neighbor to buy or sell property, you must never take advantage of each other.
25.15: When you buy land from your neighbor, the price of the land should be based on the number of years since the last jubilee. The seller will charge you only for the crop years left until the next Year of Jubilee.
25.16: The more the years, the higher the price; the fewer the years, the lower the price. After all, the person selling the land is actually selling you a certain number of harvests.
25.17: Show your fear of God by not taking advantage of each other. I, the LORD, am your God.
25.18: "If you want to live securely in the land, keep my laws and obey my regulations.
25.19: Then the land will yield bumper crops, and you will eat your fill and live securely in it.
25.20: But you might ask, `What will we eat during the seventh year, since we are not allowed to plant or harvest crops that year?'
25.21: The answer is, `I will order my blessing for you in the sixth year, so the land will produce a bumper crop, enough to support you for three years.
25.22: As you plant the seed in the eighth year, you will still be eating the produce of the previous year. In fact, you will eat from the old crop until the new harvest comes in the ninth year.'
25.23: And remember, the land must never be sold on a permanent basis because it really belongs to me. You are only foreigners and tenants living with me.
25.24: "With every sale of land there must be a stipulation that the land can be redeemed at any time.
25.25: If any of your Israelite relatives go bankrupt and are forced to sell some inherited land, then a close relative, a kinsman redeemer, may buy it back for them.
25.26: If there is no one to redeem the land but the person who sold it manages to get enough money to buy it back,
25.27: then that person has the right to redeem it from the one who bought it. The price of the land will be based on the number of years until the next Year of Jubilee. After buying it back, the original owner may then return to the land.
25.28: But if the original owner cannot afford to redeem it, then it will belong to the new owner until the next Year of Jubilee. In the jubilee year, the land will be returned to the original owner.
25.29: "Anyone who sells a house inside a walled city has the right to redeem it for a full year after its sale. During that time, the seller retains the right to buy it back.
25.30: But if it is not redeemed within a year, then the house within the walled city will become the permanent property of the buyer. It will not be returned to the original owner in the Year of Jubilee.
25.31: But a house in a village--a settlement without fortified walls--will be treated like property in the open fields. Such a house may be redeemed at any time and must be returned to the original owner in the Year of Jubilee.
25.32: "The Levites always have the right to redeem any house they have sold within the cities belonging to them.
25.33: And any property that can be redeemed by the Levites--all houses within the Levitical cities--must be returned in the Year of Jubilee. After all, the cities reserved for the Levites are the only property they own in all Israel.
25.34: The strip of pastureland around each of the Levitical cities may never be sold. It is their permanent ancestral property.
25.35: "If any of your Israelite relatives fall into poverty and cannot support themselves, support them as you would a resident foreigner and allow them to live with you.
25.36: Do not demand an advance or charge interest on the money you lend them. Instead, show your fear of God by letting them live with you as your relatives.
25.37: Remember, do not charge your relatives interest on anything you lend them, whether money or food.
25.38: I, the LORD, am your God, who brought you out of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
25.39: "If any of your Israelite relatives go bankrupt and sell themselves to you, do not treat them as slaves.
25.40: Treat them instead as hired servants or as resident foreigners who live with you, and they will serve you only until the Year of Jubilee.
25.41: At that time they and their children will no longer be obligated to you, and they will return to their clan and ancestral property.
25.42: The people of Israel are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt, so they must never be sold as slaves.
25.43: Show your fear of God by treating them well; never exercise your power over them in a ruthless way.
25.44: "However, you may purchase male or female slaves from among the foreigners who live among you.
25.45: You may also purchase the children of such resident foreigners, including those who have been born in your land. You may treat them as your property,
25.46: passing them on to your children as a permanent inheritance. You may treat your slaves like this, but the people of Israel, your relatives, must never be treated this way.
25.47: "If a resident foreigner becomes rich, and if some of your Israelite relatives go bankrupt and sell themselves to such a foreigner,
25.48: they still retain the right of redemption. They may be bought back by a close relative--
25.49: an uncle, a nephew, or anyone else who is closely related. They may also redeem themselves if they can get the money.
25.50: The price of their freedom will be based on the number of years left until the next Year of Jubilee--whatever it would cost to hire a servant for that number of years.
25.51: If many years still remain, they will repay most of what they received when they sold themselves.
25.52: If only a few years remain until the Year of Jubilee, then they will repay a relatively small amount for their redemption.
25.53: The foreigner must treat them as servants hired on a yearly basis. You must not allow a resident foreigner to treat any of your Israelite relatives ruthlessly.
25.54: If any Israelites have not been redeemed by the time the Year of Jubilee arrives, then they and their children must be set free at that time.
25.55: For the people of Israel are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I, the LORD, am your God.

26.1: "Do not make idols or set up carved images, sacred pillars, or shaped stones to be worshiped in your land. I, the LORD, am your God.
26.2: You must keep my Sabbath days of rest and show reverence for my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
26.3: "If you keep my laws and are careful to obey my commands,
26.4: I will send the seasonal rains. The land will then yield its crops, and the trees will produce their fruit.
26.5: Your threshing season will extend until the grape harvest, and your grape harvest will extend until it is time to plant grain again. You will eat your fill and live securely in your land.
26.6: "I will give you peace in the land, and you will be able to sleep without fear. I will remove the wild animals from your land and protect you from your enemies.
26.7: In fact, you will chase down all your enemies and slaughter them with your swords.
26.8: Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred of you will chase ten thousand! All your enemies will fall beneath the blows of your weapons.
26.9: "I will look favorably upon you and multiply your people and fulfill my covenant with you.
26.10: You will have such a surplus of crops that you will need to get rid of the leftovers from the previous year to make room for each new harvest.
26.11: I will live among you, and I will not despise you.
26.12: I will walk among you; I will be your God, and you will be my people.
26.13: I, the LORD, am your God, who brought you from the land of Egypt so you would no longer be slaves. I have lifted the yoke of slavery from your neck so you can walk free with your heads held high.
26.14: "However, if you do not listen to me or obey my commands,
26.15: and if you break my covenant by rejecting my laws and treating my regulations with contempt,
26.16: I will punish you. You will suffer from sudden terrors, with wasting diseases, and with burning fevers, causing your eyes to fail and your life to ebb away. You will plant your crops in vain because your enemies will eat them.
26.17: I will turn against you, and you will be defeated by all your enemies. They will rule over you, and you will run even when no one is chasing you!
26.18: "And if, in spite of this, you still disobey me, I will punish you for your sins seven times over.
26.19: I will break down your arrogant spirit by making the skies above as unyielding as iron and the earth beneath as hard as bronze.
26.20: All your work will be for nothing, for your land will yield no crops, and your trees will bear no fruit.
26.21: "If even then you remain hostile toward me and refuse to obey, I will inflict you with seven more disasters for your sins.
26.22: I will release wild animals that will kill your children and destroy your cattle, so your numbers will dwindle and your roads will be deserted.
26.23: "And if you fail to learn a lesson from this and continue your hostility toward me,
26.24: then I myself will be hostile toward you, and I will personally strike you seven times over for your sins.
26.25: I will send armies against you to carry out these covenant threats. If you flee to your cities, I will send a plague to destroy you there, and you will be conquered by your enemies.
26.26: I will completely destroy your food supply, so the bread from one oven will have to be stretched to feed ten families. They will ration your food by weight, and even if you have food to eat, you will not be satisfied.
26.27: "If after this you still refuse to listen and still remain hostile toward me,
26.28: then I will give full vent to my hostility. I will punish you seven times over for your sins.
26.29: You will eat the flesh of your own sons and daughters.
26.30: I will destroy your pagan shrines and cut down your incense altars. I will leave your corpses piled up beside your lifeless idols, and I will despise you.
26.31: I will make your cities desolate and destroy your places of worship, and I will take no pleasure in your offerings of incense.
26.32: Yes, I myself will devastate your land. Your enemies who come to occupy it will be utterly shocked at the destruction they see.
26.33: I will scatter you among the nations and attack you with my own weapons. Your land will become desolate, and your cities will lie in ruins.
26.34: Then at last the land will make up for its missed Sabbath years as it lies desolate during your years of exile in the land of your enemies. Then the land will finally rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
26.35: As the land lies in ruins, it will take the rest you never allowed it to take every seventh year while you lived in it.
26.36: "And for those of you who survive, I will demoralize you in the land of your enemies far away. You will live there in such constant fear that the sound of a leaf driven by the wind will send you fleeing. You will run as though chased by a warrior with a sword, and you will fall even when no one is pursuing you.
26.37: Yes, though no one is chasing you, you will stumble over each other in flight, as though fleeing in battle. You will have no power to stand before your enemies.
26.38: You will die among the foreign nations and be devoured in the land of your enemies.
26.39: Those still left alive will rot away in enemy lands because of their sins and the sins of their ancestors.
26.40: "But at last my people will confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors for betraying me and being hostile toward me.
26.41: Finally, when I have given full expression to my hostility and have brought them to the land of their enemies, then at last their disobedient hearts will be humbled, and they will pay for their sins.
26.42: Then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, with Isaac, and with Abraham, and I will remember the land.
26.43: And the land will enjoy its years of Sabbath rest as it lies deserted. At last the people will receive the due punishment for their sins, for they rejected my regulations and despised my laws.
26.44: "But despite all this, I will not utterly reject or despise them while they are in exile in the land of their enemies. I will not cancel my covenant with them by wiping them out. I, the LORD, am their God.
26.45: I will remember my ancient covenant with their ancestors, whom I brought out of Egypt while all the nations watched. I, the LORD, am their God."
26.46: These are the laws, regulations, and instructions that the LORD gave to the Israelites through Moses on Mount Sinai.

27.2: "Give the following instructions to the Israelites: If you make a special vow to dedicate someone to the LORD by paying the value of that person,
27.3: here is the scale of values to be used. A man between the ages of twenty and sixty is valued at fifty pieces of silver;
27.4: a woman of that age is valued at thirty pieces of silver.
27.5: A boy between five and twenty is valued at twenty pieces of silver; a girl of that age is valued at ten pieces of silver.
27.6: A boy between the ages of one month and five years is valued at five pieces of silver; a girl of that age is valued at three pieces of silver.
27.7: A man older than sixty is valued at fifteen pieces of silver; a woman older than sixty is valued at ten pieces of silver.
27.8: If you desire to make such a vow but cannot afford to pay the prescribed amount, go to the priest and he will evaluate your ability to pay. You will then pay the amount decided by the priest.
27.9: "If your vow involves giving a clean animal--one that is acceptable as an offering to the LORD--then your gift to the LORD will be considered holy.
27.10: The animal should never be exchanged or substituted for another--neither a good animal for a bad one nor a bad animal for a good one. But if such an exchange is in fact made, then both the original animal and the substitute will be considered holy.
27.11: But if your vow involves an unclean animal--one that is not acceptable as an offering to the LORD--then you must bring the animal to the priest.
27.12: He will assess its value, and his assessment will be final.
27.13: If you want to redeem the animal, you must pay the value set by the priest, plus 20 percent.
27.14: "If you dedicate a house to the LORD, the priest must come to assess its value. The priest's assessment will be final.
27.15: If you wish to redeem the house, you must pay the value set by the priest, plus 20 percent. Then the house will again belong to you.
27.16: "If you dedicate to the LORD a piece of your ancestral property, its value will be assessed by the amount of seed required to plant it--fifty pieces of silver for an area that produces five bushels of barley seed.
27.17: If the field is dedicated to the LORD in the Year of Jubilee, then the entire assessment will apply.
27.18: But if the field is dedicated after the Year of Jubilee, the priest must assess the land's value in proportion to the years left until the next Year of Jubilee.
27.19: If you decide to redeem the dedicated field, you must pay the land's value as assessed by the priest, plus 20 percent. Then the field will again belong to you.
27.20: But if you decide not to redeem the field, or if the field is sold to someone else by the priests, it can never be redeemed.
27.21: When the field is released in the Year of Jubilee, it will be holy, a field specially set apart for the LORD. It will become the property of the priests.
27.22: "If you dedicate to the LORD a field that you have purchased but which is not part of your ancestral property,
27.23: the priest must assess its value based on the years until the next Year of Jubilee. You must then give the assessed value of the land as a sacred donation to the LORD.
27.24: In the Year of Jubilee the field will be released to the original owner from whom you purchased it.
27.25: All the value assessments must be measured in terms of the standard sanctuary shekel.
27.26: "You may not dedicate to the LORD the firstborn of your cattle or sheep because the firstborn of these animals already belong to him.
27.27: However, if it is the firstborn of a ceremonially unclean animal, you may redeem it by paying the priest's assessment of its worth, plus 20 percent. If you do not redeem it, the priest may sell it to someone else for its assessed value.
27.28: "However, anything specially set apart by the LORD--whether a person, an animal, or an inherited field--must never be sold or redeemed. Anything devoted in this way has been set apart for the LORD as holy.
27.29: A person specially set apart by the LORD for destruction cannot be redeemed. Such a person must be put to death.
27.30: "A tenth of the produce of the land, whether grain or fruit, belongs to the LORD and must be set apart to him as holy.
27.31: If you want to redeem the LORD's tenth of the fruit or grain, you must pay its value, plus 20 percent.
27.32: The LORD also owns every tenth animal counted off from your herds and flocks. They are set apart to him as holy.
27.33: The tenth animal must not be selected on the basis of whether it is good or bad, and no substitutions will be allowed. If any exchange is in fact made, then both the original animal and the substituted one will be considered holy and cannot be redeemed."
27.34: These are the commands that the LORD gave to the Israelites through Moses on Mount Sinai.

1.1: One day in midspring, during the second year after Israel's departure from Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the Tabernacle in the wilderness of Sinai. He said,
1.2: "Take a census of the whole community of Israel by their clans and families. List the names of all the men
1.3: twenty years old or older who are able to go to war. You and Aaron are to direct the project,
1.4: assisted by one family leader from each tribe."
1.5: These are the tribes and the names of the leaders chosen for the task: Reuben....................... Elizur son of Shedeur
1.6: Simeon................. Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai
1.7: Judah.................... Nahshon son of Amminadab
1.8: Issachar........................ Nethanel son of Zuar
1.9: Zebulun......................... Eliab son of Helon
1.10: Ephraim son of Joseph...... Elishama son of Ammihud Manasseh son of Joseph...... Gamaliel son of Pedahzur
1.11: Benjamin.................... Abidan son of Gideoni
1.12: Dan................... Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai
1.13: Asher......................... Pagiel son of Ocran
1.14: Gad......................... Eliasaph son of Deuel
1.15: Naphtali........................ Ahira son of Enan
1.16: These tribal leaders, heads of their own families, were chosen from among all the people.
1.17: Now Moses and Aaron and the chosen leaders
1.18: called together the whole community of Israel on that very day. All the people were registered according to their ancestry by their clans and families. The men of Israel twenty years old or older were registered, one by one,
1.19: just as the LORD had commanded Moses. So Moses counted the people there in the wilderness of Sinai.
1.20: This is the number of men twenty years old or older who were able to go to war, each listed according to his own clan and family: Reuben (Jacob's oldest son)...... 46,500
1.21: those who were numbered of the tribe of Reuben were forty-six thousand five hundred.
1.23: those who were numbered of the tribe of Simeon were fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
1.25: those who were numbered of the tribe of Gad were forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.
1.27: those who were numbered of the tribe of Judah were seventy-four thousand six hundred.
1.29: those who were numbered of the tribe of Issachar were fifty-four thousand four hundred.
1.31: those who were numbered of the tribe of Zebulun were fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
1.33: those who were numbered of the tribe of Ephraim were forty thousand five hundred.
1.35: those who were numbered of the tribe of Manasseh were thirty-two thousand two hundred.
1.37: those who were numbered of the tribe of Benjamin were thirty-five thousand four hundred.
1.39: those who were numbered of the tribe of Dan were sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
1.41: those who were numbered of the tribe of Asher were forty-one thousand five hundred.
1.43: those who were numbered of the tribe of Naphtali were fifty-three thousand four hundred.
1.44: These were the men counted by Moses and Aaron and the twelve leaders of Israel, all listed according to their ancestral descent.
1.45: They were counted by families--all the men of Israel who were twenty years old or older and able to go to war.
1.47: But this total did not include the Levites.
1.48: For the LORD had said to Moses,
1.49: "Exempt the tribe of Levi from the census; do not include them when you count the rest of the Israelites.
1.50: You must put the Levites in charge of the Tabernacle of the Covenant, along with its furnishings and equipment. They must carry the Tabernacle and its equipment as you travel, and they must care for it and camp around it.
1.51: Whenever the Tabernacle is moved, the Levites will take it down and set it up again. Anyone else who goes too near the Tabernacle will be executed.
1.52: Each tribe of Israel will have a designated camping area with its own family banner.
1.53: But the Levites will camp around the Tabernacle of the Covenant to offer the people of Israel protection from the LORD's fierce anger. The Levites are responsible to stand guard around the Tabernacle."
1.54: So the Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

2.1: Then the LORD gave these instructions to Moses and Aaron:
2.2: "Each tribe will be assigned its own area in the camp, and the various groups will camp beneath their family banners. The Tabernacle will be located at the center of these tribal compounds.
2.3: "The divisions of Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun are to camp toward the sunrise on the east side of the Tabernacle, beneath their family banners. These are the names of the tribes, their leaders, and the number of their available troops: Judah....... Nahshon son of Amminadab.... 74,600
2.4: And his army was numbered at seventy-four thousand six hundred.
2.5: Issachar.... Nethanel son of Zuar.......... 54,400
2.6: And his army was numbered at fifty-four thousand four hundred.
2.7: Zebulun.... Eliab son of Helon............ 57,400
2.8: And his army was numbered at fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
2.9: So the total of all the troops on Judah's side of the camp is 186,400. These three tribes are to lead the way whenever the Israelites travel to a new campsite.
2.10: "The divisions of Reuben, Simeon, and Gad are to camp on the south side of the Tabernacle, beneath their family banners. These are the names of the tribes, their leaders, and the number of their available troops: Reuben....... Elizur son of Shedeur.......... 46,500
2.11: And his army was numbered at forty-six thousand five hundred.
2.12: Simeon.... Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.... 59,300
2.13: And his army was numbered at fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
2.14: Gad....... Eliasaph son of Deuel......... 45,650
2.15: And his army was numbered at forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.
2.16: So the total of all the troops on Reuben's side of the camp is 151,450. These three tribes will be second in line whenever the Israelites travel.
2.17: "Then the Levites will set out from the middle of the camp with the Tabernacle. All the tribes are to travel in the same order that they camp, each in position under the appropriate family banner.
2.18: "The divisions of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Benjamin are to camp on the west side of the Tabernacle, beneath their family banners. These are the names of the tribes, their leaders, and the number of their available troops: Ephraim....... Elishama son of Ammihud.... 40,500
2.19: And his army was numbered at forty thousand five hundred.
2.20: Manasseh.... Gamaliel son of Pedahzur..... 32,200
2.21: And his army was numbered at thirty-two thousand two hundred.
2.22: Benjamin.... Abidan son of Gideoni....... 35,400
2.23: And his army was numbered at thirty-five thousand four hundred.
2.24: So the total of all the troops on Ephraim's side of the camp is 108,100, and they will follow the Levites in the line of march.
2.25: "The divisions of Dan, Asher, and Naphtali are to camp on the north side of the Tabernacle, beneath their family banners. These are the names of the tribes, their leaders, and the number of their available troops: Dan.......... Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai... 62,700
2.26: And his army was numbered at sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
2.28: And his army was numbered at forty-one thousand five hundred.
2.30: And his army was numbered at fifty-three thousand four hundred.
2.31: So the total of all the troops on Dan's side of the camp is 157,600. They are to bring up the rear whenever the Israelites move to a new campsite."
2.32: In summary, the troops of Israel listed by their families totaled 603,550.
2.33: The Levites were exempted from this census by the LORD's command to Moses.
2.34: So the people of Israel did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses. Each clan and family set up camp and marched under their banners exactly as the LORD had instructed them.

3.1: This is the family line of Aaron and Moses as it was recorded when the LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai:
3.2: Aaron's sons were Nadab (the firstborn), Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
3.3: They were anointed and set apart to minister as priests.
3.4: But Nadab and Abihu died in the LORD's presence in the wilderness of Sinai when they burned before the LORD a different kind of fire than he had commanded. Since they had no sons, this left only Eleazar and Ithamar to serve as priests with their father, Aaron.
3.5: Then the LORD said to Moses,
3.6: "Call forward the tribe of Levi and present them to Aaron the priest as his assistants.
3.7: They will serve Aaron and the whole community, performing their sacred duties in and around the Tabernacle.
3.8: They will also maintain all the furnishings of the sacred tent, serving in the Tabernacle on behalf of all the Israelites.
3.9: Assign the Levites to Aaron and his sons as their assistants.
3.10: Appoint Aaron and his sons to carry out the duties of the priesthood. Anyone else who comes too near the sanctuary must be executed!"
3.11: And the LORD said to Moses,
3.12: "I have chosen the Levites from among the Israelites as substitutes for all the firstborn sons of the people of Israel. The Levites are mine
3.13: because all the firstborn sons are mine. From the day I killed all the firstborn sons of the Egyptians, I set apart for myself all the firstborn in Israel of both men and animals. They are mine; I am the LORD."
3.14: The LORD spoke again to Moses, there in the wilderness of Sinai. He said,
3.15: "Take a census of the tribe of Levi by its families and clans. Count every male who is one month old or older."
3.16: So Moses counted them, just as the LORD had commanded.
3.17: Levi had three sons, who were named Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
3.18: The clans descended from Gershon were named for two of his descendants, Libni and Shimei.
3.19: The clans descended from Kohath were named for four of his descendants, Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
3.20: The clans descended from Merari were named for two of his descendants, Mahli and Mushi. These were the Levite clans, listed according to their family groups.
3.21: The descendants of Gershon were composed of the clans descended from Libni and Shimei.
3.22: There were 7,500 males one month old or older among these Gershonite clans.
3.23: They were assigned the area to the west of the Tabernacle for their camp.
3.24: The leader of the Gershonite clans was Eliasaph son of Lael.
3.25: These two clans were responsible to care for the tent of the Tabernacle with its layers of coverings, its entry curtains,
3.26: the curtains of the courtyard that surrounded the Tabernacle and altar, the curtain at the courtyard entrance, the cords, and all the equipment related to their use.
3.27: The descendants of Kohath were composed of the clans descended from Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
3.28: There were 8,600 males one month old or older among these Kohathite clans. They were responsible for the care of the sanctuary.
3.29: They were assigned the area south of the Tabernacle for their camp.
3.30: The leader of the Kohathite clans was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
3.31: These four clans were responsible for the care of the Ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the various utensils used in the sanctuary, the inner curtain, and all the equipment related to their use.
3.32: Eleazar the priest, Aaron's son, was the chief administrator over all the Levites, with special responsibility for the oversight of the sanctuary.
3.33: The descendants of Merari were composed of the clans descended from Mahli and Mushi.
3.34: There were 6,200 males one month old or older among these Merarite clans.
3.35: They were assigned the area north of the Tabernacle for their camp. The leader of the Merarite clans was Zuriel son of Abihail.
3.36: These two clans were responsible for the care of the frames supporting the Tabernacle, the crossbars, the pillars, the bases, and all the equipment related to their use.
3.37: They were also responsible for the posts of the courtyard and all their bases, pegs, and cords.
3.38: The area in front of the Tabernacle in the east toward the sunrise was reserved for the tents of Moses and of Aaron and his sons, who had the final responsibility for the sanctuary on behalf of the people of Israel. Anyone other than a priest or Levite who came too near the sanctuary was to be executed.
3.39: So among the Levite clans counted by Moses and Aaron at the LORD's command, there were 22,000 males one month old or older.
3.40: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Now count all the firstborn sons in Israel who are one month old or older, and register each name.
3.41: The Levites will be reserved for me as substitutes for the firstborn sons of Israel; I am the LORD. And the Levites' livestock are mine as substitutes for the firstborn livestock of the whole nation of Israel."
3.42: So Moses counted the firstborn sons of the people of Israel, just as the LORD had commanded.
3.43: The total number of firstborn sons who were one month old or older was 22,273.
3.44: Now the LORD said to Moses,
3.45: "Take the Levites in place of the firstborn sons of the people of Israel. And take the livestock of the Levites as substitutes for the firstborn livestock of the people of Israel. The Levites will be mine; I am the LORD.
3.46: To redeem the 273 firstborn sons of Israel who are in excess of the number of Levites,
3.47: collect five pieces of silver for each person, each piece weighing the same as the standard sanctuary shekel.
3.48: Give the silver to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for the extra firstborn sons."
3.49: So Moses collected redemption money for the firstborn sons of Israel who exceeded the number of Levites.
3.50: The silver collected on behalf of these firstborn sons of Israel came to about thirty-four pounds in weight.
3.51: And Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons as the LORD had commanded.

4.1: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
4.2: "Take a census of the clans and families of the Kohathite division of the Levite tribe.
4.3: Count all the men between the ages of thirty and fifty who qualify to work in the Tabernacle.
4.4: "The duties of the Kohathites at the Tabernacle will relate to the most sacred objects.
4.5: When the camp moves, Aaron and his sons must enter the Tabernacle first to take down the inner curtain and cover the Ark of the Covenant with it.
4.6: Then they must cover the inner curtain with fine goatskin leather, and the goatskin leather with a dark blue cloth. Finally, they must put the carrying poles of the Ark in place.
4.7: "Next they must spread a blue cloth over the table, where the Bread of the Presence is displayed, and place the dishes, spoons, bowls, cups, and the special bread on the cloth.
4.8: They must spread a scarlet cloth over that, and finally a covering of fine goatskin leather on top of the scarlet cloth. Then they must insert the carrying poles into the table.
4.9: "Next they must cover the lampstand with a dark blue cloth, along with its lamps, lamp snuffers, trays, and special jars of olive oil.
4.10: The lampstand with its utensils must then be covered with fine goatskin leather, and the bundle must be placed on a carrying frame.
4.11: "Aaron and his sons must also spread a dark blue cloth over the gold altar and cover this cloth with a covering of fine goatskin leather. Then they are to attach the carrying poles to the altar.
4.12: All the remaining utensils of the sanctuary must be wrapped in a dark blue cloth, covered with fine goatskin leather, and placed on the carrying frame.
4.13: "The ashes must be removed from the altar, and the altar must then be covered with a purple cloth.
4.14: All the altar utensils--the firepans, hooks, shovels, basins, and all the containers--are to be placed on the cloth, and a covering of fine goatskin leather must be spread over them. Finally, the carrying poles must be put in place.
4.15: When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the sanctuary and all the sacred utensils, the Kohathites will come and carry these things to the next destination. But they must not touch the sacred objects, or they will die. So these are the objects of the Tabernacle that the Kohathites must carry.
4.16: "Eleazar son of Aaron the priest will be responsible for the oil of the lampstand, the fragrant incense, the daily grain offering, and the anointing oil. In fact, the supervision of the entire Tabernacle and everything in it will be Eleazar's responsibility."
4.17: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
4.18: "Don't let the Kohathite clans be destroyed from among the Levites!
4.19: This is what you must do so they will live and not die when they approach the most sacred objects. Aaron and his sons must always go in with them and assign a specific duty or load to each person.
4.20: Otherwise they must not approach the sanctuary and look at the sacred objects for even a moment, or they will die."
4.21: And the LORD said to Moses,
4.22: "Take a census of the clans and families of the Gershonite division of the tribe of Levi.
4.23: Count all the men between the ages of thirty and fifty who are eligible to serve in the Tabernacle.
4.24: "The duties of the Gershonites will be in the areas of general service and carrying loads.
4.25: They must carry the curtains of the Tabernacle, the Tabernacle itself with its coverings, the outer covering of fine goatskin leather, and the curtain for the Tabernacle entrance.
4.26: They are also to carry the curtains for the courtyard walls that surround the Tabernacle and altar, the curtain across the courtyard entrance, the necessary cords, and all the altar's accessories. The Gershonites are responsible for transporting all these items.
4.27: Aaron and his sons will direct the Gershonites regarding their duties, whether it involves moving or doing other work. They must assign the Gershonites the loads they are to carry.
4.28: So these are the duties assigned to the Gershonites at the Tabernacle. They will be directly responsible to Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
4.29: "Now take a census of the clans and families of the Merarite division of the Levite tribe.
4.30: Count all the men between the ages of thirty and fifty who are eligible to serve in the Tabernacle.
4.31: "Their duties at the Tabernacle will consist of carrying loads. They will be required to carry the frames of the Tabernacle, the crossbars, the pillars with their bases,
4.32: the posts for the courtyard walls with their bases, pegs, cords, accessories, and everything else related to their use. You must assign the various loads to each man by name.
4.33: So these are the duties of the Merarites at the Tabernacle. They are directly responsible to Ithamar son of Aaron the priest."
4.34: So Moses, Aaron, and the other leaders of the community counted the Kohathite division by its clans and families.
4.35: The count included all the men between thirty and fifty years of age who were eligible for service in the Tabernacle,
4.36: and the total number came to 2,750.
4.37: So this was the total of all those from the Kohathite clans who were eligible to serve at the Tabernacle. Moses and Aaron counted them, just as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
4.38: The Gershonite division was also counted by its clans and families.
4.39: The count included all the men between thirty and fifty years of age who were eligible for service in the Tabernacle,
4.40: and the total number came to 2,630.
4.41: So this was the total of all those from the Gershonite clans who were eligible to serve at the Tabernacle. Moses and Aaron counted them, just as the LORD had commanded.
4.42: The Merarite division was also counted by its clans and families.
4.43: The count included all the men between thirty and fifty years of age who were eligible for service in the Tabernacle,
4.44: and the total number came to 3,200.
4.45: So this was the total of all those from the Merarite clans who were eligible for service. Moses and Aaron counted them, just as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
4.46: So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel counted all the Levites by their clans and families.
4.47: All the men between thirty and fifty years of age who were eligible for service in the Tabernacle and for its transportation
4.49: Each man was assigned his task and told what to carry, just as the LORD had commanded through Moses. And so the census was completed, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

5.1: The LORD gave these instructions to Moses:
5.2: "Command the people of Israel to remove anyone from the camp who has a contagious skin disease or a discharge, or who has been defiled by touching a dead person.
5.3: This applies to men and women alike. Remove them so they will not defile the camp, where I live among you."
5.4: So the Israelites did just as the LORD had commanded Moses and removed such people from the camp.
5.5: Then the LORD said to Moses,
5.6: "Give these instructions to the people of Israel: If any of the people--men or women--betray the LORD by doing wrong to another person, they are guilty.
5.7: They must confess their sin and make full restitution for what they have done, adding a penalty of 20 percent and returning it to the person who was wronged.
5.8: But if the person who was wronged is dead, and there are no near relatives to whom restitution can be made, it belongs to the LORD and must be given to the priest, along with a ram for atonement.
5.9: All the sacred gifts that the Israelites bring to a priest will belong to him.
5.10: Each priest may keep the sacred donations that he receives."
5.11: And the LORD said to Moses,
5.12: "Say to the people of Israel: `Suppose a man's wife goes astray and is unfaithful to her husband.
5.13: Suppose she sleeps with another man, but there is no witness since she was not caught in the act.
5.14: If her husband becomes jealous and suspicious of his wife, even if she has not defiled herself,
5.15: the husband must bring his wife to the priest with an offering of two quarts of barley flour to be presented on her behalf. Do not mix it with olive oil or frankincense, for it is a jealousy offering--an offering of inquiry to find out if she is guilty.
5.16: " `The priest must then present her before the LORD.
5.17: He must take some holy water in a clay jar and mix it with dust from the Tabernacle floor.
5.18: When he has presented her before the LORD, he must unbind her hair and place the offering of inquiry--the jealousy offering--in her hands to determine whether or not her husband's suspicions are justified. The priest will stand before her, holding the jar of bitter water that brings a curse to those who are guilty.
5.19: The priest will put the woman under oath and say to her, "If no other man has slept with you, and you have not defiled yourself by being unfaithful, may you be immune from the effects of this bitter water that causes the curse.
5.20: But if you have gone astray while under your husband's authority and defiled yourself by sleeping with another man"--
5.21: at this point the priest must put the woman under this oath--"then may the people see that the LORD's curse is upon you when he makes you infertile.
5.22: Now may this water that brings the curse enter your body and make you infertile. "And the woman will be required to say, "Yes, let it be so."
5.23: Then the priest will write these curses on a piece of leather and wash them off into the bitter water.
5.24: He will then make the woman drink the bitter water, so it may bring on the curse and cause bitter suffering in cases of guilt.
5.25: " `Then the priest will take the jealousy offering from the woman's hand, lift it up before the LORD, and carry it to the altar.
5.26: He will take a handful as a token portion and burn it on the altar. Then he will require the woman to drink the water.
5.27: If she has defiled herself by being unfaithful to her husband, the water that brings the curse will cause bitter suffering. She will become infertile, and her name will become a curse word among her people.
5.28: But if she has not defiled herself and is pure, she will be unharmed and will still be able to have children.
5.29: " `This is the ritual law for dealing with jealousy. If a woman defiles herself by being unfaithful to her husband,
5.30: or if a man is overcome with jealousy and suspicion that his wife has been unfaithful, the husband must present his wife before the LORD, and the priest will apply this entire ritual law to her.
5.31: The husband will be innocent of any guilt in this matter, but his wife will be held accountable for her sin.'"

6.1: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the people of Israel and give them these instructions:
6.2: If some of the people, either men or women, take the special vow of a Nazirite, setting themselves apart to the LORD in a special way,
6.3: they must give up wine and other alcoholic drinks. They must not use vinegar made from wine, they must not drink other fermented drinks or fresh grape juice, and they must not eat grapes or raisins.
6.4: As long as they are bound by their Nazirite vow, they are not allowed to eat or drink anything that comes from a grapevine, not even the grape seeds or skins.
6.5: "They must never cut their hair throughout the time of their vow, for they are holy and set apart to the LORD. That is why they must let their hair grow long.
6.6: And they may not go near a dead body during the entire period of their vow to the LORD,
6.7: even if their own father, mother, brother, or sister has died. They must not defile the hair on their head, because it is the symbol of their separation to God.
6.8: This applies as long as they are set apart to the LORD.
6.9: "If their hair is defiled because someone suddenly falls dead beside them, they must wait for seven days and then shave their heads. Then they will be cleansed from their defilement.
6.10: On the eighth day they must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
6.11: The priest will offer one of the birds for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering. In this way, he will make atonement for the guilt they incurred from the dead body. Then they must renew their vow that day and let their hair begin to grow again.
6.12: The days of their vow that were completed before their defilement no longer count. They must rededicate themselves to the LORD for the full term of their vow, and each must bring a one-year-old male lamb for a guilt offering.
6.13: "This is the ritual law of the Nazirites. At the conclusion of their time of separation as Nazirites, they must each go to the entrance of the Tabernacle
6.14: and offer these sacrifices to the LORD: a one-year-old male lamb without defect for a burnt offering, a one-year-old female lamb without defect for a sin offering, a ram without defect for a peace offering,
6.15: a basket of bread made without yeast--cakes of choice flour mixed with olive oil and wafers spread with olive oil--along with their prescribed grain offerings and drink offerings.
6.16: The priest will present these offerings before the LORD: first the sin offering and the burnt offering;
6.17: then the ram for a peace offering, along with the basket of bread made without yeast. The priest must also make the prescribed grain offering and drink offering.
6.18: "Then the Nazirites will shave their hair at the entrance of the Tabernacle and put it on the fire beneath the peace-offering sacrifice.
6.19: After each Nazirite's head has been shaved, the priest will take for each of them the boiled shoulder of the ram, one cake made without yeast, and one wafer made without yeast, and put them all into the Nazirite's hands.
6.20: The priest will then lift the gifts up before the LORD in a gesture of offering. These are holy portions for the priest, along with the breast and thigh pieces that were lifted up before the LORD. After this ceremony the Nazirites may again drink wine.
6.21: "This is the ritual law of the Nazirites. If any Nazirites have vowed to give the LORD anything else beyond what is required by their normal Nazirite vow, they must fulfill their special vow exactly as they have promised."
6.22: Then the LORD said to Moses,
6.23: "Instruct Aaron and his sons to bless the people of Israel with this special blessing:
6.24: `May the LORD bless you and protect you.
6.25: May the LORD smile on you and be gracious to you.
6.26: May the LORD show you his favor and give you his peace.'
6.27: This is how Aaron and his sons will designate the Israelites as my people, and I myself will bless them."

7.1: On the day Moses set up the Tabernacle, he anointed it and set it apart as holy, along with all its furnishings and the altar with its utensils.
7.2: Then the leaders of Israel--the tribal leaders who had organized the census--came and brought their offerings.
7.3: Together they brought six carts and twelve oxen. There was a cart for every two leaders and an ox for each leader. They presented these to the LORD in front of the Tabernacle.
7.4: Then the LORD said to Moses,
7.5: "Receive their gifts and use these oxen and carts for the work of the Tabernacle. Distribute them among the Levites according to the work they have to do."
7.6: So Moses presented the carts and oxen to the Levites.
7.7: He gave two carts and four oxen to the Gershonite division for their work,
7.8: and four carts and eight oxen to the Merarite division for their work. All their work was done under the leadership of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
7.9: But he gave none of the carts or oxen to the Kohathite division, since they were required to carry the sacred objects of the Tabernacle on their shoulders.
7.10: The leaders also presented dedication gifts for the altar at the time it was anointed. They each placed their gifts before the altar.
7.11: The LORD said to Moses, "Let each leader bring his gift on a different day for the dedication of the altar."
7.12: On the first day Nahshon son of Amminadab, leader of the tribe of Judah, presented his offering.
7.13: The offering consisted of a silver platter weighing about 3 1/4 pounds and a silver basin of about 1 3/4 pounds. These were both filled with grain offerings of choice flour mixed with olive oil.
7.14: He also brought a gold container weighing about four ounces, which was filled with incense.
7.15: He brought a young bull, a ram, and a one-year-old male lamb as a burnt offering;
7.16: a male goat for a sin offering;
7.17: and two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs for a peace offering. This was the offering brought by Nahshon son of Amminadab.
7.18: On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, leader of the tribe of Issachar, presented his offering.
7.19: The offering consisted of a silver platter weighing about 3 1/4 pounds and a silver basin of about 1 3/4 pounds. These were both filled with grain offerings of choice flour mixed with olive oil.
7.20: He also brought a gold container weighing about four ounces, which was filled with incense.
7.21: He brought a young bull, a ram, and a one-year-old male lamb as a burnt offering;
7.22: a male goat for a sin offering;
7.23: and two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs for a peace offering. This was the offering brought by Nethanel son of Zuar.

7.27: He brought a young bull, a ram, and a one-year-old male lamb as a burnt offering;

7.84: So this was the dedication offering for the altar, brought by the leaders of Israel at the time it was anointed: twelve silver platters, twelve silver basins, and twelve gold incense containers.
7.85: In all, the silver objects weighed about 60 pounds, about 3 1/4 pounds for each platter and 1 3/4 pounds for each basin.
7.86: The weight of the donated gold came to about three pounds, about four ounces for each of the gold containers that were filled with incense.
7.87: Twelve bulls, twelve rams, and twelve one-year-old male lambs were donated for the burnt offerings, along with their prescribed grain offerings. Twelve male goats were brought for the sin offerings.
7.88: Twenty-four young bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats, and sixty one-year-old male lambs were donated for the peace offerings. This was the dedication offering for the altar after it was anointed.
7.89: Whenever Moses went into the Tabernacle to speak with the LORD, he heard the voice speaking to him from between the two cherubim above the Ark's cover--the place of atonement--that rests on the Ark of the Covenant. The LORD spoke to him from there.

8.1: The LORD said to Moses,
8.2: "Tell Aaron that when he sets up the seven lamps in the lampstand, he is to place them so their light shines forward."
8.3: So Aaron did this. He set up the seven lamps so they reflected their light forward, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
8.4: The entire lampstand, from its base to its decorative blossoms, was made of beaten gold. It was built according to the exact design the LORD had shown Moses.
8.5: Then the LORD said to Moses,
8.6: "Now set the Levites apart from the rest of the people of Israel and make them ceremonially clean.
8.7: Do this by sprinkling them with the water of purification. And have them shave their entire body and wash their clothing. Then they will be ceremonially clean.
8.8: Have them bring a young bull and a grain offering of choice flour mixed with olive oil, along with a second young bull for a sin offering.
8.9: Then assemble the whole community of Israel and present the Levites at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
8.10: When you bring the Levites before the LORD, the people of Israel must lay their hands on them.
8.11: Aaron must present the Levites to the LORD as a special offering from the people of Israel, thus dedicating them to the LORD's service.
8.12: "Next the Levites will lay their hands on the heads of the young bulls and present them to the LORD. One will be for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering, to make atonement for the Levites.
8.13: Then have the Levites stand in front of Aaron and his sons, and present them as a special offering to the LORD.
8.14: In this way, you will set the Levites apart from the rest of the people of Israel, and the Levites will belong to me.
8.15: After this, they may go in and out of the Tabernacle to do their work, because you have purified them and presented them as a special offering.
8.16: "Of all the people of Israel, the Levites are reserved for me. I have claimed them for myself in place of all the firstborn sons of the Israelites; I have taken the Levites as their substitutes.
8.17: For all the firstborn males among the people of Israel are mine, both people and animals. I set them apart for myself on the night I killed all the firstborn sons of the Egyptians.
8.18: Yes, I claim the Levites in place of all the firstborn sons of Israel.
8.19: And of all the Israelites, I have assigned the Levites to Aaron and his sons. They will serve in the Tabernacle on behalf of the Israelites and make atonement for them so no plague will strike them when they approach the sanctuary."
8.20: So Moses, Aaron, and the whole community of Israel dedicated the Levites, carefully following all the LORD's instructions to Moses.
8.21: The Levites purified themselves and washed their clothes, and Aaron presented them to the LORD as a special offering. He then performed the rite of atonement over them to purify them.
8.22: From then on the Levites went into the Tabernacle to perform their duties, helping Aaron and his sons. So they carried out all the commands that the LORD gave Moses concerning the Levites.
8.24: "This is the rule the Levites must follow: They must begin serving in the Tabernacle at the age of twenty-five,
8.25: and they must retire at the age of fifty.
8.26: After retirement they may assist their fellow Levites by performing guard duty at the Tabernacle, but they may not officiate in the service. This is how you will assign duties to the Levites."

9.1: The LORD gave these instructions to Moses in early spring, during the second year after Israel's departure from Egypt, while he and the rest of the Israelites were in the wilderness of Sinai:
9.2: "Tell the Israelites to celebrate the Passover at the proper time,
9.3: at twilight on the appointed day in early spring. Be sure to follow all my laws and regulations concerning this celebration."
9.4: So Moses told the people to celebrate the Passover
9.5: in the wilderness of Sinai as twilight fell on the appointed day. And they celebrated the festival there, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
9.6: But some of the men had been ceremonially defiled by touching a dead person, so they could not offer their Passover lambs that day. So they came to Moses and Aaron that day
9.7: and said, "We have become ceremonially unclean by touching a dead person. But why should we be excluded from presenting the LORD's offering at the proper time with the rest of the Israelites?"
9.8: Moses answered, "Wait here until I have received instructions for you from the LORD."
9.9: This was the LORD's reply:
9.10: "Say to the Israelites: `If any of the people now or in future generations are ceremonially unclean at Passover time because of touching a dead body, or if they are on a journey and cannot be present at the ceremony, they may still celebrate the LORD's Passover.
9.11: They must offer the Passover sacrifice one month later, at twilight on the appointed day. They must eat the lamb at that time with bitter herbs and bread made without yeast.
9.12: They must not leave any of the lamb until the next morning, and they must not break any of its bones. They must follow all the normal regulations concerning the Passover.
9.13: " `But those who are ceremonially clean and not away on a trip, yet still refuse to celebrate the Passover at the regular time, will be cut off from the community of Israel for failing to present the LORD's offering at the proper time. They will suffer the consequences of their guilt.
9.14: And if foreigners living among you want to celebrate the Passover to the LORD, they must follow these same laws and regulations. The same laws apply both to you and to the foreigners living among you.'"
9.15: The Tabernacle was set up, and on that day the cloud covered it. Then from evening until morning the cloud over the Tabernacle appeared to be a pillar of fire.
9.16: This was the regular pattern--at night the cloud changed to the appearance of fire.
9.17: When the cloud lifted from over the sacred tent, the people of Israel followed it. And wherever the cloud settled, the people of Israel camped.
9.18: In this way, they traveled at the LORD's command and stopped wherever he told them to. Then they remained where they were as long as the cloud stayed over the Tabernacle.
9.19: If the cloud remained over the Tabernacle for a long time, the Israelites stayed for a long time, just as the LORD commanded.
9.20: Sometimes the cloud would stay over the Tabernacle for only a few days, so the people would stay for only a few days. Then at the LORD's command they would break camp.
9.21: Sometimes the cloud stayed only overnight and moved on the next morning. But day or night, when the cloud lifted, the people broke camp and followed.
9.22: Whether the cloud stayed above the Tabernacle for two days, a month, or a year, the people of Israel stayed in camp and did not move on. But as soon as it lifted, they broke camp and moved on.
9.23: So they camped or traveled at the LORD's command, and they did whatever the LORD told them through Moses.

10.1: Now the LORD said to Moses,
10.2: "Make two trumpets of beaten silver to be used for summoning the people to assemble and for signaling the breaking of camp.
10.3: When both trumpets are blown, the people will know that they are to gather before you at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
10.4: But if only one is blown, then only the leaders of the tribes of Israel will come to you.
10.5: "When you sound the signal to move on, the tribes on the east side of the Tabernacle will break camp and move forward.
10.6: When you sound the signal a second time, the tribes on the south will follow. You must sound short blasts to signal moving on.
10.7: But when you call the people to an assembly, blow the trumpets using a different signal.
10.8: Only the priests, Aaron's descendants, are allowed to blow the trumpets. This is a permanent law to be followed from generation to generation.
10.9: "When you arrive in your own land and go to war against your enemies, you must sound the alarm with these trumpets so the LORD your God will remember you and rescue you from your enemies.
10.10: Blow the trumpets in times of gladness, too, sounding them at your annual festivals and at the beginning of each month to rejoice over your burnt offerings and peace offerings. The trumpets will remind the LORD your God of his covenant with you. I am the LORD your God."
10.11: One day in midspring, during the second year after Israel's departure from Egypt, the cloud lifted from the Tabernacle of the Covenant.
10.12: So the Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sinai and traveled on in stages until the cloud stopped in the wilderness of Paran.
10.13: When the time to move arrived, the LORD gave the order through Moses.
10.14: The tribes that camped with Judah headed the march with their banner, under the leadership of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
10.15: The tribe of Issachar was led by Nethanel son of Zuar.
10.16: The tribe of Zebulun was led by Eliab son of Helon.
10.17: Then the Tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonite and Merarite divisions of the Levites were next in the line of march, carrying the Tabernacle with them.
10.18: Then the tribes that camped with Reuben set out with their banner, under the leadership of Elizur son of Shedeur.
10.19: The tribe of Simeon was led by Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
10.20: The tribe of Gad was led by Eliasaph son of Deuel.
10.21: Next came the Kohathite division of the Levites, carrying the sacred objects from the Tabernacle. When they arrived at the next camp, the Tabernacle would already be set up at its new location.
10.22: Then the tribes that camped with Ephraim set out with their banner, under the leadership of Elishama son of Ammihud.
10.23: The tribe of Manasseh was led by Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
10.24: The tribe of Benjamin was led by Abidan son of Gideoni.
10.25: Last of all, the tribes that camped with Dan set out under their banner. They served as the rear guard for all the tribal camps. The tribe of Dan headed this group, under the leadership of Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
10.26: The tribe of Asher was led by Pagiel son of Ocran.
10.27: The tribe of Naphtali was led by Ahira son of Enan.
10.28: This was the order in which the tribes marched, division by division.
10.29: One day Moses said to his brother-in-law, Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, "We are on our way to the Promised Land. Come with us and we will treat you well, for the LORD has given wonderful promises to Israel!"
10.30: But Hobab replied, "No, I will not go. I must return to my own land and family."
10.31: "Please don't leave us," Moses pleaded. "You know the places in the wilderness where we should camp.
10.32: Come, be our guide and we will share with you all the good things that the LORD does for us."
10.33: They marched for three days after leaving the mountain of the LORD, with the Ark of the LORD's covenant moving ahead of them to show them where to stop and rest.
10.34: As they moved on each day, the cloud of the LORD hovered over them.
10.35: And whenever the Ark set out, Moses would cry, "Arise, O LORD, and let your enemies be scattered! Let them flee before you!"
10.36: And when the Ark was set down, he would say, "Return, O LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel!"

11.1: The people soon began to complain to the LORD about their hardships; and when the LORD heard them, his anger blazed against them. Fire from the LORD raged among them and destroyed the outskirts of the camp.
11.2: The people screamed to Moses for help; and when he prayed to the LORD, the fire stopped.
11.3: After that, the area was known as Taberah--"the place of burning"--because fire from the LORD had burned among them there.
11.4: Then the foreign rabble who were traveling with the Israelites began to crave the good things of Egypt, and the people of Israel also began to complain. "Oh, for some meat!" they exclaimed.
11.5: "We remember all the fish we used to eat for free in Egypt. And we had all the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic that we wanted.
11.6: But now our appetites are gone, and day after day we have nothing to eat but this manna!"
11.7: The manna looked like small coriander seeds, pale yellow in color.
11.8: The people gathered it from the ground and made flour by grinding it with hand mills or pounding it in mortars. Then they boiled it in a pot and made it into flat cakes. These cakes tasted like they had been cooked in olive oil.
11.9: The manna came down on the camp with the dew during the night.
11.10: Moses heard all the families standing in front of their tents weeping, and the LORD became extremely angry. Moses was also very aggravated.
11.11: And Moses said to the LORD, "Why are you treating me, your servant, so miserably? What did I do to deserve the burden of a people like this?
11.12: Are they my children? Am I their father? Is that why you have told me to carry them in my arms--like a nurse carries a baby--to the land you swore to give their ancestors?
11.13: Where am I supposed to get meat for all these people? They keep complaining and saying, `Give us meat!'
11.14: I can't carry all these people by myself! The load is far too heavy!
11.15: I'd rather you killed me than treat me like this. Please spare me this misery!"
11.16: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Summon before me seventy of the leaders of Israel. Bring them to the Tabernacle to stand there with you.
11.17: I will come down and talk to you there. I will take some of the Spirit that is upon you, and I will put the Spirit upon them also. They will bear the burden of the people along with you, so you will not have to carry it alone.
11.18: "And tell the people to purify themselves, for tomorrow they will have meat to eat. Tell them, `The LORD has heard your whining and complaints: "If only we had meat to eat! Surely we were better off in Egypt!" Now the LORD will give you meat, and you will have to eat it.
11.19: And it won't be for just a day or two, or for five or ten or even twenty.
11.20: You will eat it for a whole month until you gag and are sick of it. For you have rejected the LORD, who is here among you, and you have complained to him, "Why did we ever leave Egypt?"'"
11.21: But Moses said, "There are 600,000 foot soldiers here with me, and yet you promise them meat for a whole month!
11.22: Even if we butchered all our flocks and herds, would that satisfy them? Even if we caught all the fish in the sea, would that be enough?"
11.23: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Is there any limit to my power? Now you will see whether or not my word comes true!"
11.24: So Moses went out and reported the LORD's words to the people. Then he gathered the seventy leaders and stationed them around the Tabernacle.
11.25: And the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to Moses. He took some of the Spirit that was upon Moses and put it upon the seventy leaders. They prophesied as the Spirit rested upon them, but that was the only time this happened.
11.26: Two men, Eldad and Medad, were still in the camp when the Spirit rested upon them. They were listed among the leaders but had not gone out to the Tabernacle, so they prophesied there in the camp.
11.27: A young man ran and reported to Moses, "Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!"
11.28: Joshua son of Nun, who had been Moses' personal assistant since his youth, protested, "Moses, my master, make them stop!"
11.29: But Moses replied, "Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all the LORD's people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his Spirit upon them all!"
11.30: Then Moses returned to the camp with the leaders of Israel.
11.31: Now the LORD sent a wind that brought quail from the sea and let them fall into the camp and all around it! For many miles in every direction from the camp there were quail flying about three feet above the ground.
11.32: So the people went out and caught quail all that day and throughout the night and all the next day, too. No one gathered less than fifty bushels! They spread the quail out all over the camp.
11.33: But while they were still eating the meat, the anger of the LORD blazed against the people, and he caused a severe plague to break out among them.
11.34: So that place was called Kibroth-hattaavah--"the graves of craving"--because they buried the people there who had craved meat from Egypt.
11.35: From there the Israelites traveled to Hazeroth, where they stayed for some time.

12.1: While they were at Hazeroth, Miriam and Aaron criticized Moses because he had married a Cushite woman.
12.2: They said, "Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Hasn't he spoken through us, too?" But the LORD heard them.
12.3: Now Moses was more humble than any other person on earth.
12.4: So immediately the LORD called to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam and said, "Go out to the Tabernacle, all three of you!" And the three of them went out.
12.5: Then the LORD descended in the pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the Tabernacle. "Aaron and Miriam!" he called, and they stepped forward.
12.6: And the LORD said to them, "Now listen to me! Even with prophets, I the LORD communicate by visions and dreams.
12.7: But that is not how I communicate with my servant Moses. He is entrusted with my entire house.
12.8: I speak to him face to face, directly and not in riddles! He sees the LORD as he is. Should you not be afraid to criticize him?"
12.9: The LORD was furious with them, and he departed.
12.10: As the cloud moved from above the Tabernacle, Miriam suddenly became white as snow with leprosy. When Aaron saw what had happened,
12.11: he cried out to Moses, "Oh, my lord! Please don't punish us for this sin we have so foolishly committed.
12.12: Don't let her be like a stillborn baby, already decayed at birth."
12.13: So Moses cried out to the LORD, "Heal her, O God, I beg you!"
12.14: And the LORD said to Moses, "If her father had spit in her face, wouldn't she have been defiled for seven days? Banish her from the camp for seven days, and after that she may return."
12.15: So Miriam was excluded from the camp for seven days, and the people waited until she was brought back before they traveled again.
12.16: Then they left Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.

13.1: The LORD now said to Moses,
13.2: "Send men to explore the land of Canaan, the land I am giving to Israel. Send one leader from each of the twelve ancestral tribes."
13.3: So Moses did as the LORD commanded him. He sent out twelve men, all tribal leaders of Israel, from their camp in the wilderness of Paran.
13.4: These were the tribes and the names of the leaders: Reuben............. Shammua son of Zaccur
13.5: Simeon................. Shaphat son of Hori
13.6: Judah................ Caleb son of Jephunneh
13.7: Issachar................... Igal son of Joseph
13.8: Ephraim................. Hoshea son of Nun
13.9: Benjamin................. Palti son of Raphu
13.10: Zebulun................. Gaddiel son of Sodi
13.11: Manasseh son of Joseph...... Gaddi son of Susi
13.12: Dan................. Ammiel son of Gemalli
13.13: Asher................. Sethur son of Michael
13.14: Naphtali................ Nahbi son of Vophsi
13.15: Gad..................... Geuel son of Maki
13.16: These are the names of the men Moses sent to explore the land. By this time Moses had changed Hoshea's name to Joshua.
13.17: Moses gave the men these instructions as he sent them out to explore the land: "Go northward through the Negev into the hill country.
13.18: See what the land is like and find out whether the people living there are strong or weak, few or many.
13.19: What kind of land do they live in? Is it good or bad? Do their towns have walls or are they unprotected?
13.20: How is the soil? Is it fertile or poor? Are there many trees? Enter the land boldly, and bring back samples of the crops you see." (It happened to be the season for harvesting the first ripe grapes.)
13.21: So they went up and explored the land from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, near Lebo-hamath.
13.22: Going northward, they passed first through the Negev and arrived at Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai--all descendants of Anak--lived. (The ancient town of Hebron was founded seven years before the Egyptian city of Zoan.)
13.23: When they came to what is now known as the valley of Eshcol, they cut down a cluster of grapes so large that it took two of them to carry it on a pole between them! They also took samples of the pomegranates and figs.
13.24: At that time the Israelites renamed the valley Eshcol--"cluster"--because of the cluster of grapes they had cut there.
13.25: After exploring the land for forty days, the men returned
13.26: to Moses, Aaron, and the people of Israel at Kadesh in the wilderness of Paran. They reported to the whole community what they had seen and showed them the fruit they had taken from the land.
13.27: This was their report to Moses: "We arrived in the land you sent us to see, and it is indeed a magnificent country--a land flowing with milk and honey. Here is some of its fruit as proof.
13.28: But the people living there are powerful, and their cities and towns are fortified and very large. We also saw the descendants of Anak who are living there!
13.29: The Amalekites live in the Negev, and the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hill country. The Canaanites live along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea and along the Jordan Valley."
13.30: But Caleb tried to encourage the people as they stood before Moses. "Let's go at once to take the land," he said. "We can certainly conquer it!"
13.31: But the other men who had explored the land with him answered, "We can't go up against them! They are stronger than we are!"
13.32: So they spread discouraging reports about the land among the Israelites: "The land we explored will swallow up any who go to live there. All the people we saw were huge.
13.33: We even saw giants there, the descendants of Anak. We felt like grasshoppers next to them, and that's what we looked like to them!"

14.1: Then all the people began weeping aloud, and they cried all night.
14.2: Their voices rose in a great chorus of complaint against Moses and Aaron. "We wish we had died in Egypt, or even here in the wilderness!" they wailed.
14.3: "Why is the LORD taking us to this country only to have us die in battle? Our wives and little ones will be carried off as slaves! Let's get out of here and return to Egypt!"
14.4: Then they plotted among themselves, "Let's choose a leader and go back to Egypt!"
14.5: Then Moses and Aaron fell face down on the ground before the people of Israel.
14.6: Two of the men who had explored the land, Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, tore their clothing.
14.7: They said to the community of Israel, "The land we explored is a wonderful land!
14.8: And if the LORD is pleased with us, he will bring us safely into that land and give it to us. It is a rich land flowing with milk and honey, and he will give it to us!
14.9: Do not rebel against the LORD, and don't be afraid of the people of the land. They are only helpless prey to us! They have no protection, but the LORD is with us! Don't be afraid of them!"
14.10: But the whole community began to talk about stoning Joshua and Caleb. Then the glorious presence of the LORD appeared to all the Israelites from above the Tabernacle.
14.11: And the LORD said to Moses, "How long will these people reject me? Will they never believe me, even after all the miraculous signs I have done among them?
14.12: I will disown them and destroy them with a plague. Then I will make you into a nation far greater and mightier than they are!"
14.13: "But what will the Egyptians think when they hear about it?" Moses pleaded with the LORD. "They know full well the power you displayed in rescuing these people from Egypt.
