14.14: They will tell this to the inhabitants of this land, who are well aware that you are with this people. They know, LORD, that you have appeared in full view of your people in the pillar of cloud that hovers over them. They know that you go before them in the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night.
14.15: Now if you slaughter all these people, the nations that have heard of your fame will say,
14.16: `The LORD was not able to bring them into the land he swore to give them, so he killed them in the wilderness.'
14.17: "Please, Lord, prove that your power is as great as you have claimed it to be. For you said,
14.18: `The LORD is slow to anger and rich in unfailing love, forgiving every kind of sin and rebellion. Even so he does not leave sin unpunished, but he punishes the children for the sins of their parents to the third and fourth generations.'
14.19: Please pardon the sins of this people because of your magnificent, unfailing love, just as you have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt."
14.20: Then the LORD said, "I will pardon them as you have requested.
14.21: But as surely as I live, and as surely as the earth is filled with the LORD's glory,
14.22: not one of these people will ever enter that land. They have seen my glorious presence and the miraculous signs I performed both in Egypt and in the wilderness, but again and again they tested me by refusing to listen.
14.23: They will never even see the land I swore to give their ancestors. None of those who have treated me with contempt will enter it.
14.24: But my servant Caleb is different from the others. He has remained loyal to me, and I will bring him into the land he explored. His descendants will receive their full share of that land.
14.25: Now turn around and don't go on toward the land where the Amalekites and Canaanites live. Tomorrow you must set out for the wilderness in the direction of the Red Sea. "
14.26: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
14.27: "How long will this wicked nation complain about me? I have heard everything the Israelites have been saying.
14.28: Now tell them this: `As surely as I live, I will do to you the very things I heard you say. I, the LORD, have spoken!
14.29: You will all die here in this wilderness! Because you complained against me, none of you who are twenty years old or older and were counted in the census
14.30: will enter the land I swore to give you. The only exceptions will be Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
14.31: " `You said your children would be taken captive. Well, I will bring them safely into the land, and they will enjoy what you have despised.
14.32: But as for you, your dead bodies will fall in this wilderness.
14.33: And your children will be like shepherds, wandering in the wilderness forty years. In this way, they will pay for your faithlessness, until the last of you lies dead in the wilderness.
14.34: " `Because the men who explored the land were there for forty days, you must wander in the wilderness for forty years--a year for each day, suffering the consequences of your sins. You will discover what it is like to have me for an enemy.'
14.35: I, the LORD, have spoken! I will do these things to every member of the community who has conspired against me. They will all die here in this wilderness!"
14.36: Then the ten scouts who had incited the rebellion against the LORD by spreading discouraging reports about the land
14.37: were struck dead with a plague before the LORD.
14.38: Of the twelve who had explored the land, only Joshua and Caleb remained alive.
14.39: When Moses reported the LORD's words to the Israelites, there was much sorrow among the people.
14.40: So they got up early the next morning and set out for the hill country of Canaan. "Let's go," they said. "We realize that we have sinned, but now we are ready to enter the land the LORD has promised us."
14.41: But Moses said, "Why are you now disobeying the LORD's orders to return to the wilderness? It won't work.
14.42: Do not go into the land now. You will only be crushed by your enemies because the LORD is not with you.
14.43: When you face the Amalekites and Canaanites in battle, you will be slaughtered. The LORD will abandon you because you have abandoned the LORD."
14.44: But the people pushed ahead toward the hill country of Canaan, despite the fact that neither Moses nor the Ark of the LORD's covenant left the camp.
14.45: Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in those hills came down and attacked them and chased them as far as Hormah.

15.1: The LORD told Moses to give these instructions to the people of Israel:
15.2: "When you finally settle in the land I am going to give you,
15.3: and you want to please the LORD with a burnt offering or any other offering given by fire, the sacrifice must be an animal from your flocks of sheep and goats or from your herds of cattle. When it is an ordinary burnt offering, a sacrifice to fulfill a vow, a freewill offering, or a special sacrifice at any of the annual festivals,
15.4: whoever brings it must also give to the LORD a grain offering of two quarts of choice flour mixed with one quart of olive oil.
15.5: For each lamb offered as a whole burnt offering, you must also present one quart of wine for a drink offering.
15.6: "If the sacrifice is a ram, give three quarts of choice flour mixed with two and a half pints of olive oil,
15.7: and give two and a half pints of wine for a drink offering. This sacrifice will be very pleasing to the LORD.
15.8: "When you present a young bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice in fulfillment of a special vow or as a peace offering to the LORD,
15.9: then the grain offering accompanying it must include five quarts of choice flour mixed with two quarts of olive oil,
15.10: plus two quarts of wine for the drink offering. This will be an offering made by fire, very pleasing to the LORD.
15.11: "These are the instructions for what is to accompany each sacrificial bull, ram, lamb, or young goat.
15.12: Each of you must do this with each offering you present.
15.13: If you native Israelites want to present an offering by fire that is pleasing to the LORD, you must follow all these instructions.
15.14: And if any foreigners living among you want to present an offering by fire, pleasing to the LORD, they must follow the same procedures.
15.15: Native Israelites and foreigners are the same before the LORD and are subject to the same laws. This is a permanent law for you.
15.16: The same instructions and regulations will apply both to you and to the foreigners living among you."
15.17: The LORD also said to Moses at this time,
15.18: "Give the people of Israel the following instructions: When you arrive in the land where I am taking you,
15.19: you will eat from the crops that grow there. But you must set some aside as a gift to the LORD.
15.20: Present a cake from the first of the flour you grind and set it aside as a gift, as you do with the first grain from the threshing floor.
15.21: Throughout the generations to come, you are to present this offering to the LORD each year from the first of your ground flour.
15.22: "But suppose some of you unintentionally fail to carry out all these commands that the LORD has given you through Moses.
15.23: And suppose some of your descendants in the future fail to do everything the LORD has commanded through Moses.
15.24: If the mistake was done unintentionally, and the community was unaware of it, the whole community must present a young bull for a burnt offering. It will be pleasing to the LORD, and it must be offered along with the prescribed grain offering and drink offering and with one male goat for a sin offering.
15.25: With it the priest will make atonement for the whole community of Israel, and they will be forgiven. For it was an unintentional sin, and they have corrected it with their offering given to the LORD by fire and by their sin offering.
15.26: The whole community of Israel will be forgiven, including the foreigners living among you, for the entire population was involved in the sin.
15.27: "If the unintentional sin is committed by an individual, the guilty person must bring a one-year-old female goat for a sin offering.
15.28: The priest will make atonement for the guilty person before the LORD, and that person will be forgiven.
15.29: This same law applies both to native Israelites and the foreigners living among you.
15.30: "But those who brazenly violate the LORD's will, whether native Israelites or foreigners, blaspheme the LORD, and they must be cut off from the community.
15.31: Since they have treated the LORD's word with contempt and deliberately disobeyed his commands, they must be completely cut off and suffer the consequences of their guilt."
15.32: One day while the people of Israel were in the wilderness, they caught a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
15.33: He was apprehended and taken before Moses, Aaron, and the rest of the community.
15.34: They held him in custody because they did not know what to do with him.
15.35: Then the LORD said to Moses, "The man must be put to death! The whole community must stone him outside the camp."
15.36: So the whole community took the man outside the camp and stoned him to death, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
15.37: And the LORD said to Moses,
15.38: "Say to the people of Israel: `Throughout the generations to come you must make tassels for the hems of your clothing and attach the tassels at each corner with a blue cord.
15.39: The tassels will remind you of the commands of the LORD, and that you are to obey his commands instead of following your own desires and going your own ways, as you are prone to do.
15.40: The tassels will help you remember that you must obey all my commands and be holy to your God.
15.41: I am the LORD your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt that I might be your God. I am the LORD your God!'"

16.1: One day Korah son of Izhar, a descendant of Kohath son of Levi, conspired with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, from the tribe of Reuben.
16.2: They incited a rebellion against Moses, involving 250 other prominent leaders, all members of the assembly.
16.3: They went to Moses and Aaron and said, "You have gone too far! Everyone in Israel has been set apart by the LORD, and he is with all of us. What right do you have to act as though you are greater than anyone else among all these people of the LORD?"
16.4: When Moses heard what they were saying, he threw himself down with his face to the ground.
16.5: Then he said to Korah and his followers, "Tomorrow morning the LORD will show us who belongs to him and who is holy. The LORD will allow those who are chosen to enter his holy presence.
16.6: You, Korah, and all your followers must do this: Take incense burners,
16.7: and burn incense in them tomorrow before the LORD. Then we will see whom the LORD chooses as his holy one. You Levites are the ones who have gone too far!"
16.8: Then Moses spoke again to Korah: "Now listen, you Levites!
16.9: Does it seem a small thing to you that the God of Israel has chosen you from among all the people of Israel to be near him as you serve in the LORD's Tabernacle and to stand before the people to minister to them?
16.10: He has given this special ministry only to you and your fellow Levites, but now you are demanding the priesthood as well!
16.11: The one you are really revolting against is the LORD! And who is Aaron that you are complaining about him?"
16.12: Then Moses summoned Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they replied, "We refuse to come!
16.13: Isn't it enough that you brought us out of Egypt, a land flowing with milk and honey, to kill us here in this wilderness, and that you now treat us like your subjects?
16.14: What's more, you haven't brought us into the land flowing with milk and honey or given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Are you trying to fool us? We will not come."
16.15: Then Moses became very angry and said to the LORD, "Do not accept their offerings! I have not taken so much as a donkey from them, and I have never hurt a single one of them."
16.16: And Moses said to Korah, "Come here tomorrow and present yourself before the LORD with all your followers. Aaron will also be here.
16.17: Be sure that each of your 250 followers brings an incense burner with incense on it, so you can present them before the LORD. Aaron will also bring his incense burner."
16.18: So these men came with their incense burners, placed burning coals and incense on them, and stood at the entrance of the Tabernacle with Moses and Aaron.
16.19: Meanwhile, Korah had stirred up the entire community against Moses and Aaron, and they all assembled at the Tabernacle entrance. Then the glorious presence of the LORD appeared to the whole community,
16.20: and the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
16.21: "Get away from these people so that I may instantly destroy them!"
16.22: But Moses and Aaron fell face down on the ground. "O God, the God and source of all life," they pleaded. "Must you be angry with all the people when only one man sins?"
16.23: And the LORD said to Moses,
16.24: "Then tell all the people to get away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram."
16.25: So Moses got up and rushed over to the tents of Dathan and Abiram, followed closely by the Israelite leaders.
16.26: "Quick!" he told the people. "Get away from the tents of these wicked men, and don't touch anything that belongs to them. If you do, you will be destroyed for their sins."
16.27: So all the people stood back from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Then Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrances of their tents with their wives and children and little ones.
16.28: And Moses said, "By this you will know that the LORD has sent me to do all these things that I have done--for I have not done them on my own.
16.29: If these men die a natural death, then the LORD has not sent me.
16.30: But if the LORD performs a miracle and the ground opens up and swallows them and all their belongings, and they go down alive into the grave, then you will know that these men have despised the LORD."
16.31: He had hardly finished speaking the words when the ground suddenly split open beneath them.
16.32: The earth opened up and swallowed the men, along with their households and the followers who were standing with them, and everything they owned.
16.33: So they went down alive into the grave, along with their belongings. The earth closed over them, and they all vanished.
16.34: All of the people of Israel fled as they heard their screams, fearing that the earth would swallow them, too.
16.35: Then fire blazed forth from the LORD and burned up the 250 men who were offering incense.
16.36: And the LORD said to Moses,
16.37: "Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to pull all the incense burners from the fire, for they are holy. Also tell him to scatter the burning incense
16.38: from the burners of these men who have sinned at the cost of their lives. He must then hammer the metal of the incense burners into a sheet as a covering for the altar, for these burners have become holy because they were used in the LORD's presence. The altar covering will then serve as a warning to the people of Israel."
16.39: So Eleazar the priest collected the 250 bronze incense burners that had been used by the men who died in the fire, and they were hammered out into a sheet of metal to cover the altar.
16.40: This would warn the Israelites that no unauthorized man--no one who was not a descendant of Aaron--should ever enter the LORD's presence to burn incense. If anyone did, the same thing would happen to him as happened to Korah and his followers. Thus, the LORD's instructions to Moses were carried out.
16.41: But the very next morning the whole community began muttering again against Moses and Aaron, saying, "You two have killed the LORD's people!"
16.42: As the people gathered to protest to Moses and Aaron, they turned toward the Tabernacle and saw that the cloud had covered it, and the glorious presence of the LORD appeared.
16.43: Moses and Aaron came and stood at the entrance of the Tabernacle,
16.44: and the LORD said to Moses,
16.45: "Get away from these people so that I can instantly destroy them!" But Moses and Aaron fell face down on the ground.
16.46: And Moses said to Aaron, "Quick, take an incense burner and place burning coals on it from the altar. Lay incense on it and carry it quickly among the people to make atonement for them. The LORD's anger is blazing among them--the plague has already begun."
16.47: Aaron did as Moses told him and ran out among the people. The plague indeed had already begun, but Aaron burned the incense and made atonement for them.
16.48: He stood between the living and the dead until the plague was stopped.
16.49: But 14,700 people died in that plague, in addition to those who had died in the incident involving Korah.
16.50: Then because the plague had stopped, Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance of the Tabernacle.

17.1: Then the LORD said to Moses,
17.2: "Take twelve wooden staffs, one from each of Israel's ancestral tribes, and inscribe each tribal leader's name on his staff.
17.3: Inscribe Aaron's name on the staff of the tribe of Levi, for there must be one staff for the leader of each ancestral tribe.
17.4: Put these staffs in the Tabernacle in front of the Ark of the Covenant, where I meet with you.
17.5: Buds will sprout on the staff belonging to the man I choose. Then I will finally put an end to this murmuring and complaining against you."
17.6: So Moses gave the instructions to the people of Israel, and each of the twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron, brought Moses a staff.
17.7: Moses put the staffs in the LORD's presence in the Tabernacle of the Covenant.
17.8: When he went into the Tabernacle of the Covenant the next day, he found that Aaron's staff, representing the tribe of Levi, had sprouted, blossomed, and produced almonds!
17.9: When Moses brought all the staffs out from the LORD's presence, he showed them to the people. Each man claimed his own staff.
17.10: And the LORD said to Moses: "Place Aaron's staff permanently before the Ark of the Covenant as a warning to rebels. This should put an end to their complaints against me and prevent any further deaths."
17.11: So Moses did as the LORD commanded him.
17.12: Then the people of Israel said to Moses, "We are as good as dead! We are ruined!
17.13: Everyone who even comes close to the Tabernacle of the LORD dies. We are all doomed!"

18.1: The LORD now said to Aaron: "You, your sons, and your relatives from the tribe of Levi will be held responsible for any offenses related to the sanctuary. But you and your sons alone will be held liable for violations connected with the priesthood.
18.2: "Bring your relatives of the tribe of Levi to assist you and your sons as you perform the sacred duties in front of the Tabernacle of the Covenant.
18.3: But as the Levites go about their duties under your supervision, they must be careful not to touch any of the sacred objects or the altar. If they do, both you and they will die.
18.4: The Levites must join with you to fulfill their responsibilities for the care and maintenance of the Tabernacle, but no one who is not a Levite may officiate with you.
18.5: "You yourselves must perform the sacred duties within the sanctuary and at the altar. If you follow these instructions, the LORD's anger will never again blaze against the people of Israel.
18.6: I myself have chosen your fellow Levites from among the Israelites to be your special assistants. They are dedicated to the LORD for service in the Tabernacle.
18.7: But you and your sons, the priests, must personally handle all the sacred service associated with the altar and everything within the inner curtain. I am giving you the priesthood as your special gift of service. Any other person who comes too near the sanctuary will be put to death."
18.8: The LORD gave these further instructions to Aaron: "I have put the priests in charge of all the holy gifts that are brought to me by the people of Israel. I have given these offerings to you and your sons as your regular share.
18.9: You are allotted the portion of the most holy offerings that is kept from the fire. From all the most holy offerings--including the grain offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings--that portion belongs to you and your sons.
18.10: You must eat it as a most holy offering. All the males may eat of it, and you must treat it as most holy.
18.11: "All the other offerings presented to me by the Israelites by lifting them up before the altar also belong to you as your regular share. Any member of your family who is ceremonially clean, male and female alike, may eat of these offerings.
18.12: "I also give you the harvest gifts brought by the people as offerings to the LORD--the best of the olive oil, wine, and grain.
18.13: All the firstfruits of the land that the people present to the LORD belong to you. Any member of your family who is ceremonially clean may eat this food.
18.14: "Whatever is specially set apart for the LORD also belongs to you.
18.15: "The firstborn of every mother, whether human or animal, that is offered to the LORD will be yours. But you must always redeem your firstborn sons and the firstborn males of ritually unclean animals.
18.16: Redeem them when they are one month old. The redemption price is five pieces of silver, each piece weighing the same as the standard sanctuary shekel.
18.17: "However, you may not redeem the firstborn of cattle, sheep, or goats. They are holy and have been set apart for the LORD. Sprinkle their blood on the altar, and burn their fat as an offering given by fire, very pleasing to the LORD.
18.18: The meat of these animals will be yours, just like the breast and right thigh that are presented by lifting them up before the altar.
18.19: Yes, I am giving you all these holy offerings that the people of Israel bring to the LORD. They are for you and your sons and daughters, to be eaten as your regular share. This is an unbreakable covenant between the LORD and you and your descendants."
18.20: And the LORD said to Aaron, "You priests will receive no inheritance of land or share of property among the people of Israel. I am your inheritance and your share.
18.21: As for the tribe of Levi, your relatives, I will pay them for their service in the Tabernacle with the tithes from the entire land of Israel.
18.22: "From now on, Israelites other than the priests and Levites are to stay away from the Tabernacle. If they come too near, they will be judged guilty and die.
18.23: The Levites must serve at the Tabernacle, and they will be held responsible for any offenses against it. This is a permanent law among you. But the Levites will receive no inheritance of land among the Israelites,
18.24: because I have given them the Israelites' tithes, which have been set apart as offerings to the LORD. This will be the Levites' share. That is why I said they would receive no inheritance of land among the Israelites."
18.26: "Say this to the Levites: `When you receive the tithes from the Israelites, give a tenth of the tithes you receive--a tithe of the tithe--to the LORD as a gift.
18.27: The LORD will consider this to be your harvest offering, as though it were the first grain from your own threshing floor or wine from your own winepress.
18.28: You must present one-tenth of the tithe received from the Israelites as a gift to the LORD. From this you must present the LORD's portion to Aaron the priest.
18.29: Be sure to set aside the best portions of the gifts given to you as your gifts to the LORD.'
18.30: "Also say to the Levites: `When you present the best part, it will be considered as though it came from your own threshing floor or winepress.
18.31: You Levites and your families may eat this food anywhere you wish, for it is your compensation for serving in the Tabernacle.
18.32: You will not be considered guilty for accepting the LORD's tithes if you give the best portion to the priests. But be careful not to treat the holy gifts of the people of Israel as though they were common. If you do, you will die.'"

19.1: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
19.2: "Here is another ritual law required by the LORD: Tell the people of Israel to bring you a red heifer that has no physical defects and has never been yoked to a plow.
19.3: Give it to Eleazar the priest, and it will be taken outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence.
19.4: Eleazar will take some of its blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the Tabernacle.
19.5: As Eleazar watches, the heifer must be burned--its hide, meat, blood, and dung.
19.6: Eleazar the priest must then take cedarwood, a hyssop branch, and scarlet thread and throw them into the fire where the heifer is burning.
19.7: "Then the priest must wash his clothes and bathe himself in water. Afterward he may return to the camp, though he will remain ceremonially unclean until evening.
19.8: The man who burns the animal must also wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he, too, will remain unclean until evening.
19.9: Then someone who is ceremonially clean will gather up the ashes of the heifer and place them in a purified place outside the camp. They will be kept there for the people of Israel to use in the water for the purification ceremony. This ceremony is performed for the removal of sin.
19.10: The man who gathers up the ashes of the heifer must also wash his clothes, and he will remain ceremonially unclean until evening. This is a permanent law for the people of Israel and any foreigners who live among them.
19.11: "All those who touch a dead human body will be ceremonially unclean for seven days.
19.12: They must purify themselves on the third and seventh days with the water of purification; then they will be purified. But if they do not do this on the third and seventh days, they will continue to be unclean even after the seventh day.
19.13: All those who touch a dead body and do not purify themselves in the proper way defile the LORD's Tabernacle and will be cut off from the community of Israel. Since the water of purification was not sprinkled on them, their defilement continues.
19.14: "This is the ritual law that applies when someone dies in a tent: Those who enter that tent, and those who were inside when the death occurred, will be ceremonially unclean for seven days.
19.15: Any container in the tent that was not covered with a lid is also defiled.
19.16: And if someone outdoors touches the corpse of someone who was killed with a sword or who died a natural death, or if someone touches a human bone or a grave, that person will be unclean for seven days.
19.17: "To remove the defilement, put some of the ashes from the burnt purification offering in a jar and pour fresh water over them.
19.18: Then someone who is ceremonially clean must take a hyssop branch and dip it into the water. That person must sprinkle the water on the tent, on all the furnishings in the tent, and on anyone who was in the tent, or anyone who has touched a human bone, or has touched a person who was killed or who died naturally, or has touched a grave.
19.19: On the third and seventh days the ceremonially clean person must sprinkle the water on those who are unclean. Then on the seventh day the people being cleansed must wash their clothes and bathe themselves, and that evening they will be cleansed of their defilement.
19.20: "But those who become defiled and do not purify themselves will be cut off from the community, for they have defiled the sanctuary of the LORD. Since the water of purification has not been sprinkled on them, they remain defiled.
19.21: This is a permanent law. Those who sprinkle the water of purification must afterward wash their clothes, and anyone who touches the water of purification will remain defiled until evening.
19.22: Anything and anyone that a defiled person touches will be ceremonially defiled until evening."

20.1: In early spring the people of Israel arrived in the wilderness of Zin and camped at Kadesh. While they were there, Miriam died and was buried.
20.2: There was no water for the people to drink at that place, so they rebelled against Moses and Aaron.
20.3: The people blamed Moses and said, "We wish we had died in the LORD's presence with our brothers!
20.4: Did you bring the LORD's people into this wilderness to die, along with all our livestock?
20.5: Why did you make us leave Egypt and bring us here to this terrible place? This land has no grain, figs, grapes, or pomegranates. And there is no water to drink!"
20.6: Moses and Aaron turned away from the people and went to the entrance of the Tabernacle, where they fell face down on the ground. Then the glorious presence of the LORD appeared to them,
20.7: and the LORD said to Moses,
20.8: "You and Aaron must take the staff and assemble the entire community. As the people watch, command the rock over there to pour out its water. You will get enough water from the rock to satisfy all the people and their livestock."
20.9: So Moses did as he was told. He took the staff from the place where it was kept before the LORD.
20.10: Then he and Aaron summoned the people to come and gather at the rock. "Listen, you rebels!" he shouted. "Must we bring you water from this rock?"
20.11: Then Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with the staff, and water gushed out. So all the people and their livestock drank their fill.
20.12: But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "Because you did not trust me enough to demonstrate my holiness to the people of Israel, you will not lead them into the land I am giving them!"
20.13: This place was known as the waters of Meribah, because it was where the people of Israel argued with the LORD, and where he demonstrated his holiness among them.
20.14: While Moses was at Kadesh, he sent ambassadors to the king of Edom with this message: "This message is from your relatives, the people of Israel: You know all the hardships we have been through,
20.15: and that our ancestors went down to Egypt. We lived there a long time and suffered as slaves to the Egyptians.
20.16: But when we cried out to the LORD, he heard us and sent an angel who brought us out of Egypt. Now we are camped at Kadesh, a town on the border of your land.
20.17: Please let us pass through your country. We will be careful not to go through your fields and vineyards. We won't even drink water from your wells. We will stay on the king's road and never leave it until we have crossed the opposite border."
20.18: But the king of Edom said, "Stay out of my land or I will meet you with an army!"
20.19: The Israelites answered, "We will stay on the main road. If any of our livestock drinks your water, we will pay for it. We only want to pass through your country and nothing else."
20.20: But the king of Edom replied, "Stay out! You may not pass through our land." With that he mobilized his army and marched out to meet them with an imposing force.
20.21: Because Edom refused to allow Israel to pass through their country, Israel was forced to turn around.
20.22: The whole community of Israel left Kadesh as a group and arrived at Mount Hor.
20.23: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron at Mount Hor on the border of the land of Edom,
20.24: "The time has come for Aaron to join his ancestors in death. He will not enter the land I am giving the people of Israel, because the two of you rebelled against my instructions concerning the waters of Meribah.
20.25: Now take Aaron and his son Eleazar up Mount Hor.
20.26: There you will remove Aaron's priestly garments and put them on Eleazar, his son. Aaron will die there and join his ancestors."
20.27: So Moses did as the LORD commanded. The three of them went up Mount Hor together as the whole community watched.
20.28: At the summit, Moses removed the priestly garments from Aaron and put them on Eleazar, Aaron's son. Then Aaron died there on top of the mountain, and Moses and Eleazar went back down.
20.29: When the people realized that Aaron had died, all Israel mourned for him thirty days.

21.1: The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that the Israelites were approaching on the road to Atharim. So he attacked the Israelites and took some of them as prisoners.
21.2: Then the people of Israel made this vow to the LORD: "If you will help us conquer these people, we will completely destroy all their towns."
21.3: The LORD heard their request and gave them victory over the Canaanites. The Israelites completely destroyed them and their towns, and the place has been called Hormah ever since.
21.4: Then the people of Israel set out from Mount Hor, taking the road to the Red Sea to go around the land of Edom. But the people grew impatient along the way,
21.5: and they began to murmur against God and Moses. "Why have you brought us out of Egypt to die here in the wilderness?" they complained. "There is nothing to eat here and nothing to drink. And we hate this wretched manna!"
21.6: So the LORD sent poisonous snakes among them, and many of them were bitten and died.
21.7: Then the people came to Moses and cried out, "We have sinned by speaking against the LORD and against you. Pray that the LORD will take away the snakes." So Moses prayed for the people.
21.8: Then the LORD told him, "Make a replica of a poisonous snake and attach it to the top of a pole. Those who are bitten will live if they simply look at it!"
21.9: So Moses made a snake out of bronze and attached it to the top of a pole. Whenever those who were bitten looked at the bronze snake, they recovered!
21.10: The Israelites traveled next to Oboth and camped there.
21.11: Then they went on to Iye-abarim, in the wilderness on the eastern border of Moab.
21.12: From there they traveled to the valley of Zered Brook and set up camp.
21.13: Then they moved to the far side of the Arnon River, in the wilderness adjacent to the territory of the Amorites. The Arnon is the boundary line between the Moabites and the Amorites.
21.14: For this reason The Book of the Wars of the LORD speaks of "the town of Waheb in the area of Suphah, and the ravines; and the Arnon River
21.15: and its ravines, which extend as far as the settlement of Ar on the border of Moab."
21.16: From there the Israelites traveled to Beer, which is the well where the LORD said to Moses, "Assemble the people, and I will give them water."
21.17: There the Israelites sang this song: "Spring up, O well! Yes, sing about it!
21.18: Sing of this well, which princes dug, which great leaders hollowed out with their scepters and staffs." Then the Israelites left the wilderness and proceeded on through Mattanah,
21.19: Nahaliel, and Bamoth.
21.20: Then they went to the valley in Moab where Pisgah Peak overlooks the wasteland.
21.21: The Israelites now sent ambassadors to King Sihon of the Amorites with this message:
21.22: "Let us travel through your land. We will stay on the king's road until we have crossed your territory. We will not trample your fields or touch your vineyards or drink your well water."
21.23: But King Sihon refused to let them cross his land. Instead, he mobilized his entire army and attacked Israel in the wilderness, engaging them in battle at Jahaz.
21.24: But the Israelites slaughtered them and occupied their land from the Arnon River to the Jabbok River. They went only as far as the Ammonite border because the boundary of the Ammonites was fortified.
21.25: So Israel captured all the towns of the Amorites and settled in them, including the city of Heshbon and its surrounding villages.
21.26: Heshbon had been the capital of King Sihon of the Amorites. He had conquered a former Moabite king and seized all his land as far as the Arnon River.
21.27: For this reason the ancient poets wrote this about him: "Come to Heshbon, city of Sihon! May it be restored and rebuilt.
21.28: A fire flamed forth from Heshbon, a blaze from the city of Sihon. It burned the city of Ar in Moab; it destroyed the rulers of the Arnon heights.
21.29: Your destruction is certain, O people of Moab! You are finished, O worshipers of Chemosh! Chemosh has left his sons as refugees, and his daughters as captives of Sihon, the Amorite king.
21.30: We have utterly destroyed them, all the way from Heshbon to Dibon. We have completely wiped them out as far away as Nophah and Medeba. "
21.31: So the people of Israel occupied the territory of the Amorites.
21.32: After Moses sent men to explore the Jazer area, they captured all the towns in the region and drove out the Amorites who lived there.
21.33: Then they turned and marched toward Bashan, but King Og of Bashan and all his people attacked them at Edrei.
21.34: The LORD said to Moses, "Do not be afraid of him, for I have given you victory over Og and his entire army, giving you all his land. You will do the same to him as you did to King Sihon of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon."
21.35: And Israel was victorious and killed King Og, his sons, and his subjects; not a single survivor remained. Then Israel occupied their land.

22.1: Then the people of Israel traveled to the plains of Moab and camped east of the Jordan River, across from Jericho.
22.2: Balak son of Zippor, the Moabite king, knew what the Israelites had done to the Amorites.
22.3: And when they saw how many Israelites there were, he and his people were terrified.
22.4: The king of Moab said to the leaders of Midian, "This mob will devour everything in sight, like an ox devours grass!" So Balak, king of Moab,
22.5: sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor, who was living in his native land of Pethor near the Euphrates River. He sent this message to request that Balaam come to help him: "A vast horde of people has arrived from Egypt. They cover the face of the earth and are threatening me.
22.6: Please come and curse them for me because they are so numerous. Then perhaps I will be able to conquer them and drive them from the land. I know that blessings fall on the people you bless. I also know that the people you curse are doomed."
22.7: Balak's messengers, officials of both Moab and Midian, set out and took money with them to pay Balaam to curse Israel. They went to Balaam and urgently explained to him what Balak wanted.
22.8: "Stay here overnight," Balaam said. "In the morning I will tell you whatever the LORD directs me to say." So the officials from Moab stayed there with Balaam.
22.9: That night God came to Balaam and asked him, "Who are these men with you?"
22.10: So Balaam said to God, "Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent me this message:
22.11: `A vast horde of people has come from Egypt and has spread out over the whole land. Come at once to curse them. Perhaps then I will be able to conquer them and drive them from the land.'"
22.12: "Do not go with them," God told Balaam. "You are not to curse these people, for I have blessed them!"
22.13: The next morning Balaam got up and told Balak's officials, "Go on home! The LORD will not let me go with you."
22.14: So the Moabite officials returned to King Balak and reported, "Balaam refused to come with us."
22.15: Then Balak tried again. This time he sent a larger number of even more distinguished officials than those he had sent the first time.
22.16: They went to Balaam and gave him this message: "This is what Balak son of Zippor says: Please don't let anything stop you from coming.
22.17: I will pay you well and do anything you ask of me. Just come and curse these people for me!"
22.18: But Balaam answered them, "Even if Balak were to give me a palace filled with silver and gold, I would be powerless to do anything against the will of the LORD my God.
22.19: But stay here one more night to see if the LORD has anything else to say to me."
22.20: That night God came to Balaam and told him, "Since these men have come for you, get up and go with them. But be sure to do only what I tell you to do."
22.21: So the next morning Balaam saddled his donkey and started off with the Moabite officials.
22.22: But God was furious that Balaam was going, so he sent the angel of the LORD to stand in the road to block his way. As Balaam and two servants were riding along,
22.23: Balaam's donkey suddenly saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand. The donkey bolted off the road into a field, but Balaam beat it and turned it back onto the road.
22.24: Then the angel of the LORD stood at a place where the road narrowed between two vineyard walls.
22.25: When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing there, it tried to squeeze by and crushed Balaam's foot against the wall. So Balaam beat the donkey again.
22.26: Then the angel of the LORD moved farther down the road and stood in a place so narrow that the donkey could not get by at all.
22.27: This time when the donkey saw the angel, it lay down under Balaam. In a fit of rage Balaam beat it again with his staff.
22.28: Then the LORD caused the donkey to speak. "What have I done to you that deserves your beating me these three times?" it asked Balaam.
22.29: "Because you have made me look like a fool!" Balaam shouted. "If I had a sword with me, I would kill you!"
22.30: "But I am the same donkey you always ride on," the donkey answered. "Have I ever done anything like this before?No," he admitted.
22.31: Then the LORD opened Balaam's eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the roadway with a drawn sword in his hand. Balaam fell face down on the ground before him.
22.32: "Why did you beat your donkey those three times?" the angel of the LORD demanded. "I have come to block your way because you are stubbornly resisting me.
22.33: Three times the donkey saw me and shied away; otherwise, I would certainly have killed you by now and spared the donkey."
22.34: Then Balaam confessed to the angel of the LORD, "I have sinned. I did not realize you were standing in the road to block my way. I will go back home if you are against my going."
22.35: But the angel of the LORD told him, "Go with these men, but you may say only what I tell you to say." So Balaam went on with Balak's officials.
22.36: When King Balak heard that Balaam was on the way, he went out to meet him at a Moabite town on the Arnon River at the border of his land.
22.37: "Did I not send you an urgent invitation? Why didn't you come right away?" Balak asked Balaam. "Didn't you believe me when I said I would reward you richly?"
22.38: Balaam replied, "I have come, but I have no power to say just anything. I will speak only the messages that God gives me."
22.39: Then Balaam accompanied Balak to Kiriath-huzoth,
22.40: where the king sacrificed cattle and sheep. He sent portions of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
22.41: The next morning Balak took Balaam up to Bamoth-baal. From there he could see the people of Israel spread out below him.

23.1: Balaam said to King Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven young bulls and seven rams for a sacrifice."
23.2: Balak followed his instructions, and the two of them sacrificed a young bull and a ram on each altar.
23.3: Then Balaam said to Balak, "Stand here by your burnt offerings, and I will go to see if the LORD will respond to me. Then I will tell you whatever he reveals to me." So Balaam went alone to the top of a hill,
23.4: and God met him there. Balaam said to him, "I have prepared seven altars and have sacrificed a young bull and a ram on each altar."
23.5: Then the LORD gave Balaam a message for King Balak and said, "Go back to Balak and tell him what I told you."
23.6: When Balaam returned, the king was standing beside his burnt offerings with all the officials of Moab.
23.7: This was the prophecy Balaam delivered: "Balak summoned me to come from Aram; the king of Moab brought me from the eastern hills. `Come,' he said, `curse Jacob for me! Come and announce Israel's doom.'
23.8: But how can I curse those whom God has not cursed? How can I condemn those whom the LORD has not condemned?
23.9: I see them from the cliff tops; I watch them from the hills. I see a people who live by themselves, set apart from other nations.
23.10: Who can count Jacob's descendants, as numerous as dust? Who can count even a fourth of Israel's people? Let me die like the righteous; let my life end like theirs."
23.11: Then King Balak demanded of Balaam, "What have you done to me? I brought you to curse my enemies. Instead, you have blessed them!"
23.12: But Balaam replied, "Can I say anything except what the LORD tells me?"
23.13: Then King Balak told him, "Come with me to another place. There you will see only a portion of the nation of Israel. Curse at least that many!"
23.14: So Balak took Balaam to the plateau of Zophim on Pisgah Peak. He built seven altars there and offered a young bull and a ram on each altar.
23.15: Then Balaam said to the king, "Stand here by your burnt offering while I go to meet the LORD."
23.16: So the LORD met Balaam and gave him a message. Then he said, "Go back to Balak and give him this message."
23.17: So Balaam returned to the place where the king and the officials of Moab were standing beside Balak's burnt offerings. "What did the LORD say?" Balak asked eagerly.
23.18: This was the prophecy Balaam delivered: "Rise up, Balak, and listen! Hear me, son of Zippor.
23.19: God is not a man, that he should lie. He is not a human, that he should change his mind. Has he ever spoken and failed to act? Has he ever promised and not carried it through?
23.20: I received a command to bless; he has blessed, and I cannot reverse it!
23.21: No misfortune is in sight for Jacob; no trouble is in store for Israel. For the LORD their God is with them; he has been proclaimed their king.
23.22: God has brought them out of Egypt; he is like a strong ox for them.
23.23: No curse can touch Jacob; no sorcery has any power against Israel. For now it will be said of Jacob, `What wonders God has done for Israel!'
23.24: These people rise up like a lioness; like a majestic lion they stand. They refuse to rest until they have feasted on prey, drinking the blood of the slaughtered!"
23.25: Then Balak said to Balaam, "If you aren't going to curse them, at least don't bless them!"
23.26: But Balaam replied, "Didn't I tell you that I must do whatever the LORD tells me?"
23.27: Then King Balak said to Balaam, "Come, I will take you to yet another place. Perhaps it will please God to let you curse them from there."
23.28: So Balak took Balaam to the top of Mount Peor, overlooking the wasteland.
23.29: Balaam again told Balak, "Build me seven altars and prepare me seven young bulls and seven rams for a sacrifice."
23.30: So Balak did as Balaam ordered and offered a young bull and a ram on each altar.

24.1: By now Balaam realized that the LORD intended to bless Israel, so he did not resort to divination as he often did. Instead, he turned and looked out toward the wilderness,
24.2: where he saw the people of Israel camped, tribe by tribe. Then the Spirit of God came upon him,
24.3: and this is the prophecy he delivered: "This is the prophecy of Balaam son of Beor, the prophecy of the man whose eyes see clearly,
24.4: who hears the words of God, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who falls down with eyes wide open:
24.5: How beautiful are your tents, O Jacob; how lovely are your homes, O Israel!
24.6: They spread before me like groves of palms, like fruitful gardens by the riverside. They are like aloes planted by the LORD, like cedars beside the waters.
24.7: Water will gush out in buckets; their offspring are supplied with all they need. Their king will be greater than Agag; their kingdom will be exalted.
24.8: God brought them up from Egypt, drawing them along like a wild ox. He devours all the nations that oppose him, breaking their bones in pieces, shooting them with arrows.
24.9: Like a lion, Israel crouches and lies down; like a lioness, who dares to arouse her? Blessed is everyone who blesses you, O Israel, and cursed is everyone who curses you."
24.10: King Balak flew into a rage against Balaam. He angrily clapped his hands and shouted, "I called you to curse my enemies! Instead, you have blessed them three times.
24.11: Now get out of here! Go back home! I had planned to reward you richly, but the LORD has kept you from your reward."
24.12: Balaam told Balak, "Don't you remember what I told your messengers? I said,
24.13: `Even if Balak were to give me a palace filled with silver and gold, I am powerless to do anything against the will of the LORD.' I told you that I could say only what the LORD says!
24.14: Now I am returning to my own people. But first let me tell you what the Israelites will do to your people in the future."
24.15: This is the prophecy Balaam delivered: "This is the message of Balaam son of Beor, the prophecy of the man whose eyes see clearly,
24.16: who hears the words of God, who has knowledge from the Most High, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who falls down with eyes wide open:
24.17: I see him, but not in the present time. I perceive him, but far in the distant future. A star will rise from Jacob; a scepter will emerge from Israel. It will crush the foreheads of Moab's people, cracking the skulls of the people of Sheth.
24.18: Edom will be taken over, and Seir, its enemy, will be conquered, while Israel continues on in triumph.
24.19: A ruler will rise in Jacob who will destroy the survivors of Ir."
24.20: Then Balaam looked over at the people of Amalek and delivered this prophecy: "Amalek was the greatest of nations, but its destiny is destruction!"
24.21: Then he looked over at the Kenites and prophesied: "You are strongly situated; your nest is set in the rocks.
24.22: But the Kenites will be destroyed when Assyria takes you captive."
24.23: Balaam concluded his prophecies by saying: "Alas, who can survive when God does this?
24.24: Ships will come from the coasts of Cyprus; they will oppress both Assyria and Eber, but they, too, will be utterly destroyed."
24.25: Then Balaam and Balak returned to their homes.

25.1: While the Israelites were camped at Acacia, some of the men defiled themselves by sleeping with the local Moabite women.
25.2: These women invited them to attend sacrifices to their gods, and soon the Israelites were feasting with them and worshiping the gods of Moab.
25.3: Before long Israel was joining in the worship of Baal of Peor, causing the LORD's anger to blaze against his people.
25.4: The LORD issued the following command to Moses: "Seize all the ringleaders and execute them before the LORD in broad daylight, so his fierce anger will turn away from the people of Israel."
25.5: So Moses ordered Israel's judges to execute everyone who had joined in worshiping Baal of Peor.
25.6: Just then one of the Israelite men brought a Midianite woman into the camp, right before the eyes of Moses and all the people, as they were weeping at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
25.7: When Phinehas son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron the priest saw this, he jumped up and left the assembly. Then he took a spear
25.8: and rushed after the man into his tent. Phinehas thrust the spear all the way through the man's body and into the woman's stomach. So the plague against the Israelites was stopped,
25.9: but not before 24,000 people had died.
25.10: Then the LORD said to Moses,
25.11: "Phinehas son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron the priest has turned my anger away from the Israelites by displaying passionate zeal among them on my behalf. So I have stopped destroying all Israel as I had intended to do in my anger.
25.12: So tell him that I am making my special covenant of peace with him.
25.13: In this covenant, he and his descendants will be priests for all time, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the people of Israel."
25.14: The Israelite man killed with the Midianite woman was named Zimri son of Salu, the leader of a family from the tribe of Simeon.
25.15: The woman's name was Cozbi; she was the daughter of Zur, the leader of a Midianite clan.
25.16: Then the LORD said to Moses,
25.18: because they assaulted you with deceit by tricking you into worshiping Baal of Peor, and because of Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite leader, who was killed on the day of the plague at Peor."

26.1: After the plague had ended, the LORD said to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron, the priest,
26.2: "Take a census of all the men of Israel who are twenty years old or older, to find out how many of each family are of military age."
26.3: At that time the entire nation of Israel was camped on the plains of Moab beside the Jordan River, across from Jericho. So Moses and Eleazar the priest issued these census instructions to the leaders of Israel:
26.4: "Count all the men of Israel twenty years old and older, just as the LORD commanded Moses." This is the census record of all the descendants of Israel who came out of Egypt.
26.5: These were the clans descended from Reuben, Jacob's oldest son: The Hanochite clan, named after its ancestor Hanoch. The Palluite clan, named after its ancestor Pallu.
26.6: The Hezronite clan, named after its ancestor Hezron. The Carmite clan, named after its ancestor Carmi.
26.7: The men from all the clans of Reuben numbered 43,730.
26.8: Pallu was the ancestor of Eliab,
26.9: and Eliab was the father of Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. This Dathan and Abiram are the same community leaders who conspired with Korah against Moses and Aaron, defying the LORD.
26.10: But the earth opened up and swallowed them with Korah, and 250 of their followers were destroyed that day by fire from the LORD. This served as a warning to the entire nation of Israel.
26.11: However, the sons of Korah did not die that day.
26.12: These were the clans descended from the sons of Simeon: The Nemuelite clan, named after its ancestor Nemuel. The Jaminite clan, named after its ancestor Jamin. The Jakinite clan, named after its ancestor Jakin.
26.13: The Zerahite clan, named after its ancestor Zerah. The Shaulite clan, named after its ancestor Shaul.
26.14: The men from all the clans of Simeon numbered 22,200.
26.15: These were the clans descended from the sons of Gad: The Zephonite clan, named after its ancestor Zephon. The Haggite clan, named after its ancestor Haggi. The Shunite clan, named after its ancestor Shuni.
26.16: The Oznite clan, named after its ancestor Ozni. The Erite clan, named after its ancestor Eri.
26.17: The Arodite clan, named after its ancestor Arodi. The Arelite clan, named after its ancestor Areli.
26.18: The men from all the clans of Gad numbered 40,500.
26.19: Judah had two sons, Er and Onan, who had died in the land of Canaan.
26.20: But the following clans descended from Judah's surviving sons: The Shelanite clan, named after its ancestor Shelah. The Perezite clan, named after its ancestor Perez. The Zerahite clan, named after its ancestor Zerah.
26.21: These were the subclans descended from the Perezites: The Hezronites, named after their ancestor Hezron. The Hamulites, named after their ancestor Hamul.
26.22: The men from all the clans of Judah numbered 76,500.
26.23: These were the clans descended from the sons of Issachar: The Tolaite clan, named after its ancestor Tola. The Puite clan, named after its ancestor Puah.
26.24: The Jashubite clan, named after its ancestor Jashub. The Shimronite clan, named after its ancestor Shimron.
26.25: The men from all the clans of Issachar numbered 64,300.
26.26: These were the clans descended from the sons of Zebulun: The Seredite clan, named after its ancestor Sered. The Elonite clan, named after its ancestor Elon. The Jahleelite clan, named after its ancestor Jahleel.
26.27: The men from all the clans of Zebulun numbered 60,500.
26.28: Two clans were descended from Joseph through Manasseh and Ephraim.
26.29: These were the clans descended from Manasseh: The Makirite clan, named after its ancestor Makir. The Gileadite clan, named after its ancestor Gilead, Makir's son.
26.30: These were the subclans descended from the Gileadites: The Iezerites, named after their ancestor Iezer. The Helekites, named after their ancestor Helek.
26.31: The Asrielites, named after their ancestor Asriel. The Shechemites, named after their ancestor Shechem.
26.32: The Shemidaites, named after their ancestor Shemida. The Hepherites, named after their ancestor Hepher.
26.33: Hepher's son, Zelophehad, had no sons, but his daughters' names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
26.34: The men from all the clans of Manasseh numbered 52,700.
26.35: These were the clans descended from the sons of Ephraim: The Shuthelahite clan, named after its ancestor Shuthelah. The Bekerite clan, named after its ancestor Beker. The Tahanite clan, named after its ancestor Tahan.
26.36: This was the subclan descended from the Shuthelahites: The Eranites, named after their ancestor Eran.
26.37: The men from all the clans of Ephraim numbered 32,500. These clans of Manasseh and Ephraim were all descendants of Joseph.
26.38: These were the clans descended from the sons of Benjamin: The Belaite clan, named after its ancestor Bela. The Ashbelite clan, named after its ancestor Ashbel. The Ahiramite clan, named after its ancestor Ahiram.
26.39: The Shuphamite clan, named after its ancestor Shupham. The Huphamite clan, named after its ancestor Hupham.
26.40: These were the subclans descended from the Belaites: The Ardites, named after their ancestor Ard. The Naamites, named after their ancestor Naaman.
26.41: The men from all the clans of Benjamin numbered 45,600.
26.42: These were the clans descended from the sons of Dan: The Shuhamite clan, named after its ancestor Shuham.
26.43: All the clans of Dan were Shuhamite clans, and the men from these clans numbered 64,400.
26.44: These were the clans descended from the sons of Asher: The Imnite clan, named after its ancestor Imnah. The Ishvite clan, named after its ancestor Ishvi. The Beriite clan, named after its ancestor Beriah.
26.45: These were the subclans descended from the Beriites: The Heberites, named after their ancestor Heber. The Malkielites, named after their ancestor Malkiel.
26.46: Asher also had a daughter named Serah.
26.47: The men from all the clans of Asher numbered 53,400.
26.48: These were the clans descended from the sons of Naphtali: The Jahzeelite clan, named after its ancestor Jahzeel. The Gunite clan, named after its ancestor Guni.
26.49: The Jezerite clan, named after its ancestor Jezer. The Shillemite clan, named after its ancestor Shillem.
26.50: The men from all the clans of Naphtali numbered 45,400.
26.51: So the total number of Israelite men counted in the census numbered 601,730.
26.52: Then the LORD said to Moses,
26.53: "Divide the land among the tribes in proportion to their populations, as indicated by the census.
26.54: Give the larger tribes more land and the smaller tribes less land, each group's inheritance reflecting the size of its population.
26.55: Make sure you assign the land by lot, and define the inheritance of each ancestral tribe by means of the census listings.
26.56: Each inheritance must be assigned by lot among the larger and smaller tribal groups."
26.57: This is the census record for the Levites who were counted according to their clans: The Gershonite clan, named after its ancestor Gershon. The Kohathite clan, named after its ancestor Kohath. The Merarite clan, named after its ancestor Merari.
26.58: The Libnites, the Hebronites, the Mahlites, the Mushites, and the Korahites were all subclans of the Levites. Now Kohath was the ancestor of Amram,
26.59: and Amram's wife was named Jochebed. She also was a descendant of Levi, born among the Levites in the land of Egypt. Amram and Jochebed became the parents of Aaron, Moses, and their sister, Miriam.
26.60: To Aaron were born Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
26.61: But Nadab and Abihu died when they burned before the LORD a different kind of fire than he had commanded.
26.62: The men from the Levite clans who were one month old or older numbered 23,000. But the Levites were not included in the total census figure of the people of Israel because they were not given an inheritance of land when it was divided among the Israelites.
26.63: So these are the census figures of the people of Israel as prepared by Moses and Eleazar the priest on the plains of Moab beside the Jordan River, across from Jericho.
26.64: Not one person that was counted in this census had been among those counted in the previous census taken by Moses and Aaron in the wilderness of Sinai.
26.65: For the LORD had said of them, "They will all die in the wilderness." The only exceptions were Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

27.1: One day a petition was presented by the daughters of Zelophehad--Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. Their father, Zelophehad, was the son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Makir, son of Manasseh, son of Joseph.
27.2: These women went and stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the tribal leaders, and the entire community at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
27.3: "Our father died in the wilderness without leaving any sons," they said. "But he was not among Korah's followers, who rebelled against the LORD. He died because of his own sin.
27.4: Why should the name of our father disappear just because he had no sons? Give us property along with the rest of our relatives."
27.5: So Moses brought their case before the LORD.
27.6: And the LORD replied to Moses,
27.7: "The daughters of Zelophehad are right. You must give them an inheritance of land along with their father's relatives. Assign them the property that would have been given to their father.
27.8: Moreover announce this to the people of Israel: `If a man dies and has no sons, then give his inheritance to his daughters.
27.9: And if he has no daughters, turn his inheritance over to his brothers.
27.10: If he has no brothers, give his inheritance to his father's brothers.
27.11: But if his father has no brothers, pass on his inheritance to the nearest relative in his clan. The Israelites must observe this as a general legal requirement, just as the LORD commanded Moses.'"
27.12: One day the LORD said to Moses, "Climb to the top of the mountains east of the river, and look out over the land I have given the people of Israel.
27.13: After you have seen it, you will die as Aaron your brother did,
27.14: for you both rebelled against my instructions in the wilderness of Zin. When the people of Israel rebelled, you failed to demonstrate my holiness to them at the waters." (These are the waters of Meribah at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.)
27.15: Then Moses said to the LORD,
27.16: "O LORD, the God of the spirits of all living things, please appoint a new leader for the community.
27.17: Give them someone who will lead them into battle, so the people of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd."
27.18: The LORD replied, "Take Joshua son of Nun, who has the Spirit in him, and lay your hands on him.
27.19: Present him to Eleazar the priest before the whole community, and publicly commission him with the responsibility of leading the people.
27.20: Transfer your authority to him so the whole community of Israel will obey him.
27.21: When direction from the LORD is needed, Joshua will stand before Eleazar the priest, who will determine the LORD's will by means of sacred lots. This is how Joshua and the rest of the community of Israel will discover what they should do."
27.22: So Moses did as the LORD commanded and presented Joshua to Eleazar the priest and the whole community.
27.23: Moses laid his hands on him and commissioned him to his responsibilities, just as the LORD had commanded through Moses.

28.2: "Give these instructions to the people of Israel: The offerings you present to me by fire on the altar are my food, and they are very pleasing to me. See to it that they are brought at the appointed times and offered according to my instructions.
28.3: "Say to them: When you present your daily whole burnt offerings to the LORD, you must offer two one-year-old male lambs with no physical defects.
28.4: One lamb will be sacrificed in the morning and the other in the evening.
28.5: With each lamb you must offer a grain offering of two quarts of choice flour mixed with one quart of olive oil.
28.6: This is the regular burnt offering ordained at Mount Sinai, an offering made by fire, very pleasing to the LORD.
28.7: Along with it you must present the proper drink offering, consisting of one quart of fermented drink with each lamb, poured out in the Holy Place as an offering to the LORD.
28.8: Offer the second lamb in the evening with the same grain offering and drink offering. It, too, is an offering made by fire, very pleasing to the LORD.
28.9: "On the Sabbath day, sacrifice two one-year-old male lambs with no physical defects. They must be accompanied by a grain offering of three quarts of choice flour mixed with olive oil, and a drink offering.
28.10: This is the whole burnt offering to be presented each Sabbath day, in addition to the regular daily burnt offering and its accompanying drink offering.
28.11: "On the first day of each month, present an extra burnt offering to the LORD of two young bulls, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all with no physical defects.
28.12: These will be accompanied by grain offerings of choice flour mixed with olive oil--five quarts with each bull, three quarts with the ram,
28.13: and two quarts with each lamb. This burnt offering must be presented by fire, and it will be very pleasing to the LORD.
28.14: You must also give a drink offering with each sacrifice: two quarts of wine with each bull, two and a half pints for the ram, and one quart for each lamb. Present this monthly burnt offering on the first day of each month throughout the year.
28.15: "Also, on the first day of each month you must offer one male goat for a sin offering to the LORD. This is in addition to the regular daily burnt offering and its accompanying drink offering.
28.16: "On the appointed day in early spring, you must celebrate the LORD's Passover.
28.17: On the following day a joyous, seven-day festival will begin, but no bread made with yeast may be eaten.
28.18: On the first day of the festival you must call a sacred assembly of the people. None of your regular work may be done on that day.
28.19: You must present as a burnt offering to the LORD two young bulls, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all with no physical defects.
28.20: These will be accompanied by grain offerings of choice flour mixed with olive oil--five quarts with each bull, three quarts with the ram,
28.21: and two quarts with each of the seven lambs.
28.22: You must also offer a male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for yourselves.
28.23: You will present these offerings in addition to your regular morning sacrifices.
28.24: On each of the seven days of the festival, this is how you will prepare the food offerings to be presented by fire, very pleasing to the LORD. These will be offered in addition to the regular whole burnt offerings and drink offerings.
28.25: On the seventh day of the festival you must call another holy assembly of the people. None of your regular work may be done on that day.
28.26: "On the first day of the Festival of Harvest, when you present the first of your new grain to the LORD, you must call a holy assembly of the people. None of your regular work may be done on that day.
28.27: A special whole burnt offering will be offered that day, very pleasing to the LORD. It will consist of two young bulls, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs.
28.28: These will be accompanied by grain offerings of choice flour mixed with olive oil--five quarts with each bull, three quarts with the ram,
28.29: and two quarts with each of the seven lambs.
28.30: Also, offer one male goat to make atonement for yourselves.
28.31: These special burnt offerings, along with their drink offerings, are in addition to the regular daily burnt offering and its accompanying grain offering. Be sure that all the animals you sacrifice have no physical defects.

29.1: "The Festival of Trumpets will be celebrated on the appointed day in early autumn each year. You must call a solemn assembly of all the people on that day, and no regular work may be done.
29.2: On that day you must present a burnt offering, very pleasing to the LORD. It will consist of one young bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all with no physical defects.
29.3: These must be accompanied by grain offerings of choice flour mixed with olive oil--five quarts with the bull, three quarts with the ram,
29.4: and two quarts with each of the seven lambs.
29.5: In addition, you must sacrifice a male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for yourselves.
29.6: These special sacrifices are in addition to your regular monthly and daily burnt offerings, and they must be given with their prescribed grain offerings and drink offerings. These offerings are given to the LORD by fire and are very pleasing to him.
29.7: "Ten days later, you must call another holy assembly of all the people. On that day, the Day of Atonement, the people must go without food, and no regular work may be done.
29.8: You must present a burnt offering, very pleasing to the LORD. It will consist of one young bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all with no physical defects.
29.9: These offerings must be accompanied by the prescribed grain offerings of choice flour mixed with olive oil--five quarts of choice flour with the bull, three quarts of choice flour with the ram,
29.10: and two quarts of choice flour with each of the seven lambs.
29.11: You must also sacrifice one male goat for a sin offering. This is in addition to the sin offering of atonement and the regular daily burnt offering with its grain offering, and their accompanying drink offerings.
29.12: "Five days later, you must call yet another holy assembly of all the people, and on that day no regular work may be done. It is the beginning of the Festival of Shelters, a seven-day festival to the LORD.
29.13: That day you must present a special whole burnt offering by fire, very pleasing to the LORD. It will consist of thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with no physical defects.
29.14: Each of these offerings must be accompanied by a grain offering of choice flour mixed with olive oil--five quarts for each of the thirteen bulls, three quarts for each of the two rams,
29.15: and two quarts for each of the fourteen lambs.
29.16: You must also sacrifice a male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular daily burnt offering with its accompanying grain offering and drink offering.
29.17: "On the second day of this seven-day festival, sacrifice twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with no physical defects.
29.18: Each of these offerings of bulls, rams, and lambs must be accompanied by the prescribed grain offering and drink offering.
29.19: You must also sacrifice a male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular daily burnt offering with its accompanying grain offering and drink offering.
29.20: "On the third day of the festival, sacrifice eleven young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with no physical defects.
29.21: Each of these offerings of bulls, rams, and lambs must be accompanied by the prescribed grain offering and drink offering.
29.22: You must also sacrifice a male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular daily burnt offering with its accompanying grain offering and drink offering.
29.23: "On the fourth day of the festival, sacrifice ten young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with no physical defects.
29.24: Each of these offerings of bulls, rams, and lambs must be accompanied by the prescribed grain offering and drink offering.
29.25: You must also sacrifice a male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular daily burnt offering with its accompanying grain offering and drink offering.
29.26: "On the fifth day of the festival, sacrifice nine young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with no physical defects.
29.27: Each of these offerings of bulls, rams, and lambs must be accompanied by the prescribed grain offering and drink offering.
29.28: You must also sacrifice a male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular daily burnt offering with its accompanying grain offering and drink offering.
29.29: "On the sixth day of the festival, sacrifice eight young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with no physical defects.
29.30: Each of these offerings of bulls, rams, and lambs must be accompanied by the prescribed grain offering and drink offering.
29.31: You must also sacrifice a male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular daily burnt offering with its accompanying grain offering and drink offering.
29.32: "On the seventh day of the festival, sacrifice seven young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with no physical defects.
29.33: Each of these offerings of bulls, rams, and lambs must be accompanied by the prescribed grain offering and drink offering.
29.34: You must also sacrifice one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular daily burnt offering with its accompanying grain offering and drink offering.
29.35: "On the eighth day of the festival, call all the people to another holy assembly. You must do no regular work on that day.
29.36: You must present a burnt offering, very pleasing to the LORD. It will consist of one young bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all with no physical defects.
29.37: Each of these offerings must be accompanied by the prescribed grain offering and drink offering.
29.38: You must also sacrifice one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular daily burnt offering with its accompanying grain offering and drink offering.
29.39: "You must present these offerings to the LORD at your annual festivals. These are in addition to the sacrifices and offerings you present in connection with vows, or as freewill offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, or peace offerings."
29.40: So Moses gave all of these instructions to the people of Israel, just as the LORD had commanded him.

30.1: Now Moses summoned the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, "This is what the LORD has commanded:
30.2: A man who makes a vow to the LORD or makes a pledge under oath must never break it. He must do exactly what he said he would do.
30.3: "If a young woman makes a vow to the LORD or a pledge under oath while she is still living at her father's home,
30.4: and her father hears of the vow or pledge but says nothing, then all her vows and pledges will stand.
30.5: But if her father refuses to let her fulfill the vow or pledge on the day he hears of it, then all her vows and pledges will become invalid. The LORD will forgive her because her father would not let her fulfill them.
30.6: "Now suppose a young woman takes a vow or makes an impulsive pledge and later marries.
30.7: If her husband learns of her vow or pledge and raises no objections on the day he hears of it, her vows and pledges will stand.
30.8: But if her husband refuses to accept her vow or impulsive pledge on the day he hears of it, he nullifies her commitments, and the LORD will forgive her.
30.9: If, however, a woman is a widow or is divorced, she must fulfill all her vows and pledges no matter what.
30.10: "Suppose a woman is married and living in her husband's home when she makes a vow or pledge.
30.11: If her husband hears of it and does nothing to stop her, her vow or pledge will stand.
30.12: But if her husband refuses to accept it on the day he hears of it, her vow or pledge will be nullified, and the LORD will forgive her.
30.13: So her husband may either confirm or nullify any vows or pledges she makes to deny herself.
30.14: But if he says nothing on the day he hears of it, then he is agreeing to it.
30.15: If he waits more than a day and then tries to nullify a vow or pledge, he will suffer the consequences of her guilt."
30.16: These are the regulations the LORD gave Moses concerning relationships between a man and his wife, and between a father and a young daughter who still lives at home.

31.1: Then the LORD said to Moses,
31.2: "Take vengeance on the Midianites for leading the Israelites into idolatry. After that, you will die and join your ancestors."
31.3: So Moses said to the people, "Choose some men to fight the LORD's war of vengeance against Midian.
31.4: From each tribe of Israel, send one thousand men into battle."
31.5: So they chose one thousand men from each tribe of Israel, a total of twelve thousand men armed for battle.
31.6: Then Moses sent them out, a thousand men from each tribe, and Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest led them into battle. They carried along the holy objects of the sanctuary and the trumpets for sounding the charge.
31.7: They attacked Midian just as the LORD had commanded Moses, and they killed all the men.
31.8: All five of the Midianite kings--Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba--died in the battle. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
31.9: Then the Israelite army captured the Midianite women and children and seized their cattle and flocks and all their wealth as plunder.
31.10: They burned all the towns and villages where the Midianites had lived.
31.11: After they had gathered the plunder and captives, both people and animals,
31.12: they brought them all to Moses and Eleazar the priest, and to the whole community of Israel, which was camped on the plains of Moab beside the Jordan River, across from Jericho.
31.13: Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the people went to meet them outside the camp.
31.14: But Moses was furious with all the military commanders who had returned from the battle.
31.15: "Why have you let all the women live?" he demanded.
31.16: "These are the very ones who followed Balaam's advice and caused the people of Israel to rebel against the LORD at Mount Peor. They are the ones who caused the plague to strike the LORD's people.
31.17: Now kill all the boys and all the women who have slept with a man.
31.18: Only the young girls who are virgins may live; you may keep them for yourselves.
31.19: And all of you who have killed anyone or touched a dead body must stay outside the camp for seven days. You must purify yourselves and your captives on the third and seventh days.
31.20: Also, purify all your clothing and everything made of leather, goat hair, or wood."
31.21: Then Eleazar the priest said to the men who were in the battle, "The LORD has given Moses this requirement of the law:
31.22: Anything made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, or lead--
31.23: that is, metals that do not burn--must be passed through fire in order to be made ceremonially pure. These metal objects must then be further purified with the water of purification. But everything that burns must be purified by the water alone.
31.24: On the seventh day you must wash your clothes and be purified. Then you may return to the camp."
31.25: And the LORD said to Moses,
31.26: "You and Eleazar the priest and the family leaders of each tribe are to make a list of all the plunder taken in the battle, including the people and animals.
31.27: Then divide the plunder into two parts, and give half to the men who fought the battle and half to the rest of the people.
