14.8: And the pig may not be eaten, for though it has split hooves, it does not chew the cud. All these animals are ceremonially unclean for you. You may not eat or even touch the dead bodies of such animals.
14.9: "As for marine animals, you may eat whatever has both fins and scales.
14.10: You may not, however, eat marine animals that do not have both fins and scales. They are ceremonially unclean for you.
14.11: "You may eat any bird that is ceremonially clean.
14.12: These are the birds you may not eat: the eagle, the vulture, the osprey,
14.13: the buzzard, kites of all kinds,
14.14: ravens of all kinds,
14.15: the ostrich, the nighthawk, the seagull, hawks of all kinds,
14.16: the little owl, the great owl, the white owl,
14.17: the pelican, the carrion vulture, the cormorant,
14.18: the stork, herons of all kinds, the hoopoe, and the bat.
14.19: "All flying insects are ceremonially unclean for you and may not be eaten.
14.20: But you may eat any winged creature that is ceremonially clean.
14.21: "Do not eat anything that has died a natural death. You may give it to a foreigner living among you, or you may sell it to a foreigner. But do not eat it yourselves, for you are set apart as holy to the LORD your God. "Do not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
14.22: "You must set aside a tithe of your crops--one-tenth of all the crops you harvest each year.
14.23: Bring this tithe to the place the LORD your God chooses for his name to be honored, and eat it there in his presence. This applies to your tithes of grain, new wine, olive oil, and the firstborn males of your flocks and herds. The purpose of tithing is to teach you always to fear the LORD your God.
14.24: Now the place the LORD your God chooses for his name to be honored might be a long way from your home.
14.25: If so, you may sell the tithe portion of your crops and herds and take the money to the place the LORD your God chooses.
14.26: When you arrive, use the money to buy anything you want--an ox, a sheep, some wine, or beer. Then feast there in the presence of the LORD your God and celebrate with your household.
14.27: And do not forget the Levites in your community, for they have no inheritance as you do.
14.28: "At the end of every third year bring the tithe of all your crops and store it in the nearest town.
14.29: Give it to the Levites, who have no inheritance among you, as well as to the foreigners living among you, the orphans, and the widows in your towns, so they can eat and be satisfied. Then the LORD your God will bless you in all your work.

15.1: "At the end of every seventh year you must cancel your debts.
15.2: This is how it must be done. Creditors must cancel the loans they have made to their fellow Israelites. They must not demand payment from their neighbors or relatives, for the LORD's time of release has arrived.
15.3: This release from debt, however, applies only to your fellow Israelites--not to the foreigners living among you.
15.4: There should be no poor among you, for the LORD your God will greatly bless you in the land he is giving you as a special possession.
15.5: You will receive this blessing if you carefully obey the commands of the LORD your God that I am giving you today.
15.6: The LORD your God will bless you as he has promised. You will lend money to many nations but will never need to borrow! You will rule many nations, but they will not rule over you!
15.7: "But if there are any poor people in your towns when you arrive in the land the LORD your God is giving you, do not be hard-hearted or tightfisted toward them.
15.8: Instead, be generous and lend them whatever they need.
15.9: Do not be mean-spirited and refuse someone a loan because the year of release is close at hand. If you refuse to make the loan and the needy person cries out to the LORD, you will be considered guilty of sin.
15.10: Give freely without begrudging it, and the LORD your God will bless you in everything you do.
15.11: There will always be some among you who are poor. That is why I am commanding you to share your resources freely with the poor and with other Israelites in need.
15.12: "If an Israelite man or woman voluntarily becomes your servant and serves you for six years, in the seventh year you must set that servant free.
15.13: "When you release a male servant, do not send him away empty-handed.
15.14: Give him a generous farewell gift from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress. Share with him some of the bounty with which the LORD your God has blessed you.
15.15: Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt and the LORD your God redeemed you! That is why I am giving you this command.
15.16: But suppose your servant says, `I will not leave you,' because he loves you and your family, and he is well off with you.
15.17: In that case, take an awl and push it through his earlobe into the door. After that, he will be your servant for life. "You must do the same for your female servants.
15.18: "Do not consider it a hardship when you release your servants. Remember that for six years they have given you the services worth double the wages of hired workers, and the LORD your God will bless you in all you do.
15.19: "You must set aside for the LORD your God all the firstborn males from your flocks and herds. Do not use the firstborn of your herds to work your fields, and do not shear the firstborn of your flocks.
15.20: Instead, you and your family must eat these animals in the presence of the LORD your God each year at the place he chooses.
15.21: But if this firstborn animal has any defect, such as being lame or blind, or if anything else is wrong with it, you must not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
15.22: Instead, use it for food for your family at home. Anyone may eat it, whether ceremonially clean or unclean, just as anyone may eat a gazelle or deer.
15.23: But do not eat the blood. You must pour it out on the ground like water.

16.1: "In honor of the LORD your God, always celebrate the Passover at the proper time in early spring, for that was when the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
16.2: Your Passover sacrifice may be from either the flock or the herd, and it must be sacrificed to the LORD your God at the place he chooses for his name to be honored.
16.3: Eat it with bread made without yeast. For seven days eat only bread made without yeast, as you did when you escaped from Egypt in such a hurry. Eat this bread--the bread of suffering--so that you will remember the day you departed from Egypt as long as you live.
16.4: Let no yeast be found in any house throughout your land for seven days. And do not let any of the meat of the Passover lamb remain until the next morning.
16.5: "The Passover must not be eaten in the towns that the LORD your God is giving you.
16.6: It must be offered at the place the LORD your God will choose for his name to be honored. Sacrifice it there as the sun goes down on the anniversary of your exodus from Egypt.
16.7: Roast the lamb and eat it in the place the LORD your God chooses. Then go back to your tents the next morning.
16.8: For the next six days you may not eat bread made with yeast. On the seventh day the people must assemble before the LORD your God, and no work may be done on that day.
16.9: "Count off seven weeks from the beginning of your grain harvest.
16.10: Then you must celebrate the Festival of Harvest to honor the LORD your God. Bring him a freewill offering in proportion to the blessings you have received from him.
16.11: It is a time to celebrate before the LORD your God at the place he chooses for his name to be honored. Celebrate with your whole family, all your servants, the Levites from your towns, and the foreigners, orphans, and widows who live among you.
16.12: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, so be careful to obey all these laws.
16.13: "Another celebration, the Festival of Shelters, must be observed for seven days at the end of the harvest season, after the grain has been threshed and the grapes have been pressed.
16.14: This festival will be a happy time of rejoicing with your family, your servants, and with the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows from your towns.
16.15: For seven days celebrate this festival to honor the LORD your God at the place he chooses, for it is the LORD your God who gives you bountiful harvests and blesses all your work. This festival will be a time of great joy for all.
16.16: "Each year every man in Israel must celebrate these three festivals: the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Harvest, and the Festival of Shelters. They must appear before the LORD your God at the place he chooses on each of these occasions, and they must bring a gift to the LORD.
16.17: All must give as they are able, according to the blessings given to them by the LORD your God.
16.18: "Appoint judges and officials for each of your tribes in all the towns the LORD your God is giving you. They will judge the people fairly throughout the land.
16.19: You must never twist justice or show partiality. Never accept a bribe, for bribes blind the eyes of the wise and corrupt the decisions of the godly.
16.20: Let true justice prevail, so you may live and occupy the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
16.21: "You must never set up an Asherah pole beside the altar of the LORD your God.
16.22: And never set up sacred pillars for worship, for the LORD your God hates them.

17.1: "Never sacrifice a sick or defective ox or sheep to the LORD your God, for he detests such gifts.
17.2: "Suppose a man or woman among you, in one of your towns that the LORD your God is giving you, has done evil in the sight of the LORD your God and has violated the covenant
17.3: by serving other gods or by worshiping the sun, the moon, or any of the forces of heaven, which I have strictly forbidden.
17.4: When you hear about it, investigate the matter thoroughly. If it is true that this detestable thing has been done in Israel,
17.5: then that man or woman must be taken to the gates of the town and stoned to death.
17.6: But never put a person to death on the testimony of only one witness. There must always be at least two or three witnesses.
17.7: The witnesses must throw the first stones, and then all the people will join in. In this way, you will purge all evil from among you.
17.8: "Suppose a case arises in a local court that is too hard for you to decide--for instance, whether someone is guilty of murder or only of manslaughter, or a difficult lawsuit, or a case involving different kinds of assault. Take such cases to the place the LORD your God will choose,
17.9: where the Levitical priests and the judge on duty will hear the case and decide what to do.
17.10: The decision they make at the place the LORD chooses will always stand. You must do exactly what they say.
17.11: After they have interpreted the law and reached a verdict, the sentence they impose must be fully executed; do not modify it in any way.
17.12: Anyone arrogant enough to reject the verdict of the judge or of the priest who represents the LORD your God must be put to death. Such evil must be purged from Israel.
17.13: Then everyone will hear about it and be afraid to act so arrogantly.
17.14: "You will soon arrive in the land the LORD your God is giving you, and you will conquer it and settle there. Then you may begin to think, `We ought to have a king like the other nations around us.'
17.15: If this happens, be sure that you select as king the man the LORD your God chooses. You must appoint a fellow Israelite, not a foreigner.
17.16: The king must not build up a large stable of horses for himself, and he must never send his people to Egypt to buy horses there, for the LORD has told you, `You must never return to Egypt.'
17.17: The king must not take many wives for himself, because they will lead him away from the LORD. And he must not accumulate vast amounts of wealth in silver and gold for himself.
17.18: "When he sits on the throne as king, he must copy these laws on a scroll for himself in the presence of the Levitical priests.
17.19: He must always keep this copy of the law with him and read it daily as long as he lives. That way he will learn to fear the LORD his God by obeying all the terms of this law.
17.20: This regular reading will prevent him from becoming proud and acting as if he is above his fellow citizens. It will also prevent him from turning away from these commands in the smallest way. This will ensure that he and his descendants will reign for many generations in Israel.

18.1: "Remember that the Levitical priests and the rest of the tribe of Levi will not be given an inheritance of land like the other tribes in Israel. Instead, the priests and Levites will eat from the offerings given to the LORD by fire, for that is their inheritance.
18.2: They will have no inheritance of their own among the Israelites. The LORD himself is their inheritance, just as he promised them.
18.3: "These are the parts the priests may claim as their share from the oxen and sheep that the people bring as offerings: the shoulder, the cheeks, and the stomach.
18.4: You must also give to the priests the first share of the grain, the new wine, the olive oil, and the wool at shearing time.
18.5: For the LORD your God chose the tribe of Levi out of all your tribes to minister in the LORD's name forever.
18.6: "Any Levite who so desires may come from any town in Israel, from wherever he is living, to the place the LORD chooses.
18.7: He may minister there in the name of the LORD his God, just like his fellow Levites who are serving the LORD there.
18.8: He may eat his share of the sacrifices and offerings, even if he has a private source of income.
18.9: "When you arrive in the land the LORD your God is giving you, be very careful not to imitate the detestable customs of the nations living there.
18.10: For example, never sacrifice your son or daughter as a burnt offering. And do not let your people practice fortune-telling or sorcery, or allow them to interpret omens, or engage in witchcraft,
18.11: or cast spells, or function as mediums or psychics, or call forth the spirits of the dead.
18.12: Anyone who does these things is an object of horror and disgust to the LORD. It is because the other nations have done these things that the LORD your God will drive them out ahead of you.
18.13: You must be blameless before the LORD your God.
18.14: The people you are about to displace consult with sorcerers and fortune-tellers, but the LORD your God forbids you to do such things.
18.15: "The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your fellow Israelites, and you must listen to that prophet.
18.16: For this is what you yourselves requested of the LORD your God when you were assembled at Mount Sinai. You begged that you might never again have to listen to the voice of the LORD your God or see this blazing fire for fear you would die.
18.17: "Then the LORD said to me, `Fine, I will do as they have requested.
18.18: I will raise up a prophet like you from among their fellow Israelites. I will tell that prophet what to say, and he will tell the people everything I command him.
18.19: I will personally deal with anyone who will not listen to the messages the prophet proclaims on my behalf.
18.20: But any prophet who claims to give a message from another god or who falsely claims to speak for me must die.'
18.21: You may wonder, `How will we know whether the prophecy is from the LORD or not?'
18.22: If the prophet predicts something in the LORD's name and it does not happen, the LORD did not give the message. That prophet has spoken on his own and need not be feared.

19.1: "The LORD your God will soon destroy the nations whose land he is giving you, and you will displace them and settle in their towns and homes.
19.2: Then you must set apart three cities of refuge in the land the LORD your God is giving you to occupy.
19.3: Divide the land the LORD your God is giving you into three districts, with one of these cities in each district. Keep the roads to these cities in good repair so that anyone who has killed someone can flee there for safety.
19.4: "If someone accidentally kills a neighbor without harboring any previous hatred, the slayer may flee to any of these cities and be safe.
19.5: For example, suppose someone goes into the forest with a neighbor to cut wood. And suppose one of them swings an ax and the ax head flies off the handle, killing the other person. In such cases, the slayer could flee to one of the cities of refuge and be safe.
19.6: If the distance to the nearest city of refuge was too far, an enraged avenger might be able to chase down and kill the person who caused the death. The slayer would die, even though there was no death sentence and the first death had been an accident.
19.7: That is why I am commanding you to set aside three cities of refuge.
19.8: "If the LORD your God enlarges your territory, as he solemnly promised your ancestors, and gives you all the land he promised them,
19.9: you must designate three additional cities of refuge. (He will give you this land if you obey all the commands I have given you--if you always love the LORD your God and walk in his ways.)
19.10: That way you will prevent the death of innocent people in the land the LORD your God is giving you as a special possession, and you will not be held responsible for murder.
19.11: "But suppose someone hates a neighbor and deliberately ambushes and murders that neighbor and then escapes to one of the cities of refuge.
19.12: In that case, the leaders of the murderer's hometown must have the murderer brought back from the city of refuge and handed over to the dead person's avenger to be killed.
19.13: Do not feel sorry for that murderer! Purge the guilt of murder from Israel so all may go well with you.
19.14: "When you arrive in the land the LORD your God is giving you as a special possession, never steal someone's land by moving the boundary markers your ancestors set up to mark their property.
19.15: "Never convict anyone of a crime on the testimony of just one witness. The facts of the case must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
19.16: If a malicious witness comes forward and accuses someone of a crime,
19.17: then both the accuser and accused must appear before the priests and judges who are on duty before the LORD.
19.18: They must be closely questioned, and if the accuser is found to be lying,
19.19: the accuser will receive the punishment intended for the accused. In this way, you will cleanse such evil from among you.
19.20: Those who hear about it will be afraid to do such an evil thing again.
19.21: You must never show pity! Your rule should be life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

20.1: "When you go out to fight your enemies and you face horses and chariots and an army greater than your own, do not be afraid. The LORD your God, who brought you safely out of Egypt, is with you!
20.2: Before you go into battle, the priest will come forward to speak with the troops.
20.3: He will say, `Listen to me, all you men of Israel! Do not be afraid as you go out to fight today! Do not lose heart or panic.
20.4: For the LORD your God is going with you! He will fight for you against your enemies, and he will give you victory!'
20.5: "Then the officers of the army will address the troops and say, `Has anyone just built a new house but not yet dedicated it? If so, go home! You might be killed in the battle, and someone else would dedicate your house!
20.6: Has anyone just planted a vineyard but not yet eaten any of its fruit? If so, go home! You might die in battle, and someone else would eat from it!
20.7: Has anyone just become engaged? Well, go home and get married! You might die in the battle, and someone else would marry your fiance.'
20.8: Then the officers will also say, `Is anyone terrified? If you are, go home before you frighten anyone else.'
20.9: When the officers have finished saying this to their troops, they will announce the names of the unit commanders.
20.10: "As you approach a town to attack it, first offer its people terms for peace.
20.11: If they accept your terms and open the gates to you, then all the people inside will serve you in forced labor.
20.12: But if they refuse to make peace and prepare to fight, you must attack the town.
20.13: When the LORD your God hands it over to you, kill every man in the town.
20.14: But you may keep for yourselves all the women, children, livestock, and other plunder. You may enjoy the spoils of your enemies that the LORD your God has given you.
20.15: But these instructions apply only to distant towns, not to the towns of nations nearby.
20.16: "As for the towns of the nations the LORD your God is giving you as a special possession, destroy every living thing in them.
20.17: You must completely destroy the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, just as the LORD your God has commanded you.
20.18: This will keep the people of the land from teaching you their detestable customs in the worship of their gods, which would cause you to sin deeply against the LORD your God.
20.19: "When you are besieging a town and the war drags on, do not destroy the trees. Eat the fruit, but do not cut down the trees. They are not enemies that need to be attacked!
20.20: But you may cut down trees that you know are not valuable for food. Use them to make the equipment you need to besiege the town until it falls.

21.1: "Suppose someone is found murdered in a field in the land the LORD your God is giving you, and you don't know who committed the murder.
21.2: In such cases, your leaders and judges must determine which town is nearest the body.
21.3: Then the leaders of that town must select a young cow that has never been trained or yoked to a plow.
21.4: They must lead it to a valley that is neither plowed nor planted with a stream running through it. There they must break the cow's neck.
21.5: The Levitical priests must go there also, for the LORD your God has chosen them to minister before him and to pronounce blessings in the LORD's name. And they are to decide all lawsuits and punishments.
21.6: "The leaders of the town nearest the body must wash their hands over the young cow whose neck was broken.
21.7: Then they must say, `Our hands did not shed this blood, nor did we see it happen.
21.8: O LORD, forgive your people Israel whom you have redeemed. Do not charge your people Israel with the guilt of murdering an innocent person.' Then they will be absolved of the guilt of this person's blood.
21.9: By following these instructions and doing what is right in the LORD's sight, you will cleanse the guilt of murder from your community.
21.10: "Suppose you go to war against your enemies and the LORD your God hands them over to you and you take captives.
21.11: And suppose you see among the captives a beautiful woman, and you are attracted to her and want to marry her.
21.12: If this happens, you may take her to your home, where she must shave her head, cut her fingernails,
21.13: and change all her clothes. Then she must remain in your home for a full month, mourning for her father and mother. After that you may marry her.
21.14: But if you marry her and then decide you do not like her, you must let her go free. You may not sell her or treat her as a slave, for you have humiliated her.
21.15: "Suppose a man has two wives, but he loves one and not the other, and both have given him sons. And suppose the firstborn son is the son of the wife he does not love.
21.16: When the man divides the inheritance, he may not give the larger inheritance to his younger son, the son of the wife he loves.
21.17: He must give the customary double portion to his oldest son, who represents the strength of his father's manhood and who owns the rights of the firstborn son, even though he is the son of the wife his father does not love.
21.18: "Suppose a man has a stubborn, rebellious son who will not obey his father or mother, even though they discipline him.
21.19: In such cases, the father and mother must take the son before the leaders of the town.
21.20: They must declare: `This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious and refuses to obey. He is a worthless drunkard.'
21.21: Then all the men of the town must stone him to death. In this way, you will cleanse this evil from among you, and all Israel will hear about it and be afraid.
21.22: "If someone has committed a crime worthy of death and is executed and then hanged on a tree,
21.23: the body must never remain on the tree overnight. You must bury the body that same day, for anyone hanging on a tree is cursed of God. Do not defile the land the LORD your God is giving you as a special possession.

22.1: "If you see your neighbor's ox or sheep wandering away, don't pretend not to see it. Take it back to its owner.
22.2: If it does not belong to someone nearby or you don't know who the owner is, keep it until the owner comes looking for it; then return it.
22.3: Do the same if you find your neighbor's donkey, clothing, or anything else your neighbor loses. Don't pretend you did not see it.
22.4: "If you see your neighbor's ox or donkey lying on the road, do not look the other way. Go and help your neighbor get it to its feet!
22.5: "A woman must not wear men's clothing, and a man must not wear women's clothing. The LORD your God detests people who do this.
22.6: "If you find a bird's nest on the ground or in a tree and there are young ones or eggs in it with the mother sitting in the nest, do not take the mother with the young.
22.7: You may take the young, but let the mother go, so you may prosper and enjoy a long life.
22.8: "Every new house you build must have a barrier around the edge of its flat rooftop. That way you will not bring the guilt of bloodshed on your household if someone falls from the roof.
22.9: "Do not plant any other crop between the rows of your vineyard. If you do, you are forbidden to use either the grapes from the vineyard or the produce of the other crop.
22.10: "Do not plow with an ox and a donkey harnessed together.
22.11: "Do not wear clothing made of wool and linen woven together.
22.12: "You must put tassels on the four corners of your cloaks.
22.13: "Suppose a man marries a woman and, after sleeping with her, changes his mind about her
22.14: and falsely accuses her of having slept with another man. He might say, `I discovered she was not a virgin when I married her.'
22.15: If the man does this, the woman's father and mother must bring the proof of her virginity to the leaders of the town.
22.16: Her father must tell them, `I gave my daughter to this man to be his wife, and now he has turned against her.
22.17: He has accused her of shameful things, claiming that she was not a virgin when he married her. But here is the proof of my daughter's virginity.' Then they must spread the cloth before the judges.
22.18: The judges must then punish the man.
22.19: They will fine him one hundred pieces of silver, for he falsely accused a virgin of Israel. The payment will be made to the woman's father. The woman will then remain the man's wife, and he may never divorce her.
22.20: "But suppose the man's accusations are true, and her virginity could not be proved.
22.21: In such cases, the judges must take the girl to the door of her father's home, and the men of the town will stone her to death. She has committed a disgraceful crime in Israel by being promiscuous while living in her parents' home. Such evil must be cleansed from among you.
22.22: "If a man is discovered committing adultery, both he and the other man's wife must be killed. In this way, the evil will be cleansed from Israel.
22.23: "Suppose a man meets a young woman, a virgin who is engaged to be married, and he has sexual intercourse with her. If this happens within a town,
22.24: you must take both of them to the gates of the town and stone them to death. The woman is guilty because she did not scream for help. The man must die because he violated another man's wife. In this way, you will cleanse the land of evil.
22.25: "But if the man meets the engaged woman out in the country, and he rapes her, then only the man should die.
22.26: Do nothing to the young woman; she has committed no crime worthy of death. This case is similar to that of someone who attacks and murders a neighbor.
22.27: Since the man raped her out in the country, it must be assumed that she screamed, but there was no one to rescue her.
22.28: "If a man is caught in the act of raping a young woman who is not engaged,
22.29: he must pay fifty pieces of silver to her father. Then he must marry the young woman because he violated her, and he will never be allowed to divorce her.
22.30: "A man must not have intercourse with his father's wife, for this would violate his father.

23.1: "If a man's testicles are crushed or his penis is cut off, he may not be included in the assembly of the LORD.
23.2: "Those of illegitimate birth and their descendants for ten generations may not be included in the assembly of the LORD.
23.3: "No Ammonites or Moabites, or any of their descendants for ten generations, may be included in the assembly of the LORD.
23.4: These nations did not welcome you with food and water when you came out of Egypt. Instead, they tried to hire Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Aram-naharaim to curse you.
23.5: (But the LORD your God would not listen to Balaam. He turned the intended curse into a blessing because the LORD your God loves you.)
23.6: You must never, as long as you live, try to help the Ammonites or the Moabites in any way.
23.7: "Do not detest the Edomites or the Egyptians, because the Edomites are your relatives, and you lived as foreigners among the Egyptians.
23.8: The third generation of Egyptians who came with you from Egypt may enter the assembly of the LORD.
23.9: "When you go to war against your enemies, stay away from everything impure.
23.10: "Any man who becomes ceremonially defiled because of a nocturnal emission must leave the camp and stay away all day.
23.11: Toward evening he must bathe himself, and at sunset he may return to the camp.
23.12: "Mark off an area outside the camp for a latrine.
23.13: Each of you must have a spade as part of your equipment. Whenever you relieve yourself, you must dig a hole with the spade and cover the excrement.
23.14: The camp must be holy, for the LORD your God moves around in your camp to protect you and to defeat your enemies. He must not see any shameful thing among you, or he might turn away from you.
23.15: "If slaves should escape from their masters and take refuge with you, do not force them to return.
23.16: Let them live among you in whatever town they choose, and do not oppress them.
23.17: "No Israelite man or woman may ever become a temple prostitute.
23.18: Do not bring to the house of the LORD your God any offering from the earnings of a prostitute, whether a man or a woman, for both are detestable to the LORD your God.
23.19: "Do not charge interest on the loans you make to a fellow Israelite, whether it is money, food, or anything else that may be loaned with interest.
23.20: You may charge interest to foreigners, but not to Israelites, so the LORD your God may bless you in everything you do in the land you are about to enter and occupy.
23.21: "When you make a vow to the LORD your God, be prompt in doing whatever you promised him. For the LORD your God demands that you promptly fulfill all your vows. If you don't, you will be guilty of sin.
23.22: However, it is not a sin to refrain from making a vow.
23.23: But once you have voluntarily made a vow, be careful to do as you have said, for you have made a vow to the LORD your God.
23.24: "You may eat your fill of grapes from your neighbor's vineyard, but do not take any away in a basket.
23.25: And you may pluck a few heads of your neighbor's grain by hand, but you may not harvest it with a sickle.

24.1: "Suppose a man marries a woman but later discovers something about her that is shameful. So he writes her a letter of divorce, gives it to her, and sends her away.
24.2: If she then leaves and marries another man
24.3: and the second husband also divorces her or dies,
24.4: the former husband may not marry her again, for she has been defiled. That would be detestable to the LORD. You must not bring guilt upon the land the LORD your God is giving you as a special possession.
24.5: "A newly married man must not be drafted into the army or given any other special responsibilities. He must be free to be at home for one year, bringing happiness to the wife he has married.
24.6: "It is wrong to take a pair of millstones, or even just the upper millstone, as a pledge, for the owner uses it to make a living.
24.7: "If anyone kidnaps a fellow Israelite and treats him as a slave or sells him, the kidnapper must die. You must cleanse the evil from among you.
24.8: "Watch all contagious skin diseases carefully and follow the instructions of the Levitical priests; obey the commands I have given them.
24.9: Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam as you were coming from Egypt.
24.10: "If you lend anything to your neighbor, do not enter your neighbor's house to claim the security.
24.11: Stand outside and the owner will bring it out to you.
24.12: If your neighbor is poor and has only a cloak to give as security, do not keep the cloak overnight.
24.13: Return the cloak to its owner by sunset so your neighbor can sleep in it and bless you. And the LORD your God will count it as a righteous act.
24.14: "Never take advantage of poor laborers, whether fellow Israelites or foreigners living in your towns.
24.15: Pay them their wages each day before sunset because they are poor and are counting on it. Otherwise they might cry out to the LORD against you, and it would be counted against you as sin.
24.16: "Parents must not be put to death for the sins of their children, nor the children for the sins of their parents. Those worthy of death must be executed for their own crimes.
24.17: "True justice must be given to foreigners living among you and to orphans, and you must never accept a widow's garment in pledge of her debt.
24.18: Always remember that you were slaves in Egypt and that the LORD your God redeemed you. That is why I have given you this command.
24.19: "When you are harvesting your crops and forget to bring in a bundle of grain from your field, don't go back to get it. Leave it for the foreigners, orphans, and widows. Then the LORD your God will bless you in all you do.
24.20: When you beat the olives from your olive trees, don't go over the boughs twice. Leave some of the olives for the foreigners, orphans, and widows.
24.21: This also applies to the grapes in your vineyard. Do not glean the vines after they are picked, but leave any remaining grapes for the foreigners, orphans, and widows.
24.22: Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt. That is why I am giving you this command.

25.1: "Suppose two people take a dispute to court, and the judges declare that one is right and the other is wrong.
25.2: If the person in the wrong is sentenced to be flogged, the judge will command him to lie down and be beaten in his presence with the number of lashes appropriate to the crime.
25.3: No more than forty lashes may ever be given; more than forty lashes would publicly humiliate your neighbor.
25.4: "Do not keep an ox from eating as it treads out the grain.
25.5: "If two brothers are living together on the same property and one of them dies without a son, his widow must not marry outside the family. Instead, her husband's brother must marry her and fulfill the duties of a brother-in-law.
25.6: The first son she bears to him will be counted as the son of the dead brother, so that his name will not be forgotten in Israel.
25.7: But if the dead man's brother refuses to marry the widow, she must go to the town gate and say to the leaders there, `My husband's brother refuses to preserve his brother's name in Israel--he refuses to marry me.'
25.8: The leaders of the town will then summon him and try to reason with him. If he still insists that he doesn't want to marry her,
25.9: the widow must walk over to him in the presence of the leaders, pull his sandal from his foot, and spit in his face. She will then say, `This is what happens to a man who refuses to raise up a son for his brother.'
25.10: Ever afterward his family will be referred to as `the family of the man whose sandal was pulled off'!
25.11: "If two Israelite men are fighting and the wife of one tries to rescue her husband by grabbing the testicles of the other man,
25.12: her hand must be cut off without pity.
25.13: "You must use accurate scales when you weigh out merchandise,
25.14: and you must use full and honest measures.
25.15: Yes, use honest weights and measures, so that you will enjoy a long life in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
25.16: Those who cheat with dishonest weights and measures are detestable to the LORD your God.
25.17: "Never forget what the Amalekites did to you as you came from Egypt.
25.18: They attacked you when you were exhausted and weary, and they struck down those who were lagging behind. They had no fear of God.
25.19: Therefore, when the LORD your God has given you rest from all your enemies in the land he is giving you as a special possession, you are to destroy the Amalekites and erase their memory from under heaven. Never forget this!

26.1: "When you arrive in the land the LORD your God is giving you as a special possession and you have conquered it and settled there,
26.2: put some of the first produce from each harvest into a basket and bring it to the place the LORD your God chooses for his name to be honored.
26.3: Go to the priest in charge at that time and say to him, `With this gift I acknowledge that the LORD your God has brought me into the land he swore to give our ancestors.'
26.4: The priest will then take the basket from your hand and set it before the altar of the LORD your God.
26.5: You must then say in the presence of the LORD your God, `My ancestor Jacob was a wandering Aramean who went to live in Egypt. His family was few in number, but in Egypt they became a mighty and numerous nation.
26.6: When the Egyptians mistreated and humiliated us by making us their slaves,
26.7: we cried out to the LORD, the God of our ancestors. He heard us and saw our hardship, toil, and oppression.
26.8: So the LORD brought us out of Egypt with amazing power, overwhelming terror, and miraculous signs and wonders.
26.9: He brought us to this place and gave us this land flowing with milk and honey!
26.10: And now, O LORD, I have brought you a token of the first crops you have given me from the ground.' Then place the produce before the LORD your God and worship him.
26.11: Afterward go and celebrate because of all the good things the LORD your God has given to you and your household. Remember to include the Levites and the foreigners living among you in the celebration.
26.12: "Every third year you must offer a special tithe of your crops. You must give these tithes to the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows so that they will have enough to eat in your towns.
26.13: Then you must declare in the presence of the LORD your God, `I have taken the sacred gift from my house and have given it to the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows, just as you commanded me. I have not violated or forgotten any of your commands.
26.14: I have not eaten any of it while in mourning; I have not touched it while I was ceremonially unclean; and I have not offered any of it to the dead. I have obeyed the LORD my God and have done everything you commanded me.
26.15: Look down from your holy dwelling place in heaven and bless your people Israel and the land you have given us--a land flowing with milk and honey--just as you solemnly promised our ancestors.'
26.16: "Today the LORD your God has commanded you to obey all these laws and regulations. You must commit yourself to them without reservation.
26.17: You have declared today that the LORD is your God. You have promised to obey his laws, commands, and regulations by walking in his ways and doing everything he tells you.
26.18: The LORD has declared today that you are his people, his own special treasure, just as he promised, and that you must obey all his commands.
26.19: And if you do, he will make you greater than any other nation. Then you will receive praise, honor, and renown. You will be a nation that is holy to the LORD your God, just as he promised."

27.1: Then Moses and the leaders of Israel charged the people as follows: "Keep all these commands that I am giving you today.
27.2: When you cross the Jordan River and enter the land the LORD your God is giving you, set up some large stones and coat them with plaster.
27.3: Then write all the terms of this law on them. I repeat, you will soon cross the river to enter the land the LORD your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, promised you.
27.4: When you cross the Jordan, set up these stones at Mount Ebal and coat them with plaster, as I am commanding you today.
27.5: Then build an altar there to the LORD your God, using natural stones.
27.6: Do not shape the stones with an iron tool. On the altar you must offer burnt offerings to the LORD your God.
27.7: Sacrifice peace offerings on it also, and feast there with great joy before the LORD your God.
27.8: On the stones coated with plaster, you must clearly write all the terms of this law."
27.9: Then Moses and the Levitical priests addressed all Israel as follows: "O Israel, be quiet and listen! Today you have become the people of the LORD your God.
27.10: So obey the LORD your God by keeping all these commands and laws that I am giving you today."
27.11: That same day Moses gave this charge to the people:
27.12: "When you cross the Jordan River, the tribes of Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin must stand on Mount Gerizim to proclaim a blessing over the people.
27.13: And the tribes of Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali must stand on Mount Ebal to proclaim a curse.
27.14: Then the Levites must shout to all the people of Israel:
27.15: `Cursed is anyone who carves or casts idols and secretly sets them up. These idols, the work of craftsmen, are detestable to the LORD.' And all the people will reply, `Amen.'
27.16: `Cursed is anyone who despises father or mother.' And all the people will reply, `Amen.'
27.17: `Cursed is anyone who steals property from a neighbor by moving a boundary marker.' And all the people will reply, `Amen.'
27.18: `Cursed is anyone who leads a blind person astray on the road.' And all the people will reply, `Amen.'
27.19: `Cursed is anyone who is unjust to foreigners, orphans, and widows.' And all the people will reply, `Amen.'
27.20: `Cursed is anyone who has sexual intercourse with his father's wife, for he has violated his father.' And all the people will reply, `Amen.'
27.21: `Cursed is anyone who has sexual intercourse with an animal.' And all the people will reply, `Amen.'
27.22: `Cursed is anyone who has sexual intercourse with his sister, whether she is the daughter of his father or his mother.' And all the people will reply, `Amen.'
27.23: `Cursed is anyone who has sexual intercourse with his mother-in-law.' And all the people will reply, `Amen.'
27.24: `Cursed is anyone who kills another person in secret.' And all the people will reply, `Amen.'
27.25: `Cursed is anyone who accepts payment to kill an innocent person.' And all the people will reply, `Amen.'
27.26: `Cursed is anyone who does not affirm the terms of this law by obeying them.' And all the people will reply, `Amen.'

28.1: "If you fully obey the LORD your God by keeping all the commands I am giving you today, the LORD your God will exalt you above all the nations of the world.
28.2: You will experience all these blessings if you obey the LORD your God:
28.3: You will be blessed in your towns and in the country.
28.4: You will be blessed with many children and productive fields. You will be blessed with fertile herds and flocks.
28.5: You will be blessed with baskets overflowing with fruit, and with kneading bowls filled with bread.
28.6: You will be blessed wherever you go, both in coming and in going.
28.7: "The LORD will conquer your enemies when they attack you. They will attack you from one direction, but they will scatter from you in seven!
28.8: "The LORD will bless everything you do and will fill your storehouses with grain. The LORD your God will bless you in the land he is giving you.
28.9: "If you obey the commands of the LORD your God and walk in his ways, the LORD will establish you as his holy people as he solemnly promised to do.
28.10: Then all the nations of the world will see that you are a people claimed by the LORD, and they will stand in awe of you.
28.11: "The LORD will give you an abundance of good things in the land he swore to give your ancestors--many children, numerous livestock, and abundant crops.
28.12: The LORD will send rain at the proper time from his rich treasury in the heavens to bless all the work you do. You will lend to many nations, but you will never need to borrow from them.
28.13: If you listen to these commands of the LORD your God and carefully obey them, the LORD will make you the head and not the tail, and you will always have the upper hand.
28.14: You must not turn away from any of the commands I am giving you today to follow after other gods and worship them.
28.15: "But if you refuse to listen to the LORD your God and do not obey all the commands and laws I am giving you today, all these curses will come and overwhelm you:
28.16: You will be cursed in your towns and in the country.
28.17: You will be cursed with baskets empty of fruit, and with kneading bowls empty of bread.
28.18: You will be cursed with few children and barren fields. You will be cursed with infertile herds and flocks.
28.19: You will be cursed wherever you go, both in coming and in going.
28.20: "The LORD himself will send against you curses, confusion, and disillusionment in everything you do, until at last you are completely destroyed for doing evil and forsaking me.
28.21: The LORD will send diseases among you until none of you are left in the land you are about to enter and occupy.
28.22: The LORD will strike you with wasting disease, fever, and inflammation, with scorching heat and drought, and with blight and mildew. These devastations will pursue you until you die.
28.23: The skies above will be as unyielding as bronze, and the earth beneath will be as hard as iron.
28.24: The LORD will turn your rain into sand and dust, and it will pour down from the sky until you are destroyed.
28.25: "The LORD will cause you to be defeated by your enemies. You will attack your enemies from one direction, but you will scatter from them in seven! You will be an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
28.26: Your dead bodies will be food for the birds and wild animals, and no one will be there to chase them away.
28.27: "The LORD will afflict you with the boils of Egypt and with tumors, scurvy, and the itch, from which you cannot be cured.
28.28: The LORD will strike you with madness, blindness, and panic.
28.29: You will grope around in broad daylight, just like a blind person groping in the darkness, and you will not succeed at anything you do. You will be oppressed and robbed continually, and no one will come to save you.
28.30: "You will be engaged to a woman, but another man will ravish her. You will build a house, but someone else will live in it. You will plant a vineyard, but you will never enjoy its fruit.
28.31: Your ox will be butchered before your eyes, but you won't get a single bite of the meat. Your donkey will be driven away, never to be returned. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and no one will be there to help you.
28.32: You will watch as your sons and daughters are taken away as slaves. Your heart will break as you long for them, but nothing you do will help.
28.33: A foreign nation you have never heard about will eat the crops you worked so hard to grow. You will suffer under constant oppression and harsh treatment.
28.34: You will go mad because of all the tragedy around you.
28.35: The LORD will cover you from head to foot with incurable boils.
28.36: "The LORD will exile you and the king you crowned to a nation unknown to you and your ancestors. Then in exile you will worship gods of wood and stone!
28.37: You will become an object of horror, a proverb and a mockery among all the nations to which the LORD sends you.
28.38: "You will plant much but harvest little, for locusts will eat your crops.
28.39: You will plant vineyards and care for them, but you will not drink the wine or eat the grapes, for worms will destroy the vines.
28.40: You will grow olive trees throughout your land, but you will never use the olive oil, for the trees will drop the fruit before it is ripe.
28.41: You will have sons and daughters, but you will not keep them, for they will be led away into captivity.
28.42: Swarms of insects will destroy your trees and crops.
28.43: The foreigners living among you will become stronger and stronger, while you become weaker and weaker.
28.44: They will lend money to you, not you to them. They will be the head, and you will be the tail!
28.45: "If you refuse to listen to the LORD your God and to obey the commands and laws he has given you, all these curses will pursue and overtake you until you are destroyed.
28.46: These horrors will serve as a sign and warning among you and your descendants forever.
28.47: Because you have not served the LORD your God with joy and enthusiasm for the abundant benefits you have received,
28.48: you will serve your enemies whom the LORD will send against you. You will be left hungry, thirsty, naked, and lacking in everything. They will oppress you harshly until you are destroyed.
28.49: "The LORD will bring a distant nation against you from the end of the earth, and it will swoop down on you like an eagle. It is a nation whose language you do not understand,
28.50: a fierce and heartless nation that shows no respect for the old and no pity for the young.
28.51: Its armies will devour your livestock and crops, and you will starve to death. They will leave you no grain, new wine, olive oil, calves, or lambs, bringing about your destruction.
28.52: They will lay siege to your cities until all the fortified walls in your land--the walls you trusted to protect you--are knocked down. They will attack all the towns in the land the LORD your God has given you.
28.53: The siege will be so severe that you will eat the flesh of your own sons and daughters, whom the LORD your God has given you.
28.54: The most tenderhearted man among you will have no compassion for his own brother, his beloved wife, and his surviving children.
28.55: He will refuse to give them a share of the flesh he is devouring--the flesh of one of his own children--because he has nothing else to eat during the siege that your enemy will inflict on all your towns.
28.56: The most tender and delicate woman among you--so delicate she would not so much as touch her feet to the ground--will be cruel to the husband she loves and to her own son or daughter.
28.57: She will hide from them the afterbirth and the new baby she has borne, so that she herself can secretly eat them. She will have nothing else to eat during the siege and terrible distress that your enemy will inflict on all your towns.
28.58: "If you refuse to obey all the terms of this law that are written in this book, and if you do not fear the glorious and awesome name of the LORD your God,
28.59: then the LORD will overwhelm both you and your children with indescribable plagues. These plagues will be intense and without relief, making you miserable and unbearably sick.
28.60: He will bring against you all the diseases of Egypt that you feared so much, and they will claim you.
28.61: The LORD will bring against you every sickness and plague there is, even those not mentioned in this Book of the Law, until you are destroyed.
28.62: Though you are as numerous as the stars in the sky, few of you will be left because you would not listen to the LORD your God.
28.63: "Just as the LORD has found great pleasure in helping you to prosper and multiply, the LORD will find pleasure in destroying you, until you disappear from the land you are about to enter and occupy.
28.64: For the LORD will scatter you among all the nations from one end of the earth to the other. There you will worship foreign gods that neither you nor your ancestors have known, gods made of wood and stone!
28.65: There among those nations you will find no place of security and rest. And the LORD will cause your heart to tremble, your eyesight to fail, and your soul to despair.
28.66: Your lives will hang in doubt. You will live night and day in fear, with no reason to believe that you will see the morning light.
28.67: In the morning you will say, `If only it were night!' And in the evening you will say, `If only it were morning!' You will say this because of your terror at the awesome horrors you see around you.
28.68: Then the LORD will send you back to Egypt in ships, a journey I promised you would never again make. There you will offer to sell yourselves to your enemies as slaves, but no one will want to buy you."

29.1: These are the terms of the covenant the LORD commanded Moses to make with the Israelites while they were in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant he had made with them at Mount Sinai.
29.2: Moses summoned all the Israelites and said to them, "You have seen with your own eyes everything the LORD did in Egypt to Pharaoh and all his servants and his whole country--
29.3: all the great tests of strength, the miraculous signs, and the amazing wonders.
29.4: But to this day the LORD has not given you minds that understand, nor eyes that see, nor ears that hear!
29.5: For forty years I led you through the wilderness, yet your clothes and sandals did not wear out.
29.6: You had no bread or wine or other strong drink, but he gave you food so you would know that he is the LORD your God.
29.7: When we came here, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan came out to fight against us, but we defeated them.
29.8: We took their land and gave it to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and to the half-tribe of Manasseh as their inheritance.
29.9: "Therefore, obey the terms of this covenant so that you will prosper in everything you do.
29.10: All of you--your tribal leaders, your judges, your officers, all the men of Israel--are standing today before the LORD your God.
29.11: With you are your little ones, your wives, and the foreigners living among you who chop your wood and carry your water.
29.12: You are standing here today to enter into a covenant with the LORD your God. The LORD is making this covenant with you today, and he has sealed it with an oath.
29.13: He wants to confirm you today as his people and to confirm that he is your God, just as he promised you, and as he swore to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
29.14: But you are not the only ones with whom the LORD is making this covenant with its obligations.
29.15: The LORD your God is making this covenant with you who stand in his presence today and also with all future generations of Israel.
29.16: "Surely you remember how we lived in the land of Egypt and how we traveled through the lands of enemy nations as we left.
29.17: You have seen their detestable idols made of wood, stone, silver, and gold.
29.18: The LORD made this covenant with you so that no man, woman, family, or tribe among you would turn away from the LORD our God to worship these gods of other nations, and so that no root among you would bear bitter and poisonous fruit.
29.19: Let none of those who hear the warnings of this curse consider themselves immune, thinking, `I am safe, even though I am walking in my own stubborn way.' This would lead to utter ruin!
29.20: The LORD will not pardon such people. His anger and jealousy will burn against them. All the curses written in this book will come down on them, and the LORD will erase their names from under heaven.
29.21: The LORD will separate them from all the tribes of Israel, to pour out on them all the covenant curses recorded in this Book of the Law.
29.22: "Then the generations to come, both your own descendants and the foreigners who come from distant lands, will see the devastation of the land and the diseases the LORD will send against it.
29.23: They will find its soil turned into sulfur and salt, with nothing planted and nothing growing, not even a blade of grass. It will be just like Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the LORD destroyed in his anger.
29.24: The surrounding nations will ask, `Why has the LORD done this to his land? Why was he so angry?'
29.25: "And they will be told, `This happened because the people of the land broke the covenant they made with the LORD, the God of their ancestors, when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.
29.26: They turned to serve and worship other gods that were foreign to them, gods that the LORD had not designated for them.
29.27: That is why the LORD's anger burned against this land, bringing down on it all the curses recorded in this book.
29.28: In great anger and fury the LORD uprooted his people from their land and exiled them to another land, where they still live today!'
29.29: "There are secret things that belong to the LORD our God, but the revealed things belong to us and our descendants forever, so that we may obey these words of the law.

30.1: "Suppose all these things happen to you--the blessings and the curses I have listed--and you meditate on them as you are living among the nations to which the LORD your God has exiled you.
30.2: If at that time you return to the LORD your God, and you and your children begin wholeheartedly to obey all the commands I have given you today,
30.3: then the LORD your God will restore your fortunes. He will have mercy on you and gather you back from all the nations where he has scattered you.
30.4: Though you are at the ends of the earth, the LORD your God will go and find you and bring you back again.
30.5: He will return you to the land that belonged to your ancestors, and you will possess that land again. He will make you even more prosperous and numerous than your ancestors!
30.6: "The LORD your God will cleanse your heart and the hearts of all your descendants so that you will love him with all your heart and soul, and so you may live!
30.7: The LORD your God will inflict all these curses on your enemies and persecutors.
30.8: Then you will again obey the LORD and keep all the commands I am giving you today.
30.9: The LORD your God will make you successful in everything you do. He will give you many children and numerous livestock, and your fields will produce abundant harvests, for the LORD will delight in being good to you as he was to your ancestors.
30.10: The LORD your God will delight in you if you obey his voice and keep the commands and laws written in this Book of the Law, and if you turn to the LORD your God with all your heart and soul.
30.11: "This command I am giving you today is not too difficult for you to understand or perform.
30.12: It is not up in heaven, so distant that you must ask, `Who will go to heaven and bring it down so we can hear and obey it?'
30.13: It is not beyond the sea, so far away that you must ask, `Who will cross the sea to bring it to us so we can hear and obey it?'
30.14: The message is very close at hand; it is on your lips and in your heart so that you can obey it.
30.15: "Now listen! Today I am giving you a choice between prosperity and disaster, between life and death.
30.16: I have commanded you today to love the LORD your God and to keep his commands, laws, and regulations by walking in his ways. If you do this, you will live and become a great nation, and the LORD your God will bless you and the land you are about to enter and occupy.
30.17: But if your heart turns away and you refuse to listen, and if you are drawn away to serve and worship other gods,
30.18: then I warn you now that you will certainly be destroyed. You will not live a long, good life in the land you are crossing the Jordan to occupy.
30.19: "Today I have given you the choice between life and death, between blessings and curses. I call on heaven and earth to witness the choice you make. Oh, that you would choose life, that you and your descendants might live!
30.20: Choose to love the LORD your God and to obey him and commit yourself to him, for he is your life. Then you will live long in the land the LORD swore to give your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob."

31.1: When Moses had finished saying these things to all the people of Israel,
31.2: he said, "I am now 120 years old and am no longer able to lead you. The LORD has told me that I will not cross the Jordan River.
31.3: But the LORD your God himself will cross over ahead of you. He will destroy the nations living there, and you will take possession of their land. Joshua is your new leader, and he will go with you, just as the LORD promised.
31.4: The LORD will destroy the nations living in the land, just as he destroyed Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites.
31.5: The LORD will hand over to you the people who live there, and you will deal with them as I have commanded you.
31.6: Be strong and courageous! Do not be afraid of them! The LORD your God will go ahead of you. He will neither fail you nor forsake you."
31.7: Then Moses called for Joshua, and as all Israel watched he said to him, "Be strong and courageous! For you will lead these people into the land that the LORD swore to give their ancestors. You are the one who will deliver it to them as their inheritance.
31.8: Do not be afraid or discouraged, for the LORD is the one who goes before you. He will be with you; he will neither fail you nor forsake you."
31.9: So Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, who carried the Ark of the LORD's covenant, and to the leaders of Israel.
31.10: Then Moses gave them this command: "At the end of every seventh year, the Year of Release, during the Festival of Shelters,
31.11: you must read this law to all the people of Israel when they assemble before the LORD your God at the place he chooses.
31.12: Call them all together--men, women, children, and the foreigners living in your towns--so they may listen and learn to fear the LORD your God and carefully obey all the terms of this law.
31.13: Do this so that your children who have not known these laws will hear them and will learn to fear the LORD your God. Do this as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to occupy."
31.14: Then the LORD said to Moses, "The time has come for you to die. Call Joshua and take him with you to the Tabernacle, and I will commission him there." So Moses and Joshua went and presented themselves at the Tabernacle.
31.15: And the LORD appeared to them in a pillar of cloud at the entrance to the sacred tent.
31.16: The LORD said to Moses, "You are about to die and join your ancestors. After you are gone, these people will begin worshiping foreign gods, the gods of the land where they are going. They will abandon me and break the covenant I have made with them.
31.17: Then my anger will blaze forth against them. I will abandon them, hiding my face from them, and they will be destroyed. Terrible trouble will come down on them, so that they will say, `These disasters have come because God is no longer among us!'
31.18: At that time I will hide my face from them on account of all the sins they have committed by worshiping other gods.
31.19: "Now write down the words of this song, and teach it to the people of Israel. Teach them to sing it, so it may serve as a witness against them.
31.20: For I will bring them into the land I swore to give their ancestors--a land flowing with milk and honey. There they will become prosperous; they will eat all the food they want and become well nourished. Then they will begin to worship other gods; they will despise me and break my covenant.
31.21: Then great disasters will come down on them, and this song will stand as evidence against them, for it will never be forgotten by their descendants. I know what these people are like, even before they have entered the land I swore to give them."
31.22: So that very day Moses wrote down the words of the song and taught it to the Israelites.
31.23: Then the LORD commissioned Joshua son of Nun with these words: "Be strong and courageous! You must bring the people of Israel into the land I swore to give them. I will be with you."
31.24: When Moses had finished writing down this entire body of law in a book,
31.25: he gave these instructions to the Levites who carried the Ark of the LORD's covenant:
31.26: "Take this Book of the Law and place it beside the Ark of the Covenant of the LORD your God, so it may serve as a witness against the people of Israel.
31.27: For I know how rebellious and stubborn you are. Even now, while I am still with you, you have rebelled against the LORD. How much more rebellious will you be after my death!
31.28: Now summon all the leaders and officials of your tribes so that I can speak to them and call heaven and earth to witness against them.
31.29: I know that after my death you will become utterly corrupt and will turn from the path I have commanded you to follow. In the days to come, disaster will come down on you, for you will make the LORD very angry by doing what is evil in his sight."
31.30: So Moses recited this entire song to the assembly of Israel:

32.1: 1 "Listen, O heavens, and I will speak! Hear, O earth, the words that I say!
32.2: My teaching will fall on you like rain; my speech will settle like dew. My words will fall like rain on tender grass, like gentle showers on young plants.
32.3: I will proclaim the name of the LORD; how glorious is our God!
32.4: He is the Rock; his work is perfect. Everything he does is just and fair. He is a faithful God who does no wrong; how just and upright he is!
32.5: "But they have acted corruptly toward him; when they act like that, are they really his children? They are a deceitful and twisted generation.
32.6: Is this the way you repay the LORD, you foolish and senseless people? Isn't he your Father who created you? Has he not made you and established you?
32.7: Remember the days of long ago; think about the generations past. Ask your father and he will inform you. Inquire of your elders, and they will tell you.
32.8: When the Most High assigned lands to the nations, when he divided up the human race, he established the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of angelic beings.
32.9: For the people of Israel belong to the LORD; Jacob is his special possession.
32.10: "He found them in a desert land, in an empty, howling wasteland. He surrounded them and watched over them; he guarded them as his most precious possession.
32.11: Like an eagle that rouses her chicks and hovers over her young, so he spread his wings to take them in and carried them aloft on his pinions.
32.12: The LORD alone guided them; they lived without any foreign gods.
32.13: He made them ride over the highlands; he let them feast on the crops of the fields. He nourished them with honey from the cliffs, with olive oil from the hard rock.
32.14: He fed them curds from the herd and milk from the flock, together with the fat of lambs and goats. He gave them choice rams and goats from Bashan, together with the choicest wheat. You drank the finest wine, made from the juice of grapes.
32.15: But Israel soon became fat and unruly; the people grew heavy, plump, and stuffed! Then they abandoned the God who had made them; they made light of the Rock of their salvation.
32.16: They stirred up his jealousy by worshiping foreign gods; they provoked his fury with detestable acts.
32.17: They offered sacrifices to demons, non-gods, to gods they had not known before, to gods only recently arrived, to gods their ancestors had never feared.
32.18: You neglected the Rock who had fathered you; you forgot the God who had given you birth.
32.19: "The LORD saw this and was filled with loathing. He was provoked to anger by his own sons and daughters.
32.20: He said, `I will abandon them; I will see to their end! For they are a twisted generation, children without integrity.
32.21: They have roused my jealousy by worshiping non-gods; they have provoked my fury with useless idols. Now I will rouse their jealousy by blessing other nations; I will provoke their fury by blessing the foolish Gentiles.
32.22: For my anger blazes forth like fire and burns to the depths of the grave. It devours the earth and all its crops and ignites the foundations of the mountains.
32.23: I will heap disasters upon them and shoot them down with my arrows.
32.24: I will send against them wasting famine, burning fever, and deadly disease. They will be troubled by the fangs of wild beasts, by poisonous snakes that glide in the dust.
32.25: Outside, the sword will bring death, and inside, terror will strike both young men and young women, both infants and the aged.
32.26: I decided to scatter them, so even the memory of them would disappear.
32.27: But I feared the taunt of the enemy, that their adversaries might misunderstand and say, "Our power has triumphed! It was not the LORD who did this!"'
32.28: "Israel is a nation that lacks sense; the people are foolish, without understanding.
32.29: Oh, that they were wise and could understand this! Oh, that they might know their fate!
32.30: How could one person chase a thousand of them, and two people put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them, unless the LORD had given them up?
32.31: But the rock of our enemies is not like our Rock, as even they recognize.
32.32: Their vine grows from the vine of Sodom, from the vineyards of Gomorrah. Their grapes are poison, and their clusters are bitter.
32.33: Their wine is the venom of snakes, the deadly poison of vipers.
32.34: "`I am storing up these things, sealing them away within my treasury.
32.35: I will take vengeance; I will repay those who deserve it. In due time their feet will slip. Their day of disaster will arrive, and their destiny will overtake them.'
32.36: "Indeed, the LORD will judge his people, and he will change his mind about his servants, when he sees their strength is gone and no one is left, slave or free.
32.37: Then he will ask, `Where are their gods, the rocks they fled to for refuge?
32.38: Where now are those gods, who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their offerings? Let those gods arise and help you! Let them provide you with shelter!
32.39: Look now; I myself am he! There is no god other than me! I am the one who kills and gives life; I am the one who wounds and heals; no one delivers from my power!
32.40: Now I raise my hand to heaven and declare, "As surely as I live,
32.41: when I sharpen my flashing sword and begin to carry out justice, I will bring vengeance on my enemies and repay those who hate me.
32.42: I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will devour flesh--the blood of the slaughtered and the captives, and the heads of the enemy leaders."'
32.43: "Rejoice with him, O heavens, and let all the angels of God worship him, for he will avenge the blood of his servants. He will take vengeance on his enemies and cleanse his land and his people."
32.44: So Moses came with Joshua son of Nun and recited all the words of this song to the people.
32.45: When Moses had finished reciting these words to Israel,
32.46: he added: "Take to heart all the words I have given you today. Pass them on as a command to your children so they will obey every word of this law.
32.47: These instructions are not mere words--they are your life! By obeying them you will enjoy a long life in the land you are crossing the Jordan River to occupy."
32.48: That same day the LORD said to Moses,
32.49: "Go to Moab, to the mountains east of the river, and climb Mount Nebo, which is across from Jericho. Look out across the land of Canaan, the land I am giving to the people of Israel as their own possession.
32.50: Then you must die there on the mountain and join your ancestors, just as Aaron, your brother, died on Mount Hor and joined his ancestors.
32.51: For both of you broke faith with me among the Israelites at the waters of Meribah at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin. You failed to demonstrate my holiness to the people of Israel there.
32.52: So you will see the land from a distance, but you may not enter the land I am giving to the people of Israel."

33.1: This is the blessing that Moses, the man of God, gave to the people of Israel before his death:
33.2: "The LORD came from Mount Sinai and dawned upon us from Mount Seir; he shone forth from Mount Paran and came from Meribah-kadesh with flaming fire at his right hand.
33.3: Indeed, you love the people; all your holy ones are in your hands. They follow in your steps and accept your instruction.
33.4: Moses charged us with the law, the special possession of the assembly of Israel.
33.5: The LORD became king in Israel--when the leaders of the people assembled, when the tribes of Israel gathered."
33.6: Moses said this about the tribe of Reuben: "Let the tribe of Reuben live and not die out, even though their tribe is small."
33.7: Moses said this about the tribe of Judah: "O LORD, hear the cry of Judah and bring them again to their people. Give them strength to defend their cause; help them against their enemies!"
33.8: Moses said this about the tribe of Levi: "O LORD, you have given the sacred lots to your faithful servants the Levites. You put them to the test at Massah and contended with them at the waters of Meribah.
33.9: The Levites obeyed your word and guarded your covenant. They were more loyal to you than to their parents, relatives, and children.
33.10: Now let them teach your regulations to Jacob; let them give your instructions to Israel. They will present incense before you and offer whole burnt offerings on the altar.
33.11: Bless the Levites, O LORD, and accept all their work. Crush the loins of their enemies; strike down their foes so they never rise again."
33.12: Moses said this about the tribe of Benjamin: "The people of Benjamin are loved by the LORD and live in safety beside him. He surrounds them continuously and preserves them from every harm."
33.13: Moses said this about the tribes of Joseph: "May their land be blessed by the LORD with the choice gift of rain from the heavens, and water from beneath the earth;
33.14: with the riches that grow in the sun, and the bounty produced each month;
33.15: with the finest crops of the ancient mountains, and the abundance from the everlasting hills;
33.16: with the best gifts of the earth and its fullness, and the favor of the one who appeared in the burning bush. May these blessings rest on Joseph's head, crowning the brow of the prince among his brothers.
33.17: Joseph has the strength and majesty of a young bull; his power is like the horns of a wild ox. He will gore distant nations, driving them to the ends of the earth. This is my blessing for the multitudes of Ephraim and the thousands of Manasseh."
33.18: Moses said this about the tribes of Zebulun and Issachar: "May the people of Zebulun prosper in their expeditions abroad. May the people of Issachar prosper at home in their tents.
33.19: They summon the people to the mountain to offer proper sacrifices there. They benefit from the riches of the sea and the hidden treasures of the sand."
33.20: Moses said this about the tribe of Gad: "Blessed is the one who enlarges Gad's territory! Gad is poised there like a lion to tear off an arm or a head.
33.21: The people of Gad took the best land for themselves; a leader's share was assigned to them. When the leaders of the people were assembled, they carried out the LORD's justice and obeyed his regulations for Israel."
33.22: Moses said this about the tribe of Dan: "Dan is a lion's cub, leaping out from Bashan."
33.23: Moses said this about the tribe of Naphtali: "O Naphtali, you are rich in favor and full of the LORD's blessings; may you possess the west and the south."
33.24: Moses said this about the tribe of Asher: "May Asher be blessed above other sons; may he be esteemed by his brothers; may he bathe his feet in olive oil.
33.25: May the bolts of your gates be of iron and bronze; may your strength match the length of your days!"
33.26: "There is no one like the God of Israel. He rides across the heavens to help you, across the skies in majestic splendor.
33.27: The eternal God is your refuge, and his everlasting arms are under you. He thrusts out the enemy before you; it is he who cries, `Destroy them!'
33.28: So Israel will live in safety, prosperous Jacob in security, in a land of grain and wine, while the heavens drop down dew.
33.29: How blessed you are, O Israel! Who else is like you, a people saved by the LORD? He is your protecting shield and your triumphant sword! Your enemies will bow low before you, and you will trample on their backs!"

34.1: Then Moses went to Mount Nebo from the plains of Moab and climbed Pisgah Peak, which is across from Jericho. And the LORD showed him the whole land, from Gilead as far as Dan;
34.2: all the land of Naphtali; the land of Ephraim and Manasseh; all the land of Judah, extending to the Mediterranean Sea;
34.3: the Negev; the Jordan Valley with Jericho--the city of palms--as far as Zoar.
34.4: Then the LORD said to Moses, "This is the land I promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and I told them I would give it to their descendants. I have now allowed you to see it, but you will not enter the land."
34.5: So Moses, the servant of the LORD, died there in the land of Moab, just as the LORD had said.
34.6: He was buried in a valley near Beth-peor in Moab, but to this day no one knows the exact place.
34.7: Moses was 120 years old when he died, yet his eyesight was clear, and he was as strong as ever.
34.8: The people of Israel mourned thirty days for Moses on the plains of Moab, until the customary period of mourning was over.
34.9: Now Joshua son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him. So the people of Israel obeyed him and did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
34.10: There has never been another prophet like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face.
34.11: The LORD sent Moses to perform all the miraculous signs and wonders in the land of Egypt against Pharaoh, all his servants, and his entire land.
34.12: And it was through Moses that the LORD demonstrated his mighty power and terrifying acts in the sight of all Israel.

1.1: And after Moses, Yahweh ’s servant, died, Yahweh spoke to Joshua son of Nun, Moses’ faithful assistant, and said,
1.2: “My servant Moses is dead. Now get up! Prepare to cross the Jordan River, you and all the people. Lead them into the land that I am giving to the Israelites.
1.3: Every part of the land where you march I will give you, as I promised Moses.
1.4: Your borders will extend from the southern desert to the northern mountains of Lebanon, and from the great river Euphrates in the east, to the Mediterranean in the west—including all the land of the Hittites.
1.5: Joshua, no one will be able to defeat you for the rest of your life! I will be with you as I was with Moses, and I will never fail nor abandon you.
