2.2: It will be a day of darkness and gloom, a black and cloudy day. As the dawning light spreads across the mountains, so will a great and powerful people advance, an army such as has never been seen before and such as will never be seen again, not even in all the ages to come.
2.3: Fire blazes before them, and behind them the flame consumes. Before their eyes, the earth is like the garden of Eden, and behind them they leave a devastated wilderness. Nothing escapes them unscathed.
2.4: Their appearance is like horses prepared for battle; like war horses, they charge ahead.
2.5: They rumble like war chariots; they leap over the mountaintops. They devour the land, with the sound of a wildfire devouring stubble. They are a mighty people who are prepared for the battle.
2.6: At the sight of this army, nations panic, all their faces grow pale.
2.7: They press forward like mighty warriors, and scale walls like elite soldiers, each marching straight ahead, not swerving from his path.
2.8: They never jostle each other, for each one stays on his own path. They storm the city and burst through its defenses. Together they are unstoppable.
2.9: They rush against the city and scale its walls. They climb up into the houses and enter through the windows like thieves.
2.10: As that army advances, the earth shakes, and the heavens tremble. The sun and moon grow dark, and the stars no longer shine.
2.11: Yahweh ’s voice thunders as he leads his valiant troops. Numberless are the mighty ones who obey his commands. Yes, the day of Yahweh is great and astonishing! Who can withstand it?
2.12: “But it’s not too late,” declares Yahweh. “Come back to me now with all your heart, with fasting, weeping, and mourning.
2.13: Tearing your clothes in sorrow is not enough— tear open your hearts!” Come back to Yahweh your God, for he is gracious to welcome you home and compassionate to embrace you. Yahweh is slow to anger and so rich in extravagant love for you. He is always ready to forgive and cancel judgment.
2.14: Who knows if he will not turn around and show pity, leaving behind a blessing. Then you can bring offerings of grain and wine to be presented to Yahweh your God.
2.15: Blow the shofar in Zion! Call for a fast and proclaim a solemn assembly.
2.16: Gather the people together, and prepare them for a sacred meeting. From the oldest to the youngest, assemble the community, even the nursing infants. Let the newly wedded bride and bridegroom come from their chamber.
2.17: With everyone gathered in the courtyard, the priests, the ministers of Yahweh, must stand weeping between the portico and the altar of burnt offering. Let them face the sanctuary and intercede, saying, “Spare your people! Have pity, Yahweh! Do not expose your very own people to the contempt and sarcasm of the nations. Why give the nations cause to say, ‘Where is their God now?’ ”
2.18: Then Yahweh showed his great love for the land and showered compassion upon his people.
2.19: Yahweh answered their cry and said, “Behold, now your fast is over. I am providing you with plenty of wheat, wine, and olive oil until you are satisfied. Never again will I make you an object of scorn among the nations.
2.20: I will remove your northern enemy far from you and drive him into a dry, desolate land, with his front ranks to the Dead Sea and his rear guard to the Mediterranean Sea. I will destroy them for their boastful deeds, and people will smell the stench of their dead bodies.” Truly, he has done great things!
2.21: My land, do not fear, for your restoration has come! Be glad and rejoice, you people, for Yahweh has done marvelous things for you.
2.22: Animals of the field, do not be afraid, for the pastures of the wilderness are green again, the trees bear their fruit, and the vine and fig tree yield their richness.
2.23: Children of Zion, be glad! Celebrate the mighty acts of Yahweh your God, for he has given you a teacher of righteousness whose teaching is like the refreshing spring rains. And he will pour down the rains for you, the spring and autumn rains as before.
2.24: “The threshing floors will be full of grain, the pits beside the presses will overflow with new wine and fresh oil.
2.25: I will make up for the years the swarms of locusts ruined your harvest— the hopping-locusts, the destroying-locusts, and the cutting-locusts— my great army that I sent against you.
2.26: You will eat to your heart’s content and be satisfied. You will gloriously praise the name of Yahweh your God, who has treated you so wonderfully. And never will my people be despised again.
2.27: Then, Israel, you will know without question that I am dwelling among you. I am Yahweh your God, and no one else. I say again: no more will I surrender my people to shame.”
2.28: “Then afterward, I will pour out my Spirit on everyone. Your sons and your daughters will boldly prophesy, your elderly will have supernatural dreams, and your youth will experience ecstatic visions.
2.29: And I will even pour out my Spirit in those days upon every servant, both male and female.
2.30: “And I will display amazing wonders in the heavens and on the earth, blood and fire and columns of smoke.
2.31: The sun will be darkened, and the moon will appear as red as blood. These events will occur before the great and awesome day of Yahweh comes.
2.32: And everyone who sincerely worships Yahweh will be saved. For in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be a remnant who are spared, as I, Yahweh, have promised. They will be the chosen survivors whom I, Yahweh, will call.”

3.1: “Behold! In those days, when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,
3.2: I will gather all the nations together. I will bring them to the Valley of Yahweh ’s Judgment. I will take them to court there for all they have done against Israel— my people and my inheritance. I will execute judgment upon them because they have scattered my people among the nations and divided my land among themselves.
3.3: They cast lots for my people and sold them into slavery. They traded a boy to pay for a prostitute and trafficked a girl for a drink of wine.
3.4: And what have you done to me, Tyre and Sidon and all you regions of Philistia? Are you trying to take revenge on me? If you are, I will swiftly and speedily pay you back and return your revenge so that it lands squarely on your own heads.
3.5: For you have stolen my silver and gold and carried off my valuable treasures into your temples.
3.6: You have sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks to be taken as slaves far from their homeland.
3.7: Behold! I will rouse them to return and come back from the places to which you have sold them. I will do to you the very thing that you have done to them.
3.8: Your sons and daughters will be sold as slaves to the sons of Judah, who in turn will sell them to the Sabaeans, who live in a distant land. I, Yahweh, have spoken!”
3.9: Proclaim this message among the nations: “Prepare for war!” Awaken the champions! Let all you soldiers gather, advance, and march.
3.10: Hammer your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears. Let the weakling say, “I am a champion!”
3.11: Hurry and join the battle, all you surrounding nations. Come and assemble there. Yahweh, send down your champions, your warring angels!
3.12: “Let the nations stir themselves up and march to the Valley of Yahweh ’s Judgment. There I will sit in judgment on all the surrounding nations.
3.13: “Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe for judgment. Come and tread the grapes of wrath. The winepress is full and the vats are overflowing for their wickedness is so great!”
3.14: Multitudes! So many multitudes in the Valley of Decision! For the day of Yahweh is near in the Valley of the Verdict.
3.15: The sun and moon grow dark, and the stars no longer shine.
3.16: Yahweh roars from Zion, and his voice thunders from Jerusalem; heaven and earth tremble. But Yahweh will be a shelter for his people, a faithful fortress for Israel.
3.17: “Then you will know that I am Yahweh your God, who dwells in Zion, my holy mountain. Jerusalem will be a sanctuary, and foreigners will never conquer it again.
3.18: A time is coming when the mountains will drip with new wine and the hills will flow with milk, and all the arid streambeds of Judah will run with water year-round. A fountain will spring from Yahweh ’s temple and descend to the valley of acacia trees.
3.19: “Egypt will become a desert and Edom a desolate wilderness because of the atrocious acts of violence they committed against the people of Judah, whose innocent blood they shed in their land.
3.20: I will avenge their blood and not spare the guilty, but Judah will be inhabited forever, Jerusalem from generation to generation, and Yahweh will dwell in Zion.”
3.21: I will pardon my people's crimes, which I have not yet pardoned; and I, the LORD, will make my home in Jerusalem with my people."

1.1: There was a prophet named Amos, a herdsman from the town of Tekoa. Two years before the great earthquake, when Uzziah was king of Judah, and Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel, God revealed these prophetic visions to Amos about Israel.
1.2: Amos said: “ Yahweh comes roaring out of Zion; from Jerusalem he comes with his thunderous voice. The shepherds’ lush pastures are dried up, and the trees on top of Mount Carmel wither.”
1.3: Here is the message of Yahweh: “For the three terrible crimes of the people of Damascus— no, make that four — I will not turn back my wrath. For they have treated the people of Gilead with savage cruelty, running over them with a threshing sledge equipped with iron teeth.
1.4: So I will send fire down on the dynasty of Hazael to devour the royal palaces defended by Ben-Hadad.
1.5: I will smash the city gates of Damascus, I will cut down the ruler who sits in the Valley of Wickedness, the one who holds the royal scepter in the Paradise of Pleasure. And the people of Syria will go back to where they came from—to Kir,” declares Yahweh.
1.6: Here is the message of Yahweh: “For the three terrible crimes of the people of Gaza— no, make that four— I will not turn back my wrath. They have deported an entire community of exiles as slaves to Edom.
1.7: I will send fire down on the walls of Gaza to consume its fortresses.
1.8: I will cut off the ruler of Ashdod and the one who holds the scepter in Ashkelon. I will strike my blows against the city of Ekron, and what’s left of the Philistines will perish,” says the Lord Yahweh.
1.9: Yahweh says this: “For the three terrible crimes of the people of Tyre— no, make that four— I will not turn back my wrath. For they deported entire people groups into exile in the land of Edom. In so doing, they broke the covenant of brotherhood.
1.10: So I will send fire down on the city walls of Tyre to devour her fortresses.”
1.11: Yahweh says this: “For the three terrible crimes of the Edomites— no, make that four— I will not turn back my wrath. For Edom hunted down his relatives, the Israelites, with the sword, and he refused to show mercy. His anger never died down, and his rage continued to the end.
1.12: I will set the city of Teman on fire to burn up the fortresses of Bozrah.”
1.13: Yahweh says this: “For the three terrible crimes of the Ammonites— no, make that four— I will not turn back my wrath. In order to seize more land for themselves, they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead.
1.14: Therefore I will burn down the city walls of Rabbah to consume its fortresses. War cries will be heard on the day of battle; like a whirlwind, war will ravage the land.
1.15: Ammon’s king will be taken into captivity, he and his officials with him,” says Yahweh.

2.1: Yahweh says this: “For the three terrible crimes of the Moabites— no, make that four— I will not turn back my wrath. They burned the bones of the king of Edom to lime.
2.2: So I will send fire down into Moab to devour the fortresses of Kerioth. Moab will perish in the heat of battle amid war cries and the blaring of shofars.
2.3: I will destroy Moab’s ruler and slaughter all officials there with him,” says Yahweh.
2.4: Yahweh says this: “For the three terrible crimes of Judah— no, make that four— I will not turn back my wrath because they have despised Yahweh ’s instructions and not kept his commandments. Their lies, which their ancestors followed, have led them astray.
2.5: I will send fire down on Judah to devour the fortresses of Jerusalem.”
2.6: Yahweh says this: “For the three terrible crimes of Israel— no, make that four— I will not turn back my wrath. For a few pieces of silver, they sold honest people into slavery. They even sold the poor, who couldn’t pay their debts, for a pair of sandals.
2.7: They trample the poor and helpless into the dirt and shove aside the rights of the destitute. A son and his father have sex with the same woman, and by doing so, they profane my holy name.
2.8: They lay themselves down beside every altar on garments taken as security for debts, and in the house of God they drink the wine they got from those who have been fined.
2.9: “Yet it was I who destroyed the Amorites before your very eyes. They stood as tall as cedar trees and as strong as oaks. I destroyed them root and branch.
2.10: It was I who brought you up from Egypt and led you for forty years through the desert to possess the land of the Amorites.
2.11: I raised up prophets from your sons and Nazirites from your young men. People of Israel, is this not true? I, Yahweh, have spoken!
2.12: “But you made the Nazirites drink wine and break their vow. You ordered the prophets, ‘You’d better not prophesy.’
2.13: Very well! I will press you down like a cart overloaded with grain.
2.14: Even the swiftest runner will not escape, physical strength will not be enough to protect the strong, nor will the mighty warrior be able to save himself.
2.15: The archer will not stand his ground, the fastest runners will not escape, nor will the one who flees on horseback save his life.
2.16: In that day, even the bravest of warriors will throw down his arms and run away. I, Yahweh, have spoken.”

3.1: Israelites, listen to this prophecy that Yahweh pronounces against you, against all the people I rescued from Egypt.
3.2: “Of all the nations of the earth, you are the only one I have intimately known and have always cared for. That is why I will punish you for all your wrongdoings.”
3.3: Do two walk together unless they have agreed to do so?
3.4: Does the lion roar in the bush if it has no prey? Does the lion growl in his lair if it has seized nothing?
3.5: Does a bird alight on a trap on the ground if there is no bait inside? Does the net spring up from the ground if it has caught nothing?
3.6: Does the war trumpet sound in the city without the people being frightened? Does calamity come to a city if it has not passed through Yahweh ’s hands?
3.7: Indeed, Lord Yahweh does nothing without revealing his secrets to his servants the prophets.
3.8: The lion has roared! Who is not afraid? Lord Yahweh has spoken! Who will not prophesy?
3.9: Proclaim to the strongholds of Assyria and Egypt, and say to them, “Gather on the hills around Samaria; take a good, hard look at the rampant disorder within the city and see how oppressed the people are.”
3.10: “They don’t even know how to do right,” declares Yahweh. “They hoard in their palaces the spoils of their violence and extortion.
3.11: Therefore, I, Lord Yahweh, say: an enemy will soon overrun the land. He will topple your strongholds and plunder your palaces.”
3.12: This is what Yahweh says: “As a shepherd can only rescue two leg bones or a piece of an ear out of the jaws of a lion, so the Israelites who live in Samaria will only be able to salvage one leg of a bed and a piece of a headboard from their ravaged city.”
3.13: “I, Lord Yahweh, the Mighty God of Angel Armies, say: Listen! Warn Jacob’s descendants.
3.14: On the day when I punish Israel for her crimes, I will also destroy the altars of Bethel. The horns of the altar will be hacked off and fall to the ground.
3.15: I will tear down the winter house of the wealthy along with your summer house. Your luxury homes decorated with ivory and your lovely mansions will likewise be destroyed. I, Yahweh, have spoken.”

4.1: Listen to this, you women of Samaria! You’re like the fattened, well-fed cows of Bashan grazing on the fertile mountain of Samaria. You women who exploit the weak and crush the poor and then command your husbands: “Bring us some drinks!”
4.2: Lord Yahweh has sworn by his holiness: “Behold, the day is soon coming when they will use hooks to drag you away, every last one of you with fishhooks.
4.3: They will force you like cattle in a chute through the gaps of the broken walls and herd you off toward Hermon. I, Yahweh, have spoken.”
4.4: “Go to Bethel and sin! Go to Gilgal and sin some more! You sin when you bring your sacrifices each morning. You sin when you bring your tithes every third day
4.5: and burn your thank offerings of bread made with yeast. Brag about your extra offerings, people of Israel, for this is what makes you happy! I, Lord Yahweh, have spoken.
4.6: “In every town, I left you hungry — a food shortage in all your villages— and still, you would not hunger for me. I, Yahweh, have spoken.
4.7: “I even withheld the rain from you three months short of harvest. I sent rain to fall on one town but not on another. One field had plenty of rain, and another became dry as dust.
4.8: People would stagger from city to city, longing for a drink of water yet never quenching their thirst. And still you had no thirst for me. I, Yahweh, have spoken.
4.9: “I struck your crops with blight and disease and dried up your many gardens and vineyards. Locusts kept devouring your fig trees and olive trees, and still, you would not return to me. I, Yahweh, have spoken.
4.10: “I sent plagues against you like I did against Egypt. I killed your young men with the sword and stole away all your war horses. I filled your nostrils with the stench of your unburied corpses, and still, you would not return to me. I, Yahweh, have spoken.
4.11: “I destroyed some of you like I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. Your survivors were like burning sticks plucked from a fire, and still, you would not return to me. I, Yahweh, have spoken.
4.12: “So here is what I plan to do to you, Israel, and because of what I am planning, prepare to meet your God.”
4.13: Behold, the Mountain-Maker and Wind-Creator, who reveals his intimate thoughts to people, who changes the dawn into darkness and moves over the mountains of the earth. His name is Yahweh, the God of Angel Armies.

5.1: Listen to this funeral song that I sing over you, people of Israel:
5.2: “Virgin Israel has fallen, never to rise again. There she lies, abandoned on her own soil, with no one to lift her up.”
5.3: Lord Yahweh says this: “The city that deployed a thousand soldiers will only have a hundred come back, and the city that deployed a hundred soldiers will only have ten survivors.”
5.4: For Yahweh says this to the people of Israel: “ Come, seek me, and you will live.
5.5: But don’t go down to seek me at Beersheba. Don’t try to find me at Bethel’s shrines or at the altars at Gilgal. For Gilgal will be taken into exile, and Bethel will be brought to nothing.”
5.6: Come back to Yahweh and live, or he will sweep down like fire upon the people of Israel. The fire will burn at Bethel with no one there to put out the flames.
5.7: They turn justice into a bitter pill to swallow and trample righteousness into the mud.
5.8: Creator of Constellations—Maker of the Pleiades and Orion, you turn the deepest darkness into dawn and daylight into the darkest night. You draw up drops of water distilled from the sea to drench the earth with pouring rain. Yahweh is your name.
5.9: You destroy the mighty with a blinding flash and overwhelm their strongholds with certain destruction.
5.10: They hate the one who challenges injustice and despise the one who declares the whole truth in court.
5.11: For I know how outrageous are your many sins and how many crimes you have committed. You persecute the righteous, trample on the rights of the poor, and seize their grain through extortion. By taking bribes, you prevent them from getting justice in the courts. This is why you will not live in the fine stone houses you build or enjoy the fruits of your luxury. You will not drink wine from the lush vineyards you plant, for your judgment is imminent.
5.12: For I know the vast number of your sins and rebellions. You oppress good people by taking bribes and deprive the poor of justice in the courts.
5.13: Yes, the smartest thing for the prudent is to remain silent in such an evil time as this.
5.14: Devote yourself to what is good, not evil, so that you may live. And Yahweh, the God of Angel Armies, will really be with you, just as you claim he is.
5.15: Hate what is evil, love what is right, and let justice prevail in the courts. It may be that Yahweh, God of Angel Armies, will show mercy to the remnant of Israel.
5.16: Because of Israel’s sins, Lord Yahweh, God of Angel Armies, says this: “Wailing and sorrow everywhere! In every street they will mourn the dead. Those who work in the fields will be expected to mourn along with the professional mourners.
5.17: There will be wailing in all the vineyards, for I will pass through your midst to punish you,” declares Yahweh.
5.18: Woe to you who long for the day of Yahweh! Why do you long for the day of Yahweh? Its arrival will mean darkness, not light.
5.19: You will be seized like someone who runs from a lion and a bear charges at him. Then he hides indoors and leans his hand against the wall only to have a venomous snake bite him.
5.20: Will not the day of Yahweh bring darkness, not light— a day of gloom without a ray of light?
5.21: “I hate your religious festivals; I absolutely despise them! Your pious gatherings make me sick!
5.22: Even though you offer me your burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. And though you bring me choice peace offerings of fattened animals, I won’t even look at them.
5.23: Spare me the monotonous melodies of your ‘worship.’ I don’t want to hear your strumming guitars anymore. It’s just noise to me.
5.24: However, I delight in a land where justice flows like a river and where true righteousness rolls like a steady flowing stream.
5.25: Listen, people of Israel! Didn’t you worship me with your offerings and sacrifices during those forty years in the wilderness?
5.26: Now you carry around the pagan idols that you made to worship your phony king, Sakkuth, and your very own star-god, Kaiwan.
5.27: Therefore, you can carry them all the way beyond Damascus, where I am about to drive you into captivity,” says Yahweh. God of Angel Armies is his name!

6.1: Woe to you living so comfortably in Zion! Woe to you who live with a false sense of security on Mount Samaria, the elite of this foremost nation, on whom Israel’s people pin their hopes.
6.2: Travel to the city of Calneh and see for yourself what happened. Then go on from there to Hamath, the great capital city of the Hittites. Make your way down to Gath in Philistia, and ask yourself — are you better than these kingdoms? Is their territory larger than yours?
6.3: You refuse to consider the day when disaster will come, yet all your evil only brings that day closer.
6.4: Lying on luxurious beds inlaid with ivory and sprawled out on your couches, you feast on lambs from the flock and stall-fattened veal.
6.5: You compose songs like David and strum away on your harps.
6.6: You guzzle wine by the bucketful, and slather yourselves with the finest lotions. Yet you do not grieve over Israel’s impending doom.
6.7: That is why they will be the first to go into captivity. Their lying around while enjoying the good life will come to an end.
6.8: Lord Yahweh has sworn by his own being — Yahweh, God of Angel Armies, declares: “I hate the pride of the people of Jacob, and I despise their strongholds, I will hand over their capital city to their enemies and everything in it.”
6.9: Even if there are ten hiding in a house, they will all die.
6.10: If a relative who is to light a memorial fire for the dead comes to carry the bodies out of the house for burial and asks, “Is anyone else inside the house with you?” and that person answers, “No,” then the one who asked will say, “Quiet! We must not mention the name of Yahweh.”
6.11: Behold, Yahweh strikes with his command: “Houses large and small will be smashed to pieces!”
6.12: Can horses gallop over rocky cliffs? Can boulder-strewn hills be plowed with oxen? Of course not! Yet you have managed to pervert justice into poison and the sweet fruits of righteousness into bitter fruit.
6.13: You rejoice over conquering the city of Lo Debar, saying, “Wasn’t it by our own strength that we captured Karnaim for ourselves?”
6.14: But look, house of Israel, Yahweh, God of Angel Armies, declares to you: “I will raise up a mighty nation to come against you, and they will oppress you and overrun your land from the northern to the southern borders of your kingdom.”

7.1: This is what Lord Yahweh revealed to me in a vision: Behold! Just after the hay had been cut for the king, when the new young grass started to grow again, I saw Yahweh forming a swarm of mature locusts.
7.2: I watched as they began eating all the vegetation in the land, so I pleaded with God, saying, “Lord Yahweh, please forgive us, I beg you, or we will not survive! Our nation is so helpless.”
7.3: My prayer moved God’s heart to compassion. Yahweh said: “It will not happen.”
7.4: In another vision, Yahweh revealed this to me: Behold! He was calling for punishment by fire. The scorching heat dried up the deep sources of water beneath the land and made the farmlands like dust.
7.5: So I pleaded with God, saying, “Lord Yahweh, please don’t do this, I beg you, or we will not survive! Our nation is so helpless.”
7.6: Because of my prayer, God’s heart was stirred with compassion. “This also will not happen,” said Yahweh.
7.7: Lord Yahweh revealed this to me in another vision: I saw the Lord standing by a wall built true to plumb, holding a plumb line in his hand.
7.8: “Amos, what do you see?” Yahweh asked me. “A plumb line,” I replied. Then the Lord said, “Behold, I am about to set a plumb line up against my people Israel to test them. Never again will I look the other way when they sin.
7.9: I will destroy the high places where Isaac’s descendants worship, and I will ruin the holy places of Israel. With my sword in hand, I will attack the dynasty of Jeroboam.”
7.10: Then Amaziah the chief priest of Bethel sent the following message to Jeroboam king of Israel: “Amos has conspired against you in the very heart of Israel. We cannot stand his speeches!
7.11: For Amos says, ‘Jeroboam is going to die by the sword, and Israel will go into captivity far from its native land.’ ”
7.12: Amaziah said to Amos, “Go away, you seer. Why don’t you escape to Judah while there is time? You can always prophesy there and make your living.
7.13: But don’t stay around here and prophesy at Bethel anymore. This is the national temple, the place where the king worships.”
7.14: Amos replied, “I am not a prophet, nor am I one of the sons of the prophets. I am merely a rancher, and I cultivate fig trees.
7.15: But one day, Yahweh called me as I was managing my flocks and said to me, ‘Go and prophesy to my people Israel.’
7.16: “So now, Amaziah, listen to what Yahweh says. You say: ‘Do not prophesy against Israel, and do not prophesy doom on Isaac’s descendants!’
7.17: Very well. This is what Yahweh says: ‘Your wife will become a prostitute in the streets, and your sons and daughters will fall in battle. Your land will be measured, divided up, and given to others. And you yourself will die in a pagan land, and Israel will go into captivity far from its own land!’ ”

8.1: Lord Yahweh revealed this to me in another vision: a basket of ripe fruit.
8.2: “Amos, what do you see?” he asked. “A basket of ripe fruit,” I replied. Then Yahweh said, “The time is ripe for my people Israel. I will not continue to overlook their sins.
8.3: On that day, those singing songs in the temple will wail instead,” declares the Lord Yahweh. “There will be corpses piled up everywhere. They will be cast out in silence.”
8.4: Listen to this, all you who trample on the poor and reduce the needy to nothing!
8.5: You say to yourselves, “We can’t wait for these holy days to be over so that we can sell our corn!” And, “When will this Sabbath be over so that we can open the storage and sell our wheat? Then we can overcharge our customers, shortchange them, and deceive them by tampering with the scales.
8.6: We can even sell the worthless chaff we sweep up for silver. We can buy the poor with silver and make them our slaves because they cannot pay their debts, even a debt so small as that of a pair of sandals.”
8.7: Yahweh, the Majesty of Jacob, has sworn an oath: “I will never forget all the evil they have done.
8.8: That is why the earth will tremble for this, and all who live on it mourn. All of the land will rise up like the river Nile— inundated and stirred up by floodwaters— and then subside, just like the river of Egypt!”
8.9: “On that day,” declares Lord Yahweh, “I will make the sun set at noon and darken the earth in the middle of the day.
8.10: I will turn your festivals into funerals, and all your lively singing into funeral dirges. I will make you all wear sackcloth and shave your heads, as if you were mourning the death of an only child. That day will be bitter to the end.”
8.11: “Behold, the days are coming,” declares Lord Yahweh, “when I will send a famine on the land. People will not hunger for food nor thirst for water but will starve for a word from Yahweh.
8.12: People will stagger from sea to sea and wander from the north to the east searching for a revelation from Yahweh, but they will not hear from me.
8.13: On that day, even your beautiful young women and strong young men will collapse from thirst.
8.14: Those who swear by Ashimah, the idol of Samaria, who say, ‘Long live your golden calf-god of Dan!’ and say, ‘As surely as the god of Beersheba lives!’— they will all fall, never to rise again.”

9.1: I saw the Lord standing over the altar, and he gave the command: “Smash the top of the pillars so that the foundations shake! Shatter the pillars and make them crumble upon the heads of all the worshipers. And any survivors I will kill by the sword. Whoever runs away will not go far. Whoever tries to escape will not make it.
9.2: Even if they were to dig their way down to the underworld, my hand would haul them out. Even if they were to climb up to heaven, I would drag them down from there.
9.3: If they were to hide on top of Mount Carmel, I would hunt them down and snatch them. If they were to try to hide from my eyes at the bottom of the sea, I would order the serpent there to bite them.
9.4: If their enemies were to herd them into captivity, even there I would order the sword to kill them. Yes, I will fix my eyes on them to destroy them and not to help them.”
9.5: Lord Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, you touch the earth and it melts, and everyone on earth mourns. All of the land will rise up like the river Nile— inundated and stirred up by floodwaters— and then subside, just like the river of Egypt.
9.6: You build your lofty stairway in the heavens and suspend your superdome over the earth. You summon the waters of the sea and pour them over the face of the earth: Yahweh is your name!
9.7: “Israel, I think as much of the Ethiopians as I do of you; you’re all the same to me,” declares Yahweh. “ Yes, I brought you out from Egypt. But didn’t I also bring out the Philistines from Crete and the Syrians from Kir?
9.8: Behold, the eyes of Lord Yahweh are on the sinful kingdom of Israel. I will wipe it off the face of the earth. Yet I will not completely destroy the descendants of Jacob,” declares Yahweh.
9.9: “Behold, I will speak the command to scatter the people of Israel among all the nations. I will sift them the way sand is shaken in a sieve, through which not a single pebble falls to the ground.
9.10: All the sinners of my people will die by the sword who say, ‘Nothing bad could ever happen to us.’ ”
9.11: “One day I will restore David’s tabernacle that has fallen. I will repair its broken places and raise up its ruins and fix it up like new. I will rebuild it and make it what it was long ago.
9.12: As a result, David’s people will conquer the nations over which they once ruled for me, down to the last remnant of Edom.
9.13: Behold, I, Yahweh, make this decree: The days of acceleration are coming, when the harvest will be so great that those plowing the field will overtake those still reaping the harvest, and the ones treading the grapes will overtake those who are planting. Blessings will stream forth like new wine pouring from every mountain, and every hill will flow with favor.
9.14: I will restore prosperity and good fortune to the captives of Israel. They will rebuild the ruined cities to live in. They will plant vineyards to produce their wine. And plant lush gardens and orchards to eat their produce.
9.15: And I will plant them in their own land, never to be uprooted again from the land that I have given them. I, Yahweh, your God, have spoken.”

1.1: This is the vision that Lord Yahweh revealed to Obadiah concerning Edom. We have heard a report from Yahweh: “I have sent a messenger throughout the nations, saying, ‘Rise up! Let us march against this people. Prepare for war!’
1.2: “Behold, I have reduced you to the least among the nations. You are now utterly despised.
1.3: Your proud heart has deceived you; you who are perched in the hidden places of the rock, whose home is in the heights. You think to yourself, ‘Who can ever topple me to the ground?’
1.4: Though you soar like an eagle, and your nest is nestled among the stars, I am more than able to bring you down from there. I, Yahweh, have spoken.”
1.5: “When thieves come at night to rob your home, wouldn’t they only steal the things they wanted? When people gather grapes, wouldn’t they miss a few and leave some gleanings behind? But you, Edom—your enemies will totally destroy you!
1.6: How Esau’s descendants will be looted, their hidden treasures sought out and ransacked!
1.7: Your allies will deceive you. They will overpower you and chase you off your homeland. Your ‘trusted friends’ will lay a trap for you, and you’ll have no clue it’s coming.
1.8: In that day, will I not destroy all the wise men of Edom and erase all their pseudo -intelligence from the mountains of Esau? I, Yahweh, have spoken.
1.9: Teman, all your brave warriors will be shattered so that everyone will be destroyed from Esau’s mountain.”
1.10: “Shame will cover you and you will be annihilated because you violently slaughtered your relatives, the Israelites.
1.11: You deserted Israel at her time of need. On that day of infamy, you stood aloof and did nothing as foreigners broke through the city gates of Jerusalem and divided the city among themselves by casting lots. Strangers carried off all her treasures, and you were as one with the invaders.
1.12: Do not gloat over your relatives on the day of their misfortune. Do not rejoice over the people of Judah on the day of their ruin. Do not boast that they suffered such anguish.
1.13: You should not have entered my people’s city on their day of calamity. You should not have feasted your eyes on their suffering on their day of misery. You should not have seized their wealth on their day of sorrow.
1.14: You should not have waited at the crossroads to cut off those who tried to escape. Why did you hand over their survivors on the day of their distress?”
1.15: “The day of Yahweh is drawing near for all the nations. As you have done to others, so will it be done to you: you will be paid back for all that your deeds deserve.
1.16: “Just as you have drunk and caroused on my sacred hill, so all the surrounding nations will drink continually from my bitter cup of judgment. They will drink and drink and gulp it down, but they will stagger and be destroyed.”
1.17: “But on Mount Zion a remnant will escape, for that place will be a reconsecrated sanctuary. And Jacob’s tribes will possess what is rightfully theirs by inheritance.
1.18: Then the people of Judah will be a fire, the people of Israel a flame, and the people of Esau like stubble. They will set them on fire and consume them, and there will be no survivors from Esau’s descendants. I, Yahweh, have spoken.”
1.19: People from southern Judah will capture Edom; those from the western foothills will occupy Philistia; Israelites will take back the territory of Ephraim and Samaria; and the people of Benjamin will possess Gilead.
1.20: The company of exiles from among the people of Israel will possess the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath while the exiles from Jerusalem now in Sardis will occupy the cities of southern Judah.
1.21: Victorious deliverers will go out from Mount Zion to rule over the land of Edom, and the kingdom will be Yahweh ’s.

1.1: One day Yahweh revealed to Jonah, Amittai’s son, this message:
1.2: “Arise! Leave at once for the great city of Nineveh and proclaim judgment against her, for the wickedness of her people is staring me in the face.”
1.3: But Jonah bolted and ran in the opposite direction, determined to run away from the presence of Yahweh. He went down to the coastal city of Joppa and found a ship bound for Tarshish. He paid his fare, went down into the hold of the ship, and set sail for Tarshish to flee from the presence of Yahweh.
1.4: But Yahweh unleashed a powerful, violent wind on the sea. The ship was caught in such a great tempest that it was in jeopardy of shattering.
1.5: The sailors were terrified. Each of them began to call on his own god for help. In order to lighten the ship they hurled the cargo and tackle overboard. Jonah, however, had gone down below and lain down in the hold and was fast asleep.
1.6: The captain went below and asked Jonah, “How can you be sleeping so soundly at a time like this? Get up! Call on your god! Maybe he will feel sorry for us and not leave us to die.”
1.7: Then the sailors said to each other, “Come on. Let’s cast lots to find out who is to blame for bringing us this calamity.” They cast lots, and the lot pointed to Jonah.
1.8: So they interrogated him. “Tell us,” they said, “what is the purpose of your journey? Where do you come from? What is your country, and who are your people?”
1.9: “I’m a Hebrew,” he replied. “I worship the God of heaven, the Creator of both sea and dry land. His name is Yahweh.”
1.10: Jonah added, “ I am his prophet, but I’m trying to escape from him.” Hearing this, the sailors were gripped with fear and said, “What terrible thing have you done?
1.11: What can we do to you to make the sea calm down for us?” Even as they spoke, the storm and waves were getting worse and worse.
1.12: Then Jonah said, “It’s all my fault that you are caught in this violent storm. So just pick me up and throw me into the sea, and it will calm down for you.”
1.13: Reluctant to sacrifice Jonah, the sailors rowed frantically trying to return to shore, but they got nowhere. All the while, the sea was raging even wilder than before.
1.14: Losing hope, they began to pray to Yahweh and said, “Please, Yahweh, God of Jonah, don’t let us perish on account of Jonah. And don’t hold it against us for throwing this man overboard. For you, Yahweh, have acted in accordance with your will.”
1.15: So the sailors took hold of Jonah and tossed him into the foaming sea. Then all at once, the sea stopped raging.
1.16: Awestruck, the men were gripped with the fear of Yahweh, and they made vows and offered sacrifices to Jonah’s God, Yahweh.
1.17: Meanwhile, Yahweh directed a huge fish to be at that very spot in order to swallow Jonah. And Jonah was kept alive in the stomach of the fish for three days and three nights.

2.1: This is Jonah’s prayer to Yahweh, his God, from out of the darkness inside the huge fish:
2.2: “I called out to Yahweh from a place of total desperation and he answered me. From inside the belly of Sheol I cried out, and you heard my voice.
2.3: The waters closed in all around me; all your mighty waves and currents crashed over me. For you cast me into the deep, and I sank down to the bottom of the sea.
2.4: I actually assumed that you had banished me from your sight. Yet, I know that I will one day gaze again upon your holy temple.
2.5: The waters rose to choke me to death. The sea was closing in around me— seaweed tightened around my head.
2.6: I sank down into the abyss, to the roots of the mountains, where the barred gates of that realm would lock me in forever. But you, Yahweh, are my God; you raised my life from the pit.
2.7: When my life was ebbing away, my thoughts turned toward you. My cries rose before you in your holy, heavenly temple, and my prayer entered your heart, Yahweh.
2.8: It’s true —some abandon faithful love to you by worshiping worthless idols.
2.9: But I will sing songs of praise and offer my sacrifices to you. I will keep every vow I’ve made to you, Yahweh, for salvation comes only from you.”
2.10: So Yahweh spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto the dry land.

3.1: Yahweh spoke to the prophet Jonah for the second time.
3.2: “Arise!” he said. “Leave at once for the great city of Nineveh and preach to the people the message I give you.”
3.3: This time, Jonah set out for Nineveh in obedience to the word of Yahweh. Now Nineveh was a very important city to God. It took three days to traverse the entire city.
3.4: When Jonah entered the city, he walked a day’s journey and began to preach: “ God will destroy this city in forty days!”
3.5: The people of Nineveh believed Jonah’s message and turned to God. To show they had repented, they called for a fast and put on sackcloth, from the greatest to the least of them.
3.6: When the news reached the king of Nineveh, he arose from his throne, took off his royal robe, put on sackcloth, and sat down in ashes.
3.7: He then issued this proclamation: “People of Nineveh, by decree of the king and his nobles, no person or animal, herd or flock, may eat anything; they must not consume any food or water.
3.8: Each of you must cover yourself and your livestock with burlap and call on God with all your might. Everyone must turn away from his or her evil ways and violent behavior.
3.9: Who knows? Perhaps God may show us mercy and be willing to change his mind. Perhaps he will relent and turn from unleashing his fierce anger so that we will not die.”
3.10: When God saw their sincere efforts to turn from their wicked ways, he decided not to punish the people of Nineveh and did not bring upon them the disaster he said would come.

4.1: Jonah was extremely upset that God would show mercy to Nineveh. Indignant, he fell into a rage.
4.2: He prayed to Yahweh and said, “God, I knew this is what would happen even before I left home. For I know that you are a tender, compassionate God, who is extremely patient, rich in faithful love. And I know you are always ready to relent from inflicting disaster. That was why I attempted to flee to Tarshish.
4.3: So now, Yahweh, please take my life, for death seems better to me than life.”
4.4: Yahweh replied, “What good reason do you have to be so angry?”
4.5: Then Jonah went out east of Nineveh, where he made himself a makeshift shelter. He sat there under its shade waiting to see what would happen to the city.
4.6: Now Lord Yahweh arranged for a gourd plant to grow up over Jonah to provide him shade to rest in and to soothe his sour demeanor. Jonah was thrilled with the plant.
4.7: But at dawn the next day, God sent a worm to chew through the plant—and it withered.
4.8: As the sun rose into the sky, God sent a scorching east wind. The wind and blazing sun beat down so hard on Jonah’s head that he was starting to faint. So he begged God to end his life, saying, “I’m better off dead than alive.”
4.9: God said to Jonah, “Are you right to be so angry about the plant that gave you shade?” He replied, “I have every right to be angry, angry enough to die!”
4.10: Yahweh replied, “You are concerned for the vine, which you did not plant, nor did you do anything to make it grow. It sprang up one night and died the next.
4.11: Should I not have compassion for the great city of Nineveh, in which there are more than 120,000 people who cannot tell their right hand from their left, to say nothing of all the animals?”

1.1: This is the prophetic message Yahweh revealed to Micah of Moresheth. He delivered these prophecies during the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah. These are his supernatural visions concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
1.2: Listen, you peoples—all of you! Earth, pay attention —and everyone on it. From his holy temple, the Lord Yahweh himself will testify against you.
1.3: For behold, Yahweh is leaving his dwelling place. Here he comes to tread upon the high places of the land.
1.4: Mountains melt beneath his feet, like wax melting near a raging fire. Valleys are split wide open, like water pouring down a steep slope.
1.5: All of this is because of the rebellion of Jacob’s tribes, the sin of the people of Israel. So who is to blame for the rebellion of Jacob? Is it not the people of Samaria? Who is to blame for the idolatry of the high places of Judah? Is it not the people of Jerusalem?
1.6: “So I will wrestle Samaria to the ground, and she will become nothing more than an open field for planting vines. I will roll the stones of her buildings down into the valley until I have laid bare her foundations.
1.7: I will hammer to pieces all her gilded pagan idols, all the gifts given to her sacred prostitutes will be scorched by fire. I will turn all her precious idols into a pile of rubble. For she—Samaria—gathered her treasured idols as a prostitute collects her fees, and now these idols will become a prostitute’s wages again.”
1.8: I will mourn and wail because of this. I will walk around barefoot and bare to show my sorrow. I will howl like a jackal and mourn like an owl.
1.9: For her wound is incurable, and her infection is spreading to Judah. It has even reached the gateway of my people, to Jerusalem itself.
1.10: Show no tears in Showtown (Gath). People of Dusty House (Beth Leaphrah), wallow in the dust of your despair!
1.11: You’ll take a different path, Glamour-Girl-Town (Shaphir); you’ll go into exile naked and ashamed. You citizens of Outbound City (Zaanan) are stuck at home. Your next-door neighbor (Beth Ezel) is in mourning and will no longer be able to help you.
1.12: The women of Bitterville (Maroth) writhed in labor pains, hoping for good to come. Instead, Yahweh sent down disaster all the way to the gates of Jerusalem itself.
1.13: Start up your chariots, you people of Ponytown (Lachish), for the sin of the daughter of Zion can be traced back to you, where Israel’s sin began.
1.14: People of Judah, give gifts to Moresheth Gath, as you would to a daughter who is leaving home to be married. The Domiciles of Deception (Beth Achzib) will deceive the kings of Israel.
1.15: People of Mareshah, Yahweh will again bring a conqueror against you, and the glory of Israel will flee to the cave of Adullam.
1.16: Cut off your hair and make yourselves bald, for your delightful children are taken away. Make yourselves as bald as a vulture, for your children have been taken away from you into exile.

2.1: Disaster is ahead for those who plot evil. They’re as good as dead! Disaster is ahead for those who scheme as they lie on their bed. No sooner is it dawn than they act on their plan just because they can.
2.2: They covet someone’s field and seize it for themselves, and they take over his house as well. They defraud a man of his home and another man of his inheritance.
2.3: So here’s what Yahweh has to say about that: “Now I am the one plotting a disaster for those who plot to defraud others, a disaster from which you cannot escape. You will no longer walk with heads held high, for a catastrophe will bring you low.
2.4: And when that time comes, people will adopt a taunting proverb about you and sing this mournful song to mock your sad experience: ‘We have lost everything! God has divided up our people’s lands with no one left to restore it to our hands. Our property has been seized and given to our captors—the traitors.’ ”
2.5: Because of this, when Yahweh restores the land to his people, those corrupt leaders will have no stake in Yahweh ’s assembly nor have any part in the distribution of land.
2.6: They berate me continually. “Don’t prophesy,” they say to me. “Don’t keep prophesying on and on about these things! Disgrace will not overtake us.”
2.7: Should Jacob’s descendants even be asking, “Is the Spirit of Yahweh really so short-tempered that he would do such things to us?” “When I speak, don’t my words produce good within the one who obeys them?
2.8: But you wealthy oppressors of the poor have become like enemies attacking my people. When men return home from war and think they are finally safe at home, there you are, ready to snatch the coats off their backs as security for the money they owe you.
2.9: You wrongly evict the women of my people from the very homes they love, forever depriving their children of the honor of their inheritance.
2.10: Get up and get out! This is no longer your resting place. Because of this defilement, I will completely destroy you, and your destruction will be severe beyond measure.
2.11: If a lying windbag comes to deceive you, saying, ‘I prophesy wine and liquor will flow for you,’ he would be the ideal prophet for a people like this.”
2.12: “I will regather the tribes of Jacob. Yes, I will regather the remnant of Israel. I will bring you together like sheep in a fold, like a flock within their pasture, a noisy, excited multitude.
2.13: “The Barrier-Breaker will lead them out into freedom. They will all break out, passing through the enemy’s gates. Their king will advance before their eyes with Yahweh himself leading the way!”

3.1: Then I said, “Listen, you leaders of the tribes of Jacob, you princes among the people of Israel. Is it not your duty to see that justice prevails?
3.2: Yet you hate what is good and love what is evil. You skin my people alive, pulling the flesh off their bones.
3.3: Like butchers, you tear the skin off my people. You break their bones and chop them up like stew meat for the pot. Like wild animals, you rip the flesh off their bones and devour my people.
3.4: Then you will cry out to him, but he will not answer your prayers. Yahweh will hide his face from you rulers because you have totally misused your power.”
3.5: Here is what Yahweh says against the prophets who lead my people so far from the truth: “So long as they pay you, you prophesy peace. But if they don’t, you threaten war.
3.6: So, darkness will close in around you, and you will receive no prophetic visions. A shroud of darkness will bring your predictions to an end. The sun will set for the prophets, and the daylight will go dark for them.
3.7: Then shame will silence the seers. Confusion will cover those who predict the future. Humiliated, they will all put their hands over their mouths because there is no word from God.”
3.8: Not so with me, for I am full of power! Yahweh ’s breath fills me with a sense of justice and courage to expose the rebellion of Jacob’s tribes and the sin of the people of Israel.
3.9: Now hear this, you leaders of the tribes of Jacob, you princes of the people of Israel: You hate justice and distort right into wrong.
3.10: Indeed, you build up Zion and Jerusalem but upon an immoral foundation of murder and malice.
3.11: Her judges render verdicts for the highest bidder, her priests preach for a price, her prophets prophesy for a fee, and yet they pretend to depend upon Yahweh. “Isn’t Yahweh on our side?” they say. “How could any disaster come upon us?”
3.12: That is why, thanks to you, Zion will return to farmland, Jerusalem to a pile of rubble, and the Temple Mount will be deserted — overgrown with thickets.

4.1: In the future, the mountain of Yahweh ’s temple will be raised up as the head of the mountains, towering over all the hills. A sparkling stream of every nation will flow into it.
4.2: Many peoples will come and say, “Everyone, come! Let’s go up higher to Yahweh ’s mountain, to the house of Jacob’s God; then he can teach us his ways, and we can walk in his paths.” Zion will be the center of instruction, and the word of Yahweh will go out from Jerusalem.
4.3: He will judge fairly between strong, distant nations and settle disputes among many peoples. The swords they used against each other they will beat into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. No nation will take up weapons against another, nor will they prepare for war anymore.
4.4: But everyone will relax under their own fig trees and vineyards with no one to trouble them. For Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, has decreed it.
4.5: Though all the nations walk in the name of their own gods, we will walk in the name of Yahweh, our God, forever and ever.
4.6: I, Yahweh, declare: “In that day of hope I will gather the lame and bring together the wandering outcasts and those whom I have bruised.
4.7: I will make a new beginning with those who are crippled and far from home. My remnant will be transformed into a mighty nation. And I, Yahweh, will reign over them on Mount Zion from now and throughout eternity.
4.8: “And to you, Tower of the Flock, where the daughter of Zion is lifted up, your royal dominion will arrive. His kingship will come to you, Daughter Jerusalem.”
4.9: Why are you wailing? Why are you writhing like a woman in labor? Have you no king to help you? And your wise leader, has he perished?
4.10: Groan and writhe in anguish, like a woman in hard labor, daughter of Zion, for now, you must leave the city and live out in the open field. Off to Babylon you must go! Yet, one day you will be rescued from there, for Yahweh will deliver you from the clutches of your enemies.
4.11: Many nations have now gathered to attack you. They say, “Let’s destroy Jerusalem so that we can gloat over capturing Zion.”
4.12: But they do not know Yahweh ’s plans, and they do not understand his strategy: he has brought them together to punish them, like grain is brought to be beaten on the threshing floor to separate the good from the worthless.
4.13: “Arise, start your threshing, daughter of Zion, for I will make you strong as a bull with iron horns and bronze hooves so that you can crush many peoples. And you must devote to Yahweh what they have stolen and bring their wealth to me, the Lord of the whole earth.”

5.1: Now you are walled in. They have laid siege against us. They smack the ruler of Israel’s face with a rod.
5.2: “But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, so small among the clans of Judah, from your people will come a ruler who will rule Israel for me. He will burst forth from the first sunrise from the days of eternity!”
5.3: Therefore, Yahweh will hand Israel over to her enemies until the labor pains are over and the child is born. And then the remnant of his brothers in exile will be reunited with the Israelites.
5.4: He will take his stand and will lead and feed his flock with the strength that comes from Yahweh and with the majesty of the name of his God. With this shepherd, they will live in safety, for his greatness will extend to the ends of the earth.
5.5: He himself will be their peace. When the Assyrian army sets foot on our soil to invade our land, we will raise up more than enough mighty captains to conquer them.
5.6: They will shepherd the Assyrians with the sword, the land of Nimrod with the drawn sword. And Yahweh will deliver us from the Assyrians, when they invade our land and tread on our territory.
5.7: Then the remnant of Jacob will be scattered among many peoples. They will be like the refreshing dew from Yahweh, like raindrops on the meadows, which do not wait on man’s command and are beyond human control.
5.8: Then the scattered remnant of Jacob will live among the nations. They will be like lions among the animals of the forest, like fierce lions among flocks of sheep, they will pounce on their prey with no one to rescue.
5.9: You will be victorious over your foes, and all your enemies will be torn to pieces.
5.10: “When that day comes,” declares Yahweh, “I will destroy your horses and demolish your chariots.
5.11: I will destroy the cities of your country and tear down all your strongholds.
5.12: I will dismantle the witchcraft in your land, and you will no longer cast spells.
5.13: I shall tear away your idols and your sacred stone pillars from among you. You will no longer worship things that your own hands have made.
5.14: I will uproot your sacred poles and level your cities.
5.15: I will punish with furious anger the nations who have disobeyed me.”

6.1: Now listen to what Yahweh says: “Stand up and state your case. The mountains will be your witnesses, so let the hills hear your defense.
6.2: Listen, mountains, to Yahweh ’s accusation; pay attention, you enduring foundations of the earth, for I, Yahweh, have an indictment against my people, and I will prosecute my case against Israel.
6.3: My people, what have I done to deserve your neglect? How have I made you tired of me? Answer me!
6.4: Did I not rescue you from Egypt and ransom you from slavery? I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to lead you.
6.5: Please remember this, my people: King Balak of Moab planned to curse you, and how did the prophet Balaam son of Beor answer him? He spoke Yahweh ’s blessing over you! Remember how I parted the Jordan so that you could cross over from Acacia to Gilgal. Now you should know through all my saving acts that I have treated you fairly.”
6.6: What should I bring when I enter Yahweh ’s presence and bow down before God Most High? Should I approach him with burnt offerings, with year-old calves to sacrifice?
6.7: Will he be pleased with thousands of rams and with endless streams of olive oil? Should I offer him my firstborn for my wrongdoing, my own offspring for the sins of my life?
6.8: No! Listen, O Adam’s offspring, Yahweh has made it plain to you what is best. He has shown you what he really is longing for from you— only to promote justice, to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God.
6.9: Yahweh ’s voice is calling out to the city. Wise is the one who fears the name of Yahweh. “So pay attention, O tribe, to the one who called you together!
6.10: Can I overlook the treasures that fill the homes of evil people who cheated others? They use false measures, which I despise.
6.11: Do you really expect me to forgive those who cheat others with a bag of wrong weights and dishonest scales?
6.12: The wealthy are steeped in violence, and the people are liars and speak deceitfully.
6.13: As for me, I will deal you a crippling blow to ruin you for your sins.
6.14: You will eat but not be satisfied; you will still be hungry. You will acquire but save nothing because what you save, I will send your enemies to destroy.
6.15: You will plant crops but not reap a harvest, press olives for its oil and never be able to rub it on yourselves, and tread grapes but never drink the wine.
6.16: For you live by the standards of the dynasty of Omri and follow the evil ways of Ahab and his household. Because you walk after their example, you force me to make an example out of you! I will hand you over to ruin and make you a laughingstock among the nations. People everywhere will treat you with contempt.”

7.1: I’m so depressed and disappointed, like a hungry man who went to the field after the harvest had been gathered and found nothing remaining, not even the gleanings— nor a single cluster of grapes nor any of those firstfruit figs I love.
7.2: The godly have vanished from the land: there is not a decent person left. They are all out for each other’s blood, they hunt each other with a net.
7.3: Concerning evil, both hands do it well. Officials and judges ask for bribes, the man in power pronounces whatever he pleases, and the prominent plot as one.
7.4: The best and brightest is like a briar bush, the most honest of them like a thorn hedge. Now here comes the punishment your prophets proclaimed. Confusion confronts you!
7.5: Don’t dare to trust in a neighbor or place your confidence in a friend. Watch your words even with the wife you love.
7.6: For the son insults his father, the daughter rebels against her mother, and the daughter-in-law quarrels with her mother-in-law. One’s enemies come from within your own household.
7.7: But as for me, I will keep watching for Yahweh to break through. I will wait for the God who will save me, and I know my God will hear my cry.
7.8: Listen, my enemy. Don’t gloat over me when I fall, for I will get back up even stronger. Whenever I feel darkness around me, Yahweh himself will be the light that surrounds me.
7.9: I must endure Yahweh ’s anger for a while because I have sinned against him. Yet he will still defend my cause and right every wrong done to me. He will expose it all and bring me out into the light, and I will experience firsthand his vindication.
7.10: When my enemy sees this, she will be disgraced and covered with shame— she who sneered, “Where is this God of yours, Yahweh?” I’ll see it with my own eyes as she is trampled down like mud in the streets.
7.11: What a day that will be! A day for rebuilding your walls! A day for expanding your borders!
7.12: A day when people come to you from everywhere— from the cities of Assyria, Egypt, and Tyre and all the way from the river Euphrates, from across the seas, and from every mountainous land.
7.13: Those lands will become desolate because of the corruption of their inhabitants.
7.14: Our kind Shepherd, watch over us, the flock that is your special inheritance. With your staff, lead your people to pasture. For we are like a flock confined to live in a forest with meadowland all around us. Let us graze again in the fertile fields of Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old.
7.15: “I will show you mighty miracles as in the days when you came out of Egypt.”
7.16: When the nations see your miracles, they will be ashamed, seeing that their power counts for nothing. They will put their hands over their mouths, too dumbfounded by your might to even speak, and their ears will become deaf.
7.17: Let them lick the dust like snakes, like the crawling things of the earth. Let them come slinking out of their strongholds, trembling in terror before you, Yahweh.
7.18: Who is a merciful God like you? Your grace wipes the slate clean of guilt and pardons the rebellion of the remnant of your people. You don’t hold your anger against us forever, but you delight in showing faithful, tender love.
7.19: Once more we ask: have tender mercy on us, tread our iniquities under your feet, and hurl all our sins to the bottom of the sea.
7.20: You will demonstrate endless faithfulness to Jacob’s tribes and to Abraham’s descendants your constant love, just like you swore to our ancestors in ancient times.

1.1: This is the book of the vision of Nahum who was from the village of Elkosh. A prophecy concerning Nineveh:
1.2: Yahweh is a God who tolerates no rivals. Lord Yahweh will take vengeance on his foes. He punishes his adversaries and keeps wrath for his enemies.
1.3: Yahweh is very slow to anger but so great in power; Yahweh will not let the guilty go unpunished. He marches out in the whirlwind and storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
1.4: He rebukes the sea and dries it up and makes all the rivers run dry. At his rebuke, the lush meadows of Bashan and Carmel wither; the flowering fields of Lebanon fade.
1.5: In his presence, the mountains quake and the hills melt away. When he appears, the earth heaves, and the world and all who dwell in it are laid waste.
1.6: Who can stand before an angry God? Who can face his fiery fury? When his wrath erupts, it pours out like lava, and boulders are broken to bits as he approaches.
1.7: The goodness of Yahweh is beyond belief! For when trouble comes, we run into his heart and hide. He always cares for those who seek refuge in him.
1.8: But with an overwhelming flood, he will make a complete end of Nineveh, and darkness will overtake his enemies.
1.9: Whatever evil plot you hatch against Yahweh, he will so completely thwart that it will not rise up a second time.
1.10: They will be like drunkards from their carousing— like entangled thorns, they will be consumed as dry stubble.
1.11: From you, Nineveh, came one who plotted evil against Yahweh, a wicked, worthless strategist.
1.12: Yahweh says, “Although your enemies are many and secure in their alliances, they will nonetheless be mowed down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, my people, I will not do it again.
1.13: And now I will break his yoke of bondage from your neck and tear away your shackles of Assyrian oppression.”
1.14: Yahweh has decreed against you, Nineveh: “Your dynasty is over! Every idol in the temple of your gods I will destroy, your carved and engraved idols. I will dig your grave, for you are nothing to me.”
1.15: What a beautiful sight to behold— the precious feet of the messenger coming over the mountains to announce good news and to proclaim peace! People of Judah, celebrate your feasts, keep your solemn promises to God, for the wicked one will never pass through you again; he is completely cut off.

2.1: Nineveh, an attacker is poised to advance against you. Place your guards along the top of the walls; set lookouts on the road. Go ahead, get ready for battle; gather all your forces, but it will be in vain.
2.2: For Yahweh is about to restore the majesty of Jacob and Israel her glory. For you have plundered everything and ruined their vineyards.
2.3: The invading soldiers’ shields are scarlet, each warrior robed in red. The metal of the Babylonian chariots gleams like fire on the day they are made ready for battle, and the wooden spears are brandished in anticipation.
2.4: The chariots race madly through the streets of Nineveh; they dash wildly through the public squares, gleaming like torches, darting like lightning.
2.5: The king of Assyria summons his elite commanders, but they stumble while attempting to advance. The attackers run swiftly to the city wall; the protective canopy for the battering ram is set up.
2.6: The floodgates are opened; the royal palace is inundated by the surging torrent and collapses.
2.7: Nineveh is stripped, taken captive, and carried into exile. Her maidservants moan like doves and beat their breasts in sorrow.
2.8: The people rush out of Nineveh like water pours out of a broken dam. The officers shout, “Stop! Stop!” but no one turns back.
2.9: Plunder the silver, plunder the gold! Look! There is no end of the treasure — heaps of every precious thing.
2.10: Desolation! Devastation! Destruction! Hearts melting, knees knocking, stomachs churning, faces turning pale.
2.11: What has happened now to the lions’ den where the fierce lions were fed, where the lion and lioness once lived, where the cubs frolicked, cozy and fearless?
2.12: Like a lion, Assyria once killed his prey and tore it to pieces, filling his cave with meat for his mate and her cubs.
2.13: “Behold, I am your enemy,” declares Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies. “I will burn your chariots to ashes, and the sword will slaughter your young lions. No longer will you prey upon the land, and your messengers will announce no more victories.”

3.1: Doomed is the city of bloodshed, embodiment of treachery and thievery, where the murdering never stops!
3.2: Listen to the crack of the whip, the rumble of the chariot wheels, the thunder of horses’ hooves, and charging chariots.
3.3: Horsemen advancing, gleaming swords and glistening spears, hosts of slain, heaps of corpses, dead bodies, too many to count. People stumble over the carcasses.
3.4: This is because you lustfully lured the nations like a wanton whore. You acted so gracefully, yet you are a mistress of witchcraft. You sold entire nations into the sex trade and bewitched whole families into slavery.
3.5: Behold, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, declares to you: “I am your enemy! I will lift up your skirt over your face, and I will make nations gawk at your nakedness and kingdoms at your shame.
3.6: I will pelt you with filth and make you an object of scorn and will treat you with contempt.
3.7: And all who look at you will turn their backs on you and say, ‘Poor Nineveh is a pile of rubble; who will grieve for you? Who will have sympathy for you?’ ”
3.8: Are you any better than Thebes, which once sat by the Nile surrounded by water, her moat of defense, a mighty river?
3.9: Ethiopia and Egypt were her endless strength; Somalia and Libya were her helpful allies.
3.10: Yet the people of Thebes became exiles and were carried off into captivity. Their infants were dashed to pieces on every street corner. They cast lots for her honored men— all the best and brightest were bound in chains and taken captive.
3.11: You will fall into a drunken stupor. You will go into hiding and seek refuge from the enemy.
3.12: All your fortified cities are like fig trees with first-ripe figs: shake the tree and they fall right into the open mouth of the eater.
3.13: Behold, all who remain in the midst of your cities are the women. The borders of your land are wide open to your enemies. Fire will devour your fortresses.
3.14: Go ahead and draw plenty of water and prepare for the siege. Strengthen your defenses. Get mud, trample the clay, make more bricks.
3.15: Yet the fire will devour you there. You will be slaughtered by the sword. It will consume you like locusts. You multiplied like hopping locusts and like swarming grasshoppers.
3.16: Your merchants multiplied until they were more than the stars in the sky. Like locusts they stripped the land, spread their wings, and flew away.
3.17: Your officials were as numerous as grasshoppers, your scribes like a swarm of locusts. On a cold day, they settle on the stone fences, but when the sun appears, they abandon you and fly away; no one knows where they are.
3.18: Emperor of Assyria, your shepherds slumber, your nobles nod off to sleep soundly. All your people are like sheep scattered on the mountains with no one to bring them home.
3.19: There is no remedy for your injuries; your wound is fatal. All who hear the news about you applaud for joy over your downfall. For whoever was untouched by your endless evil?

1.1: This is the vision of Habakkuk the prophet:
1.2: Yahweh, how long must I cry for help and you turn a deaf ear? My heart cries out, “Save us from this brutality!” but you do not save.
1.3: Why do you make me stare at injustice? Why do you tolerate such trouble and wrongdoing? Destruction and violence surround me; strife and conflict are everywhere.
1.4: Therefore, the law is not enforced, and so justice never prevails. The wicked overwhelm the righteous so that justice is perverted.
1.5: “Look at the nations and observe— you’ll be stunned by what you see. For while you watch, I am about to do something so surprising in your days that you would not believe it even if you were told.
1.6: I am raising up the Babylonians to punish you — that fierce and fearsome people, who sweep across the whole earth to seize houses they do not own.
1.7: They are a feared and dreaded people. In their autocratic arrogance, they become a law unto themselves.
1.8: Their horses are swifter than leopards, fiercer than wolves on the prowl at dusk. Their cavalry charges headlong; their horsemen come from afar. They soar swiftly like an eagle swooping to devour.
1.9: Their armies invade, intent on violent conquest. Their terrifying hordes advance like a desert wind and gather prisoners as numerous as grains of sand.
1.10: They are a people who mock kings and scoff at those in authority. They laugh at every stronghold; they pile up earthen siege ramps and capture them.
1.11: Then they hurry on, like the wind that blows by and disappears. They are guilty men who worship their own power as if it were a god.”
1.12: Yahweh, have you not always been the everlasting God? You are my God, my Holy One, who will not die. Yahweh, you have appointed the Babylonians to execute judgment; my Rock, you have raised them up so they can punish us.
1.13: Your eyes are so pure that you cannot stand the sight of evil; nor do you look on wickedness with favor. Why then do you tolerate the treacherous? Why are you so silent while sinners devour those more righteous than themselves?
1.14: Have you only made us like fish, to be caught and killed by the wicked; like swarming schools of fish with no ruler?
1.15: Then the Babylonians pull them up with fishhooks and drag them in with their nets. Gleefully, they gather them up in their dragnets, shouting for joy over their catch.
1.16: They even offer sacrifices and burn incense in honor of their nets, as if these were gods. For their nets enable them to live luxuriously and eat the finest food.
1.17: How long will you allow them to fill and empty their throw nets? Will they forever destroy nations without mercy?

2.1: I will wait at my watchpost and station myself on the tower. I’ll keep watching to see what he’ll say to me and consider the reply when he answers my argument.
2.2: Then Yahweh replied: “Write down the revelation; write it legibly on clay tablets so that whoever reads it may run and explain it to others.
2.3: The vision still awaits an appointed time; it speaks of the end and will not prove to be false. When the appointed time comes, it will happen with breathless haste. Although it may seem slow, just be patient and wait. For it will surely come right on time.
2.4: “Look at the proud, puffed up with pride! They are crooked to the core. But the righteous will live by his faith.”
2.5: “Wealth is deceitful. The proud are full of themselves but have empty souls. They are as greedy as the grave. And just like death itself, they are never satisfied. They gather and grasp for themselves all the wealth of the nations and take all the people captive.
2.6: “All these conquered nations will one day taunt them, saying, ‘You are doomed, you who pile up stolen goods! How long will you amass wealth by extortion?’
2.7: Will not your creditors suddenly arise? Will they not wake up and terrify you? Before you know it, you will become their prey.
2.8: Since you have plundered many nations, the peoples who are left will plunder you. For you have killed many people; you have acted violently against lands and cities and everyone within them.
2.9: “You are doomed, you who enrich your family by cheating others! You build your luxurious home on high thinking you’ll be safe from harm’s reach.
2.10: Your schemes to ruin the lives and homes of others bring shame upon your own house. You are as good as dead for doing this.
2.11: The stones of the wall will cry out to accuse you, and your wooden rafters will echo it.
2.12: “You are doomed, you who build a city with bloodshed and establish it upon evil!
2.13: I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, have decreed: The efforts of the nations are nothing but fuel for the fire, for all they have built will go up in smoke.
2.14: Yet the entire earth is being filled with the revelation of the glory of Yahweh, just as waters fill the sea.
2.15: “You are doomed, you who delight to mix drinks for neighbors, pouring wine from pitchers until they are dead drunk just so that you can gaze on their naked bodies!
2.16: Now you will be drunk with shame instead of honor. Now it is your turn! Drink your fill and let your nakedness be exposed. The cup of punishment that Yahweh holds in his right hand is now coming around to you. Your former glory will be covered with your vomit of disgrace.
2.17: Your violent acts against Lebanon will violently overwhelm you. Since you killed its animals, animals will terrify you. For you have killed many people and acted violently against lands and cities and everyone in them.
2.18: “You are doomed, you who say to a piece of dead wood, ‘Come to life!’ Or to lifeless stone, ‘Get up!’ Can something dead give revelation? Even though it is covered with gold and silver, there is no breath in it. Of what use is an idol carved by a craftsman? Or a metal image that gives misleading oracles? For the one who makes it trusts the work of human hands; a god that cannot even talk.”
2.19: How terrible it will be for you who beg lifeless wooden idols to save you. You ask speechless stone images to tell you what to do. Can an idol speak for God? They may be overlaid with gold and silver, but they are lifeless inside.
2.20: Yahweh is in his holy temple; let everyone on earth be silent before him.

3.1: This is the passionate prayer of Habakkuk the prophet.
3.2: Yahweh, I know the things that have made you famous. I am stunned when I consider your miracles. Do them again in our day! Let this generation experience your mighty deeds. Yahweh, show us your mercy even in this time of turmoil.
3.3: God came from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran. The heavens blazed with the brightness of his glory while the earth echoed his praises.
3.4: The brilliance of his glory is bright as the sun; twin bolts of lightning flash from his hand — there is the hiding place of his power.
3.5: A plague marched in front of him; a consuming pestilence followed at his heels.
3.6: When he stood up, the earth shook. At his glance, nations trembled, mountains crumbled, and age-old hills collapsed, but his paths are everlasting.
3.7: In my vision, I saw the tents of Cushan trembling in distress and the tent curtains of the Midianites shaking in anguish.
3.8: Yahweh, was it the rivers that made you angry or stirred up your rage? Was it the sea that made you furious when you rode your horses and chariots of salvation?
3.9: Your bow is strung and ready for action, and with a word, you commission your arrows to hit their mark. You carved open the earth with rivers.
3.10: The mountains saw you and trembled. Torrential rains flooded the earth; the ocean depths roared and lifted their waves on high.
3.11: Sun and moon stood still in the sky when your speeding arrows flashed and your glittering spear gleamed.
3.12: In your fury you marched across the earth, and in your anger you trampled the nations.
3.13: You came to save your people, to win the victory with your Messiah. You crushed the head of the house of wickedness and stripped him from head to toe.
3.14: You pierced his head with his own arrows when his warriors stormed out to scatter us, gloating as they slaughtered their wretched victims in hiding.
3.15: You trampled the sea with your horses, churning the great waters.
3.16: I hear all this, and my heart pounds; my teeth chatter with fear at the sound. My body goes limp, and my legs tremble. Yet my heart quietly rests. I know the day of trouble is ahead for the people invading us.
3.17: Even if my fig trees do not blossom and my vines grow no grapes, if my olive crop fails and my fields produce no harvest, and even if all my sheep die and I’m left with no cattle in my barn,
3.18: I still have Yahweh, and I will rejoice in him. Yes, I will dance with joy no matter what, for I have a Savior-God!
3.19: Yahweh is the Lord of my strength; he makes my feet sure-footed as a deer bounding upon the high places. These are the lyrics for the conductor of my string ensemble.

1.1: This is the prophetic message Yahweh gave to Zephaniah son of Cushi, grandson of Gedaliah, great-grandson of Amariah, great-great-grandson of Hezekiah. Zephaniah received this message during the time when Josiah, the son of Amon, ruled Judah.
