1.2: “I, Yahweh, declare that I will certainly sweep away every living thing from the land— animals and humans, birds and fish. I will topple the wicked and their idols and sweep away man from the land.”
1.3: "I will sweep away both people and animals alike. Even the birds of the air and the fish in the sea will die. I will reduce the wicked to heaps of rubble, along with the rest of humanity," says the LORD.
1.4: “I will punish Judah and all who live in Jerusalem. I will wipe out every trace of Baal from the land along with the names of the pagan priests or any priest who has turned away from me.
1.5: I will punish those who bow down on their rooftops to worship the sun, moon, and stars and those with divided loyalties who bow before Yahweh and swear allegiance to me but also swear their oaths in the name of their king.
1.6: I, Yahweh, will punish those who have turned their back on me, who do not seek me nor pray for me to guide them.”
1.7: Be silent before the Lord God, for the day of Yahweh is near. “I have prepared a sacrifice and have consecrated my invited guests.
1.8: On the day of Yahweh ’s sacrifice, I will punish the royal family, your officials, and all who dress like pagan priests.
1.9: At that time, I will punish all who worship Dagon and fill the palace of their rulers with violence and deception.
1.10: “I, Yahweh, declare: A cry for help will be heard from the Fish Gate in Jerusalem, wailing from the wealthier, newer part of the city. A loud crash will echo from the hills.
1.11: Wail, you who live in the market area because all the merchants will be dead, and those who weigh out silver will be wiped out.
1.12: “When that time comes, I will search Jerusalem with lamps and punish those stagnating in their self-satisfied smugness. They say in their hearts, ‘ Yahweh is aloof and can do nothing for us, either good or bad.’
1.13: Yet all their hoarded wealth will be looted and their houses leveled. They will build houses but never move in, plant vineyards but never drink the wine.”
1.14: The great day of Yahweh is near, right around the corner, closer than you think and coming fast. How bitter will be the sound of the day of Yahweh, when even the brave warriors weep in anguish.
1.15: It will be a day of wrath, a day of terror and trouble, a day of desolation and distress, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness,
1.16: a day of shofar blasts and battle shouts against fortified cities and all the lofty towers.
1.17: “I will bring such distress on people that they will grope their way like the blind for having sinned against me. Their blood will be poured out like dust, yes, their flesh like dung.
1.18: On that day, I will display my great anger, and none of their silver or gold will save them. My avenging zeal will burn like a fire on that day, to consume the entire land. For I will bring a terrible and sudden end that will destroy everyone living in the land.”

2.1: Go ahead and gather yourselves together, you shameless people! Gather yourselves together and turn back to Yahweh
2.2: before the appointed time arrives. Repent before you are blown away like chaff, which is swept away in a day, before Yahweh pours out on you his fiery anger— the day of Yahweh ’s burning fury.
2.3: All who are meek and humble on earth, seek the mercy of Yahweh. All who obey his commands, pursue righteousness and discover true humility. For maybe, just maybe, Yahweh will shelter you on the day of his anger.
2.4: “For Gaza will be deserted, and Ashkelon devastated. Ashdod will be driven out in broad daylight, and Ekron left desolate.
2.5: Doom to you who live on the seacoast, to the nation of Cherethites! And Canaan, land of the Philistines, the word of Yahweh is bad news for you. I will destroy and annihilate you.
2.6: Your coastal lands will be reduced to pastureland, to grazing grounds for shepherds and folds for flocks.
2.7: Your land will be occupied by the remnant of the people of Judah. During the day, they will find pasture by the sea, and at night, they will rest in the houses of Ashkelon. Yahweh their God will care for them, and make them prosper again.”
2.8: “I, Yahweh, have heard the crude taunts of Moab and the vile insults of the Ammonites as they scorned my people and boasted that they would annex the land of Judah.
2.9: For as surely as I live, I, Yahweh, God of Israel, Commander of Angel Armies, decree: Moab will become like Sodom and the Ammonites like Gomorrah. The remnant of my people will plunder them; the survivors of my nation will possess them. Their lands will become barren forever, a land of nothing but salt pits and piles of weeds.
2.10: This will be the price of their pride, of having taunted and boasted against the people of Yahweh, who commands angel armies.
2.11: I, Yahweh, will be terrifying to them, for I will make all the gods of the earth vanish. And the people of every nation will bow down and worship me wherever they live.”
2.12: “You Ethiopians, too, will be killed by my sword.”
2.13: “I will attack the northern land of Assyria and destroy it all. Nineveh will be left as desolate and dry as a desert.
2.14: It will be nothing more than a resting place for flocks and herds, along with all creatures of every kind. The vulture and owl will nest at night in its ruins. Owls will hoot from the windows, and crows will caw in the doorways— for all their once-fancy cedar woodwork will be exposed to the elements.
2.15: This is the once-proud city, living so happy and carefree and thinking to herself, ‘I am so amazing, and I have no rival!’ Yet look at her now! What has she become? Nothing but a pile of rubble and a lair for wild beasts. Everyone who passes by will hiss with scorn and shake their fists.”

3.1: Doomed is the filthy and foul city— the city of oppression!
3.2: Her people do not listen to the voice of God and will not accept correction. They do not trust in Yahweh anymore and do not want a close relationship with their God.
3.3: Her rulers are roaring lions, and her judges are ravenous wolves who hunt in the evening, too greedy to leave even a bone till the morning.
3.4: Her prophets are proud, reckless impostors. Her priests profane the holy place and openly break the Law.
3.5: In spite of all this, Yahweh the Righteous resides in Jerusalem, and all he does is just and true. Morning by morning, he brings justice to light, and day by day, he never fails. Yet the wicked are shameless.
3.6: “I have destroyed proud nations and toppled their high towers. I filled their streets with rubble so no one walks through them. Their cities have been demolished. Everyone is gone. Not one is left.
3.7: I thought, ‘Certainly, now you will revere me. Now you will yield to my correction.’ Then I would not need to punish them again and destroy their homes. But no, they were just as eager to do whatever was evil.
3.8: “So wait patiently for me,” declares Yahweh. “Wait for the day when I rise to seize the prey. For I have determined to gather the nations and assemble the kingdoms so that they will experience my fury and know how great my anger is. For the land will be consumed by the fire of my avenging zeal.”
3.9: “For then I will change the impure speech of all the people to the pure speech of praise so that all may worship my name together and serve me shoulder to shoulder.
3.10: From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, my worshipers from distant lands will bring me gifts.”
3.11: “When that day comes, you will never again be put to shame over your former acts of rebellion. For I will remove from your midst all who are arrogant and who boast in their self-importance. You will never again strut about in pride on my holy mountain.
3.12: But I will leave a remnant among you: a humble and lowly people who will find their hiding place in the beautiful name of Yahweh.
3.13: They will do no wrong and only speak the truth, nor will they use any form of deceit. They will be content like grazing sheep. They will rest, and no one will frighten them.”
3.14: Go ahead, sing for joy, daughter of Zion. People of Israel, get excited and shout aloud. Rejoice, let blissful praise fill your heart, fair daughter of Jerusalem.
3.15: Yahweh has canceled out his judgments against you. He has turned your accuser away. Yahweh, your King, is here within you, Israel; you have nothing more to fear.
3.16: On that day, the message for Jerusalem will be: Zion, do not yield to fear. Don’t let your heart be discouraged.
3.17: Yahweh, your God, is inside you. He is the Warrior-Savior who takes such delight in you that it will make him leap for joy and shout with great gladness. Yes, he will soothe you with his love. He will sing over you his song of praise.
3.18: “I will remove the sadness over your appointed feasts, and you will not be ashamed about them again.
3.19: Behold, at the right time, I will deal with those who mistreat you. I will rescue the weak and regather the scattered ones. I will turn their shame into praise when I restore their honor across the land.
3.20: On that day, I will be your guide to bring you home; at that time, I will gather you together. You can be sure of this: I will give you a good name, and you will be admired among all the peoples of the earth as I restore your fortunes before your own eyes. I, Yahweh, have spoken.”

1.1: On the first day of the month of Elul during the second year Darius was emperor of Persia, the word of Yahweh was spoken through the prophet Haggai. He delivered this prophecy to the appointed governor of Judah, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and to the high priest, Joshua son of Jehozadak.
1.2: “ Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, says this: ‘These people procrastinate by saying that this is not the right time to finish rebuilding Yahweh ’s house.’ ”
1.3: Then Yahweh spoke the following message to the people using Haggai as his mouthpiece:
1.4: “ Really? Is this the right time for you to be living in your expensive houses while my house lies in ruins?
1.5: So now, I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, say to you: You had better be intentional about the path you choose.
1.6: You have planted much but harvested very little. You fill your plates, but you are never full. You drink but are still thirsty. You put on clothes but not enough to keep warm. You earn wages, but your money burns a hole in your pocket and quickly runs out.
1.7: “I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, repeat: Be intentional about the path you take.
1.8: Now, go up the mountain, cut some timber, and rebuild my house, and I will take pleasure in it and manifest my glory there. It is I, Yahweh, who say so.
1.9: “You hoped for abundant crops, but instead you gathered little. When you brought in your meager harvest, I caused it to spoil. It is I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, asking you, ‘Why?’ It is because my house lies in ruins while each of you runs to his own house.
1.10: That is why the sky has withheld the rain and the ground its crops.
1.11: I have called down drought on the land and hills—your grain, oil, and new wine. It has affected both people and animals and spoiled all your attempts to grow food.”
1.12: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest, and the entire remnant of the people obeyed the voice of Yahweh their God. They recognized that Yahweh their God had sent Haggai to them, so they obeyed his words. And the people were filled with holy awe toward Yahweh.
1.13: Then the messenger of Yahweh, Haggai, spoke Yahweh ’s promise to the people: “I am with you to bless you —declares Yahweh.”
1.14: And Yahweh stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel governor of Judah, the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest, and the spirit of the entire remnant of the people, and they came together to rebuild the temple of Yahweh, their God, the Commander of Angel Armies.
1.15: They began their work on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month.

2.1: In the second year of King Darius, the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the word of Yahweh happened through the prophet Haggai as follows,
2.2: “Go and give this urgent message to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the high priest Joshua son of Jehozadak, and all the remnant of the people:
2.3: “Did anyone from among you see the magnificent glory of the original temple? And how does it look to you now? Does it not seem as nothing in your eyes?
2.4: “I, Yahweh say to you, Zerubbabel, be courageous! Joshua, son of Jehozadak, high priest, be courageous! All you living in the land, take heart! Go to work, for I am with you, says Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies.
2.5: I, Yahweh, will keep the covenant that I made with you when you came out of Egypt. My Spirit is still present among you, so be fearless.
2.6: “For I declare to you: Very soon, I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, will once again shake the heavens and earth, the land and sea.
2.7: “I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, will shake every nation, and the treasures of the nations will flow in, and I will fill this temple with glory.
2.8: “I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, declare to you, all the silver and gold is mine.
2.9: “I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, declare to you, the glory of this new temple will surpass the glory of the original, and I will grant peace and prosperity in this place. “I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, have spoken.”
2.10: In the second year of Darius, on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the word of Yahweh was spoken to the prophet Haggai as follows:
2.11: “I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, say to you: ‘Ask the priests for their ruling on this:
2.12: If someone holds consecrated meat from a sacrifice and carries it in the fold of his priestly robe, could his robe then pass on holiness if it comes into contact with bread, stew, wine, olive oil, or any kind of food at all?’ ” “No,” the priests replied.
2.13: Haggai then said, “If anyone is ritually unclean by contact with a corpse and touches any of these things, would it become unclean?” The priests replied, “Yes, it is unclean.”
2.14: Then Haggai said, “So it is the same with this people. Yahweh declares: ‘The nation is unclean in my eyes. Everything they produce is unclean to me, and everything they offer at the altar is also unclean.’ ”
2.15: “Now consider carefully your recent past before you started rebuilding Yahweh ’s temple.
2.16: Stop and remember what condition you were in. You would come expecting to scoop twenty measures of grain but find only ten. You would come expecting to draw fifty measures of wine from a vat but find only twenty.
2.17: I struck the produce of your labor by sending hail, hot desert winds to wither your grain, and damp winds to make it rot. Yet you still would not return to me —declares Yahweh.
2.18: “Today is the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day the people resumed the building of my temple. So be intentional from today forward.
2.19: The seed is still in the storehouse, isn’t it? Until now, the grapevines, fig trees, pomegranate and olive trees have not produced a harvest, but from now on, I will certainly bless you, and your harvest will be plentiful.”
2.20: On that same day, the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the word of Yahweh happened a second time to Haggai, as follows:
2.21: “Tell these words to Zerubbabel governor of Judah: ‘I am going to shake the heavens and the earth.
2.22: I will topple thrones and destroy the dynasties of foreign kingdoms. I will crash their chariots and their riders. Horses and their riders will die, for their riders will kill one another with the sword.
2.23: I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, declare, when that day comes, I will take you, my servant Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and make you like a signet ring. For I have chosen you to be mine. I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies have spoken.’ ”

1.1: In October of the second year that Darius was emperor of Persia, Yahweh spoke to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, saying,
1.2: “ I, Yahweh, was intensely angry with your ancestors.
1.3: So give the people this message: ‘ Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, says to you: “Come back to me, and I will come back to you,” says Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies.
1.4: Do not be like your ancestors. Long ago my prophets warned them, saying, “Turn your lives around completely and end your evil, wicked ways.” But they refused to listen to me or obey me.
1.5: And where did they end up? And the prophets, did they live forever?
1.6: But my words and warnings, which I gave through my servants the prophets, proved to be true. Your ancestors ignored them, and so they were punished. As a result, they repented, saying, “ Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, has punished us as he warned he would do and as our sinful ways have deserved.” ’ ”
1.7: On February 15 (the month of Shvat), in the second year of Darius’ reign, Yahweh spoke to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo.
1.8: That night I had a vision. Behold, I saw a man sitting on a reddish-brown horse in the shadows of a grove of myrtles. And behind him I saw other horses—some brown, tan, and white with riders upon them.
1.9: There was another angel there who talked with me, and I asked him, “What do these represent, my lord?” And the angel who was talking to me said, “Let me show you.”
1.10: Then the man standing among the myrtles spoke up and said, “These are Yahweh ’s agents sent to patrol the earth.”
1.11: Then the horsemen reported to the angel of Yahweh who stood among the myrtles, “We have been patrolling the land, and indeed, all is peacefully at rest.”
1.12: Yahweh ’s angel then spoke and said, “ Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, you have inflicted your anger on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah for the past seventy years. How many more years will pass before you once again show them that you love them?”
1.13: Yahweh then replied to the angel who was talking to me with kind and comforting words.
1.14: So the angel told me to proclaim these words of Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies: “My heart burns with passion for Jerusalem and Zion,
1.15: but I am deeply angry with the careless and complacent nations. I was only mildly angry with my people, but the nations I used to punish them acted too severely.
1.16: Therefore, I have returned to Jerusalem with mercy and kindness. I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, have decreed to rebuild my house there. Surveyors will stretch my measuring line over Jerusalem to rebuild the city.”
1.17: The angel also told me to proclaim, “I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, decree that my cities will once more overflow with prosperity. I will comfort Zion once again and claim Jerusalem as my own.”
1.18: Then I looked up and had a vision. Behold, I saw four horns.
1.19: I asked the angel who was talking to me, “What do these represent?” And he answered, “These are the four horns that scattered Jerusalem, Judah, and Israel.”
1.20: Then Yahweh opened my eyes to see four conquering craftsmen.
1.21: And I asked, “What are they coming to do?” He replied, “They have come to terrify and hammer out justice among the nations who lifted their horns to completely crush the land of Judah and scatter its inhabitants.”

2.1: Then I looked up again and had another vision. Behold, I saw a man with a measuring line in his hand.
2.2: I asked him, “Where are you going with that?” “To measure Jerusalem,” he replied, “to calculate her width and length.”
2.3: And behold, the angel who was talking with me left, and another angel came out to meet him.
2.4: He said to him, “Run, and tell the surveyor to stop measuring, for Jerusalem will be too full of people and animals to measure or be enclosed by walls.
2.5: So, I, Yahweh, will be a protective wall of fire surrounding her and a radiant glory within her.”
2.6: “Look out! Look out! Flee from Babylon,” declares Yahweh, “for like the four winds of heaven I have scattered you in every direction,” declares Yahweh.
2.7: “Escape, Zion, you who live within the fair city of Babylon!”
2.8: For Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, sent me after glory. And he warns the nations who plundered you: “Whoever touches you, my precious ones, touches the apple of my eye.
2.9: Now behold, I will raise my fist against them to crush them, and those whom they enslaved will plunder them. Then you will know that Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, has sent me.”
2.10: I, Yahweh, declare to you: “It’s time to sing out and rejoice, my daughter Zion, for now I am coming to live among you.”
2.11: At that time, people from many nations will be converted to Yahweh and become his people, and he will live among them. Then you will know that Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, has sent me to you.
2.12: The people of Judah will become Yahweh ’s special people, his inheritance in the holy land, and he will again choose Jerusalem.
2.13: Let everyone be silent before Yahweh, for now he is stirring from his holy dwelling place.

3.1: Then I was shown another vision. I saw Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of Yahweh dressed in filthy clothes. On Joshua’s right was the accuser, standing there ready to prosecute him. The angel of Yahweh said to Satan, “ Yahweh rebukes you, Satan! Yes, Yahweh rebukes you, for he has chosen Jerusalem. And he has rescued Joshua, like a stick snatched out of the fire.”
3.2: And the LORD said to Satan, "I, the LORD, reject your accusations, Satan. Yes, the LORD, who has chosen Jerusalem, rebukes you. This man is like a burning stick that has been snatched from a fire."
3.3: Jeshua's clothing was filthy as he stood there before the angel.
3.4: Then the angel said to those heavenly council members who were standing before him, “Remove Joshua’s filthy clothes.” Then he said to Joshua, “Behold, I have taken your guilt away, and I will clothe you with splendid robes.”
3.5: And I spoke up and requested, “Let them also put a clean turban on his head.” So they dressed him in clean clothes and put on his head a clean turban while the angel of Yahweh stood nearby.
3.6: So the angel of Yahweh solemnly assured Joshua with these words:
3.7: “ Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, declares to you, ‘If you walk in my ways and live in obedience to me, you will preside over my temple and keep watch over my courts. And I will let you come and go in the same way as your fellow council members standing here.’ ”
3.8: “ ‘So listen, high priest Joshua, you and your fellow priests seated here are beautiful symbols of what is to come. Behold, I will reveal my servant, the Branch!
3.9: And behold, I have laid a stone before Joshua, a precious, unique stone with seven eyes. And I will engrave a special inscription on it,’ says Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies. “ ‘And in a single day, I will remove the sin of the people of this land.
3.10: And at that time, everyone will invite his friends to come and have fellowship under their own vine and their own fig tree. I, Yahweh, have spoken.’ ”

4.1: Then the angel who had been explaining the visions came back and roused me as someone awakened from sleep.
4.2: And he asked me, “What do you see?” As I focused my eyes, I replied, “I see a solid gold lampstand with a bowl for the oil on top. It has seven lamps, and each lamp has a golden spout for the wicks.
4.3: And I also see two olive trees overshadowing the lampstand, one on the right and one on the left.”
4.4: So I asked the angel who was talking to me, “My lord, what do these things represent?”
4.5: The angel answered, “Do you not know what they are?” “No, my lord,” I said.
4.6: Here is the message of Yahweh to Zerubbabel: “ You will not succeed by military might nor by your own strength but by my Spirit,” says Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies.
4.7: “And what are you, O mighty mountain? Before you, Zerubbabel, this mountain of obstacles will crumble. Then he will set the capstone in place to shouts of ‘Grace and beauty be upon it!’ ”
4.8: Then another message from Yahweh came to me:
4.9: “With his own hands, Zerubbabel has laid the foundation of this temple, and with his own hands he will finish it. Then you will know that Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, has sent me to you.
4.10: “Those who despise the day of small beginnings will rejoice when they see Zerubbabel holding the plumb line in his hands. “The seven lamps represent the seven eyes of Yahweh that keep a close watch over everything on earth.”
4.11: Then I asked the angel two questions: “What about these two olive trees on each side of the lampstand?
4.12: And what are the two branches from which golden oil flows through the two golden pipes?”
4.13: He replied, “Don’t you know what these are?” “No, my lord,” I answered.
4.14: So he explained, “These branches are the two sons of oil who serve the Lord of all the earth.”

5.1: Then I had another vision. I looked up and saw a flying scroll.
5.2: The angel asked me, “What do you see?” I replied, “I see a flying scroll. It looks about thirty-five feet long and seventeen feet wide.”
5.3: Then he explained to me its meaning: “This scroll contains God’s curse against evildoers sweeping over the whole land. On one side of the scroll, it says that the Lord will banish every thief. On the other side, it says that he will banish everyone who lies using his name.
5.4: Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, declares, ‘I will release this curse, and it will enter the house of the thief and of anyone who lies using my name. The curse will remain in his house until it consumes it—walls, beams, and all.’ ”
5.5: Then the angel who was talking to me appeared and said, “Look at what is coming.”
5.6: I asked, “What is it?” He replied, “It is a barrel, and it is carrying the guilt of all the people of the land of Judah.”
5.7: As I looked, the angel removed the heavy lid made of lead from the barrel, and a woman was seated inside.
5.8: The angel said, “This is Lady Wickedness.” And he shoved her back into the barrel and clamped the lead lid over her.
5.9: I looked up and suddenly two women appeared, soaring swiftly in the sky with outstretched wings like those of a stork. They lifted the barrel high in the sky and flew away with it.
5.10: So I asked the angel who was talking to me, “Where are they taking the barrel?”
5.11: He replied, “To the wicked land of Babylon, where they will build a temple and make a pedestal for it. They will place it there and worship it.”

6.1: Then I looked once more and had another vision. I saw four chariots coming out between two mountains of bronze.
6.2: The first chariot was pulled by reddish-brown horses, the second by black horses,
6.3: the third by white horses, and the fourth by dappled horses—all of them mighty.
6.4: I asked the angel who was talking to me, “What do these represent, my lord?”
6.5: The angel explained, “These are the four winds of heaven. They are being dispatched after standing before the Lord of all the earth.
6.6: The black horses are leaving for the land of the north, the white ones for the west, and the dappled for the land of the south.”
6.7: The strong horses came out eager to patrol the world. He said, “Go and patrol the earth,” and off they went.
6.8: Then he called to me and said, “Watch, the ones going to the land of the north are going to make my Spirit descend upon that region.”
6.9: Then another message from Yahweh came to me:
6.10: “Go at once to the home of Josiah the son of Zephaniah. There you will receive gifts from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who have just arrived among the exiles in Babylon.
6.11: Accept their gifts of gold and silver and make a crown to place on the head of the high priest Joshua son of Jehozadak.
6.12: And say this to him, ‘This is what Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, says: “Behold the man whose name is the Branch! He will branch out and flourish from his place, and he will build Yahweh ’s sanctuary.
6.13: Yes, he will build Yahweh ’s sanctuary and will be clothed with majesty. He will sit on his throne and rule. He will be a priest ruling on his throne. These two offices will flow together with perfect harmony.
6.14: Joshua’s crown will be placed in my temple as a memorial to the donors Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and in recognition of the generosity of Josiah the son of Zephaniah.
6.15: And those in distant lands will come to assist the building of Yahweh ’s sanctuary.” “ ‘When this happens, you will know for certain that Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, has sent me to you. This will happen if you faithfully obey the voice of Yahweh your God.’ ”

7.1: In the fourth year of Emperor Darius, on the seventh of December, Yahweh spoke again to Zechariah.
7.2: Now the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-Melech with a delegation to Jerusalem to pray for the favor of Yahweh.
7.3: So they went to the prophets and priests who were at the Temple of Yahweh and asked them: “For many years, each July we have mourned and fasted. Should we continue to do this?”
7.4: Then Yahweh spoke this message to me:
7.5: “Ask all the priests and the people of the land: ‘For nearly seventy years, you have been fasting and mourning in the fifth and seventh months. Have you truly been doing this to honor me?
7.6: And when you ate and drank, were you not doing it for your own pleasure?
7.7: Did not Yahweh speak these things to you through the prophets in the past? Have you forgotten what he told you when Jerusalem and the surrounding towns were prosperous and secure and when the southland and western foothills were inhabited?’ ”
7.8: Yahweh spoke again to Zechariah, saying,
7.9: “Here is the message of Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies: “Apply the law fairly. “Demonstrate tender love and compassion toward all.
7.10: “Never oppress the widow and the fatherless, the foreigner and the poor. “And do not secretly plot to harm someone.”
7.11: But they would not listen; they turned their backs on him, and they stopped up their ears rather than stopping to hear.
7.12: Their hearts became as hard as a rock. They refused to listen to the teaching of Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies. And they would not hear the words he spoke by his Spirit through the earlier prophets. So Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, became very angry.
7.13: Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, says, “Even when I called for them, they would not listen. Therefore, I would not listen when they prayed to me for help.
7.14: Like a whirlwind, I swept them away to live in distant lands as foreigners.” After they were scattered, the country was left so desolate that it became impassable. What once was a land of delights they turned into a desert of desolation.

8.1: Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, spoke to me, saying,
8.2: “I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, say to you: My heart burns with passion for Zion, and my jealousy for her makes me red-hot with anger toward her enemies.
8.3: “I, Yahweh, have this to say: I will return to Jerusalem and live there on Mount Zion. Then Jerusalem will be known as my faithful city and Zion as my holy mountain, the mountain of Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies.
8.4: “I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, say to you: Men and women will once again sit in the parks and squares of Jerusalem, each with a staff to lean on because of their great age.
8.5: And the parks and squares of the city will bustle with boys and girls playing outside.
8.6: “I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, have this to say: If this seems too marvelous for the remnant of my people to believe today, remember this—is there anything too marvelous for me? For I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, have spoken.
8.7: “Here is what I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, say to you: Behold, I will rescue my people from the countries of the east and the west.
8.8: I will bring them back to live in the heart of Jerusalem, and they will be my beloved people, and I will be their faithful God.
8.9: “This is what I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, have to say: Be encouraged, you who now hear these words spoken by the prophets who were there when the foundation was laid for the house of Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies. May your hearts be brave so that the temple may be built.
8.10: For up till now, there was no money to hire men or animals; neither has there been security for people to come and go because I had turned them against each other.
8.11: But now, I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, will not treat the remnant of this people as I have in the past.
8.12: For now they will plant in peace. Fresh dew will fall from the sky, and the soil will be fertile. Their vineyards will be lush and fruitful. I will grant the remnant of my people all these things.
8.13: Judah and Jerusalem, your names have been used as curses among all the nations, but now you will become the symbol of a blessing. Yes, I will save you to be a blessing, so do not be afraid. Let your hearts be brave!
8.14: “For I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, say to you: Just as I determined to bring calamity when your ancestors made me angry and I showed no pity,
8.15: so now I have determined to treat Judah and Jerusalem well and make them prosperous. So do not be afraid!
8.16: “Here is what you must do: Speak the truth to one another. Pursue justice in your courts, and hand down verdicts that are sound.
8.17: Have no evil scheme in your hearts against one another. Do not take delight in committing perjury, for these are things that I hate, declares Yahweh.”
8.18: Then Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, spoke these words to me:
8.19: “I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, say this to you: Instead of having days of fasting in the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months, the people of Judah are to have cheerful, joy-filled festivals. Simply live together peacefully and love truth.”
8.20: Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, says this, “In the future, people from many nations and cities will come streaming to Jerusalem.
8.21: Citizens of one city will say to the people of another city: ‘We must certainly go and worship Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, and seek his blessing. I am determined to go.’ ”
8.22: Yes, many peoples and many nations will worship Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, in Jerusalem and seek his blessing.
8.23: Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, says this, “In that day, there will be ten men who take hold of the robe of a Jew. They will come from all nations, speaking every language, and will say: ‘We have heard that God is with you! We want to go with you.’ ”

9.1: A prophecy: The weighty message of Yahweh pertains to the region of Hadrach, and it will come to rest upon Damascus. “ Yahweh keeps an eye on every person and on all the tribes of Israel
9.2: and even on Hamath, which borders Damascus, and on Tyre and Sidon with all their great wisdom.
9.3: The people of Tyre have built for themselves a fortress. They have swept up piles of silver like dust and gathered mounds of gold like the dirt of the streets.
9.4: Behold! The Lord will take away all she has, burn her city to the ground, and sink her warships into the sea.
9.5: Ashkelon will see it and be afraid; Gaza will see it and writhe in agony. Ekron will witness the loss of her hopes; the king of Gaza will perish, and Ashkelon will be deserted.
9.6: Foreigners will live in Ashdod. Yes, I will destroy the pride of the Philistine people.
9.7: I will stop them from eating meat with its blood and take the forbidden food from between their teeth. But their remnant, too, will become a part of the people of God, like a clan in Judah. And the people of Ekron will also become a part of God’s people as did the Jebusites.
9.8: I will stand guard before my temple to defend it from all who march against it. No oppressor will overrun them ever again, for now, I am constantly on the alert.”
9.9: “My daughter Zion, let your heart and soul rejoice! Rejoice, my daughter Jerusalem, and shout your cheerful praises! Look! Your King comes to you. He is righteous and fully qualified to save you. Yet he comes to you so humbly, riding on a donkey; sitting meekly on a colt, a young foal of a donkey.
9.10: I, the Lord, will banish war chariots and horses from Israel and Jerusalem. I will break the bows used in war. Your king will proclaim peace and well-being to the nations. His dominion will stretch from sea to sea, from the river to the ends of the earth.
9.11: As for you, Zion, because of my covenant with you sealed with blood, I have set your captives free from the waterless pit of their prison.”
9.12: “Come running back home to your fortress, you hope-filled prisoners! This very day, I vow I will restore to you double blessing for your trouble.
9.13: My people will be my weapons, for I have bent Judah as my bow and made Ephraim my arrow. I will awaken and stir up your sons, Zion, against the sons of Greece. I will use you like a warrior’s sword.”
9.14: Then Yahweh will appear above them, and his arrow will flash like lightning. The Lord Yahweh will sound the shofar and advance in the great storm of his power.
9.15: And Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, will be their shield. Their slinging stones shall conquer and subdue the enemy, spilling their blood like wine from an overfilled bowl, like the blood that stains the corners of the altar.
9.16: On that day, Yahweh their God will rescue them and make a way. For they are like a beloved flock of sheep to him, yes, precious like the gemstones of a diadem that will sparkle throughout his land.
9.17: How beautiful and splendid they will be! Young men will flourish by eating the grain, and the maidens by drinking the new wine.

10.1: Ask Yahweh for rain in the season of the latter rain. For Yahweh is the Thunderstorm-Maker. He will give them the outpouring of rain, causing the grain of the field to flourish.
10.2: The household gods babble nonsense, the fortune tellers see false visions, dreamers peddle delusions and give comfort in vain. Therefore, the people have strayed like scattered, suffering, lost sheep because they have no shepherd.
10.3: “I am enraged at the so-called shepherds, and I will vent my anger and punish the proud leaders. I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, care deeply for my flock, the people of Judah. I will transform them from a shepherdless flock of sheep into brave battle horses of splendor.
10.4: Out of them will emerge the cornerstone and the tent peg. From them will emerge battle bows and warrior captains. Together
10.5: they will be like warriors trampling the foe in battle like mud in the streets. They will fight because Yahweh fights with them; they will defeat and humiliate the horsemen.
10.6: “I will make the people of Judah mighty and the descendants of Joseph victorious. And I will bring them back home because I have compassion on them. They will be as though I had never rejected them, for I am Yahweh their God, and I will answer their prayers.
10.7: The people of Israel will be like warriors. Their hearts will be cheered as though by wine. Their children will see this and be full of joy, and their hearts will celebrate and rejoice in Yahweh.
10.8: “I will whistle to call them home as a shepherd gathers his sheep, for I have redeemed them. And they will be as numerous as ever before.
10.9: Though I sowed my people as seed among the nations, they will remember me in those faraway lands. They will all return and rear their children.
10.10: For I will bring them home from Egypt and gather them back from Assyria; I will lead them back into the land of Gilead and Lebanon, yet even there they will not have enough space.
10.11: “I will cross the turbulent sea of trouble and calm its waves. All the depths of the Nile will dry up. I will humble arrogant Assyria and dismantle the power of Egypt.
10.12: I will make my people mighty in me, and they will walk in my name. I, Yahweh, declare it.”

11.1: Open your borders, Lebanon. Let fire consume your cedar trees.
11.2: Cry in sorrow, cypress, for the towering cedar trees have toppled— the high and mighty ones are destroyed. Wail, oaks of Bashan, for the thick forest has been felled.
11.3: Listen! It’s the sound of the wailing of shepherds. Their glory is gone, their rich pastures destroyed. Listen! It’s the sound of the young lions roaring. The thickets of the Jordan have been ravaged.
11.4: This is what my God, Yahweh, says: “Shepherd the inhabitants of this land, for they are like a flock doomed for slaughter.
11.5: Those who buy them slaughter them without remorse. And the merchants who sell them say, ‘Blessed be Yahweh, I have become rich!’ Even the hirelings—their own shepherds—show no pity for the sheep. I will no longer show mercy to the inhabitants of the land,” declares Yahweh. “Instead, I will cause each one to fall into the clutches of his neighbor and into the clutches of his king. They will devastate the land, and I will not rescue anyone from their power.”
11.6: And likewise, I will no longer have pity on the inhabitants of the land," says the LORD. "I will let them fall into each other's clutches, as well as into the clutches of their king. They will turn the land into a wilderness, and I will not protect them."
11.7: So I became a shepherd for the sheep doomed for slaughter, especially for those sheep who had been trafficked. I took two staffs in my hand; one I named “Affection,” and the other I named “Union,” and I cared for the sheep myself.
11.8: So I removed three shepherds in one month, for I ran out of patience with the sheep-traffickers, and they hated me.
11.9: And I told them, “I am not going to be your shepherd anymore. Those doomed to die can die; those doomed for destruction can perish; and the rest can devour one another.”
11.10: Then I took my staff, “Affection,” and broke it in half to revoke the covenant that I had made with the whole nation of Israel.
11.11: So it was annulled on that day, and the sheep-traffickers, who were watching me, realized that Yahweh was speaking through me.
11.12: Then I said to them, “If it seems right to you, give me my wages; if not, never mind.” So they weighed out my wages: thirty shekels of silver.
11.13: Yahweh said to me, “Now, hand your silver over to the treasury, these thirty pieces of silver—this wonderful sum at which they valued me.” So I took the thirty shekels of silver and handed them over to the treasury in the house of Yahweh.
11.14: Then I broke in half my second staff, “Union,” to symbolize the breaking of brotherly bonds between Judah and Israel.
11.15: Next, Yahweh said to me, “Once again, act the part of a worthless shepherd and take with you the shepherd’s gear.
11.16: For behold, I am now raising up a shepherd in the land who will not care about the lost, who will not go in search of the stray, who will not heal the injured, who will not feed the healthy sheep, but instead, he will eat the meat of the fattest sheep and even tear off their hooves.
11.17: “Doom is ahead for the worthless shepherd who deserts his flock! May the sword strike his arm and gouge his right eye! May his arm shrivel completely and his right eye be totally blind!”

12.1: A prophecy. A message of Yahweh to Israel. “I, Yahweh, the Heaven-Unfolder, the Earth-Foundation-Layer, and the Spirit-Shaper of every human spirit, announce to you:
12.2: “Behold! I am about to make Jerusalem an intoxicating cup filled with the wine of my wrath. Any nation around her who dares to drink from it will stagger and fall. And a siege will be laid against Judah and Jerusalem.
12.3: “In that day, when all the nations join forces against her, I will make Jerusalem like a heavy stone. All who lift it will severely injure themselves.
12.4: “In that day, I will confuse every horse with panic and their riders with madness,” says Yahweh. “ Yes, I will strike the horses of the enemies with blindness, but I will watch over the people of Judah.
12.5: Then the leaders of Judah will say to themselves, ‘The people of Jerusalem are strong because Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, is their God.’
12.6: “In that day, I will make Judah’s leaders like a blazing pot in a pile of dry brush, like a flaming torch in straw. They will destroy in all directions the surrounding nations. The people of Jerusalem will continue to live safely in their own city.
12.7: I, Yahweh, will save the tents of Judah first so that the descendants of David and the people of Jerusalem do not receive more honor than the rest of Judah.
12.8: “In that day, my wraparound presence will protect the people of Jerusalem. And in that day I will transform the weakest among them to become as mighty as David, and the dynasty of David will be like God, like the angel of Yahweh going before them.”
12.9: “I am determined in that day to destroy all the nations who attack Jerusalem.
12.10: But I will pour out over the rulers and people of Jerusalem the Spirit of Grace and the Spirit of Prayer. And they will gaze upon me, the Pierced One. They will mourn for the one they pierced as though for an only child and weep bitterly for him as people weep for a firstborn child.
12.11: In that day, the mourning in Jerusalem will be as great as the mourning for Hadad Rimmon in the Plain of Megiddo.
12.12: And the people of the land will mourn each clan by itself and their women by themselves: The clan of David’s family and their women, the clan of Nathan’s family and their women,
12.13: the clan of Levi’s family and their women, the clan of Shimei’s family and their women,
12.14: and all the rest of the clans and their women.”

13.1: “In that day, I will tear open a flowing fountain for the family of David and the people of Jerusalem—a fountain to wash away sin and impurity.”
13.2: “I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, declare: In that day, I will eliminate idolatry from the land, and no one will remember the names of idols anymore. I will also rid the land of false prophets and unclean spirits.
13.3: Therefore, if anyone continues prophesying falsely, his parents who gave him life will say to him, ‘You must forfeit your life since you speak lies in Yahweh ’s name.’ And even while he is prophesying, his parents who gave him life will pierce him through.
13.4: “In that day, every false prophet will be ashamed to prophesy and share their so-called visions. No longer will false prophets wear the coarse robe to deceive people into thinking they are genuine prophets.
13.5: Instead, they will admit, ‘I am not a prophet. I have been living off the land as a farmer ever since my youth.’
13.6: And if anyone asks him, ‘What are those scars on your back?’ he will reply, ‘I was wounded in the house of my dear friends.’ ”
13.7: “Awake my sword! Strike my shepherd! Strike the man who stands close to me,” declares Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies. “If you strike the shepherd, the sheep will scatter. I will even set myself against the young ones.
13.8: “So it will be, throughout the land,” declares Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies. “Two-thirds of the people will be struck down, and the other third will remain.
13.9: I will cause the remaining third to pass through the fire, to refine them as silver is refined. And I will test them as gold is tested. They will call on my name, and I will answer them; I will say to them, ‘You are my people,’ and they will say, ‘ Yahweh is our God!’ ”

14.1: Behold, Yahweh, will have his day! And Jerusalem, when that day comes, your plunder will be divided in your midst.
14.2: For I will gather all the nations to Jerusalem for battle. The city will be captured, the houses ransacked, and the women raped. Half the people will go into exile, but the rest will be allowed to remain in the city.
14.3: Then Yahweh will intervene and fight against those nations as when he fights on a day of battle.
14.4: On that day, his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem. Then the Mount of Olives will be divided down the middle, forming a wide valley that runs from east to west. So half the Mount will move backward to the north and the other half to the south.
14.5: When this happens, you will escape by way of my newly formed valley, which will extend as far as Azal. You will flee as your ancestors fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. And Yahweh your God will come and all the holy ones with him.
14.6: On that day, there will be no light, neither cold nor frost.
14.7: It will be a unique day, a day known only to Yahweh. There will be no more day and night, and even at evening, it will remain light.
14.8: On that day, living waters will flow from Jerusalem, half toward the Dead Sea, half toward the Mediterranean Sea. And they will flow in the summer and winter.
14.9: Then King Yahweh will rule over the whole world. When that day comes, Yahweh will be the one and only God, and everyone will acknowledge him by one single name.
14.10: The entire land of Judah will be transformed into a fertile plain, from Geba in the north to Rimmon south of Jerusalem. But Jerusalem will remain standing high above the plain from the Benjamin Gate to the site of the first gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king’s winepresses.
14.11: People will live there securely, for the city will never again be doomed to destruction. Jerusalem will be safe to live in.
14.12: And Yahweh will bring a devastating plague upon all the nations who have fought against Jerusalem. Their flesh will rot while they stand on their feet. Their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongues will rot in their mouths.
14.13: And on that day, Yahweh will cause their hearts to panic. Each one will seize his neighbor and strike him. Fighting will break out one against another
14.14: until even the people of Judah will fight against the people of Jerusalem. The people of Jerusalem will gather all the riches of the surrounding nations: vast amounts of gold, silver, and clothing.
14.15: And a similar plague will afflict the horses, mules, camels, donkeys, and all the other animals in the camp of their enemies.
14.16: Afterward, the survivors of all the nations that have attacked the city will return to Jerusalem each year to worship the King of the world, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, and to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.
14.17: And if any of the people groups of the world do not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King of the world, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, no rain will fall upon their land.
14.18: And if the Egyptian people do not make this pilgrimage, then Yahweh will send the same plague he sent the other nations that did not celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.
14.19: This will be the punishment for Egypt and the punishment for all the nations that fail to come up to keep the Feast of Tabernacles.
14.20: When that day comes, the very bells on the horses will have inscribed on them, “Holy to Yahweh.” Even the cooking pots of the house of Yahweh will be as sacred as the sprinkling bowls set before the altar.
14.21: Yes, every cooking pot in Jerusalem and in Judah will be holy to Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, and acceptable to use for anyone who comes to offer a sacrifice. And at that time there will be no merchant in the house of Yahweh, who commands the armies of heaven.

1.1: This is divine revelation —the message Yahweh gave to Israel through Malachi.
1.2: “I, Yahweh, say to you: I have always loved you. “But you ask, ‘How have you shown us your love?’ “I, Yahweh, say to you: Were not Esau and Jacob twins? Yet I have loved Jacob and his descendants
1.3: more than Esau and his descendants, whom I rejected. And I have turned the hill country of Esau into a barren wasteland and left his land to the desert jackals.
1.4: “The people of Edom vow, ‘Though we have been shattered, we will rebuild the ruins.’ “But this is what I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, say: You may build, but I will demolish it again. People will call you ‘The Wicked Land’ and ‘The People under the Perpetual Anger of Yahweh.’
1.5: “ Israel, you will witness this with your own eyes and say, ‘The greatness of Yahweh extends even beyond our own borders.’ ”
1.6: “I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, say to you priests, ‘Sons honor their fathers, and servants respect their masters. Yet if I am your father, why don’t you honor me? If I am your master, why don’t you respect me? You have despised my glorious name.’ “But you ask, ‘How have we despised your name?’
1.7: “You place defiled food on my sacred altar. “Still you ask, ‘How have we defiled you?’ “By treating Yahweh ’s table as though it deserves no respect.
1.8: Is it not wrong to offer your blind, lame, and sick animals as sacrifices to me? Try offering them to your governor! Would he be pleased with you? Would he show you favor?” asks Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies.
1.9: “Now try flattering me with inappropriate sacrifices that I may be gracious to you. When you offer me such sacrifices, do you expect me to show you favor?” asks Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies.
1.10: “It would be far better to halt temple worship altogether and one of you shut the temple gates so that you would not keep lighting worthless fires on my altar. I am not pleased with you, and I will not accept any offering from your hands,” says Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies.
1.11: “From one end of the world to the other, my name will be great among the nations. In every place, incense and a pure offering will be offered to my name. All over the world my name will receive honor,” says Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies.
1.12: “But your actions dishonor me. You profane my name by being bored with the Lord’s table and considering it to be common. You say that what you offer me has no worth.
1.13: You also say, ‘We’re fed up with all this!’ And you turn up your nose in disgust,” says Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies. “You offer me injured, crippled, or diseased animals, but I won’t accept your sacrifices. This is Yahweh speaking to you.
1.14: “A curse rests on the cheat who has a perfect male offering in his flock and vows to give it but then sacrifices a puny, imperfect animal to me. For I am a great King,” says Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, “and my name is to be formidable among the nations.”

2.1: “And now, this is my warning for you priests:
2.2: I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, am speaking to you. If you do not listen and fervently devote your heart to honor my name, then I will send the curse upon you and convert your blessings into curses. Yes, I have already done so since you have not dedicated your heart to honor me.
2.3: “Behold! I will rebuke your descendants. I will smear feces on your faces—the dung from your festival sacrifices—and you priests will be tossed away with the animal waste.
2.4: And then you will know that I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, have sent you this commandment so that my covenant with Levi may endure.
2.5: My covenant with his tribe was a covenant to give them a full, peaceful life. All this I gave to him so that he would revere me, and indeed, he honored me and stood in awe of my name.
2.6: He gave the people solid instruction and spoke nothing false. He walked with me in peace and integrity and turned many from evil.
2.7: “Listen, you priests, descendants of Levi. Your lips should be a gateway to sacred truths when people come to you for instruction because you are the messengers of Yahweh, who rules over all.
2.8: But you have turned from my path, and your teachings have caused many to stumble. You have corrupted the covenant with Levi. So I have caused you to be despised and humiliated before all the people. For you have not followed my ways but have shown partiality in matters of the law. This is Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, speaking to you.”
2.9: "So I have made you despised and humiliated in the eyes of all the people. For you have not obeyed me but have shown partiality in your interpretation of the law."
2.10: Have we not all one Father, the one God who created us? So why do we cheat one another and violate the covenant that God made with our ancestors?
2.11: The people of Judah have been unfaithful. A horrible atrocity has been committed throughout the land and even in Jerusalem. They have married foreign women who worship their strange gods and in this way have defiled Yahweh ’s temple, which he loves.
2.12: May Yahweh punish the one who has done such a despicable thing, whoever he may be, even though he brings offerings to the Lord Almighty. May Yahweh banish his entire family from the community of Israel!
2.13: Another thing you do: You drown Yahweh ’s altar with tears. You weep and wail because he no longer values your offerings or accepts with pleasure what you bring him.
2.14: “Why not?” you ask. It is because you promised before Yahweh to be faithful to the wife you chose in your youth. She is your partner, and you are bound to her by covenant, yet you have betrayed her.
2.15: Has God not made them one with a shared Spirit in their union? And what does he desire but godly children from your union? So guard your spirit and do not be disloyal to the wife of your youth.
2.16: “I, Yahweh, the God of Israel, say to you: ‘He who does not love his wife but hates her and divorces her overwhelms her with cruelty. So guard your spirit and do not abandon her.’ This is Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, speaking to you.”
2.17: You weary Yahweh with your words. Yet you ask, “How have we wearied him?” By saying, “Evildoers are good in the eyes of Yahweh, and he is pleased with them.” And you ask, “Where is the God of justice?”

3.1: “Behold! I am sending my messenger, who will prepare the way before me. Then suddenly, the Lord whom you long for will enter his temple. The messenger of the covenant, your soul’s delight, will certainly come,” says Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies.
3.2: But who can endure the day of his coming? Who will not fall down in worship when the Lord is unveiled? For he will carry out a purifying process. He will be like a refiner’s fire or a launderer’s bleach.
3.3: He will be as a silversmith who sits refining and purifying silver. He will purify the Levites, refining his priests until they are like pure gold and fine silver. Then I, Yahweh, will have those who bring me offerings in righteousness.
3.4: And the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasing to me, as in former times and years past.
3.5: “So I will come near to you and put you on trial. I will be quick to testify against sorcerers, adulterers, and those who lie under oath, against those who cheat workers of their wages, who oppress the widows and orphans and ignore the immigrants but who do not live in awe of me. This is Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, speaking to you.
3.6: Truly, I, Yahweh, have not changed. And you, children of Jacob, you haven’t changed either.”
3.7: “Ever since the time of your ancestors, you have turned away from my laws and evaded them. Return to me, and I will return to you,” says Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies. “But you ask, ‘How do we need to return?’
3.8: “Is it right for people to rob God? Yet you rob me. “But you ask, ‘How could we possibly rob you?’ “You withhold your tithes and offerings.
3.9: You are under a curse—the whole lot of you are guilty of robbing me.
3.10: Bring the full amount of your tithes into the temple treasury so that there may be ample provisions in my house. Test me and see if I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, will fling open the floodgates of heaven for you and pour down upon you an overflowing blessing that you will not be able to contain.
3.11: I will defeat the devourer so that it will not destroy the fruits of your fields, and your vines will be full of grapes,” says Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies.
3.12: “Then all the nations will call you blessed, for you will be a land in which God takes delight. I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, promise you this.”
3.13: “Your harsh, rebellious words are in defiance of me,” says Yahweh. “But you ask, ‘What words are you talking about?’
3.14: “You have said, ‘It’s no use serving God. What do we gain by keeping his requirements and observing these mourning ceremonies before Yahweh?
3.15: But now, we will call proud people blessed. Even evildoers prosper, and those who provoke God escape punishment.’ ”
3.16: Then those who lived in awe of Yahweh began discussing these things, and Yahweh noticed and listened. A scroll of remembrance was written in the presence of Yahweh. It included the names of those who lived in awe of Yahweh and honored his name.
3.17: “They will be mine,” says Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies. “And on the day when I make up my treasured possession, I will show them mercy, just as a compassionate father is gentle with his faithful son.
3.18: And you will once again see that I make a distinction between the righteous and the wicked, between those who serve me and those who do not.”

4.1: “You see, there is a day coming, raging like a fiery furnace. On that day, all the proud and wicked people will burn up like straw thrown into a furnace. Neither stalks nor roots will remain. I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, declare it.
4.2: “But for you who stand in awe at the sound of my name, a new dawn is coming. For the sun of righteousness will rise with healing radiating from its wings. And you will be free and leap for joy like calves released from the stall.
4.3: In the day that I, Yahweh, Commander of Angel Armies, am preparing, you will overcome and trample down the wicked like they were ashes under your feet.”
4.4: “Remember the law of my servant Moses, the commands and instructions I gave him at Mount Sinai for all Israel to obey.
4.5: “Keep watching, for I am sending you the prophet Elijah before that great and fearful day of Yahweh arrives.
4.6: He will return the fathers’ hearts to their children and the children’s hearts to their fathers so that I can come and bless and not strike the land with a curse.”

1.1: This is the scroll of the genealogy of Jesus, the Anointed One, the son of David and descendant of Abraham.
1.2: Abraham had a son named Isaac, who had a son named Jacob, who had a son named Judah (he and his brothers became the tribes of Israel).
1.3: Judah and Tamar had twin sons, Perez and Zerah. Perez had a son named Hezron, who had a son named Ram,
1.4: who had a son named Amminadab, who had a son named Nashon,
1.5: who had a son named Salmon, who, along with Rahab, had a son named Boaz. Boaz and Ruth had a son named Obed, who was the father of Jesse,
1.6: and Jesse had a son named David, who became the king.
1.7: Then David and Bathsheba had a son named Solomon, who had a son named Rehoboam, who had a son named Abijah, who had a son named Asa,
1.8: who had a son named Jehoshaphat, who had a son named Joram, who had a son named Uzziah,
1.9: who had a son named Jotham, who had a son named Ahaz, who had a son named Hezekiah,
1.10: who had a son named Manasseh, who had a son named Amos, who had a son named Josiah,
1.11: who was the father of Jeconiah. It was during the days of Jeconiah and his brothers that Israel was taken captive and deported to Babylon.
1.12: About the time of their captivity in Babylon, Jeconiah had a son named Shealtiel, who had a son named Zerubbabel,
1.13: who had a son named Abiud, who had a son named Eliakim,
1.14: who had a son named Azor, who had a son named Zadok, who had a son named Achim, who had a son named Eliud,
1.15: who had a son named Eleazar, who had a son named Matthan, who had a son named Jacob,
1.16: who was the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary the mother of Jesus, who is called “the Anointed One.”
1.17: So from Abraham to David were fourteen generations, and from David to the Babylonian captivity, fourteen generations, and from the Babylonian captivity to Christ, fourteen generations.
1.18: This is how the birth of Jesus Christ took place. His mother, Mary, had promised Joseph to be his wife, but while she was still a virgin she became pregnant through the power of the Holy Spirit.
1.19: Her fiancé, Joseph, was a righteous man full of integrity and he didn’t want to disgrace her, but when he learned of her pregnancy he secretly planned to break the engagement.
1.20: While he was still debating with himself about what to do, he fell asleep and had a supernatural dream. An angel from the Lord appeared to him and said, “Joseph, descendant of David, don’t hesitate to take Mary into your home as your wife, because the power of the Holy Spirit has conceived a child in her womb.
1.21: She will give birth to a son and you are to name him ‘Savior,’ for he is destined to give his life to save his people from their sins.”
1.22: This happened to fulfill what the Lord had spoken through his prophet:
1.23: Listen! A virgin will be pregnant, she will give birth to a Son, and he will be known as “Emmanuel,” which means in Hebrew, “God became one of us.”
1.24: When Joseph woke from his dream, he did all that the angel of the Lord instructed him to do. He took Mary to be his wife,
1.25: but they refrained from having sex until she gave birth to her firstborn son, whom they named “Jesus.”

2.1: Jesus was born in Bethlehem near Jerusalem during the reign of King Herod. After Jesus’ birth a group of spiritual priests from the East came to Jerusalem
2.2: and inquired of the people, “Where is the child who is born king of the Jewish people? We observed his star rising in the sky and we’ve come to bow before him in worship.”
2.3: King Herod was shaken to the core when he heard this, and not only he, but all of Jerusalem was disturbed when they heard this news.
2.4: So he called a meeting of the Jewish ruling priests and religious scholars, demanding that they tell him where the promised Messiah was prophesied to be born.
2.5: “He will be born in Bethlehem, in the land of Judah,” they told him. “Because the prophecy states:
2.6: And you, little Bethlehem, are not insignificant among the clans of Judah, for out of you will emerge the Shepherd-King of my people Israel!”
2.7: Then Herod secretly summoned the spiritual priests from the East to ascertain the exact time the star first appeared.
2.8: And he told them, “Now go to Bethlehem and carefully look there for the child, and when you’ve found him, report to me so that I can go and bow down and worship him too.”
2.9: And on their way to Bethlehem, the same star they had seen in the East suddenly reappeared! Amazed, they watched as it went ahead of them and stopped directly over the place where the child was.
2.10: And when they saw the star, they were so ecstatic that they shouted and celebrated with unrestrained joy.
2.11: When they came into the house and saw the young child with Mary, his mother, they fell to the ground at his feet and worshiped him. Then they opened their treasure chests full of gifts and presented him with gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
2.12: Afterward they returned to their own country by another route because God had warned them in a dream not to go back to Herod.
2.13: After they had gone, Joseph had another dream. An angel of the Lord appeared to him and said, “Get up now and flee to Egypt. Take Mary and the little child and stay there until I tell you to leave, for Herod intends to search for the child to kill him.”
2.14: So that very night he got up and took Jesus and his mother and made their escape to Egypt
2.15: and remained there until Herod died. All of this fulfilled what the Lord had spoken through his prophet: I summon my Son out of Egypt.
2.16: When Herod realized that he had been tricked by the wise men, he was infuriated. So he sent soldiers with orders to slaughter every baby boy two years old and younger in Bethlehem and throughout the surrounding countryside, based on the time frame he was given from interrogating the wise men.
2.17: This fulfilled the words of the prophet Jeremiah:
2.18: I hear the screams of anguish, weeping, and wailing in Ramah. Rachel is weeping uncontrollably for her children. And she refuses to be comforted, because they are dead and gone.
2.19: After Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared again to Joseph in a dream while he was still in Egypt,
2.20: saying, “Go back to the land of Israel and take the child and his mother with you, for those who sought to kill the child are dead.”
2.21: So he awoke and took Jesus and Mary and returned to the land of Israel.
2.22: But when he heard that Archelaus, Herod’s son, had succeeded him as ruler over all of the territory of Judah, he was afraid to go back. Then he had another dream from God, warning him to avoid that region and instructing him instead to go to the province of Galilee.
2.23: So he settled his family in the village of Nazareth, fulfilling the prophecy that he would be known as the “Branch.”

3.1: It was at this time that John the Baptizer began to preach in the desert of Judah. His message was this:
3.2: “Heaven’s kingdom is about to appear—so you’d better keep turning away from evil and turn back to God!”
3.3: Isaiah was referring to John when he prophesied: A thunderous voice! One will be crying out in the wilderness, “Prepare yourself for the Lord’s coming and level a straight path inside your hearts for him.”
3.4: Now, John wore clothing made from camel’s hair, tied at his waist with a leather strap, and his food consisted of dried locusts and wild honey.
3.5: A steady stream of people from Jerusalem, all the surrounding countryside, and the region near the Jordan came out to the wilderness to be baptized by him.
3.6: And while they were publicly confessing their sins, he would immerse them in the Jordan River.
3.7: But when he saw many coming from among the wealthy elite of Jewish society and many of the religious leaders known as Pharisees coming to witness the baptism, he began to denounce them, saying, “You offspring of vipers! Who warned you to slither away like snakes from the fire of God’s judgment?
3.8: You must prove your repentance by a changed life.
3.9: And don’t presume you can get away with merely saying to yourselves, ‘But we’re Abraham’s descendants!’ For I tell you, God can awaken these stones to become sons of Abraham!
3.10: The axe is now ready to cut down the trees at their very roots. Every fruitless, rotten tree will be chopped down and thrown into the fire.
3.11: Those who repent I baptize with water, but there is coming a man after me who is more powerful than I. In fact, I’m not even worthy enough to pick up his sandals. He will submerge you into union with the Spirit of Holiness and with a raging fire!
3.12: He comes with a winnowing fork in his hands and comes to his threshing floor to sift what is worthless from what is pure. And he is ready to sweep out his threshing floor and gather his wheat into his granary, but the straw he will burn up with a fire that can’t be extinguished!”
3.13: Then Jesus left Galilee to come to the Jordan to be baptized by John.
3.14: But when he waded into the water, John resisted him, saying, “Why are you doing this? I’m the one who needs to be baptized by you, and yet you come to be baptized by me?”
3.15: Jesus replied, “It is only right to do all that God requires.” Then John baptized Jesus.
3.16: And as Jesus rose up out of the water, the heavenly realm opened up over him and he saw the Holy Spirit descend out of the heavens and rest upon him in the form of a dove.
3.17: Then suddenly the voice of the Father shouted from the sky, saying, “This is my Son—the Beloved! My greatest delight is in him.”

4.1: Afterward, the Holy Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness to experience the ordeal of testing by the accuser.
4.2: And after fasting for forty days, Jesus was extremely hungry.
4.3: Then the tempter came to him and said, “How can you possibly be the Son of God and go hungry? Just command these stones to be turned into loaves of bread.”
4.4: He answered, “The Scriptures say: Bread alone will not satisfy, but true life is found in every word that constantly goes forth from God’s mouth.”
4.5: Then the accuser transported Jesus to the holy city of Jerusalem and perched him at the highest point of the temple
4.6: and said to him, “If you’re really God’s Son, jump, and the angels will catch you. For it is written in the Scriptures: He will command his angels to protect you and they will lift you up so that you won’t even bruise your foot on a rock.”
4.7: Once again Jesus said to him, “The Scriptures say: You must never put the Lord your God to a test.”
4.8: And the third time the accuser lifted Jesus up onto a very high mountain range and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and all the splendor that goes with it.
4.9: “All of these kingdoms I will give to you,” the accuser said, “if only you will kneel down before me and worship me.”
4.10: But Jesus said, “Go away, Satan! For the Scriptures say: Kneel before the Lord your God and worship only him.”
4.11: At once the accuser left him, and angels suddenly gathered around Jesus to minister to his needs.
4.12: When Jesus heard that John the Baptizer had been thrown into prison, he went back into Galilee.
4.13: Jesus moved from Nazareth to make his home in Capernaum, which is by Lake Galilee in the land of Zebulun and Naphtali.
4.14: He did this to make the prophecy of Isaiah come true:
4.15: Listen, you who live in the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, along the road to the sea and on the other side of the Jordan, and Galilee—the land of the Gentiles!
4.16: You who spend your days shrouded in darkness can now say, “We have seen a brilliant Light.” And those who live in the dark shadow land of death can now say, “The Dawning Light arises on us.”
4.17: From that time on Jesus began to proclaim his message with these words: “Keep turning away from your sins and come back to God, for heaven’s kingdom realm is now accessible.”
4.18: As he was walking by the shore of Lake Galilee, Jesus noticed two fishermen who were brothers. One was nicknamed Keefa (later called Peter), and the other was Andrew, his brother. Watching as they were casting their nets into the water,
4.19: Jesus called out to them and said, “Come and follow me, and I will transform you into men who catch people for God.”
4.20: Immediately they dropped their nets and left everything behind to follow Jesus.
4.21: Leaving there, Jesus found three other men sitting in a boat, mending their nets. Two were brothers, Jacob and John, and they were with their father, Zebedee. Jesus called Jacob and John to his side and said to them, “Come and follow me.”
4.22: And at once they left their boat and their father, and began to follow Jesus.
4.23: Jesus ministered from place to place throughout all of the province of Galilee. He taught in the synagogues, preaching the wonderful news of the kingdom and healing every kind of sickness and disease among the people.
4.24: His fame spread throughout all Syria! Many people who were in pain and suffering with every kind of illness were brought to Jesus for their healing—epileptics, paralytics, and those tormented by demonic powers were all set free. Everyone who was brought to Jesus was healed!
4.25: This resulted in massive crowds of people following him, including people from Galilee, Jerusalem, the land of Judah, the region of the Ten Cities known as the Decapolis, and beyond the Jordan River.

5.1: One day Jesus saw a vast crowd of people gathering to hear him, so he went up the slope of a hill and sat down. With his followers and disciples spread over the hillside,
5.2: Jesus began to teach them:
5.3: “What happiness comes to you when you feel your spiritual poverty! For yours is the realm of heaven’s kingdom.
5.4: “What delight comes to you when you wait upon the Lord! For you will find what you long for.
5.5: “What blessing comes to you when gentleness lives in you! For you will inherit the earth.
5.6: “How enriched you are when you crave righteousness! For you will be satisfied.
5.7: “How blessed you are when you demonstrate tender mercy! For tender mercy will be demonstrated to you.
5.8: “What bliss you experience when your heart is pure! For then your eyes will open to see more and more of God.
5.9: “How joyful you are when you make peace! For then you will be recognized as a true child of God.
5.10: “How enriched you are when persecuted for doing what is right! For then you experience the realm of heaven’s kingdom.
5.11: “How blessed you are when people insult and persecute you and speak all kinds of cruel lies about you because of your love for me!
5.12: So leap for joy—since your heavenly reward is great. For you are being rejected the same way the prophets were before you.
5.13: “Your lives are like salt among the people. But if you, like salt, become bland, how can your ‘saltiness’ be restored? Flavorless salt is good for nothing and will be thrown out and trampled on by others.
5.14: “Your lives light up the world. For how can you hide a city that stands on a hilltop?
5.15: And who would light a lamp and then hide it in an obscure place? Instead, it’s placed where everyone in the house can benefit from its light.
5.16: So don’t hide your light! Let it shine brightly before others, so that your commendable works will shine as light upon them, and then they will give their praise to your Father in heaven.”
5.17: “If you think I’ve come to set aside the law of Moses or the writings of the prophets, you’re mistaken. I have come to bring to perfection all that has been written.
5.18: Indeed, I assure you, as long as heaven and earth endure, not even the smallest detail of the Law will be done away with until its purpose is complete.
5.19: So whoever violates even the least important of the commandments, and teaches others to do so, will be called least in heaven’s kingdom. But whoever obeys them and teaches their truths to others will be called great in heaven’s kingdom.
5.20: For I tell you, unless your lives are more pure and full of integrity than the religious scholars and the Pharisees, you will never enter heaven’s kingdom.”
5.21: “You’re familiar with the commandment taught to those of old: ‘Do not murder or you will be judged.’
5.22: But I’m telling you, if you hold anger in your heart toward a fellow believer, you are subject to judgment. And whoever demeans and insults a fellow believer is answerable to the congregation. And whoever calls down curses upon a fellow believer is in danger of being sent to a fiery hell.
5.23: “So then, if you are presenting a gift before the altar and suddenly you remember a quarrel you have with a fellow believer,
5.24: leave your gift there in front of the altar and go at once to apologize to the one who is offended. Then, after you have reconciled, come to the altar and present your gift.
5.25: It is always better to come to terms with the one who wants to sue you before you go to trial, or you may be found guilty by the judge, and he will hand you over to the officers, who will throw you into prison.
5.26: Believe me, you won’t get out of prison until you have paid the full amount!”
5.27: “Your ancestors have been taught, ‘Never commit adultery.’
5.28: However, I say to you, if you look with lust in your eyes at a woman who is not your wife, you’ve already committed adultery in your heart.
5.29: If your right eye seduces you to fall into sin, then go blind in your right eye! For you’re better off losing sight in one eye than to have your whole body thrown into hell.
5.30: And if your right hand entices you to sin, let it go limp and useless! For you’re better off losing a part of your body than to have it all thrown into hell.
5.31: “It has been said, ‘Whoever divorces his wife must give her legal divorce papers.’
5.32: However, I say to you, if anyone divorces his wife for any reason, except for infidelity, he causes her to commit adultery, and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.”
5.33: “Again, your ancestors were taught, ‘Never swear an oath that you don’t intend to keep, but keep your vows to the Lord God.’
