5.34: However, I say to you, don’t bind yourself by taking an oath at all. Don’t swear by heaven, for heaven is where God’s throne is placed.
5.35: Don’t swear an oath by the earth, because it is the rug under God’s feet, and not by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the Great King.
5.36: And why would you swear by your own head, because it’s not in your power to turn a single hair white or black? But just let your words ring true.
5.37: A simple ‘Yes’ or ‘No’ will suffice. Anything beyond this springs from a deceiver.
5.38: “Your ancestors have also been taught, ‘Take an eye in exchange for an eye and a tooth in exchange for a tooth.’
5.39: However, I say to you, don’t repay an evil act with another evil act. But whoever insults you by slapping you on the right cheek, turn the other to him as well.
5.40: If someone is determined to sue you for your coat, give him the shirt off your back as a gift in return.
5.41: And should people in authority take advantage of you, do more than what they demand.
5.42: Learn to generously share what you have with those who ask for help, and don’t close your heart to the one who comes to borrow from you.”
5.43: “Your ancestors have also been taught ‘Love your neighbors and hate the one who hates you.’
5.44: However, I say to you, love your enemy, bless the one who curses you, do something wonderful for the one who hates you, and respond to the very ones who persecute you by praying for them.
5.45: For that will reveal your identity as children of your heavenly Father. He is kind to all by bringing the sunrise to warm and rainfall to refresh whether a person does what is good or evil.
5.46: What reward do you deserve if you only love the loveable? Don’t even the tax collectors do that?
5.47: How are you any different from others if you limit your kindness only to your friends? Don’t even the ungodly do that?
5.48: Since you are children of a perfect Father in heaven, become perfect like him.”

6.1: “Examine your motives to make sure you’re not showing off when you do your good deeds, only to be admired by others; otherwise, you will lose the reward of your heavenly Father.
6.2: So when you give to the poor, don’t announce it and make a show of it just to be seen by people, like the hypocrites in the streets and in the marketplace. They’ve already received their reward!
6.3: But when you demonstrate generosity, do it with pure motives and without drawing attention to yourself.
6.4: Give secretly and your Father, who sees all you do, will reward you openly.”
6.5: “Whenever you pray, be sincere and not like the pretenders who love the attention they receive while praying before others in the meetings and on street corners. Believe me, they’ve already received their reward.
6.6: But whenever you pray, go into your innermost chamber and be alone with Father God, praying to him in secret. And your Father, who sees all you do, will reward you openly.
6.7: When you pray, there is no need to repeat empty phrases, praying like the Gentiles do, for they expect God to hear them because of their many words.
6.8: There is no need to imitate them, since your Father already knows what you need before you ask him.
6.9: Pray like this: ‘Our Beloved Father, dwelling in the heavenly realms, may the glory of your name be the center on which our lives turn.
6.10: Manifest your kingdom realm, and cause your every purpose to be fulfilled on earth, just as it is in heaven.
6.11: We acknowledge you as our Provider of all we need each day.
6.12: Forgive us the wrongs we have done as we ourselves release forgiveness to those who have wronged us.
6.13: Rescue us every time we face tribulation and set us free from evil. For you are the King who rules with power and glory forever. Amen.’
6.14: “ And when you pray, make sure you forgive the faults of others so that your Father in heaven will also forgive you.
6.15: But if you withhold forgiveness from others, your Father withholds forgiveness from you.”
6.16: “When you fast, don’t look gloomy and pretend to be spiritual. They want everyone to know they’re fasting, so they appear in public looking miserable and disheveled. Believe me, they’ve already received their reward.
6.17: When you fast, don’t let it be obvious, but instead, wash your face and groom yourself and realize that your Father in the secret place is the one who is watching all that you do in secret and will continue to reward you.”
6.18: Then no one will suspect you are fasting, except your Father, who knows what you do in secret. And your Father, who knows all secrets, will reward you.
6.19: “Don’t keep hoarding for yourselves earthly treasures that can be stolen by thieves. Material wealth eventually rusts, decays, and loses its value.
6.20: Instead, stockpile heavenly treasures for yourselves that cannot be stolen and will never rust, decay, or lose their value.
6.21: For your heart will always pursue what you esteem as your treasure.
6.22: “The eyes of your spirit allow revelation-light to enter into your being. If your heart is unclouded, the light floods in!
6.23: But if your eyes are focused on money, the light cannot penetrate and darkness takes its place. How profound will be the darkness within you if the light of truth cannot enter!
6.24: “How could you worship two gods at the same time? You will have to hate one and love the other, or be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t worship the true God while enslaved to the god of money!”
6.25: “This is why I tell you to never be worried about your life, for all that you need will be provided, such as food, water, clothing—everything your body needs. Isn’t there more to your life than a meal? Isn’t your body more than clothing?
6.26: “Consider the birds—do you think they worry about their existence? They don’t plant or reap or store up food, yet your heavenly Father provides them each with food. Aren’t you much more valuable to your Father than they?
6.27: So, which one of you by worrying could add anything to your life?
6.28: “And why would you worry about your clothing? Look at all the beautiful flowers of the field. They don’t work or toil,
6.29: and yet not even Solomon in all his splendor was robed in beauty like one of these!
6.30: So if God has clothed the meadow with hay, which is here for such a short time and then dried up and burned, won’t he provide for you the clothes you need—you of little faith?
6.31: “So then, forsake your worries! Why would you say, ‘What will we eat?’ or ‘What will we drink?’ or ‘What will we wear?’
6.32: For that is what the unbelievers chase after. Doesn’t your heavenly Father already know the things your bodies require?
6.33: “So above all, constantly seek God’s kingdom and his righteousness, then all these less important things will be given to you abundantly.
6.34: Refuse to worry about tomorrow, but deal with each challenge that comes your way, one day at a time. Tomorrow will take care of itself.”

7.1: “Refuse to be a critic full of bias toward others, and you will not be judged.
7.2: For you’ll be judged by the same standard that you’ve used to judge others. The measurement you use on them will be used on you.
7.3: Why would you focus on the flaw in someone else’s life and fail to notice the glaring flaws of your own?
7.4: How could you say to your friend, ‘Let me show you where you’re wrong,’ when you’re guilty of even more?
7.5: You’re being hypercritical and a hypocrite! First acknowledge and deal with your own ‘blind spots,’ and then you’ll be capable of dealing with the ‘blind spot’ of your friend.
7.6: “Who would hang earrings on a dog’s ear or throw pearls in front of wild pigs? They’ll only trample them under their feet and then turn around and tear you to pieces!
7.7: “Ask, and the gift is yours. Seek, and you’ll discover. Knock, and the door will be opened for you.
7.8: For every persistent one will get what he asks for. Every persistent seeker will discover what he longs for. And everyone who knocks persistently will one day find an open door.
7.9: “Do you know of any parent who would give his hungry child, who asked for food, a plate of rocks instead?
7.10: Or when asked for a piece of fish, what parent would offer his child a snake instead?
7.11: If you, imperfect as you are, know how to lovingly take care of your children and give them what’s best, how much more ready is your heavenly Father to give wonderful gifts to those who ask him?”
7.12: “In everything you do, be careful to treat others in the same way you’d want them to treat you, for that is the essence of all the teachings of the Law and the Prophets.
7.13: Enter through the narrow gate because the wide gate and broad path is the way that leads to destruction—nearly everyone chooses that crowded road!
7.14: The narrow gate and the difficult way leads to eternal life—so few even find it!”
7.15: “Constantly be on your guard against phony prophets. They come disguised as lambs, appearing to be genuine, but on the inside they are like wild, ravenous wolves!
7.16: You can spot them by their actions, for the fruits of their character will be obvious. You won’t find sweet grapes hanging on a thorn bush, and you’ll never pick good fruit from a tumbleweed.
7.17: So if the tree is good, it will produce good fruit; but if the tree is bad, it will bear only rotten fruit and deserves to be cut down and burned.
7.18: A good tree can't produce bad fruit, and a bad tree can't produce good fruit.
7.19: So every tree that does not produce good fruit is chopped down and thrown into the fire.
7.20: You’ll know them by the obvious fruit of their lives and ministries.”
7.21: “Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter into heaven’s kingdom. It is only those who persist in doing the will of my heavenly Father.
7.22: On the day of judgment many will say to me, ‘Lord, Lord, don’t you remember us? Didn’t we prophesy in your name? Didn’t we cast out demons and do many miracles in your name?’
7.23: But I will have to say to them, ‘Go away from me, you lawless rebels! I’ve never been joined to you!’
7.24: “Everyone who hears my teaching and applies it to his life can be compared to a wise man who built his house on an unshakable foundation.
7.25: When the rains fell and the flood came, with fierce winds beating upon his house, it stood firm because of its strong foundation.
7.26: “But everyone who hears my teaching and does not apply it to his life can be compared to a foolish man who built his house on sand.
7.27: When it rained and rained and the flood came, with wind and waves beating upon his house, it collapsed and was swept away.”
7.28: By the time Jesus finished speaking, the crowds were awestruck by his teaching,
7.29: because his words carried such great authority, quite unlike the religious scholars.

8.1: After he came down from teaching on the hillside, massive crowds began following him.
8.2: Suddenly, a leper walked up to Jesus and threw himself down before him in worship and said, “Lord, you have the power to heal me . . . if you really want to.”
8.3: Jesus reached out his hand and touched the leper and said, “Of course I want to heal you—be healed!” And instantly, all signs of leprosy disappeared!
8.4: Then Jesus said to him, “Don’t speak to anyone, but go at once and find a priest and show him what has happened to you. Make sure to take the offering Moses commanded so he can certify your healing.”
8.5: When Jesus entered the village of Capernaum, a captain in the Roman army approached him, asking for a miracle.
8.6: “Lord,” he said, “I have a son who is lying in my home, paralyzed and suffering terribly.”
8.7: Jesus responded, “I will go with you and heal him.”
8.8: But the Roman officer interjected, “Lord, who am I to have you come into my house? I understand your authority, for I too am a man who walks under authority and have authority over soldiers who serve under me. I can tell one to go and he’ll go, and another to come and he’ll come. I command my servants and they’ll do whatever I ask. So I know that all you need to do is to stand here and command healing over my son and he will be instantly healed.”
8.9: I know, because I am under the authority of my superior officers and I have authority over my soldiers. I only need to say, 'Go,' and they go, or 'Come,' and they come. And if I say to my slaves, 'Do this or that,' they do it."
8.10: Jesus was astonished when he heard this and said to those who were following him, “He has greater faith than anyone I’ve encountered in Israel!
8.11: Listen to what I am about to tell you. Multitudes of Gentiles will stream from the east and the west, to enter into the heavenly kingdom with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
8.12: But many Israelites, born to be heirs of the kingdom, will be turned away and banished into the darkness where there will be bitter weeping and unbearable anguish.”
8.13: Then Jesus turned to the Roman officer and said, “Go home. All that you have believed for will be done for you!” And his son was healed at that very moment.
8.14: Then Jesus entered Peter’s home and found Peter’s mother-in-law bedridden, severely ill with a fever.
8.15: The moment Jesus touched her hand she was healed! Immediately she got up and began to make dinner for them.
8.16: That evening the people brought to him many who were demonized. And by Jesus only speaking a word of healing over them, they were totally set free from their torment, and everyone who was sick received their healing!
8.17: In doing this, Jesus fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah: He put upon himself our weaknesses, and he carried away our diseases and made us well.
8.18: At the sight of large crowds gathering around him, Jesus gave orders to his disciples to get ready to sail back over to the other side of the lake.
8.19: Just then, a religious scholar approached him and said, “Teacher, I’ll follow you wherever you go!”
8.20: Jesus replied, “Foxes have dens, birds have nests, but the Son of Man has no true home in this world.”
8.21: Then another man spoke up and said, “Lord, I’ll follow you, but first I must take care of my aged father and bury him when he dies.”
8.22: But Jesus said to him, “Now is the time to follow me, and let those who are dead bury their own dead.”
8.23: They all got into a boat and began to cross over to the other side of the lake. And Jesus, exhausted, fell asleep.
8.24: Suddenly a violent storm developed, with waves so high the boat was about to be swamped. Yet Jesus continued to sleep soundly.
8.25: The disciples woke him up, saying, “Save us, Lord! We’re going to die!”
8.26: But Jesus reprimanded them. “Why are you gripped with fear? Where is your faith?” Then he stood and rebuked the storm, saying, “Be still!” And instantly it became perfectly calm.
8.27: The disciples were astonished by this miracle and said to one another, “Who is this Man? Even the wind and waves obey his Word.”
8.28: When they arrived on the other side of the lake, in the region of the Gadarenes, two demonized men confronted Jesus. They lived among the tombs of a cemetery and were considered so extremely violent that no one felt safe passing through that area.
8.29: The demons screamed at Jesus, shouting, “Son of God, what do you want with us? Leave us alone! Have you come to torment us before the appointed time?”
8.30: There was a large herd of pigs feeding nearby.
8.31: And the demons pleaded, “If you cast us out, send us into that herd of pigs.”
8.32: Jesus commanded, “Then go!” And at once the demons came out of the men and went into the pigs. Then the entire herd of crazed pigs stampeded down the steep slope and fell into the water and drowned.
8.33: The men who were herding the pigs fled to the nearby town and informed the people of all that had happened to the demonized men.
8.34: Then everyone from the town went out to confront Jesus and urged him to go away and leave them alone.

9.1: Jesus got into the boat and returned to what was considered his hometown, Capernaum.
9.2: Just then some people brought a paraplegic man to him, lying on a sleeping mat. When Jesus perceived the strong faith within their hearts, he said to the paralyzed man, “My son, be encouraged, for your sins have been forgiven.”
9.3: These words prompted some of the religious scholars to think, “Why, that’s nothing but blasphemy!”
9.4: Jesus supernaturally perceived their thoughts, and said to them, “Why do you carry such evil in your hearts?
9.5: Which is easier to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or, ‘Stand up and walk!’?
9.6: But now, to convince you that the Son of Man has been given authority to forgive sins, I say to this man, ‘Stand up, pick up your mat, and walk home.’ ”
9.7: Immediately the man sprang to his feet and left for home.
9.8: When the crowds witnessed this miracle, they were awestruck. They shouted praises to God because he had given such authority to human beings.
9.9: As Jesus left Capernaum he came upon a tax-collecting station, where a Jewish man named Matthew was collecting taxes for the Romans. “Come, follow me,” Jesus said to him. Immediately Matthew jumped up and began to follow Jesus.
9.10: Jesus went to Matthew’s house and made himself at home. Many other tax collectors and outcasts of society were invited to eat with Jesus and his disciples.
9.11: When those known as the Pharisees saw what was happening, they were indignant, and they kept asking Jesus’ disciples, “Why would your Master dine with such lowlifes?”
9.12: When Jesus overheard this, he spoke up and said, “Healthy people don’t need to see a doctor, but the sick will go for treatment.”
9.13: Then he added, “Now you should go and study the meaning of the verse: I want you to show mercy, not just offer me a sacrifice. For I have come to invite the outcasts of society and sinners, not those who think they are already on the right path.”
9.14: The disciples of John the Baptizer approached Jesus with this question: “Why is it that we and the Pharisees fast regularly, but not your disciples?”
9.15: Jesus replied, “How can the sons of the bridal chamber grieve when the Bridegroom is next to them? But the days of fasting will come when the Bridegroom is taken away from them.
9.16: And who would mend worn-out clothing with new fabric? When the new cloth shrinks it will rip, making the hole worse than before.
9.17: And who would pour fresh, new wine into an old wineskin? Eventually the wine will ferment and make the wineskin burst, losing everything—the wine is spilled and the wineskin ruined. Instead, new wine is always poured into a new wineskin so that both are preserved.”
9.18: While Jesus was still speaking, an influential Jewish leader approached and knelt before him, saying, “Help me! My daughter has just died. Please come and place your hand upon her so that she will live again.”
9.19: So Jesus and his disciples got up and went with him.
9.20: Suddenly, a woman came from behind Jesus and touched the tassel of his prayer shawl for healing. She had been suffering from continual bleeding for twelve years, but had faith that Jesus could heal her.
9.21: For she kept saying to herself, “If I could only touch his prayer shawl I would be healed.”
9.22: Just then Jesus turned around and looked at her and said, “My daughter, be encouraged. Your faith has healed you.” And instantly she was healed!
9.23: When Jesus finally entered the home of the Jewish leader, he saw a noisy crowd of mourners, wailing and playing a funeral dirge on their flutes.
9.24: He told them, “You must leave, for the little girl is not dead; she’s only asleep.” Then everyone began to ridicule him.
9.25: After he made the crowd go outside, he went into the girl’s room and gently took hold of her hand. She immediately stood to her feet!
9.26: And the news of this incredible miracle spread everywhere.
9.27: As Jesus left the house, two blind men began following him, shouting out over and over, “Son of David, show us mercy and heal us!”
9.28: And they followed him right into the house where Jesus was staying. So Jesus asked them, “Do you believe that I have the power to restore sight to your eyes?” They replied, “Yes Lord, we believe!”
9.29: Then Jesus put his hands over their eyes and said, “You will have what your faith expects!”
9.30: And instantly their eyes opened—they could see! Then Jesus warned them sternly, “Make sure that you tell no one what just happened!”
9.31: But unable to contain themselves, they went out and spread the news everywhere!
9.32: While they were leaving, some people brought before Jesus a demonized man who couldn’t speak.
9.33: Jesus cast the demon out of him, and immediately the man began to speak plainly. The crowds marveled in astonishment, saying, “We’ve never seen miracles like this in Israel!”
9.34: But the Pharisees kept saying, “The chief of demons is helping him drive out demons.”
9.35: Jesus walked throughout the region with the joyful message of God’s kingdom realm. He taught in their meeting houses, and wherever he went he demonstrated God’s power by healing every kind of disease and illness.
9.36: When he saw the vast crowds of people, Jesus’ heart was deeply moved with compassion, because they seemed weary and helpless, like wandering sheep without a shepherd.
9.37: He turned to his disciples and said, “The harvest is huge and ripe! But there are not enough harvesters to bring it all in.
9.38: As you go, plead with the Owner of the Harvest to thrust out many more reapers to harvest his grain!”

10.1: Jesus gathered his twelve disciples and imparted to them authority to cast out demons and to heal every sickness and every disease.
10.2: Now, these are the names of the twelve apostles: first, Simon, who is nicknamed Peter, and Andrew, his brother. And then Jacob and John, sons of Zebedee.
10.3: Next were Phillip and Bartholomew; then Thomas and Matthew, the tax collector; Jacob the son of Alphaeus; Thaddeus;
10.4: Simon, the former member of the Zealot party, and Judas the locksmith, who eventually betrayed Jesus.
10.5: Jesus sent out the Twelve with these instructions: “Don’t go into any Gentile or Samaritan territory.
10.6: Go instead and find the lost sheep among the people of Israel.
10.7: And as you go, preach this message: ‘Heaven’s kingdom realm is accessible, close enough to touch.’
10.8: You must continually bring healing to lepers and to those who are sick, and make it your habit to break off the demonic presence from people, and raise the dead back to life. Freely you have received the power of the kingdom, so freely release it to others.
10.9: You won’t need a lot of money.
10.10: Travel light, and don’t even pack an extra change of clothes in your backpack. Trust God for everything, because the one who works for him deserves to be provided for.
10.11: “Whatever village or town you enter, search for an honorable man who will let you into his home until you leave for the next town.
10.12: Once you enter a house, speak to the family there and say, ‘God’s blessing of peace be upon this house!’
10.13: And if those living there welcome you, let your peace come upon the house. But if you are rejected, that blessing of peace will come back upon you.
10.14: And if anyone doesn’t listen to you and rejects your message, when you leave that house or town, shake the dust off your feet.
10.15: Mark my words, on the day of judgment the wicked people who lived in the land of Sodom and Gomorrah will have a lesser degree of judgment than the city that rejects you, for the people of Sodom and Gomorrah did not have the opportunity that was given to them!
10.16: Now, remember, it is I who sends you out, even though you feel vulnerable as lambs going into a pack of wolves. So be as shrewd as snakes yet as harmless as doves.”
10.17: “Be on your guard! For there will be those who will betray you before their religious councils and brutally beat you with whips in their public gatherings.
10.18: And because you follow me, they will take you to stand trial in front of rulers and even kings as an opportunity to testify of me before them and the unbelievers.
10.19: So when they arrest you, don’t worry about how to speak or what you are to say, for the Holy Spirit will give you at that very moment the words to speak.
10.20: It won’t be you speaking but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.
10.21: “A brother will betray his brother unto death—even a father his child! Children will rise up against their parents and have them put to death.
10.22: Expect to be hated by all because of my name, but be faithful to the end and you will experience life and deliverance.
10.23: And when they persecute you in one town, flee to another. But I promise you this: you will not deliver all the cities and towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.
10.24: “A student is not superior to his teacher any more than a servant would be greater than his master.
10.25: The student must be satisfied to share his teacher’s fate and the servant his master’s. If they have called the head of the family ‘lord of flies,’ no wonder they malign the members of his family.
10.26: “Don’t be afraid or intimidated by others, for God will bring everything out into the open and every secret will be told.
10.27: What I say to you in the dark, repeat in broad daylight, and what you hear in a whisper, announce it publicly.
10.28: Don’t be in fear of those who can kill only the body but not your soul. Fear only God, who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
10.29: You can buy two sparrows for only a copper coin, yet not even one sparrow falls from its nest without the knowledge of your Father. Aren’t you worth much more to God than many sparrows?
10.30: So don’t worry. For your Father cares deeply about even the smallest detail of your life.
10.31: So don't be afraid; you are more valuable to him than a whole flock of sparrows.
10.32: “If you openly and publicly acknowledge me, I will freely and openly acknowledge you before my heavenly Father.
10.33: But if you publicly deny that you know me, I will also deny you before my heavenly Father.
10.34: “Perhaps you think I’ve come to spread peace and calm over the earth—but my coming will bring conflict and division, not peace.
10.35: Because of me, A son will turn against his father, a daughter her mother and against her mother-in-law.
10.36: Within your own families you will find enemies.
10.37: “Whoever loves father or mother or son or daughter more than me is not fit to be my disciple.
10.38: And whoever comes to me must follow in my steps and be willing to share my cross and experience it as his own, or he is not worthy of me.
10.39: Those who cling to their lives will give up true life. But those who let go of their lives for my sake and surrender it all to me will discover true life!
10.40: “Whoever receives you receives me, and whoever receives me receives the One who sent me.
10.41: Whoever receives a prophet because he is God’s messenger will share a prophet’s reward. And whoever welcomes a righteous person because he follows me will also share in his reward.
10.42: And whoever gives a cup of cold water to one of my disciples, I promise you, he will not go unrewarded.”

11.1: After Jesus finished giving instructions to his twelve disciples, he went on to minister in different villages throughout the region.
11.2: Now, while John the Baptizer was in prison, he heard about the wonderful deeds of the Christ, so he sent his disciples to ask him this question:
11.3: “Are you really the one the prophets said would come, or should we still wait for another?”
11.4: Jesus answered them, “Give John this report:
11.5: ‘The blind see again, the crippled walk, lepers are cured, the deaf hear, the dead are raised back to life, and the poor and broken now hear of the hope of salvation!’
11.6: And tell John that the blessing of heaven comes to those who are not offended over me.”
11.7: As they were leaving, Jesus began to speak to the crowd about John. “What kind of man did you see when you went out into the wilderness? Did you expect to see a man who would be easily intimidated?
11.8: Who was he? Did you expect to see a man decked out in the splendid fashion of the day? Those who wear fancy clothes live like kings in palaces.
11.9: Or did you encounter a true prophet out in the lonely wilderness? Yes, John was a prophet like those of the past, but he is even more than that!
11.10: He was the fulfillment of this Scripture: See, I am sending my prophetic messenger who will go ahead of me and prepare hearts to receive me.
11.11: “For I tell you the truth, throughout history there has never been a man who surpasses John the Baptizer. Yet the least of those who now experience heaven’s kingdom will become even greater than he.
11.12: From the moment John stepped onto the scene until now, the realm of heaven’s kingdom is bursting forth, and passionate people have taken hold of its power.
11.13: For all the prophets and the Torah prophesied until John appeared.
11.14: If you can receive this truth, John is the Elijah who was destined to come.
11.15: So listen and understand what I’m telling you.
11.16: “How could I describe the people of this generation? You’re like children playing games on the playground, yelling at their playmates,
11.17: ‘You don’t like it when we want to play Wedding! And you don’t like it when we want to play Funeral! You will neither dance nor mourn.’
11.18: Why is it that when John came to you, neither feasting nor drinking wine, you said, ‘He has a demon in him!’?
11.19: Yet when the Son of Man came and went to feasts and drank wine, you said, ‘Look at this man! He is nothing but a glutton and a drunkard! He spends all his time with tax collectors and other sinners.’ But God’s wisdom will become visible by those who embrace it.”
11.20: Then Jesus began to openly denounce the cities where he had done most of his mighty miracles, because the people failed to turn away from sin and return to God.
11.21: He said, “How tragic it will be for the city of Korazin! And how horrible for the city of Bethsaida! For if the powerful miracles that I performed in Korazin and Bethsaida had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have humbled themselves and repented, and turned from their sins.
11.22: Tyre and Sidon will be better off on judgment day than you!
11.23: And Capernaum—do you really think you’ll be exalted because of the great miracles I have done there? No! You’ll be brought down to the depths of hell because of your rejection of me. For if the miracles I worked in your streets were done in Sodom, it would still be standing today!
11.24: But I tell you, it will be more bearable for the region of Sodom in the day of judgment than it will be for you.”
11.25: Then Jesus exclaimed, “Father, thank you, for you are Lord, the Supreme Ruler over heaven and earth! And you have hidden the great revelation of your authority from those who are proud and think they are wise and unveiled it instead to little children.
11.26: Yes, Father, you’ve chosen this gracious plan to extend your kingdom.
11.27: You have entrusted me with all that you are and all that you have. No one fully and intimately knows the Son except the Father. And no one fully and intimately knows the Father except the Son. But the Son is able to unveil the Father to anyone he chooses.
11.28: “Are you weary, carrying a heavy burden? Come to me. I will refresh your life, for I am your oasis.
11.29: Simply join your life with mine. Learn my ways and you’ll discover that I’m gentle, humble, easy to please. You will find refreshment and rest in me.
11.30: For all that I require of you will be pleasant and easy to bear.”

12.1: One Saturday, on the day of rest, Jesus and his disciples were walking through a field of wheat. The disciples were hungry, so they plucked off some heads of grain and rubbed them in their hands to eat.
12.2: But when some of the Pharisees saw what was happening, they said to him, “Look! Your disciples shouldn’t be harvesting grain on the Sabbath!”
12.3: Jesus responded, “Haven’t you ever read what King David and his men did when they were hungry?
12.4: They entered the house of God and ate the sacred bread of God’s presence, violating the law by eating bread that only the priests were allowed to eat.
12.5: “And haven’t you read in the Torah that the priests violated the rules of the Sabbath by carrying out their duties in the temple on a Saturday, and yet they are without blame?
12.6: But I say to you, there is one here who is even greater than the temple.
12.7: If only you could learn the meaning of the words ‘I want compassion more than a sacrifice,’ you wouldn’t be condemning my innocent disciples.
12.8: For the Son of Man exercises his lordship over the Sabbath.”
12.9: Then Jesus left them and went into the synagogue where
12.10: he encountered a man who had an atrophied, paralyzed hand. The fault-finding Pharisees asked Jesus, “Is it permissible to perform a work of healing on the Sabbath?” They only asked him this question because they hoped to accuse him of breaking the Jewish laws.
12.11: He answered them, “If any of you had a lamb that fell into a ditch on the Sabbath, wouldn’t you reach out your hand and lift it out?
12.12: Isn’t a man much more valuable than a lamb? So of course, it’s always proper to do miracles, even on the Sabbath.”
12.13: Then he turned to the man and said, “Hold out your hand!” And as he stretched it out, it was restored, exactly like the other.
12.14: Immediately the Pharisees went out and started to scheme about how they would destroy him.
12.15: Jesus knew what they were thinking, so he left by another way. Massive crowds followed him from there, and he healed all who were sick.
12.16: However, he sternly warned them not to tell others or disclose his real identity,
12.17: in order to fulfill the prophecy of Isaiah:
12.18: Take a careful look at my servant, my chosen one. I love him dearly and I find all my delight in him. I will breathe my Spirit upon him and he will decree justice to the nations.
12.19: He will not quarrel or raise his voice in public.
12.20: He won’t brush aside the bruised and broken. He will be gentle with the weak and feeble, until his victory releases justice.
12.21: And the fame of his name will birth hope among the people.
12.22: Then a man was brought before Jesus who had a demon spirit that made him both blind and mute. Jesus healed him instantly, and he could see and talk again!
12.23: The crowds went wild with amazement as they witnessed this miracle. And they kept saying to one another, “Could this man be the Messiah?”
12.24: But when the Pharisees overheard what the people were saying, they said, “He casts out demons by the power of Satan, the prince of demons!”
12.25: Jesus supernaturally perceived their thoughts and motives, so he told them this parable: “Any kingdom that fights against itself is reduced to ruins. And any family or community splintered by strife will fall apart.
12.26: So if Satan casts out Satan, he is making war on himself. How then could his kingdom stand?
12.27: So if Satan empowers me to cast out demons, who empowers your exorcists to cast them out? Go ask them, let them be your judges.
12.28: But, if I drive out demons by the power of the Spirit of God, then the end of Satan’s kingdom has come!
12.29: Who would dare enter the house of a mighty man and steal his property? First he must be overpowered and tied up by one who is stronger than he. Then his entire house can be plundered.
12.30: “ So join with me, for if you’re not on my side you are against me. And if you refuse to help me gather the spoils, you are making things worse.
12.31: This is why I warn you. God will forgive people for every sin and blasphemy except one. There is no forgiveness for the sin of blasphemy against the Holy Spirit.
12.32: If anyone speaks evil of me, the Son of Man, he can be forgiven; but if anyone speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will never be forgiven, now or ever!”
12.33: “You must determine if a tree is good or rotten. You can recognize good trees by their delicious fruit. But if you find rotten fruit, you can be certain that the tree is rotten. The fruit defines the tree.
12.34: But you who are known as the Pharisees are rotten to the core like venomous snakes. How can your words be good if you are rotten within? For what has been stored up in your hearts will be heard in the overflow of your words!
12.35: “When virtue is stored within, the hearts of good, upright people will produce good fruit. But when evil is hidden within, those who are evil will produce evil fruit.
12.36: You can be sure of this: when the day of judgment comes, everyone will be held accountable for every careless word he has spoken.
12.37: Your very words will be used as evidence, and your words will declare you either innocent or guilty.”
12.38: Then a few Jewish scholars and Pharisees spoke up and said, “Teacher, why don’t you perform a miraculous sign for us.”
12.39: Jesus replied, “Only evil people who are unfaithful to God would demand a sign. There will be no sign given to you except the sign of the prophet Jonah.
12.40: For as Jonah was in the belly of the huge sea creature for three days and three nights, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights.
12.41: The people of Nineveh will also rise up on the day of judgment to condemn this generation. For they all repented when they heard the preaching of Jonah. And there is one greater than Jonah here preaching to you today!
12.42: Even the Queen of Sheba will rise up on the day of judgment to condemn this generation for its unbelief! She journeyed from a far and distant land just to hear the wisdom of King Solomon. Yet now there is one greater than Solomon speaking to you today.”
12.43: “When a demon is cast out of a person, it roams around a dry region, looking for a place to rest, but never finds it.
12.44: Then it says, ‘I’ll return to the house I moved out of,’ and so it goes back, only to find that the house is vacant, warm, and ready for it to move back in.
12.45: So it goes looking for seven other demons more evil than itself, and they all enter together to live there. Then the person’s condition becomes much worse than it was in the beginning. This describes what will also happen to the people of this evil generation.”
12.46: While Jesus was still speaking to the crowds, his mother and brothers came and stood outside, asking for him to come out and speak with them.
12.47: Then someone said, “Look, your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to have a word with you.”
12.48: But Jesus just looked at him and said, “Let me introduce you to my true mother and brothers.”
12.49: Then gesturing to the disciples gathered around him, he said, “Look closely, for this is my true family.
12.50: When you obey my heavenly Father, that makes you a part of my true family.”

13.1: Later that day, Jesus left the house and sat by the lakeshore to teach the people.
13.2: Soon, there were so many people surrounding him that he had to teach sitting in a boat while the large crowd stood on the shore.
13.3: He taught them many things by using stories, parables to illustrate spiritual truths, saying: “Consider this: There was a farmer who went out to sow seeds.
13.4: As he cast his seeds, some fell along the beaten path and the birds came and ate them.
13.5: Others fell onto gravel that had no topsoil. They quickly shot up,
13.6: but when the days grew hot, they were scorched and withered because they had insufficient roots.
13.7: Others fell among the thorns, so when they sprouted, the thorns choked them.
13.8: But other seeds fell on good, rich soil that kept producing a good harvest. Some yielded thirty, some sixty, and some even one hundred times as much as he planted!
13.9: If you’re able to understand this, then you need to respond.”
13.10: Then his disciples approached Jesus and asked, “Why do you always speak to people in these hard-to-understand parables?”
13.11: He explained, “You’ve been given the intimate experience of insight into the hidden mysteries of the realm of heaven’s kingdom, but they have not.
13.12: For everyone who listens with an open heart will receive progressively more revelation until he has more than enough. But those who don’t listen with an open, teachable heart, even the understanding that they think they have will be taken from them.
13.13: That’s why I teach the people using parables, because they think they’re looking for truth, yet because their hearts are unteachable, they never discover it. Although they will listen to me, they never fully perceive the message I speak.
13.14: The prophecy of Isaiah describes them perfectly: Although they listen carefully to everything I speak, they don’t understand a thing I say. They look and pretend to see, but the eyes of their hearts are closed.
13.15: Their minds are dull and slow to perceive, their ears are plugged and are hard of hearing, and they have deliberately shut their eyes to the truth. Otherwise they would open their eyes to see, and open their ears to hear, and open their minds to understand. Then they would turn to me and I would instantly heal them.
13.16: “But blissful are your eyes, for they see. Delighted are your ears, for they are open to hear all these things.
13.17: Many prophets and godly people yearned to see these days of miracles that you’ve been favored to see. They would have given everything to hear the revelation you’ve been favored to hear.
13.18: “Now you are ready to hear the explanation of the parable of the sower:
13.19: “What was sown along the path represents the one who listens to the message of the kingdom but doesn’t understand it. The Adversary then comes and snatches away what was sown into his heart.
13.20: “The one sown on gravel represents the person who gladly hears the kingdom message, but his experience remains shallow.
13.21: Shortly after he hears it, troubles and persecutions come because of the kingdom message he received. Then he quickly falls away, for the truth didn’t sink deeply into his heart.
13.22: “The one sown among thorns represents one who receives the message, but all of life’s busy distractions, his divided heart, and his ambition for wealth result in suffocating the kingdom message and it becomes fruitless.
13.23: “But what was sown on good, rich soil represents the one who hears and fully embraces the message of the kingdom. Their lives bear good fruit—some yield a harvest of thirty, sixty, even one hundred times as much as was sown.”
13.24: Then Jesus taught them another parable: “Heaven’s kingdom can be compared to a farmer who planted good seed in his field.
13.25: But when everyone was asleep, an enemy came and planted weeds among the wheat and ran away.
13.26: When the wheat sprouted and bore grain, the weeds also appeared.
13.27: So the farmer’s hired hands came to him and said, ‘Sir, wasn’t that good seed that you sowed in the field? Where did all these weeds come from?’
13.28: “He answered, ‘This has to be the work of an enemy!’ “They replied, ‘Do you want us to go and gather up all the weeds?’
13.29: “ ‘No,’ he said. ‘If you pull out the weeds you might uproot the wheat at the same time.
13.30: Let them both grow together until the harvest. At that time, I’ll tell my harvesters to gather the weeds first and tie them all in bundles to be burned. Then they will harvest the wheat and put it into my barn.’ ”
13.31: Then Jesus taught them another parable: “Heaven’s kingdom can be compared to the tiny mustard seed that a man takes and plants in his field.
13.32: Although the smallest of all the seeds, it eventually grows into the greatest of garden plants, becoming a tree for birds to come and build their nests in its branches.”
13.33: Then he taught them another parable: “Heaven’s kingdom can be compared to yeast that a woman takes and blends into three measures of flour and then waits until all the dough rises.”
13.34: Whenever Jesus addressed the crowds, he always spoke in allegories. He never spoke without using parables.
13.35: He did this to fulfill the prophecy: I will speak to you in allegories. I will reveal secrets that have been concealed since before the foundation of the world.
13.36: Jesus left the crowds and went inside the house where he was staying. Then his disciples approached him and asked, “Please explain the deeper meaning of the parable of the weeds growing in the field of wheat.”
13.37: He answered, “The man who sowed his field with good seed is the Son of Man.
13.38: And the field is the world. The good seeds I sow are the children of the kingdom realm. The weeds are the children of the Evil One,
13.39: and the enemy who sows them is the devil. The harvest points to the end of this age, and the harvesters are God’s messengers.
13.40: As the weeds are bundled up and thrown into the fire, so it will be at the close of the age.
13.41: The Son of Man will send his messengers, and they will uproot everything out of his kingdom. All the lawless ones and everything that causes sin will be removed.
13.42: And they will throw them into the fiery furnace, where they will experience great sorrow and anguish.
13.43: Then the righteous will shine like the brightness of the sun in their Father’s kingdom realm. If you’re able to understand this, then you’d better respond!”
13.44: “Heaven’s kingdom realm can be illustrated like this: “A person discovered that there was hidden treasure in a field. Upon finding it, he hid it again. Because of uncovering such treasure, he was overjoyed and sold all that he possessed to buy the entire field just so he could have the treasure.
13.45: “Heaven’s kingdom realm is also like a jewel merchant in search of rare pearls.
13.46: When he discovered one very precious and exquisite pearl, he immediately gave up all he had in exchange for it.”
13.47: “Again, heaven’s kingdom realm is like a fisherman who casts his large net into the lake, catching an assortment of fish.
13.48: When the net was filled, the fishermen hauled it up on the shore, and they all sat down to sort out their catch. They collected the good in baskets and threw the bad away.
13.49: And so it will be at the close of the age. The messengers will come and separate the evil from among the godly
13.50: and throw them into the fiery furnace, where they will experience great sorrow and anguish.
13.51: Now do you understand all this?” “Yes,” they replied.
13.52: He responded, “Every scholar of the Scriptures, who is instructed in the ways of heaven’s kingdom realm, is like a wealthy home owner with his house filled with treasures both new and old.”
13.53: Right after Jesus taught this series of parables, he left from there.
13.54: When Jesus arrived in his hometown of Nazareth, he began teaching the people in the synagogue. Everyone was dazed, overwhelmed with astonishment over the depth of revelation they were hearing. They said to one another, “Where did this man get such great wisdom and miraculous powers?
13.55: Isn’t he just the craftsman’s son? Isn’t his mother named Mary, and his four brothers Jacob, Joseph, Simon, and Judah?
13.56: And don’t his sisters all live here in Nazareth? From where then did he get all this revelation and power?”
13.57: And the people became offended and began to turn against him. Jesus said, “There’s only one place a prophet isn’t honored—his own hometown!”
13.58: And their unbelief kept him from doing many mighty miracles in Nazareth.

14.1: At that time Herod, the Roman ruler over Galilee, heard reports about Jesus.
14.2: He told his officials, “This man has to be John the Baptizer who has come back from the dead. That’s why he has this power to work miracles.”
14.3: For Herod had earlier arrested John for confronting him for taking the wife of his brother Philip. He had John thrown in prison and placed in chains
14.4: because John had repeatedly said to him, “It’s not legal or proper for you to be married to Herodias, your sister-in-law!”
14.5: So Herod wanted John dead, but he was afraid of the crowds who flocked to John because they considered him to be a prophet.
14.6: During Herod’s birthday celebration, the daughter of Herodias danced before Herod and all his distinguished guests, which greatly pleased the king.
14.7: So he said to her in front of them all, “I give you my oath, ask of me anything you wish and it will be yours!”
14.8: Because she had been instructed by her mother, she said, “I want the head of John the Baptizer here on a platter!”
14.9: This grieved the king, but because of his oath in front of all of his guests,
14.10: he had John beheaded in prison.
14.11: They brought in his head and displayed it to her on a platter, and she then had it shown to her mother.
14.12: John’s disciples went into the prison and carried his body away and buried it. Then they left to find Jesus and tell him what had happened.
14.13: On hearing this, Jesus slipped away privately by boat to be alone. But when the crowds discovered he had sailed away, they emerged from all the nearby towns and followed him on foot.
14.14: So when Jesus landed he had a huge crowd waiting for him. Seeing so many people, his heart was deeply moved with compassion toward them, so he healed all the sick who were in the crowd.
14.15: Later that afternoon the disciples came to Jesus and said, “It’s going to be dark soon and the people are hungry, but there’s nothing to eat here in this desolate place. You should send the crowds away to the nearby villages to buy themselves some food.”
14.16: “They don’t need to leave,” Jesus responded. “You can give them something to eat.”
14.17: They answered, “But all we have is five barley loaves and two fish.”
14.18: “Let me have them,” Jesus replied.
14.19: Then he had everyone sit down on the grass and he then took the five loaves and two fish. He looked up into heaven, gave thanks to God, and broke the bread into pieces. He then gave it to his disciples, who in turn gave it to the crowds.
14.20: And everyone ate until they were satisfied, for the food was multiplied in front of their eyes! They picked up the leftovers and filled up twelve baskets full!
14.21: There were about five thousand men who were fed, in addition to many women and children!
14.22: As soon as the people were fed, Jesus told his disciples to get into their boat and to go to the other side of the lake while he stayed behind to dismiss the people.
14.23: After the crowds dispersed, Jesus went up into the hills to pray. And as night fell he was there praying alone.
14.24: But the disciples, who were now in the middle of the lake, ran into trouble, for their boat was tossed about by the high winds and heavy seas.
14.25: At about four o’clock in the morning, Jesus came to them, walking on the waves!
14.26: When the disciples saw him walking on top of the water, they were terrified and screamed, “A ghost!”
14.27: Then Jesus said, “Be brave and don’t be afraid. I am here!”
14.28: Peter shouted out, “Lord, if it’s really you, then have me join you on the water!”
14.29: “Come and join me,” Jesus replied. So Peter stepped out onto the water and began to walk toward Jesus.
14.30: But when he realized how high the waves were, he became frightened and started to sink. “Save me, Lord!” he cried out.
14.31: Jesus immediately stretched out his hand and lifted him up and said, “What little faith you have! Why would you let doubt win?”
14.32: And the very moment they both stepped into the boat, the raging wind ceased.
14.33: Then all the disciples bowed down before him and worshiped Jesus. They said in adoration, “You are truly the Son of God!”
14.34: After they crossed over and landed at Gennesaret,
14.35: the people living there quickly recognized who he was. They were quick to spread the news throughout the surrounding region that Jesus had come to them.
14.36: So they brought him all their sick, begging him to let them touch the fringe of his cloak. And everyone who touched it was instantly healed!

15.1: Then the Pharisees and religious scholars came from Jerusalem and asked Jesus this question:
15.2: “Why do your disciples ignore the traditions of our elders? For example, they don’t ceremonially wash their hands before they eat bread.”
15.3: Jesus answered, “And why do you ignore the commandment of God because of your traditions?
15.4: For didn’t God say, ‘Honor your father and mother,’ and, ‘Whoever abuses or insults his father or mother must be put to death?’
15.5: “But you teach that it’s permissible to say to your parents when they are in financial need, ‘Whatever gift you would have received from me I can keep for myself, since I dedicated it as an offering to God.’
15.6: This doesn’t honor your father or mother. And you have elevated your tradition above the words of God.
15.7: Frauds and hypocrites! Isaiah described you perfectly when he said:
15.8: These people honor me only with their words, for their hearts are so very distant from me.
15.9: They pretend to worship me, but their worship is nothing more than the empty traditions of men.”
15.10: Then Jesus turned to the crowd and said, “Come, listen and open your heart to understand.
15.11: What truly contaminates a person is not what he puts into his mouth but what comes out of his mouth. That’s what makes people defiled.”
15.12: Then his disciples approached him and said, “Don’t you know that what you just said offended the Pharisees?”
15.13: Jesus replied, “Every plant that my heavenly Father didn’t plant is destined to be uprooted.
15.14: Stay away from them, for they’re nothing more than blind guides. Do you know what happens when a blind man pretends to guide another blind man? They both stumble into a ditch!”
15.15: Peter spoke up and said, “Will you explain to us what you mean by your parable?”
15.16: Jesus said, “Even after all that I’ve taught you, you still remain clueless?
15.17: Is it hard to understand that whatever you eat enters the stomach only to pass out into the sewer?
15.18: But what comes out of your mouth reveals the core of your heart. Words can pollute, not food.
15.19: You will find living within an impure heart evil ideas, murderous thoughts, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, lies, and slander.
15.20: That’s what pollutes a person. Eating with unwashed hands doesn’t defile anyone.”
15.21: Then Jesus left and went north into the non-Jewish region of Lebanon.
15.22: He encountered there a Canaanite woman who shouted out to him, “Lord, Son of David, show mercy to me! My daughter is horribly afflicted by a demon that torments her.”
15.23: But Jesus never answered her. So his disciples said to him, “Why do you ignore this woman who is crying out to us?”
15.24: Jesus said, “I’ve only been sent to the lost sheep of Israel.”
15.25: But she came and bowed down before him and said, “Lord, help me!”
15.26: Jesus responded, “It’s not right for a man to take bread from his children and throw it out to the dogs.”
15.27: “You’re right, Lord,” she replied. “But even puppies get to eat the crumbs that fall from the prince’s table.”
15.28: Then Jesus answered her, “Dear woman, your faith is strong! What you desire will be done for you.” And at that very moment, her daughter was instantly set free from demonic torment.
15.29: After leaving Lebanon, Jesus went to Lake Galilee and climbed a hill nearby and sat down.
15.30: Then huge crowds of people streamed up the hill, bringing with them the lame, blind, deformed, mute, and many others in need of healing. They laid them at Jesus’ feet and he healed them all.
15.31: And the crowds marveled with amazement, astounded over the things they were witnessing with their own eyes! The lame were walking, the mute were speaking, the crippled were made well, and the blind could see. For three days everyone celebrated the miracles as they exalted and praised the God of Israel!
15.32: Jesus called his disciples to himself and said, “I care deeply about all these people, for they’ve already been with me for three days without food. I don’t want to send them away fasting or else they may be overcome by weakness on their journey home.”
15.33: The disciples said to him, “Where in the world are we going to find enough food in this desolate place to feed this crowd?”
15.34: “How many barley loaves do you have?” Jesus asked. “Seven,” they replied, “and a few small fish.”
15.35: So he gave the order, “Have the people sit down on the grass.”
15.36: Then he took the seven loaves and the fish and gave thanks to God. He broke the bread and gave it to his disciples, who then distributed the food to the crowds.
15.37: When everyone was full and satisfied, they gathered up the leftovers. And from what was once seven loaves and a few fish, they filled seven baskets!
15.38: There were four thousand men who ate the food Jesus multiplied, and even more including the women and children!
15.39: After dismissing the crowd, Jesus got into the boat and crossed over to the region of Magdala.

16.1: One day some of the Pharisees and those of the Jewish sect known as the Sadducees approached Jesus, insisting that he prove to them that he was the Messiah. “Show us a supernatural sign from heaven,” they demanded.
16.2: Jesus answered, “You can read the signs of the weather, for you say, ‘Red sky at night, sailors delight.’
16.3: And, ‘Red sky in the morning, sailors take warning.’ You’re so adept at forecasting the weather by looking at the sky, but you’re absolutely clueless in reading the obvious signs of the times.
16.4: A wicked and wayward generation always asks for signs, but the only sign I provide for you will be the sign of Jonah the prophet.” Then he turned away and left them.
16.5: Later, as Jesus and his disciples crossed over to the other side of Lake Galilee, the disciples realized they had forgotten to bring any loaves of bread.
16.6: Jesus spoke up and said, “Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and the Sadducees.”
16.7: Thinking Jesus was scolding them over not bringing bread, they began to discuss it among themselves.
16.8: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “You have such little faith! Why are you arguing with one another about having no bread?
16.9: Are you so slow to understand? Have you forgotten the miracle of feeding the five thousand families and how each of you ended up with a basket full of fragments?
16.10: And how seven loaves of bread fed four thousand families with baskets left over?
16.11: Don’t you understand? I’m not talking about bread, but I’m warning you to avoid the yeast of the Pharisees and the Sadducees.”
16.12: Then finally they realized he wasn’t talking about yeast found in bread, but the error of the teachings of the Pharisees and the Sadducees.
16.13: When Jesus came to Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples this question: “What are the people saying about me, the Son of Man? Who do they believe I am?”
16.14: They answered, “Some are convinced you are John the Baptizer, others say you are Elijah reincarnated, or Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.”
16.15: “But you—who do you say that I am?” Jesus asked.
16.16: Simon Peter spoke up and said, “You are the Anointed One, the Son of the living God!”
16.17: Jesus replied, “You are favored and privileged Simeon, son of Jonah! For you didn’t discover this on your own, but my Father in heaven has supernaturally revealed it to you.
16.18: I give you the name Peter, a stone. And this rock will be the bedrock foundation on which I will build my church— my legislative assembly, and the power of death will not be able to overpower it!
16.19: I will give you the keys of heaven’s kingdom realm to forbid on earth that which is forbidden in heaven, and to release on earth that which is released in heaven.”
16.20: He then gave his disciples strict orders not to tell anyone that he was the Messiah.
16.21: From then on Jesus began to clearly reveal to his disciples that he was destined to go to Jerusalem and suffer injustice from the elders, leading priests, and religious scholars. He also explained that he would be killed and three days later be raised to life again.
16.22: Peter took him aside to correct him privately. He reprimanded Jesus over and over, saying to him, “God forbid, Master! Spare yourself. You must never let this happen to you!”
16.23: Jesus turned to Peter and said, “Get out of my way, you Satan! You are a hindrance to me, because your thoughts are only filled with man’s viewpoints and not with the ways of God.”
16.24: Then Jesus said to his disciples, “If you truly want to follow me, you should at once completely reject and disown your own life. And you must be willing to share my cross and experience it as your own, as you continually surrender to my ways.
16.25: For if you choose self-sacrifice and lose your lives for my glory, you will continually discover true life. But if you choose to keep your lives for yourselves, you will forfeit what you try to keep.
16.26: For even if you were to gain all the wealth and power of this world—at the cost of your own life—what good would that be? And what could be more valuable to you than your own soul?
16.27: I, the Son of Man, will one day return with my messengers and in the splendor and majesty of my Father. And then I will reward each person according to what they have done.
16.28: But I promise you, there are some standing here now who won’t experience death until they have witnessed the coming of the Son of Man in the presence and the power of the kingdom realm of God!”

17.1: Six days later Jesus took Peter and the two brothers, Jacob and John, and hiked up a high mountain to be alone.
17.2: Then Jesus’ appearance was dramatically altered. A radiant light as bright as the sun poured from his face. And his clothing became luminescent—dazzling like lightning. He was transfigured before their very eyes.
17.3: Then suddenly, Moses and Elijah appeared, and they spoke with Jesus.
17.4: Peter blurted out, “Lord, it’s so wonderful that we are all here together! If you want, I’ll construct three shrines, one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
17.5: But while Peter was still speaking, a bright radiant cloud spread over them, enveloping them all. And God’s voice suddenly spoke from the cloud, saying, “This is my dearly loved Son, the constant focus of my delight. Listen to him!”
17.6: The three disciples were dazed and terrified by this phenomenon, and they fell facedown to the ground.
17.7: But Jesus walked over and touched them, saying, “Get up and stop being afraid.”
17.8: When they finally opened their eyes and looked around, they saw no one else there but Jesus.
17.9: As they all hiked down the mountain together, Jesus ordered them, “Don’t tell anyone of the divine appearance you just witnessed. Wait until the Son of Man is raised from the dead.”
17.10: His disciples asked him, “Why do all the religious scholars insist that Elijah must first appear before the Anointed One comes?”
17.11: He answered them, “They’re right. Elijah must come first and restore all things.
17.12: But Elijah has already appeared. And yet they didn’t recognize him, so they did to him whatever they pleased. And the Son of Man is destined to suffer the same abuse as what they did to him.”
17.13: Then the disciples realized that Jesus was referring to John the Baptizer all along.
17.14: They came to where a large crowd had gathered to wait for Jesus. A man came and knelt before him
17.15: and said, “Lord, please show your tender mercy toward my son. He has a demon who afflicts him. He has epilepsy, and he suffers horribly from seizures. He often falls into the cooking fire or into the river.
17.16: I brought him to your followers, but they weren’t able to heal him.”
17.17: Jesus replied, “Where is your faith? Can’t you see how wayward and wrong this generation is? How much longer do I stay with you and put up with your doubts? Bring your son to me.”
17.18: Then Jesus rebuked the demon and it came out of him and the boy was instantly healed!
17.19: Later the disciples came to him privately and asked, “Why couldn’t we cast out the demon?”
17.20: He told them, “It was because of your lack of faith. I promise you, if you have faith inside of you no bigger than the size of a small mustard seed, you can say to this mountain, ‘Move away from here and go over there,’ and you will see it move! There is nothing you couldn’t do!
17.21: But this kind is cast out only through prayer and fasting.”
17.22: When they all gathered together in Galilee, Jesus said to them, “The Son of Man is going to be betrayed and turned over to his enemies.
17.23: They will kill him and in three days he will be resurrected.” When the disciples heard these words they were devastated.
17.24: After they arrived in Capernaum, the collectors of the temple tax approached Peter and asked, “Does your teacher pay the tax for the upkeep of the temple, like the rest of us?”
17.25: “Of course he does,” Peter answered. When Peter walked into the house, and before he had a chance to speak, Jesus spoke up and said, “Peter, I have a question for you. Who pays tolls or taxes to a king? Is tax collected from the king’s own children, or from his subjects?”
17.26: “From his subjects,” Peter answered. Jesus replied, “That’s right. The children get off free without paying taxes.
17.27: But so that we don’t offend them, go to the lake and throw out your hook, and the first fish that rises up will have a coin in its mouth. It will be the exact amount you need to pay the temple tax for both of us.”

18.1: At that time the disciples came to ask Jesus, “Who is considered to be the greatest in heaven’s kingdom realm?”
18.2: Jesus called a little one to his side and said to them,
18.3: “Learn this well: Unless you dramatically change your way of thinking and become teachable like a little child, you will never be able to enter in.
18.4: Whoever continually humbles himself to become like this little child is the greatest one in heaven’s kingdom realm.
18.5: And if you tenderly care for this little one on my behalf, you are tenderly caring for me.
18.6: But if anyone abuses one of these little ones who believes in me, it would be better for him to have a heavy boulder tied around his neck and be hurled into the deepest sea than to face the punishment he deserves!
18.7: “Misery will come to the one who lures people away into sin. Troubles and obstacles to your faith are inevitable, but great devastation will come to the one guilty of causing others to stumble!
18.8: If your hand clings to sin, cut it off and throw it away. If your foot continually steps onto sin’s path, cut it off and throw it away. For it is better for you to enter into heaven crippled and maimed than to have both hands and both feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.
18.9: And if your eye is always focusing on sin, pluck it out and throw it away. For it is better for you to enter into heaven with one eye than to be thrown into hell fire with two.
18.10: “Be careful that you not corrupt one of these little ones. For I can assure you that in heaven each of their guardian angels always sees the face of my heavenly Father.”
18.11: “The Son of Man has come to give life to all who are lost.
18.12: Think of it this way: If a man owns a hundred sheep and one lamb wanders away and is lost, won’t he leave the ninety-nine grazing the hillside and thoroughly search for the one lost lamb?
18.13: And if he finds his lost lamb, he rejoices over it, more than over the ninety-nine that never went astray.
18.14: Now you should understand that it is never the desire of your heavenly Father that a single one of these little ones should be lost.”
18.15: “If your fellow believer sins against you, you must go to that one privately and attempt to resolve the matter. If he responds, your relationship is restored.
18.16: But if his heart is closed to you, then go to him again, taking one or two others with you. You’ll be fulfilling what the Scripture teaches when it says, ‘Every word may be verified by the testimony of two or three witnesses.’
18.17: And if he refuses to listen, then share the issue with the congregation in hopes of restoration. If he still refuses to respond, even to the church, then you must disregard him as though he were an outsider, on the same level as an unrepentant sinner.
18.18: “Receive this truth: Whatever you forbid on earth will be considered to be forbidden in heaven, and whatever you release on earth will be considered to be released in heaven.
18.19: Again, I give you an eternal truth: If two of you agree to ask God for something in a symphony of prayer, my heavenly Father will do it for you.
18.20: For wherever two or three come together in honor of my name, I am right there with them!”
18.21: Later Peter approached Jesus and said, “How many times do I have to forgive my fellow believer who keeps offending me? Seven times?”
18.22: Jesus answered, “Not seven times, Peter, but seventy times seven times!
18.23: The lessons of forgiveness in heaven’s kingdom realm can be illustrated like this: “There once was a king who had servants who had borrowed money from the royal treasury. He decided to settle accounts with each of them.
18.24: As he began the process, it came to his attention that one of his servants owed him one billion dollars. So he summoned the servant before him and said to him, ‘Pay me what you owe me.’
18.25: When his servant was unable to repay his debt, the king ordered that he be sold as a slave along with his wife and children and every possession they owned as payment toward his debt.
18.26: The servant threw himself facedown at his master’s feet and begged for mercy. ‘Please be patient with me. Just give me more time and I will repay you all that I owe.’
18.27: Upon hearing his pleas, the king had compassion on his servant, and released him, and forgave his entire debt.
18.28: “No sooner had the servant left when he met one of his fellow servants, who owed him twenty thousand dollars He seized him by the throat and began to choke him, saying, ‘You’d better pay me right now everything you owe me!’
18.29: His fellow servant threw himself facedown at his feet and begged, ‘Please be patient with me. If you’ll just give me time, I will repay you all that is owed.’
18.30: But the one who had his debt forgiven stubbornly refused to forgive what was owed him. He had his fellow servant thrown into prison and demanded he remain there until he repaid the debt in full.
18.31: “When his associates saw what was going on, they were outraged and went to the king and told him the whole story.
18.32: The king said to him, ‘You scoundrel! Is this the way you respond to my mercy? Because you begged me, I forgave you the massive debt that you owed me.
18.33: Why didn’t you show the same mercy to your fellow servant that I showed to you?’
18.34: In a fury of anger, the king turned him over to the prison guards to be tortured until all his debt was repaid.
18.35: In this same way, my heavenly Father will deal with any of you if you do not release forgiveness from your heart toward your fellow believer.”

19.1: After Jesus finished teaching them, he left Galilee and made his way toward the district of Judea, east of the Jordan River.
19.2: Massive crowds followed him and he healed all who were sick.
19.3: The Pharisees were intent on putting Jesus to the test with difficult questions, so they approached him and asked, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?”
19.4: “Haven’t you read the Scriptures about creation?” Jesus replied. “The Creator made us male and female from the very beginning,
19.5: and ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and live with his wife. And the two will become one flesh.’
19.6: From then on, they are no longer two, but united as one. So what God unites let no one divide!”
19.7: They responded, “So then why did Moses command us to give a certificate of divorce and it would be lawful?”
19.8: Jesus said, “Moses permitted you to divorce because your hearts are so hard and stubborn, but originally there was no such thing.
19.9: But I say to you, whoever leaves his wife for any reason other than immorality, then takes another wife is living in adultery. And whoever takes a divorced woman in marriage is also living in adultery.”
19.10: His disciples spoke up and said, “If this is the standard, then it seems better to never get married.”
19.11: “Not everyone is meant to remain single—only those whom God gives grace to be unmarried.
19.12: For some are born to celibacy; others have been made eunuchs by others. And there are some who have chosen to live in celibacy for the sacred purpose of heaven’s kingdom realm. Let those who can, accept this truth for themselves.”
19.13: Then they brought little children to Jesus so that he would lay his hands on them, bless them, and pray for them. But the disciples scolded those who brought the children, saying, “Don’t bother him with this now!”
19.14: Jesus overheard them and said, “I want little children to come to me, so never interfere with them when they want to come, for heaven’s kingdom realm is composed of beloved ones like these! Listen to this truth: No one will enter the kingdom realm of heaven unless he becomes like one of these!”
19.15: Then he laid his hands on each of them and went on his way.
19.16: Then a young man approached Jesus and bowed before him, saying, “Wonderful teacher —is there a good work I have to do to obtain eternal life?”
19.17: Jesus answered, “Why would you call me wonderful? God alone is wonderful. And why would you ask what good work you need to do? Keep the commandments and you’ll enter into the life of God.”
19.18: “Which ones?” he asked. Jesus said, “Don’t murder, don’t commit adultery, don’t steal, don’t lie,
19.19: honor your father and mother, and love those around you as you love yourself.”
19.20: “But I’ve always obeyed every one of them without fail,” the young man replied. “What else do I lack?”
19.21: Jesus said to him, “If you really want to be perfect, go now and sell everything you own. Give your money to the poor and your treasure will be transferred into heaven. Then come back and follow me for the rest of your life.”
19.22: When the young man heard these words, he walked away sad, for he had great wealth.
19.23: Then Jesus turned to his disciples and said, “Listen. Do you understand how difficult it is for the rich to enter into heaven’s kingdom realm?
19.24: In fact, it’s easier to stuff a heavy rope through the eye of a needle than it is for the wealthy to enter into God’s kingdom realm!”
19.25: Stunned and bewildered, his disciples asked, “Then who in the world can possibly be saved?”
19.26: Looking into their eyes, Jesus replied, “Humanly speaking, no one, because no one can save himself. But what seems impossible to you is never impossible to God!”
19.27: Then Peter blurted out, “Here we are. We’ve given up everything to follow you. What reward will there be for us?”
19.28: Jesus responded, “Listen to the truth: In the age of the restoration of all things, when the Son of Man sits on his glorious throne, you who have followed me will have twelve thrones of your own, and you will govern the twelve tribes of Israel.
19.29: For anyone who has left behind their home and property, leaving family—brothers or sisters, mothers or fathers, or children—for my sake, they will be repaid a hundred times over and will inherit eternal life.
19.30: But many who push themselves to be first will find themselves last. And those who are willing to be last will find themselves to be first.”

20.1: “This will help you understand the way heaven’s kingdom operates: “There once was a wealthy landowner who went out at daybreak to hire all the laborers he could find to work in his vineyard.
20.2: After agreeing to pay them the standard day’s wage, he put them to work.
20.3: Then at nine o’clock, as he was passing through the town square, he found others standing around without work.
20.4: He told them, ‘Come and work for me in my vineyard and I’ll pay you a fair wage.’
20.5: So off they went to join the others. He did the same thing at noon and again at three o’clock, making the same arrangement as he did with the others.
20.6: “Hoping to finish his harvest that day, he went to the town square again at five o’clock and found more who were idle. So he said to them, ‘Why have you been here all day without work?’
20.7: “ ‘Because no one hired us,’ they answered. “So he said to them, ‘Then go and join my crew and work in my vineyard.’
20.8: “When evening came, the owner of the vineyard went to his foreman and said, ‘Call in all the laborers, line them up, and pay them the same wages, starting with the most recent ones I hired and finishing with the ones who worked all day.’
20.9: “When those hired late in the day came to be paid, they were given a full day’s wage.
20.10: And when those who had been hired first came to be paid, they were convinced that they would receive more. But everyone was paid the standard wage.
20.11: When they realized what had happened, they were offended and complained to the landowner, saying,
20.12: ‘You’re treating us unfairly! They’ve only worked for one hour while we’ve labored and sweated all day under the scorching sun. You’ve made them equal to us!’
20.13: “The landowner replied, ‘Friends, I’m not being unfair—I’m doing exactly what I said. Didn’t you agree to work for the standard wage?
20.14: If I want to give those who only worked for an hour equal pay, what does that matter to you?
20.15: Don’t I have the right to do what I want with what is mine? Why should my generosity make you jealous of them?’
20.16: “ Now you can understand what I meant when I said that the first will end up last and the last will end up being first. Everyone is invited, but few are the chosen.”
20.17: Jesus was about to go to Jerusalem, so he took his twelve disciples aside privately and said to them,
20.18: “Listen to me. We’re on our way to Jerusalem, and I need to remind you that the Son of Man will be handed over to the religious leaders and scholars, and they will sentence him to be executed.
20.19: And they will hand him over to the Romans to be mocked, tortured, and crucified. Yet three days later he will be raised to life again.”
20.20: The wife of Zebedee approached Jesus with her sons, Jacob and John. She knelt before him and asked him for a favor.
20.21: He said to her, “What is it that you want?” She answered, “Make the decree that these, my sons, will rule with you in your kingdom—one sitting on your right hand, one on your left.”
20.22: Jesus replied, “You don’t know what you are asking.” Then, looking in the eyes of Jacob and John, Jesus said, “Are you prepared to drink from the cup of suffering that I am about to drink? And are you able to endure the baptism into death that I am about to endure?” They answered him, “Yes, we are able.”
20.23: “You will indeed drink the cup of my suffering and be immersed into my death,” Jesus told them. “But to be the ones who sit at the place of highest honor is not mine to decide. My Father is the one who chooses them and prepares them.”
20.24: The other ten disciples were listening to all of this, and a jealous anger arose among them against the two brothers.
20.25: Jesus, knowing their thoughts, called them to his side and said, “Kings and those with great authority in this world rule oppressively over their subjects, like tyrants.
20.26: But this is not your calling. You will lead by a completely different model. The greatest one among you will live as the one who is called to serve others,
20.27: because the greatest honor and authority is reserved for the one with the heart of a servant.
20.28: For even the Son of Man did not come expecting to be served but to serve and give his life in exchange for the salvation of many.”
20.29: As Jesus left Jericho a huge crowd gathered and followed him.
