20.30: And there were two blind men sitting on the roadside. When they heard that it was Jesus passing by, they shouted, “Son of David, show us mercy, Lord!”
20.31: Those in the crowd scolded them and told them to be quiet. But the blind men shouted even louder, “Jesus, Son of David, show us mercy, Lord!”
20.32: So Jesus stopped and had them brought to him. He asked them, “What do you want me to do for you?”
20.33: They said, “Lord, we want to see! Heal us!”
20.34: Jesus was deeply moved with compassion toward them. So he touched their eyes, and instantly they could see! Jesus said to them, “Your faith has healed you.” And all the people praised God because of this miracle. And the two men became his followers from that day onward.

21.1: Now, as they were approaching Jerusalem they arrived at the place of the stables near the Mount of Olives. Jesus sent two of his disciples ahead, saying,
21.2: “As soon as you enter the village, you will find a donkey tethered along with her young colt. Untie them both and bring them to me.
21.3: And if anyone stops you and asks, ‘What are you doing?’ just tell them, ‘The Lord of All needs them,’ and he will let you take them.”
21.4: All of this happened to fulfill the prophecy:
21.5: Tell Zion’s daughter: “Look, your King arrives! He’s coming to you humbly, sitting on a donkey, riding on a donkey’s colt.”
21.6: So the two disciples went on ahead and did as Jesus had instructed them.
21.7: They brought the donkey and her colt to him and placed their cloaks and prayer shawls on the colt, and Jesus rode on it.
21.8: Then an exceptionally large crowd gathered and carpeted the road before him with their cloaks and prayer shawls. Others cut down branches from trees to spread in his path.
21.9: Jesus rode in the center of the procession—crowds going before him and crowds coming behind him, and they all shouted, “Bring the victory, Lord, Son of David! He is the blessed one sent from the Lord Yahweh! We celebrate with praises to God in the highest!”
21.10: As Jesus entered Jerusalem, the people went wild with excitement—the entire city was thrown into an uproar!
21.11: Some asked, “Who is this man?” And the crowds shouted back, “This is Jesus! He’s the prophet from Nazareth of Galilee!”
21.12: Upon entering Jerusalem Jesus went directly into the temple area and drove away all the merchants who were buying and selling their goods. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the stands of those selling doves.
21.13: And he said to them, “My dwelling place will be known as a house of prayer, but you have made it into a hangout for thieves!”
21.14: Then the blind and the crippled came into the temple courts, and Jesus healed them all. And the children circled around him shouting out, “Blessings and praises to the Son of David!”
21.15: But when the chief priests and religious scholars heard the children shouting and saw all the wonderful miracles of healing, they were furious.
21.16: They said to Jesus, “Don’t you hear what these children are saying? This is not right!” Jesus answered, “Yes, I hear them. But have you never read the Scripture, ‘From the lips of children and infants you have ordained praise’?”
21.17: Jesus then left at once for the nearby village of Bethany, where he spent the night.
21.18: While walking back into the city the next morning, he got hungry.
21.19: He noticed a lone fig tree by the side of the path and walked over to see if there was any fruit on it, but there was none—he found only leaves. So he spoke to the fig tree and said, “You will be barren and will never bear fruit again!” Instantly the fig tree shriveled up right in front of their eyes!
21.20: Astonished, his disciples asked, “How did you make this fig tree instantly wither and die?”
21.21: Jesus replied, “Listen to the truth. If you do not doubt God’s power and speak out of faith’s fullness, you can also speak to a tree and it will wither away. Even more than that, you could say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and be thrown into the sea’ and it will be done.
21.22: Everything you pray for with the fullness of faith you will receive!”
21.23: After this Jesus went into the temple courts and taught the people. The leading priests and Jewish elders approached him and interrupted him and asked, “By what power do you do these things, and who granted you the authority to teach here?”
21.24: Jesus answered them, “I too have a question to ask you. If you can answer this question, then I will tell you by what power I do these things.
21.25: Where did John’s authority to baptize come from? From heaven or from people?”
21.26: They stepped away and debated among themselves, saying, “How should we answer this? If we say from heaven, he will say to us, ‘Then why didn’t you respond to John and believe what he said?’ But if we deny that God gave John his authority, we’ll be mobbed by the people, for they’re convinced that John was God’s prophet.”
21.27: So they finally answered, “We don’t know.” “Then neither will I tell you from where my power comes to do these things!” he replied.
21.28: Jesus said to his critics, “Tell me what you think of this parable: “There once was a man with two sons. The father came to the first and said, ‘Son, I want you to go and work in the vineyard today.’
21.29: The son replied, ‘I’d rather not.’ But afterward, he deeply regretted what he said to his father, changed his mind, and decided to go to the vineyard.
21.30: The father approached the second son and said the same thing to him. The son replied, ‘Father, I will go and do as you said.’ But he never did—he didn’t go to the vineyard.
21.31: Tell me now, which of these two sons did the will of his father?” They answered him, “The first one.” Jesus said, “You’re right. For many sinners, tax collectors, and prostitutes are going into God’s kingdom realm ahead of you!
21.32: John came to show you the path of righteousness, yet the despised and outcasts believed in him, but you did not. When you saw them turn, you neither repented of your ways nor believed his words.”
21.33: “Pay close attention to this parable,” Jesus said. “There once was an honorable man who planted a vineyard. He built a fence around it, dug out a pit for pressing the grapes, and erected a watchtower. Afterward he leased the land to tenant farmers and then went a distance away.
21.34: At harvest time he sent his servants to the tenants to collect the portion that was due him as the lord of the vineyard.
21.35: But the tenants seized his servants and beat one, killed another, and stoned another.
21.36: So the landowner sent other servants, even more than at first, but they were mistreated the same way.
21.37: Finally, he sent his own son to them, and he said to himself, ‘Perhaps with my own son standing before them they will be ashamed of what they’ve done.’
21.38: But when the tenants saw the son, they said, ‘This is the heir! Let’s kill him and then we can have his inheritance!’
21.39: So they seized him, took him outside the vineyard, and murdered him.
21.40: “You tell me, when the lord of the vineyard comes, what do you think he will do to those tenants?”
21.41: They answered, “He will bring a horrible death to those who did this evil and he will completely destroy them. Then he’ll lease his vineyard to different tenants who will be faithful to give him the portion he deserves.”
21.42: Jesus said to them, “Haven’t you ever read the Scripture that says: The very stone the builder rejected as flawed has now become the most important cornerstone. This was the Lord’s plan — isn’t it marvelous to behold?
21.43: “This is why I say to you that the kingdom realm of God will be taken from you and given to a people who will bear its fruit.
21.44: The one who comes against this stone will be broken, but the one on whom it falls will be pulverized!”
21.45: When the leading priests and the Pharisees realized that the parable was referring to them, they were
21.46: outraged and wanted to arrest him at once. But they were afraid of the reaction of the crowds, because the people considered him to be a prophet.

22.1: As was his custom, Jesus continued to teach the people by using allegories.
22.2: He illustrated the reality of heaven’s kingdom realm by saying, “There once was a king who arranged an extravagant wedding feast for his son.
22.3: On the day the festivities were set to begin, he sent his servants to summon all the invited guests, but they chose not to come.
22.4: So the king sent even more servants to inform the invited guests, saying, ‘Come, for the sumptuous feast is now ready! The oxen and fattened cattle have been killed and everything is prepared, so come! Come to the wedding feast for my son and his bride!’
22.5: “But the invited guests were not impressed. One was preoccupied with his business; another went off to his farming enterprise.
22.6: And the rest seized the king’s messengers and shamefully mistreated them, and even killed them.
22.7: This infuriated the king! So he sent his soldiers to execute those murderers and had their city burned to the ground.
22.8: “Then the king said to his servants, ‘The wedding feast is ready, yet those who had been invited to attend didn’t deserve the honor.
22.9: Now I want you to go into the streets and alleyways and invite anyone and everyone you find to come and enjoy the wedding feast in honor of my son.’
22.10: “So the servants went out into the city streets and invited everyone to come to the wedding feast, good and bad alike, until the banquet hall was crammed with people!
22.11: Now, when the king entered the banquet hall, he looked with glee over all his guests. But then he noticed a guest who was not wearing the wedding robe provided for him.
22.12: So he said, ‘My friend, how is it that you’re here and you’re not wearing your wedding garment?’ But the man was speechless.
22.13: “Then the king turned to his servants and said, ‘Tie him up and throw him into the outer darkness, where there will be great sorrow, with weeping and grinding of teeth.’
22.14: For everyone is invited to enter in, but few respond in excellence.”
22.15: Then the Pharisees came together to make a plan to entrap Jesus with his own words.
22.16: So they sent some of their disciples together with some staunch supporters of Herod. They said to Jesus, “Teacher, we know that you’re an honest man of integrity and you teach us the truth of God’s ways. We can clearly see that you’re not one who speaks only to win the people’s favor, because you speak the truth without regard to the consequences.
22.17: So tell us, then, what you think. Is it proper for us Jews to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
22.18: Jesus knew the malice that was hidden behind their cunning ploy and said, “Why are you testing me, you imposters who think you have all the answers?
22.19: Show me one of the Roman coins.” So they brought him a silver coin used to pay the tax.
22.20: “Now, tell me, whose head is on this coin and whose inscription is stamped on it?”
22.21: “Caesar’s,” they replied. Jesus said, “Precisely, for the coin bears the image of the emperor Caesar. Well, then, you should pay the emperor what is due to the emperor. But because you bear the image of God, give back to God all that belongs to him.”
22.22: The imposters were baffled in the presence of all the people. When they realized once again that they were unable to trap Jesus, they went away stunned.
22.23: Some of the Sadducees, a religious group that denied there was a resurrection of the dead, came to ask Jesus this question:
22.24: “Teacher, the law of Moses teaches that if a man dies before he has children, his brother should marry the widow and raise up children for his brother’s family line.
22.25: Now, there was a family with seven brothers. The oldest got married but soon died, leaving his widow for his brother.
22.26: The second brother married and also died, and the third also. This was repeated down to the seventh brother,
22.27: when finally the woman also died. So here’s our dilemma:
22.28: Which of the seven brothers will be the woman’s husband when she’s resurrected from the dead, since they all were once married to her?”
22.29: Jesus answered them, “You are deluded, because your hearts are not filled with the revelation of the Scriptures or the power of God.
22.30: For after the resurrection, men and women will not marry, just like the angels of heaven don’t marry.
22.31: Haven’t you read what God said:
22.32: ‘I am the Living God, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”
22.33: When the crowds heard this they were dazed and astonished over his teaching!
22.34: When the Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, they called a meeting to discuss how to trap Jesus.
22.35: Then one of them, a religious scholar, posed this question to test him:
22.36: “Teacher, which commandment in the law is the greatest?”
22.37: Jesus answered him, “ ‘Love the Lord your God with every passion of your heart, with all the energy of your being, and with every thought that is within you.’
22.38: This is the great and supreme commandment.
22.39: And the second is like it in importance: ‘You must love your friend in the same way you love yourself.’
22.40: Contained within these commandments to love you will find all the meaning of the Law and the Prophets.”
22.41: While all the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus took the opportunity to pose a question of his own:
22.42: “What do you think about the Anointed One? Whose son is he?” “The son of David,” they replied.
22.43: Then Jesus said to them, “How is it that David, inspired by the Holy Spirit, could call his son the Lord? For didn’t he say:
22.44: The Lord said to my Lord, ‘Sit beside me in the place of authority until I subdue all your enemies under your feet’?
22.45: “So how could David call his own son ‘the Lord’?”
22.46: No one could come up with an answer. And from that day on none of the Pharisees had the courage to question Jesus any longer.

23.1: Then Jesus addressed both the crowds and his disciples and said,
23.2: “The religious scholars and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat as the authorized interpreters of the Law.
23.3: So listen and follow what they teach, but don’t do what they do, for they tell you one thing and do another.
23.4: They tie on your backs an oppressive burden of religious obligations and insist that you carry them, but will never lift a finger to help ease your load.
23.5: Everything they do is done for show and to be noticed by others. They want to be seen as holy, so they wear oversized prayer boxes on their arms and foreheads with Scriptures inside, and wear extra-long tassels on their outer garments.
23.6: They crave the seats of highest honor at banquets and in their meeting places.
23.7: And how they love to be admired by men with their titles of respect, aspiring to be recognized in public and have others call them ‘Reverend.’
23.8: “But you are to be different from that. You are not to be called ‘master,’ for you have only one Master, and you are all brothers and sisters.
23.9: And you are not to be addressed as ‘father,’ for you have one Father, who is in heaven.
23.10: Nor are you to be addressed as ‘teacher,’ for you have one Teacher, the Anointed One.
23.11: The greatest among you will be the one who always serves others.
23.12: Remember this: If you have a lofty opinion of yourself and seek to be honored, you will be humbled. But if you have a modest opinion of yourself and choose to humble yourself, you will be honored.”
23.13: “Great sorrow awaits you religious scholars and you Pharisees—such frauds and pretenders! You do all you can to keep people from experiencing the reality of heaven’s kingdom realm. Not only do you refuse to enter in, you also forbid anyone else from entering in!
23.14: “ Great sorrow awaits you religious scholars and you Pharisees—frauds and pretenders! For you eat up the widow’s household with the ladle of your prayers. Because of this, you will receive a greater judgment.
23.15: “Great sorrow awaits you religious scholars and you Pharisees—such frauds and pretenders! For you will travel over land and sea to find one disciple, only to make him twice the child of hell as yourselves.
23.16: “You blind guides! Great sorrow awaits you, for you teach that there’s nothing binding when you swear by God’s temple, but if you swear by the gold of the temple, you are bound by your oath.
23.17: You are deceived and blind! Which is greater, the gold or the temple that makes the gold sacred?
23.18: And you say that whoever takes an oath by swearing, ‘By the altar,’ it is nothing. But if you swear, ‘By the gift upon the altar,’ then you are obligated to keep your oath.
23.19: What deception! For what is greater, the gift or the altar that makes the gift sacred?
23.20: Whoever swears by the altar swears by the altar and everything offered on it.
23.21: And whoever swears by the temple swears by it and the one who dwells in it.
23.22: And whoever swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by God, who sits upon it.
23.23: “Great sorrow awaits you religious scholars and Pharisees—frauds and pretenders! For you are obsessed with peripheral issues, like insisting on paying meticulous tithes on the smallest herbs that grow in your gardens. These matters are fine, yet you ignore the most important duties of all: to walk in the love of God, to display mercy to others, and to live with integrity. Readjust your values and place first things first.
23.24: What blind guides! Nitpickers! You will spoon out a gnat from your drink, yet at the same time you’ve gulped down a camel without realizing it!
23.25: “Great sorrow awaits you religious scholars and Pharisees—frauds and imposters! You are like one who will only wipe clean the outside of a cup or bowl, leaving the inside filthy. You are foolish to ignore the greed and self-indulgence that live like germs within you.
23.26: You are blind to your evil. Shouldn’t the one who cleans the outside also be concerned with cleaning the inside? You need to have more than clean dishes; you need clean hearts!
23.27: “Great sorrow awaits you religious scholars and Pharisees—frauds and imposters! You are nothing more than tombs painted over with white paint—tombs that look shining and beautiful on the outside but filled with rotting corpses on the inside.
23.28: Outwardly you masquerade as righteous people, but inside your hearts you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
23.29: “Great sorrow awaits you religious scholars and Pharisees—frauds and imposters! You build memorials for the prophets your ancestors killed and decorate the monuments of the godly people your ancestors murdered.
23.30: Then you boast, ‘If we had lived back then, we would not have joined them in killing the prophets.’
23.31: But your words and deeds testify that you are just like them and prove that you are indeed the descendants of those who murdered the prophets.
23.32: Go ahead and finish what your ancestors started!
23.33: You are nothing but snakes in the grass, the offspring of poisonous vipers! How will you escape the judgment of hell if you refuse to turn in repentance?
23.34: “For this reason I will send you more prophets and wise men and teachers of truth. Some you will crucify, and some you will beat mercilessly with whips in your meeting houses, abusing and persecuting them from city to city.
23.35: As your penalty, you will be held responsible for the righteous blood spilled and the murders of every godly person throughout your history—from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah, son of Jehoiada, whom you killed as he stood in the temple between the brazen altar and the Holy Place.
23.36: I tell you the truth: the judgment for all these things will fall upon this generation!”
23.37: “O Jerusalem, Jerusalem—you are the city that murders your prophets! You are the city that stones the very messengers who were sent to deliver you! So many times I have longed to gather a wayward people, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings—but you were too stubborn to let me.
23.38: And now it is too late, since your city will be left in ruins.
23.39: For you will not see me again until you are able to say, ‘We welcome the one who comes to us in the name of the Lord.’ ”

24.1: As Jesus was leaving the temple courts, his disciples came to him and pointed out the beautiful architecture of the temple.
24.2: And Jesus turned to them and said, “Take a good look at all these things, for I’m telling you, there will not be one stone left upon another. It will all be leveled!”
24.3: Later, when they arrived at the Mount of Olives, his disciples came privately to where he was sitting and said, “Tell us, when will these things happen? And what sign should we expect to signal your coming and the completion of this age?”
24.4: Jesus answered, “At that time deception will run rampant. So beware that you are not fooled!
24.5: For many will appear on the scene claiming my authority or saying about themselves, ‘I am the Anointed One,’ and they will lead many astray.
24.6: “You will hear of wars and revolutions on every side, with more rumors of wars to come. Don’t panic or give in to your fears, for the breaking apart of the world’s systems is destined to happen. But it won’t yet be the end; it will still be unfolding.
24.7: “Nations will go to war against nations and kingdoms against kingdoms. And there will be terrible earthquakes, horrible epidemics, and famines in place after place.
24.8: This is how the birth pains of the new age will begin!”
24.9: “You can expect to be persecuted, even killed; for you will be hated by all the nations because of your love for me.
24.10: Then many will stop following me and fall away, and they will betray one another and hate one another.
24.11: And many lying prophets will arise, deceiving multitudes and leading them away from the path of truth.
24.12: There will be such an increase of the sin of lawlessness that those whose hearts once burned with passion for God and others will grow cold.
24.13: But hold your hope firmly to the end and you will experience life and deliverance.
24.14: “Yet through it all, the good news of heaven’s kingdom will be proclaimed all over the world, providing every nation with a demonstration of the reality of God. And after that the end of this age will arrive.”
24.15: “When you witness what Daniel prophesied, ‘the disgusting destroyer,’ taking its stand in the Holy Place [let the reader learn],
24.16: then those in the land of Judah must escape to the higher ground.
24.17: On that day, if you happen to be outside, don’t go back inside to gather belongings.
24.18: And if you’re working out in the field, don’t run back home to get a coat.
24.19: It will be especially hard for pregnant women and for those nursing their babies in those days.
24.20: So pray that your escape will not be during the winter months or on a Sabbath.
24.21: For this will be a time of great misery beyond the magnitude of anything the world has ever seen or ever will see. Unless God limited those days, no one would escape.
24.22: But because of his love for those chosen to be his, he will shorten that time of trouble.
24.23: “And you will hear reports from some, saying, ‘Look, he has returned,’ ‘The Messiah is over here,’ or ‘The Messiah is over there!’ Don’t believe it.
24.24: For there will be imposters falsely claiming to be God’s ‘Anointed One,’ and false prophets will arise to perform miracle signs to lead astray, if possible, those God has chosen to be his.
24.25: Remember this, for I prophesy it will happen!
24.26: So if someone says to you, ‘Look, the Anointed One has returned! He’s in the desert,’ don’t go chasing after him. Or if they say to you, ‘Look, he’s here in our house,’ don’t believe it.
24.27: The appearing of the Son of Man will burst forth with the brightness of lightning shining from the eastern sky to the west.
24.28: How do birds of prey know where the dead body is? They just know instinctively, and so you will know when I appear.”
24.29: “Then immediately this is what will take place: ‘The sun will be darkened and the moon give no light. The stars will fall from the sky and all the cosmic powers will be shaken.’
24.30: Then the sign announcing the Son of Man will appear in the sky, and all the nations of the earth will mourn over him. And they will see the Son of Man appearing in the clouds of heaven, revealed with mighty power, great splendor, and glory.
24.31: And he will send his messengers with the loud blast of the trumpet, and with a great voice they will gather his beloved chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other!”
24.32: “Now learn the lesson from the parable of the fig tree. When spring arrives and it sends out its tender branches and sprouts leaves, you know that summer is near.
24.33: So it will be with you, for when you observe all these things taking place, you will know that he is near, even at the door!
24.34: I assure you, the end of this age will not come until all I have spoken comes to pass.
24.35: The earth and sky will wear out and fade away before one word I speak loses its power or fails to accomplish its purpose.”
24.36: “Concerning that day and exact hour, no one knows when it will arrive, not even the angels of heaven —only the Father knows.
24.37: For it will be like it was in the days of Noah when the Son of Man appears.
24.38: Before the flood, people lived their lives eating, drinking, marrying, and having children.
24.39: They didn’t realize the end was near until Noah entered the ark, and then suddenly, the flood came and took them all away in judgment. It will happen the same way when the Son of Man appears.
24.40: At that time, two men will be working on the farm; one will be taken away in judgment, the other left.
24.41: Two women will be grinding grain; one will be taken away in judgment, the other left.
24.42: This is why you must stay alert: because no one knows the day your Lord will come.
24.43: “But realize this: If a homeowner had known what time of night the burglar would come to rob his house, he would have been alert and ready, and not let his house be robbed.
24.44: So always be ready, alert, and prepared, because at an hour when you’re not expecting him, the Son of Man will come.”
24.45: “What would qualify a servant to manage his master’s house? He would be a wise servant who is both faithful and dependable. The master would commission him to oversee others, for he would lead them well and give them food at the right time.
24.46: What joy and blessing will come to that faithful servant when the master comes home to find him serving with excellence!
24.47: I can promise you, the master will raise him up and put him in charge of all that he owns.
24.48: “But the evil servant says in his heart, ‘My master delays his coming, and who knows when he will return?’ And because of the delay, the servant mistreats those in his master’s household. Instead of caring for the ones he was appointed to serve,
24.49: he abuses the other servants and begins to party with drunkards.
24.50: Let me tell you what will happen to him. His master will suddenly return unexpectedly, and he will remove the abusive, selfish servant from his position of trust.
24.51: And the master will cut him in two and assign him to the place of great sorrow and anguish along with all the other hypocrites.”

25.1: “When my coming draws near, heaven’s kingdom realm can be compared to ten maidens who took their oil lamps and went outside to meet the bridegroom and his bride.
25.2: Five of them were foolish and ill-prepared, for they took no extra oil for their lamps. Five of them were wise, for they took flasks of olive oil with their lamps.
25.3: The five who were foolish took no oil for their lamps,
25.4: but the other five were wise enough to take along extra oil.
25.5: When the bridegroom didn’t come when they expected, they all grew drowsy and fell asleep.
25.6: Then suddenly, in the middle of the night, they were awakened by the shout ‘Get up! The bridegroom is here! Come out and have an encounter with him!’
25.7: So all the girls got up and trimmed their lamps.
25.8: But the foolish ones were running out of oil, so they said to the five wise ones, ‘Share your oil with us, because our lamps are going out!’
25.9: “ ‘We can’t,’ they replied. ‘We don’t have enough for all of us. You’ll have to go and buy some for yourselves!’
25.10: “While the five girls were out buying oil, the bridegroom appeared. Those who were ready and waiting were escorted inside with him and the wedding party to enjoy the feast. And then the door was locked.
25.11: Later, the five foolish girls came running up to the door and pleaded, ‘Lord, Lord, let us come in!’
25.12: “But he called back, ‘Go away! Do I know you? I can assure you, I don’t even know you!’
25.13: “That is the reason you should always stay awake and be alert, because you don’t know the day or the hour when the Bridegroom will appear.”
25.14: “Again, heaven’s kingdom is like a wealthy man who went on a long journey and summoned all his trusted servants and assigned his financial management over to them.
25.15: Before he left on his journey, he entrusted a bag of five thousand gold coins to one of his servants, to another a bag of two thousand gold coins, and to the third a bag of one thousand gold coins, each according to his ability to manage.
25.16: “The one entrusted with five thousand gold coins immediately went out and traded with the money, and he doubled his investment.
25.17: In the same way, the one who was entrusted with two thousand gold coins traded with the sum and likewise doubled his investment.
25.18: But the one who had been entrusted with one thousand gold coins dug a hole in the ground and buried his master’s money.
25.19: “After much time had passed, the master returned to settle accounts with his servants.
25.20: The one who was entrusted with five thousand gold coins came and brought ten thousand, saying, ‘See, I have doubled your money.’
25.21: “Commending his servant, the master replied, ‘You have done well, and proven yourself to be my loyal and trustworthy servant. Because you have been a faithful steward to manage a small sum, now I will put you in charge of much, much more. You will experience the delight of your master, who will say to you, “Enter into the joy of your Lord!” ’
25.22: “Then the one who had been entrusted with two thousand gold coins came in and said, ‘See, my master, I have doubled what you have entrusted to me.’
25.23: “Commending his servant, the master replied, ‘You have done well, and proven yourself to be my loyal and trustworthy servant. Because you were faithful to manage a small sum, now I will put you in charge of much, much more. You will experience the delight of your master, who will say to you, “Enter into the joy of your Lord!” ’
25.24: “Then the one who had been entrusted with one thousand gold coins came to his master and said, ‘Look, sir. I know that you are a hard man to please and you’re a shrewd and ruthless businessman who grows rich on the backs of others.
25.25: I was afraid of you, so I went and hid your money and buried it in the ground. But here it is—take it, it’s yours.’
25.26: “But his master said to him, ‘You’re an untrustworthy and lazy servant! If you knew I was a shrewd and ruthless business man who always makes a profit, why didn’t you deposit my money in the bank?
25.27: Then I would have received it all back with interest when I returned.
25.28: But because you were unfaithful, I will take the one thousand gold coins and give them to the one who has ten thousand.
25.29: For the one who has will be given more, until he overflows with abundance. And the one with hardly anything, even what little he has will be taken from him.’
25.30: “Then the master said to his other servants, ‘Now, throw that good-for-nothing servant far away from me into the outer darkness, where there will be great misery and anguish!’ ”
25.31: “When the Son of Man appears in his majestic glory, with all his angels by his side, he will take his seat on his throne of splendor,
25.32: and all the nations will be gathered together before him. And like a shepherd who separates the sheep from the goats, he will separate all the people.
25.33: The ‘sheep’ he will put on his right side and the ‘goats’ on his left.
25.34: Then the King will turn to those on his right and say, ‘You have a special place in my Father’s heart. Come and experience the full inheritance of the kingdom realm that has been destined for you from before the foundation of the world!
25.35: For when you saw me hungry, you fed me. When you found me thirsty, you gave me drink. When I had no place to stay, you invited me in,
25.36: and when I was poorly clothed, you covered me. When I was sick, you tenderly cared for me, and when I was in prison you visited me.’
25.37: “Then the godly will answer him, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty and give you food and something to drink?
25.38: When did we see you with no place to stay and invite you in? When did we see you poorly clothed and cover you?
25.39: When did we see you sick and tenderly care for you, or in prison and visit you?’
25.40: “And the King will answer them, ‘Don’t you know? When you cared for one of the least of these, my little ones, my true brothers and sisters, you demonstrated love for me.’
25.41: “Then to those on his left the King will say, ‘Leave me! For you are under the curse of eternal fire that has been destined for the devil and all his demons.
25.42: For when you saw me hungry, you gave me no food, and when you saw me thirsty, you gave me no drink.
25.43: I had no place to stay, and you refused to take me in as your guest. When you saw me poorly clothed, you closed your hearts and did not clothe me. When you saw that I was sick, you didn’t lift a finger to help me, and when I was imprisoned, you never came to visit me.’
25.44: “And then those on his left will say, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty and not give you food and something to drink? When did we see you homeless, or poorly clothed? When did we see you sick and not help you, or in prison and not visit you?’
25.45: “Then he will answer them, ‘Don’t you know? When you refused to help one of the least important among these my little ones, my true brothers and sisters, you refused to help and honor me.’
25.46: And they will depart from his presence into eternal punishment. But the godly and beloved ‘sheep’ will enter into eternal bliss.”

26.1: After Jesus had completed his teachings, he said to his disciples,
26.2: “You know that the Feast of the Passover begins in two more days. That’s when the Son of Man will be betrayed and handed over to be crucified.”
26.3: Meanwhile, the prominent priests and religious leaders of the nation were gathered in the palace of Caiaphas the high priest.
26.4: That’s when they made their decision to secretly have Jesus captured and killed.
26.5: But they all agreed, “We can’t do this during the Passover celebrations or we could have a riot on our hands.”
26.6: Then Jesus went to Bethany, to the home of Simon, a man Jesus had healed of leprosy. A woman came into the house, holding an alabaster flask filled with expensive, fragrant oil. She came right to Jesus, and in a lavish gesture of devotion, she poured out the costly oil, and it cascaded over his head as he was at the table.
26.7: During supper, a woman came in with a beautiful jar of expensive perfume and poured it over his head.
26.8: When the disciples saw this, they were offended. “What a total waste!” they grumbled.
26.9: “We could have sold it for a great deal of money and given it to the poor.”
26.10: Jesus knew their thoughts and said to them, “Why are you critical of this woman? She has done a beautiful act of kindness.
26.11: You will always have someone poor whom you can help, but you will not always have me.
26.12: When she poured the fragrant oil over me, she was preparing my body for burial.
26.13: I promise you that when this wonderful gospel spreads all over the world, the story of her lavish devotion to me will also be mentioned in memory of her.”
26.14: One of the twelve apostles, Judas the locksmith, went to the leading priests
26.15: and said, “How much are you willing to pay me to betray Jesus into your hands?” They agreed to pay him thirty silver coins.
26.16: Immediately Judas began to scheme and look for an opportunity to betray him.
26.17: On the first day of Passover, the day when all bread made with yeast was removed from every Jewish home, the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Where should we prepare the Passover meal for you?”
26.18: He answered them, “My heart longs with great desire to eat this Passover meal with you. Go into Jerusalem and you will encounter a man. Tell him that the teacher says, ‘My appointed time is near. I am coming to your home to eat the Passover meal with my disciples.’ ”
26.19: The disciples did as Jesus had instructed them, and they prepared the Passover meal.
26.20: When evening came he took his place at the table and dined with the Twelve.
26.21: While they were eating, Jesus spoke up and said, “One of you is about to betray me.”
26.22: Feeling deeply hurt by these words, one after another asked him, “You don’t mean me, do you?”
26.23: He answered, “It is one who has shared meals with me as an intimate friend.
26.24: All that was prophesied of me will take place, but how terrible it will be for the one who betrays the Son of Man. It would be far better for him if he had never been born!”
26.25: Then finally, Judas the traitor spoke up and asked him, “Teacher, perhaps it is I?” Jesus answered, “You said it.”
26.26: As they ate, Jesus took the bread and blessed it and broke it and gave it to his disciples. He said to them, “This is my body. Eat it.”
26.27: Then taking the cup of wine, he gave thanks to the Father, he entered into covenant with them, saying, “This is my blood. Each of you must drink it in fulfillment of the covenant.
26.28: For this is the blood that seals the new covenant. It will be poured out for many for the complete forgiveness of sins.
26.29: The next time we drink this, I will be with you and we will drink it together with a new understanding in the kingdom realm of my Father.”
26.30: Then they sang a psalm and left for the Mount of Olives.
26.31: Along the way Jesus said to them, “Before the night is over, you will all desert me. This will fulfill the prophecy of the Scripture that says: I will strike down the shepherd and all the sheep will scatter far and wide!
26.32: “But after I am risen, I will go ahead of you to Galilee and will meet you there.”
26.33: Then Peter spoke up and said, “Even if all the rest lose courage and fall away, I will still be beside you, Jesus!”
26.34: “Are you sure, Peter?” Jesus said. “In fact, before the rooster crows a few hours from now, you will have denied me three times.”
26.35: Peter replied, “I absolutely will never deny you, even if I have to die with you!” And all the others said the same thing.
26.36: Then Jesus led his disciples to an orchard called “The Oil Press.” He told them, “Sit here while I go and pray nearby.”
26.37: He took Peter, Jacob, and John with him. However, an intense feeling of great sorrow plunged his soul into agony.
26.38: And he said to them, “My heart is overwhelmed and crushed with grief. It feels as though I’m dying. Stay here and keep watch with me.”
26.39: Then he walked a short distance away, and overcome with grief, he threw himself facedown on the ground and prayed, “My Father, if there is any way you can deliver me from this suffering, please take it from me. Yet what I want is not important, for I only desire to fulfill your plan for me.” Then an angel from heaven appeared to strengthen him.
26.40: Later, he came back to his three disciples and found them all sound asleep. He awakened Peter and said to him, “Could you not stay awake with me for even one hour?
26.41: Keep alert and pray that you’ll be spared from this time of testing. Your spirit is eager enough, but your humanity is weak.”
26.42: Then he left them for a second time to pray in solitude. He said to God, “My Father, if there is not a way that you can deliver me from this suffering, then your will must be done.”
26.43: He came back to the disciples and found them sound asleep, for they couldn’t keep their eyes open.
26.44: So he left them and went away to pray the same prayer for the third time.
26.45: When he returned again to his disciples, he awoke them, saying, “Are you still sleeping? Don’t you know the hour has come for the Son of Man to be handed over to the authority of sinful men?
26.46: Get up and let’s go, for the betrayer has arrived.”
26.47: At that moment Judas, his once-trusted disciple, appeared, along with a large crowd of men armed with swords and clubs. They had been sent to arrest Jesus by order of the ruling priests and Jewish religious leaders.
26.48: Now, Judas, the traitor, had arranged to give them a signal that would identify Jesus, for he had told them, “Jesus is the one whom I will kiss. So seize him!”
26.49: Judas quickly stepped up to Jesus and said, “Shalom, Rabbi,” and he kissed him on both cheeks.
26.50: “My beloved friend,” Jesus said, “is this why you’ve come?” Then the armed men seized Jesus to arrest him.
26.51: But one of the disciples pulled out a dagger and swung it at the servant of the high priest, slashing off his ear.
26.52: Jesus said to him, “Put your dagger away. For all those who embrace violence will die by violence.
26.53: Don’t you realize that I could ask my heavenly Father for angels to come at any time to deliver me? And instantly he would answer me by sending more than twelve legions of angels to come and protect us.
26.54: But that would thwart the prophetic plan of God. For it has been written that it would happen this way.”
26.55: Then Jesus turned to the mob and said, “Why would you arrest me with swords and clubs as though I were an outlaw? Day after day I sat in the temple courts with you, teaching the people, yet you didn’t arrest me.
26.56: But all of this fulfills the prophecies of the Scriptures.” At that point all of his disciples ran away and abandoned him.
26.57: Those who arrested Jesus led him away to Caiaphas, the chief priest, and to a meeting where the religious scholars and the supreme Jewish council were already assembled.
26.58: Now, Peter had followed the mob from a distance all the way to the chief priest’s courtyard. And after entering, he sat with the servants of the chief priest who had gathered there, waiting to see how things would unfold.
26.59: The chief priests and the entire supreme Jewish council of leaders were doing their best to bring false charges against Jesus, because they were looking for a reason to put him to death.
26.60: Many false witnesses came forward, but the evidence could not be corroborated. Finally two men came forward
26.61: and declared, “This man said, ‘I can destroy God’s temple and build it again in three days!’ ”
26.62: Then the chief priest stood up and said to Jesus, “Have you nothing to say about these allegations? Is what they’re saying about you true?”
26.63: But Jesus remained silent before them. So the chief priest said to him, “I charge you under oath—in the name of the living God, tell us once and for all if you are the anointed Messiah, the Son of God!”
26.64: Jesus answered him, “You just said it yourself. And more than that, you are about to see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of God, the Almighty. And one day you will also see the Son of Man coming in the heavenly clouds!”
26.65: This infuriated the chief priest, and as an act of outrage, he tore his robe and shouted, “What blasphemy! No more witnesses are needed, for you heard this grievous blasphemy.”
26.66: Turning to the council he said, “Now, what is your verdict?” “He’s guilty and deserves the death penalty!” they answered.
26.67: Then they spat on his face and slapped him. Others struck him over and over with their fists.
26.68: Then they taunted him by saying, “Oh, Anointed One, prophesy to us! Tell us which one of us is about to hit you next?”
26.69: Meanwhile, Peter was still sitting outside in the courtyard when a servant girl came up to him and said, “I recognize you. You were with Jesus the Galilean.”
26.70: In front of everyone Peter denied it and said, “I don’t have a clue what you’re talking about.”
26.71: Later, as he stood near the gateway of the courtyard, another servant girl noticed him and said, “I know this man is a follower of Jesus the Nazarene!”
26.72: Once again, Peter denied it, and with an oath he said, “I tell you, I don’t know the man!”
26.73: A short time later, those standing nearby approached Peter and said, “We know you’re one of his disciples—we can tell by your speech. Your Galilean accent gives you away!”
26.74: Peter denied it, and using profanity he said, “I don’t know the man!” At that very moment the sound of a crowing rooster pierced the night.
26.75: Then Peter remembered the prophecy of Jesus, “Before the rooster crows you will have denied me three times.” With a shattered heart, Peter left the courtyard, sobbing with bitter tears.

27.1: Before dawn that morning, all the chief priests and religious leaders resolved to take action against Jesus and decided that he should be executed.
27.2: So they bound him and led him away to Pilate, the Roman governor.
27.3: Now, when Judas, the betrayer, saw that Jesus had been sentenced to death, remorse filled his heart. He returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and religious leaders,
27.4: saying, “I have sinned by betraying an innocent man.” They replied, “Why are you bothering us? That’s your problem.”
27.5: Then Judas flung the silver coins inside the temple and went out and hanged himself.
27.6: The chief priests, picking up the pieces of silver, said, “We can’t keep this, for it’s unlawful to put blood money into the temple treasury.”
27.7: So after some deliberation, they decided to purchase the potter’s field of clay, to use as a cemetery for burying strangers.
27.8: That’s why that land has been called “The Field of Blood.”
27.9: This fulfilled the prophecy of Zechariah: They took the thirty pieces of silver, the price at which he was valued by the people of Israel, the price of a precious man,
27.10: And they bought the potter’s field, as the Lord directed.
27.11: As Jesus stood in front of the Roman governor, Pilate asked him, “So, you are the king of the Jews?” Jesus answered, “You have just spoken it.”
27.12: Then he was accused by the chief priests and religious leaders, but he remained silent.
27.13: Pilate said, “Don’t you hear these allegations?”
27.14: But Jesus offered no defense to any of the charges, much to the great astonishment of Pilate.
27.15: Now, every year at Passover it was the custom of the governor to pardon a prisoner and release him to the people—anyone they wanted.
27.16: And at that time, Pilate was holding in custody a notorious criminal named Jesus Barabbas.
27.17: So as the crowds of people assembled outside of Pilate’s residence, he went out and offered them a choice. He asked them, “Who would you want me to release to you today, Jesus who is called Barabbas, or Jesus who is called the Anointed One?”
27.18: (Now, Pilate was fully aware that the religious leaders had handed Jesus over to him because of their bitter jealousy.)
27.19: Just then, as Pilate was presiding over the tribunal, his wife sent him an urgent message: “Don’t harm that holy man, for I suffered a horrible nightmare last night about him!”
27.20: Meanwhile, the chief priest and the religious leaders were inciting the crowd to ask for Barabbas to be freed and to have Jesus killed.
27.21: So Pilate asked them again, “Which of the two men would you like me to release for you?” They shouted, “Barabbas.”
27.22: Pilate asked them, “Then what would you have me to do with Jesus who is called the Anointed One?” They all shouted back, “Crucify him!”
27.23: “Why?” Pilate asked. “What has he done wrong?” But they kept shouting out, “Crucify him!”
27.24: When Pilate realized that a riot was about to break out and that it was useless to try to reason with the crowd, he sent for a basin of water. After washing his hands in front of the people, he said, “I am innocent of the blood of this righteous man. The responsibility for his death is now yours!”
27.25: And the crowd replied, “Let his blood be on us and on our children!”
27.26: So he released Barabbas to the people. He ordered that Jesus be beaten with a whip of leather straps embedded with metal, and afterward be crucified.
27.27: Then the guards took him into their military compound, where a detachment of nearly six hundred soldiers surrounded him.
27.28: They stripped off his clothing and placed a scarlet robe on him to make fun of him.
27.29: Then they braided a crown of thorns and forcefully shoved it onto his head. After placing a reed staff in his right hand, they knelt down before him and mocked him, saying, “Hail, king of the Jews!”
27.30: Then they spat in his face and took the reed staff from his hand and hit him repeatedly on his head, driving the crown of thorns deeper.
27.31: When they finished ridiculing him, they took off the scarlet robe and put his own clothes back on him and led him away to be crucified.
27.32: And as they came out of the city, they stopped an African man named Simon, from Libya, and compelled him to carry the cross for Jesus.
27.33: They brought Jesus to Golgotha, which means “Skull Hill.”
27.34: And there the soldiers offered him a mild painkiller, a drink of wine mixed with gall, but after tasting it, he refused to drink it.
27.35: Then they crucified Jesus, nailing his hands and feet to the cross. The soldiers divided his clothing among themselves by rolling dice to see who would win them.
27.36: And the soldiers stood there to watch what would happen and to keep guard over him.
27.37: Above his head they placed a sign that read, “This is Jesus of Nazareth, King of Israel.”
27.38: Two criminals were also crucified with Jesus, one on each side of him.
27.39: And those who passed by shook their heads and ridiculed him,
27.40: saying, “We heard you boast that you could destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days! Why don’t you save yourself now? If you’re really God’s Son, come down from the cross!”
27.41: Even the ruling priests, with the Jewish scholars and religious leaders, joined in the mockery
27.42: and kept on saying, “He saved others, but he can’t even save himself! Israel’s king, is he? He should pull out the nails and come down from the cross right now; then we’ll believe in him!
27.43: He puts his trust in God, so let’s see if it’s true, and see if God really wants to rescue him, for he said, ‘I am the Son of God.’ ”
27.44: Even the two criminals who were crucified with Jesus began to taunt him, hurling their insults on him.
27.45: For three hours, beginning at noon, a sudden and unexpected darkness came over the earth.
27.46: And at three o’clock Jesus shouted with a mighty voice in Aramaic, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” —that is, “My God, My God, why have you deserted me?”
27.47: Some who were standing near the cross misunderstood and said, “He’s calling for Elijah.”
27.48: One bystander ran and got a sponge, soaked it with sour wine, then put it on a stick and held it up for Jesus to drink.
27.49: But the rest said, “Leave him alone! Let’s see if Elijah comes to rescue him.”
27.50: Jesus passionately cried out, took his last breath, and gave up his spirit.
27.51: At that moment the veil in the Holy of Holies was torn in two from the top to the bottom. The earth shook violently, rocks were violently split apart,
27.52: and graves were opened. Then many of the holy ones who had died were brought back to life and came out of their graves.
27.53: And after Jesus’ resurrection, they were seen by many people walking in Jerusalem.
27.54: Now, when the Roman military officer and his soldiers witnessed what was happening and felt the powerful earthquake, they were extremely terrified. They said, “There is no doubt, this man was the Son of God!”
27.55: Watching from a distance were many of the women who had followed him from Galilee and given him support.
27.56: Among them were Mary Magdalene; Mary, the mother of Jacob and Joseph; and the mother of Jacob and John.
27.57: At the end of the day, a wealthy man named Joseph, a follower of Jesus from the village of Ramah,
27.58: approached Pilate and asked if he could take custody of the body of Jesus. So Pilate consented and ordered that the body be given to him.
27.59: Then Joseph wrapped the body in a shroud of fine linen and placed it in his own unused tomb, which had only recently been cut into the rock.
27.60: They rolled a large stone to seal the entrance of the tomb and left.
27.61: Sitting across from the tomb were Mary Magdalene and the other Marys, watching all that took place.
27.62: The next day, the day after Preparation Day for Passover, the chief priests and the Pharisees went together to Pilate.
27.63: They said to him, “Our master, we remember that this imposter claimed that he would rise from the dead after three days.
27.64: So please, order the tomb to be sealed until after the third day. Seal it so that his disciples can’t come and steal the corpse and tell people he rose from the dead. Then the last deception would be worse than the first!”
27.65: “I will send soldiers to guard the tomb,” Pilate replied. “Go with them and make the tomb as secure as possible.”
27.66: So they left and sealed the stone, and Pilate’s soldiers secured the tomb.

28.1: After the Sabbath ended, at the first light of dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to take a look at the tomb.
28.2: Suddenly, the earth shook violently beneath their feet as the angel of the Yahweh descended from heaven. Lightning flashed around him and his robe was dazzling white! The guards were stunned and terrified—lying motionless like dead men. Then the angel walked up to the tomb, rolled away the stone, and sat on top of it!
28.3: His face shone like lightning, and his clothing was as white as snow.
28.4: The guards shook with fear when they saw him, and they fell into a dead faint.
28.5: The women were breathless and terrified, until the angel said to them, “There’s no reason to be afraid. I know you’re here looking for Jesus, who was crucified.
28.6: He isn’t here—he has risen victoriously, just as he said! Come inside the tomb and see the place where our Lord was lying.
28.7: Then run and tell his disciples that he has risen from the dead! I give you his message: ‘I am going ahead of you to Galilee and you will see me there.’ ”
28.8: They rushed quickly to tell his disciples, and their hearts were filled with fear, awe, and great joy at the same time.
28.9: Along the way, Jesus suddenly appeared in front of them and said, “Rejoice!” They were so overwhelmed by seeing him that they bowed down and grasped his feet in adoring worship.
28.10: Then Jesus said to them, “Throw off all your fears. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee. They will find me there.”
28.11: After the women left the tomb, a few of the guards went into Jerusalem and told the chief priests everything they had seen and heard.
28.12: So the chief priests called a meeting with all the religious leaders and came up with a plan. They bribed the guards with a large sum of money
28.13: and told them, “Tell everyone, ‘While we were asleep, his disciples came at night and stole his body!’
28.14: If Pilate finds out about this, don’t worry. We’ll make sure you don’t get blamed.”
28.15: So they took the money and did as they were told. (That is why the story of the guards is still circulated among the Jews to this day.)
28.16: Meanwhile, the eleven disciples heard the wonderful news from the women and left for Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had arranged to meet them.
28.17: The moment they saw him, they worshiped him, but some still had lingering doubts.
28.18: Then Jesus came close to them and said, “All authority of the universe has been given to me.
28.19: Now wherever you go, make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
28.20: And teach them to faithfully follow all that I have commanded you. And never forget that I am with you every day, even to the completion of this age.”

1.1: This is the beginning of the wonderful news about Jesus the Messiah, the Son of God.
1.2: It starts with Isaiah the prophet, who wrote: Listen! I am sending my messenger ahead of you and he will prepare your way!
1.3: He is a thunderous voice of one who shouts in the wilderness: “Prepare your hearts for the coming of the Lord Yahweh, and clear a straight path inside your hearts for him!”
1.4: John the Baptizer was the messenger who appeared in the wilderness, preaching a baptism of repentance for the complete cancellation of sins.
1.5: A steady stream of people came to be dipped in the Jordan River as they publicly confessed their sins. They came from all over southern Israel, including nearly all the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
1.6: John wore a rough garment made from camel hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and honey.
1.7: And this is the message he kept preaching: “There is a man coming after me who is greater and a lot more powerful than I am. I’m not even worthy to bend down and untie the strap of his sandals.
1.8: I’ve baptized you into water, but he will baptize you into the Spirit of Holiness!”
1.9: One day, Jesus came from the Galilean village of Nazareth and had John immerse him in the Jordan River.
1.10: The moment Jesus rose up out of the water, John saw the heavenly realm split open, and the Holy Spirit descended upon him like a dove.
1.11: At the same time, a voice spoke from heaven, saying: “You are my Son, my cherished one, and my greatest delight is in you!”
1.12: Immediately after this he was compelled by the Holy Spirit to go into an uninhabited desert region.
1.13: He remained there in the wilderness for forty days, enduring the ordeals of Satan’s tests. He encountered wild animals, but also angels who appeared and ministered to his needs.
1.14: Later on, after John the Baptizer was arrested, Jesus went back into the region of Galilee and preached the wonderful gospel of God’s kingdom.
1.15: His message was this: “At last the fulfillment of the age has come! It is time for God’s kingdom to be experienced in its fullness! Turn your lives back to God and put your trust in the hope-filled gospel!”
1.16: As Jesus was walking along the shore of Lake Galilee, he noticed two brothers fishing: Simon and Andrew. He watched them as they were casting their nets into the sea
1.17: and said to them, “Come follow me and I will transform you into fishers of men instead of fish!”
1.18: Immediately they dropped their nets and left everything behind to follow Jesus.
1.19: Walking a little farther, Jesus found two other brothers sitting in a boat, along with their father, mending their nets. Their names were Jacob and John, and their father Zebedee.
1.20: Jesus immediately walked up to them and invited the two brothers to become his followers. Jacob and John dropped their nets, stood up, left their father in the boat with the hired men, and followed Jesus.
1.21: Then Jesus and his disciples went to Capernaum, and he immediately started teaching on the Sabbath day in the synagogue.
1.22: The people were awestruck by his teaching, because he taught in a way that demonstrated God’s authority, which was quite unlike the religious scholars.
1.23: Suddenly, during the meeting, a demon-possessed man screamed out,
1.24: “Hey! Leave us alone! Jesus the victorious, I know who you are. You’re God’s Holy One and you have come to destroy us!”
1.25: Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Silence! You are bound! Come out of him!”
1.26: The man’s body shook violently in spasms, and the demon hurled him to the floor until it finally came out of him with a deafening shriek!
1.27: The crowd was awestruck and kept saying among themselves, “What is this new teaching that comes with such authority? With merely a word he commands demons to come out and they obey him!”
1.28: So the reports about Jesus spread like wildfire throughout every community in Galilee.
1.29: Now, as soon as they left the meeting, they went straight to Simon and Andrew’s house, along with Jacob and John.
1.30: Simon’s mother-in-law was bedridden, sick with a high fever, so the first thing they did was to tell Jesus about her.
1.31: He walked up to her bedside, gently took her hand, and raised her up! Her fever disappeared and she began to serve them.
1.32: Later in the day, just after the Sabbath ended at sunset, the people kept bringing to Jesus all who were sick and tormented by demons,
1.33: until the whole village was crowded around the house.
1.34: Jesus healed many who were sick with various diseases and cast out many demons. But he would not permit the demons to speak, because they knew who he really was.
1.35: The next morning, Jesus got up long before daylight, left the house while it was dark, and made his way to a secluded place to give himself to prayer.
1.36: Later, Simon and his friends searched for him,
1.37: and when they finally tracked him down, they told him, “Everyone is looking for you—they want you!”
1.38: Jesus replied, “We have to go on to the surrounding villages so that I can share my message with the people there, for that is my mission.”
1.39: So he went throughout the region of Galilee, preaching in the Jewish synagogues and casting out demons.
1.40: On one occasion, a leper came and threw himself down in front of Jesus, pleading for his healing, saying, “You have the power to heal me right now if only you really want to!”
1.41: Being deeply moved with tender compassion, Jesus reached out and touched the skin of the leper and told him, “Of course I want you to be healed—so now, be cleansed!”
1.42: Instantly his leprous sores completely disappeared and his skin became smooth!
1.43: Jesus sent him away with a very stern warning,
1.44: saying, “Don’t say anything to anyone about what just happened, but go find a priest and show him that you’ve been healed. Then bring the offering that Moses commanded for your cleansing as a living testimony to everyone.”
1.45: But no sooner did the man leave than he began to proclaim his healing publicly and tell the story everywhere. Jesus’ growing fame prevented him from entering the villages openly, which forced him to remain in isolated places. Even so, a steady stream of people flocked to him from everywhere.

2.1: Several days later, Jesus returned to Capernaum, and the news quickly spread that he was back in town.
2.2: Soon there were so many people crowded inside the house to hear him that there was no more room, even outside the door. While Jesus was preaching the word of God,
2.3: four men arrived, carrying a paralyzed man.
2.4: But when they realized that they couldn’t even get near him because of the crowd, they went up on top of the house and tore away the roof above Jesus’ head. And when they had broken through, they lowered the paralyzed man on a stretcher right down in front of him!
2.5: When Jesus saw the extent of their faith, he said to the paralyzed man, “My son, your sins are now forgiven.”
2.6: This offended some of the religious scholars who were present, and they reasoned among themselves,
2.7: “Who does he think he is to speak this way? This is blasphemy for sure! Only God himself can forgive sins!”
2.8: Jesus supernaturally perceived their thoughts and said to them, “Why are you being so skeptical?
2.9: Which is easier, to say to this paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are now forgiven,’ or, ‘Stand up and walk!’?
2.10: But to convince you that the Son of Man has been given authority to forgive sins,
2.11: I say to this man, ‘Stand up, pick up your stretcher, and walk home.’ ”
2.12: Immediately the man was healed and sprang to his feet in front of everyone and left for home. When the crowd witnessed this miracle, they were awestruck. They shouted praises to God and said, “We’ve never seen anything like this before!”
2.13: Jesus went out to walk near Lake Galilee, and a massive crowd gathered, so he taught them.
2.14: As he walked along, he found Levi, the son of Alphaeus, sitting at a tax booth, collecting taxes. He approached him and said, “Come follow me.” Immediately he got up from his booth and began to follow Jesus.
2.15: Later, Jesus and his disciples went to have a meal with Levi. Among the guests in Levi’s home were many tax collectors and notable sinners sharing a meal with Jesus, for there were many kinds of people who followed him.
2.16: But when the religious scholars and the Pharisees found out that Jesus was keeping company and dining with sinners and tax collectors, they were indignant. So they approached Jesus’ disciples and said to them, “Why is it that someone like Jesus defiles himself by eating with sinners and tax collectors?”
2.17: But when Jesus overheard their complaint, he said to them, “Who goes to the doctor for a cure? Those who are well or those who are sick? I have not come to call the ‘righteous,’ but those who are sinners and bring them to repentance.”
2.18: One time, the disciples of John the Baptizer and the Pharisees were fasting. So they came to Jesus and asked, “Why is it that John’s disciples and disciples of the Pharisees are fasting but your disciples are not?”
2.19: Jesus answered, “How can the sons of the bridal chamber fast when the bridegroom is next to them? As long as the bridegroom is with them they won’t,
2.20: but the days of fasting will come when the Bridegroom is taken from them.
2.21: “And who would mend worn-out clothing with new fabric? When the new cloth shrinks, it will rip, making the tear worse than before.
2.22: And who would pour new wine into an old wineskin? Eventually the wine will ferment and make the wineskin burst, losing everything—the wine will be spilled and the wineskin ruined. Instead, new wine is always poured into new wineskins.”
2.23: One Sabbath, Jesus and his disciples were walking through a field of wheat. The disciples were hungry, so they plucked off some heads of grain to eat.
2.24: But when some of the Pharisees saw what was happening, they said to him, “Look! Your disciples shouldn’t be harvesting grain on the Sabbath!”
2.25: Jesus responded, “Haven’t you ever read what King David and his men did when they were hungry?
2.26: They entered the house of God when Abiathar was high priest and ate the sacred bread of God’s presence. They violated the law by eating bread that only the priests were allowed to eat. But there is one here who is even greater than the temple.”
2.27: Then he said to them, “The Sabbath was made for the sake of people, and not people for the Sabbath.
2.28: For this reason the Son of Man exercises his lordship over the Sabbath.”

3.1: Then Jesus left them and went again into the synagogue, where he encountered a man who had an atrophied, paralyzed hand.
3.2: Everyone was watching Jesus closely to see if he would heal the man on the Sabbath, giving them a reason to accuse him of breaking Sabbath rules.
3.3: Jesus said to the man with the paralyzed hand, “Stand here in the middle of the room.”
3.4: Then he turned to all those gathered there and said, “Is it against the law to do evil on the Sabbath or to do good? To destroy a life or to save one?” But no one answered him a word.
3.5: Then looking around at everyone, Jesus was moved with indignation and grieved by the hardness of their hearts and said to the man, “Now stretch out your hand!” As he stretched out his hand, it was instantly healed!
3.6: After this happened, the Pharisees left abruptly and began to plot together with the friends and supporters of Herod Antipas on how they would kill Jesus.
3.7: Once again Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the lakeside, but a massive crowd of people followed him from all around the provinces of Galilee and southern Israel.
3.8: Vast crowds came from Jerusalem, Idumea, beyond the Jordan, and from Lebanon. Large numbers of people swarmed in from everywhere when they heard of him and his wonderful works.
3.9: The crowd pressed so closely to Jesus that he instructed his disciples to bring him a small boat to get into and keep from being crushed by the crowd.
3.10: For he had healed so many that the sick kept pushing forward just so they could touch Jesus.
3.11: And whenever a demon saw him, it would throw the person down at Jesus’ feet, screaming out, “You are the Son of God!”
3.12: But Jesus would silence the demons and sternly order them not to reveal who he was.
3.13: Afterward, Jesus went up on a mountainside and called to himself the men he wanted to be his close companions, so they went up with him.
3.14: He appointed the Twelve, whom he named apostles. He wanted them to be continually at his side as his friends, and so that he could send them out to preach
3.15: and have authority to heal the sick and to cast out demons.
3.16: He appointed his Twelve and gave Simon the nickname Peter the Rock.
3.17: And he gave the brothers, Jacob and John, the sons of Zebedee, the nickname Benay-Regah, which means “passionate sons.”
3.18: The others were Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, Jacob the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Nationalist,
3.19: and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him.
3.20: Then Jesus went home, but once again a large crowd gathered around him, which prevented him from even eating a meal.
3.21: When his own family heard that he was there, they went out to seize him, for they said, “He’s insane!”
3.22: The religious scholars who arrived from Jerusalem were saying, “Satan has possessed him! He casts out demons by the authority of the prince of demons!”
3.23: Jesus called them to himself and spoke to them using parables. “How can Satan cast out Satan?
3.24: No kingdom can endure if it is divided against itself,
3.25: and a fragmented household will not be able to stand, for it is divided.
3.26: And if Satan fights against himself he will not endure, and his end has come.”
3.27: Jesus said to them, “Listen. No one is able to break into a mighty man’s house and steal his property unless he first overpowers the mighty man and ties him up. Then his entire house can be plundered and his possessions taken.
3.28: I tell you this timeless truth: All sin will be forgiven, even all the blasphemies that are spoken.
3.29: But there can never be forgiveness for the one who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit, for he is guilty of an eternal sin!”
3.30: (This is because they said he was empowered by a demon spirit.)
3.31: Then Jesus’ mother and his brothers came and stood outside and sent a message to him, asking that he come out and speak with them.
3.32: When the crowd sitting around Jesus heard this, they spoke up, and said to him, “Jesus, your mother and brothers are outside looking for you.”
3.33: He answered them, “Who is my true mother and my true brothers?”
3.34: Then looking in the eyes of those who were sitting in a circle around him, he said, “Here are my true family members.
3.35: For whoever does the will of God is my brother, my sister, and my mother!”

4.1: Once again Jesus went to teach the people at the shore of Lake Galilee and a massive crowd surrounded him. The crowd was so huge that he had to get into a boat and teach the people from there.
4.2: He taught them many things by using parables to illustrate spiritual truths, saying:
4.3: “Consider this: A sower went out to sow.
4.4: As he sowed some fell along the beaten path and soon the birds came and ate it.
4.5: Some fell onto gravel with no topsoil and quickly sprouted since the soil had no depth.
4.6: But when the days grew hot, the sprouts were scorched and withered because they had insufficient roots.
4.7: Some fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
4.8: But some fell onto good, rich soil that kept producing a good harvest. Some yielded thirty, some sixty—and some a hundredfold!
4.9: If you understand this, then you need to respond.”
4.10: Afterward, Jesus’ disciples and those close to him remained behind to ask Jesus about his parables.
4.11: He said to them, “The privilege of intimately knowing the mystery of God’s kingdom realm has been granted to you, but not to the others, where everything is revealed in parables.
4.12: “For even when they see what I do, they will not understand, and when they hear what I say, they will learn nothing, otherwise they would repent and be forgiven.”
4.13: Then he said to them, “If you don’t understand this parable, how will you understand any parable?
4.14: Let me explain: The farmer sows the message of the kingdom.
4.15: What falls on the beaten path represents those who hear the message, but immediately Satan appears and snatches it from their hearts.
4.16: And what is sown on gravel represents those who hear the message and receive it joyfully,
4.17: but because their hearts fail to sink a deep root, they don’t endure for long. For when trouble or persecution comes on account of the message, they immediately wilt and fall away.
4.18: And what is sown among thorns represents those who hear the message,
4.19: but they allow the cares of this life and the seduction of wealth and the desires for other things to crowd out and choke the message so that it produces nothing.
4.20: “But what is sown on good soil represents those who open their hearts to receive the message and their lives bear good fruit—some yield a harvest of thirty, sixty, even a hundredfold!”
4.21: He also gave them this parable: “No one lights a lamp only to place it under a basket or under the bed. It is meant to be placed on a lampstand.
4.22: For there is nothing that is hidden that won’t be disclosed, and there is no secret that won’t be brought out into the light!
4.23: If you understand what I’m saying, you need to respond!”
4.24: Then he said to them, “Be diligent to understand the meaning behind everything you hear, for as you do, more understanding will be given to you. And according to your longing to understand, much more will be added to you.
4.25: For those who listen with open hearts will receive more revelation. But those who don’t listen with open hearts will lose what little they think they have!”
4.26: Jesus also told them this parable: “God’s kingdom realm is like someone spreading seed on the ground.
4.27: He goes to bed and gets up, day after day, and the seed sprouts and grows tall, though he knows not how.
4.28: All by itself it sprouts, and the soil produces a crop; first the green stem, then the head on the stalk, and then the fully developed grain in the head.
4.29: Then, when the grain is ripe, he immediately puts the sickle to the grain, because harvest time has come.”
4.30: And he told them this parable: “How can I describe God’s kingdom realm? Let me illustrate it with this parable.
4.31: It is like the mustard seed, the tiniest of all the seeds,
4.32: yet when it springs up and grows, it becomes the largest plant in the garden, with so many large spreading branches, even birds can nest in its shade.”
4.33: Jesus used many parables such as these as he taught the people, and they learned according to their ability to understand.
4.34: He never spoke to them without using parables, but would wait until he was alone with his disciples to explain to them their meanings.
4.35: That same day, after it grew dark, Jesus said to his disciples, “Let’s cross over to the other side of the lake.”
4.36: Leaving the crowd behind, the disciples got into the boat in which Jesus was already sitting, and they took him with them. Other boats sailed with them.
4.37: Suddenly, as they were crossing the lake, a ferocious storm arose, with violent winds and waves that were crashing into the boat until it was nearly swamped.
4.38: But Jesus was calmly sleeping in the stern, resting on a cushion.
4.39: So they shook him awake, saying, “Teacher, don’t you even care that we are all about to die!” Fully awake, he rebuked the storm and shouted to the sea, “Hush! Be still!” All at once the wind stopped howling and the water became perfectly calm.
4.40: Then he turned to his disciples and said to them, “Why are you so afraid? Haven’t you learned to trust yet?”
4.41: But they were overwhelmed with fear and awe and said to one another, “Who is this man who has such authority that even the wind and waves obey him?”

5.1: They arrived at the other side of the lake, at the region of the Gerasenes.
5.2: As Jesus stepped ashore, a demon-possessed madman came out of the graveyard and confronted him.
5.3: The man had been living there among the tombs, and no one was able to restrain him, not even with chains.
5.4: For every time they attempted to chain his hands and feet with shackles, he would snap the chains and break the shackles in pieces. He was so strong that no one had the power to subdue him.
5.5: Day and night he could be found lurking in the cemetery or in the vicinity, shrieking and cutting himself with stones!
5.6: When he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran to him and threw himself down before him,
5.7: shouting at the top of his lungs, “Leave me alone, Jesus, Son of the Most High God! Swear in God’s name that you won’t torture me!”
5.8: (For Jesus had already said to him, “Come out of that man, you demon spirit!”)
5.9: Jesus said to him, “What is your name?” “Mob,” he answered. “They call me Mob because there are thousands of us in his body!”
5.10: He begged Jesus repeatedly not to expel them out of the region.
5.11: Nearby there was a large herd of pigs feeding on the hillside.
5.12: The demons begged him, “Send us into the pigs. Let us enter them!”
5.13: So Jesus gave them permission, and the demon horde immediately came out of the man and went into the pigs! This caused the herd to rush madly down the steep slope and fall into the lake, drowning about two thousand pigs!
5.14: At this, the herdsmen ran to the nearby villages, telling everyone along the way what had happened, and the people came out to see for themselves.
5.15: When they found Jesus, they saw the demonized man sitting there, properly clothed and in his right mind. Seeing what had happened to the man possessed by many demons, the people became afraid.
5.16: Those who had witnessed this miracle reported the news to the people and included what had happened to the pigs.
5.17: Then they asked Jesus to leave their region.
5.18: And as Jesus began to get into the boat to depart, the man who had been set free from demons asked him, “Could I go with you?”
5.19: Jesus answered, “No,” but said to him, “Go back to your home and to your family and tell them what the Lord has done for you. Tell them how he had mercy on you.”
5.20: So the man left and went into the region of Jordan and parts of Syria to tell everyone he met about what Jesus had done for him, and all the people marveled!
5.21: After Jesus returned from across the lake, a huge crowd of people quickly gathered around him on the shoreline.
5.22: Just then, a man saw that it was Jesus, so he pushed through the crowd and threw himself down at his feet. His name was Jairus, a Jewish official who was in charge of the synagogue.
5.23: He pleaded with Jesus, saying over and over, “Please come with me! My little daughter is at the point of death, and she’s only twelve years old! Come and lay your hands on her and heal her and she will live!”
5.24: Immediately Jesus went with him, and the huge crowd followed, pressing in on him from all sides.
