15.2: This raised concerns among the Jewish religious leaders and experts of the law. Indignant, they grumbled and complained, saying, “Look at how this man associates with all these notorious sinners and welcomes them all to come to him!”
15.3: In response, Jesus gave them this illustration:
15.4: “There once was a shepherd with a hundred lambs, but one of his lambs wandered away and was lost. So the shepherd left the ninety-nine lambs out in the open field and searched in the wilderness for that one lost lamb. He didn’t stop until he finally found it. With exuberant joy, he raised it up, placed it on his shoulders, and carried it back with cheerful delight!
15.5: And then you would joyfully carry it home on your shoulders.
15.6: Returning home, he called all his friends and neighbors together and said, ‘Let’s have a party! Come and celebrate with me the return of my lost lamb. It wandered away, but I found it and brought it home.’ ”
15.7: Jesus continued, “In the same way, there will be a glorious celebration in heaven over the rescue of one lost sinner who repents, comes back home, and returns to the fold—more so than for all the righteous people who never strayed away.”
15.8: Jesus gave them another parable: “There once was a woman who had ten valuable silver coins. When she lost one of them, she swept her entire house, diligently searching every nook and cranny for that one lost coin.
15.9: When she finally found it, she gathered all her friends and neighbors for a celebration, telling them, ‘Come and celebrate with me! I had lost my precious silver coin, but now I’ve found it.’
15.10: That’s the way God responds every time one lost sinner repents and turns to him. He says to all his angels, ‘Let’s have a joyous celebration, for the one who was lost, I have found!’ ”
15.11: Then Jesus said, “Once there was a father with two sons.
15.12: The younger son came to his father and said, ‘Father, don’t you think it’s time to give me my share of your estate?’ So the father went ahead and distributed between the two sons their inheritance.
15.13: Shortly afterward, the younger son packed up all his belongings and traveled off to see the world. He journeyed to a far-off land where he soon wasted all he was given in a binge of extravagant and reckless living.
15.14: “With everything spent and nothing left, he grew hungry, because there was a severe famine in that land.
15.15: So he begged a farmer in that country to hire him. The farmer hired him and sent him out to feed the pigs.
15.16: The son was so famished, he was willing even to eat the slop given to the pigs, because no one would feed him a thing.
15.17: “Humiliated, the son finally realized what he was doing, and he thought, ‘There are many workers at my father’s house who have all the food they want with plenty to spare. They lack nothing. Why am I here dying of hunger, feeding these pigs and eating their slop?
15.18: I want to go back home to my father’s house, and I’ll say to him, “Father, I was wrong. I have sinned against you.
15.19: I’ll never again be worthy to be called your son. Please, Father, just treat me like one of your employees.” ’
15.20: “So the young son set off for home. From a long distance away, his father saw him coming, dressed as a beggar, and great compassion swelled up in his heart for his son who was returning home. The father raced out to meet him, swept him up in his arms, hugged him dearly, and kissed him over and over with tender love.
15.21: “Then the son said, ‘Father, I was wrong. I have sinned against you. I could never deserve to be called your son. Just let me be—’ “The father interrupted and said, ‘Son, you’re home now!’
15.22: “Turning to his servants, the father said, ‘Quick, bring me the best robe, my very own robe, and I will place it on his shoulders. Bring the ring, the seal of sonship, and I will put it on his finger. And bring out the best shoes you can find for my son.
15.23: Let’s prepare a great feast and celebrate.
15.24: For my beloved son was once dead, but now he’s alive! Once he was lost, but now he is found!’ And everyone celebrated with overflowing joy.
15.25: “Now, the older son was out working in the field when his brother returned, and as he approached the house, he heard the music of celebration and dancing.
15.26: He called over one of the servants and asked, ‘What’s going on?’
15.27: “The servant replied, ‘It’s your younger brother. He’s returned home and your father is throwing a party to celebrate his homecoming.’
15.28: “The older son became angry and refused to go in and celebrate. So his father came out and pleaded with him, ‘Come and enjoy the feast with us!’
15.29: “The son said, ‘Father, listen! How many years have I worked like a slave for you, performing every duty you’ve asked as a faithful son? And I’ve never once disobeyed you. But you’ve never thrown a party for me because of my faithfulness. Never once have you even given me a goat that I could feast on and celebrate with my friends as this son of yours is doing now.
15.30: Look at him! He comes back after wasting your wealth on prostitutes and reckless living, and here you are throwing a great feast to celebrate—for him!’
15.31: “The father said, ‘My son, you are always with me by my side. Everything I have is yours to enjoy.
15.32: It’s only right to rejoice and celebrate like this, because your brother was once dead and gone, but now he is alive and back with us again. He was lost, but now he is found!’ ”

16.1: Jesus taught his disciples using this story: “Once a very rich man hired a manager to run his business and oversee all his wealth. But soon a rumor spread that the manager was wasting his master’s money.
16.2: So the master called him in and said, ‘Is it true that you are mismanaging my estate? You need to provide me with a complete audit of everything you oversee for me. I’ve decided to dismiss you.’
16.3: “The manager thought, ‘Now what am I going to do? I’m finished here. I can’t hide what I’ve done, and I’m too proud to beg.
16.4: I have an idea that will secure my future. It will win me favor and secure friends who can take care of me and help me when I get fired!’
16.5: “So the dishonest manager hatched his scheme. He went to everyone who owed his master money, one by one, and asked them, ‘How much do you owe my master?’
16.6: One debtor owed twenty thousand dollars, so he said to him, ‘Let me see your bill. Pay me now and we’ll settle for twenty percent less.’ The clever manager scratched out the original amount owed and reduced it by twenty percent. And to another who owed two hundred thousand dollars, he said, ‘Pay me now and we’ll reduce your bill by fifty percent.’ And the clever manager scratched out the original amount owed and reduced it by half.
16.7: "'And how much do you owe my employer?' he asked the next man. 'A thousand bushels of wheat,' was the reply. 'Here,' the manager said, 'take your bill and replace it with one for only eight hundred bushels. '
16.8: “Even though his master was defrauded, when he found out about the shrewd way this manager had feathered his own nest, he congratulated the clever scoundrel for what he’d done to provide for his future.” Jesus continued, “Remember this: The sons of darkness interact more wisely than the sons of light.
16.9: Use the wealth of this world to demonstrate your friendship with God by winning friends and blessing others. Then, when it runs out, your generosity will provide you with an eternal reward.
16.10: “The one who faithfully manages the little he has been given will be promoted and trusted with greater responsibilities. But those who cheat with the little they have been given will not be considered trustworthy to receive more.
16.11: If you have not handled the riches of this world with integrity, why should you be trusted with the eternal treasures of the spiritual world?
16.12: And if you’ve not proven yourself faithful with what belongs to another, why should you be given wealth of your own?
16.13: It is impossible for a person to serve two masters at the same time. You will be forced to love one and reject the other. One master will be despised and the other will have your loyal devotion. Your choice between God and the wealth of this world is no different. You must enthusiastically love one and definitively reject the other.”
16.14: Now, the Jewish religious leaders listening to Jesus were lovers of money. They laughed at what he said and mocked his teachings,
16.15: so Jesus addressed them directly. “You always want to look spiritual in the eyes of others, but you have forgotten the eyes of God, which see what is inside you. The very things that you approve of and applaud are the things God despises.
16.16: The law of Moses and the revelation of the prophets have prepared you for the arrival of the kingdom announced by John. Since that time, the wonderful news of God’s kingdom is being preached, and people’s hearts burn with extreme passion to receive it.
16.17: Heaven and earth will disintegrate before even the smallest detail of the Law will fail or lose its power.
16.18: “It is wrong for you to divorce your wife so that you can marry another—that is adultery. And when you take that one you lusted after as your wife, and contribute to the breakup of her marriage, you commit adultery again.”
16.19: Jesus continued. “There once was a very rich man who had the finest things imaginable, living every day enjoying his life of opulent luxury.
16.20: Outside the gate of his mansion was a poor beggar named Lazarus. He lay there every day, covered with boils, and all the neighborhood dogs would come and lick his open sores. The only food he had to eat was the garbage that the rich man threw away.
16.21: As Lazarus lay there longing for scraps from the rich man's table, the dogs would come and lick his open sores.
16.22: “One day poor Lazarus died, and the angels of God came and escorted his spirit into paradise.
16.23: “The day came that the rich man also died. In hell he looked up from his torment and saw Abraham in the distance, and Lazarus was standing beside him in the glory.
16.24: The rich man shouted, ‘Father Abraham! Father Abraham! Have mercy on me. Send Lazarus to dip his finger in water and come to cool my tongue, for I am in agony in these flames of fire!’
16.25: “But Abraham responded, ‘My friend, don’t you remember? While you were alive, you had all you desired. You surrounded yourself in luxury, while Lazarus had nothing. Now Lazarus dwells in the comforts of paradise and you are in agony.
16.26: Besides, between us is a huge chasm that cannot be bridged, nor can anyone cross from one realm to the other, even if he wanted.’
16.27: “The rich man continued, ‘Then let me ask you, Father Abraham, please send Lazarus to my relatives.
16.28: Tell him to witness to my five brothers and warn them not to end up where I am in this place of torment.’
16.29: “Abraham replied, ‘They’ve already had plenty of warning. They have the teachings of Moses and the revelation of the prophets; let them hear them.’
16.30: “ ‘What if they’re not listening?’ the rich man added. ‘If someone from the dead were to go and warn them, they would surely repent.’
16.31: “Abraham said to him, ‘If they wouldn’t listen to Moses and the prophets, neither would they be convinced if someone were raised from the dead!’ ”

17.1: One day Jesus taught his disciples: “Betrayals are inevitable, but great devastation will come to the one guilty of betraying others.
17.2: It would be better for him to have a heavy boulder tied around his neck and be hurled into the deepest sea than to face the punishment of betraying one of my dear ones! So be alert to your brother’s condition,
17.3: and if you see him going the wrong direction, cry out and correct him. If there is true repentance on his part, forgive him.
17.4: No matter how many times in one day your brother sins against you and says, ‘I’m sorry; I am changing; forgive me,’ you need to forgive him each and every time.”
17.5: Upon hearing this, the apostles said to Jesus, “Lord, you must increase our measure of faith!”
17.6: Jesus responded, “If you have even the smallest measure of faith, it would be powerful enough to say to this large tree, ‘My faith will pull you up by the roots and throw you into the sea,’ and it will respond to your faith and obey you.”
17.7: Jesus continued, “After a servant has finished his work in the field or with the livestock, he doesn’t immediately sit down to relax and eat. No, a true servant prepares the food for his master and makes sure his master is served his meal before he sits down to eat his own.
17.8: He must first prepare his master's meal and serve him his supper before eating his own.
17.9: Does the servant expect to be thanked for doing what is required of him?
17.10: So learn this lesson: After doing all that is commanded of you, simply say, ‘We are mere servants, undeserving of special praise, for we are just doing what is expected of us and fulfilling our duties.’ ”
17.11: On his way to Jerusalem Jesus passed through the border region between Samaria and Galilee.
17.12: As he entered one village, ten men approached him, but they kept their distance, for they were lepers.
17.13: They shouted to him, “Mighty Lord, our wonderful Master! Won’t you have mercy on us and heal us?”
17.14: When Jesus stopped to look at them, he spoke these words: “Go to be examined by the Jewish priests.” They set off, and they were healed while walking along the way.
17.15: One of them, a Samaritan, when he discovered that he was completely healed, turned back to find Jesus, shouting out joyous praises and glorifying God.
17.16: When he found Jesus, he fell down at his feet and thanked him over and over, saying to him, “You are the Messiah.”
17.17: “So where are the other nine?” Jesus asked. “Weren’t there ten who were healed?
17.18: They all refused to return to give thanks and give glory to God except you, a foreigner from Samaria?”
17.19: Then Jesus said to the healed man lying at his feet, “Arise and go. It was your faith that brought you salvation and made you whole.”
17.20: Jesus was once asked by the Jewish religious leaders, “When will God’s kingdom come?” Jesus responded, “God’s kingdom does not come simply by obeying principles or waiting for signs.
17.21: The kingdom is not discovered in one place or another, for God’s kingdom realm is already expanding within some of you.”
17.22: Later, Jesus addressed this again with his apostles, saying, “The time is coming when a great passion will be awakened within you to see me again. Yes, you will long to see the beginning of the days of the Son of Man, but you won’t be able to find me.
17.23: You will hear reports from some who will say, ‘Look, he has returned,’ ‘He’s over here,’ or, ‘He’s over there!’ Don’t believe it or run after them, for their claims will be false.
17.24: The day of the Son of Man will burst forth with the brightness of a lightning strike that shines from one end of the sky to the other, illuminating the earth.
17.25: “But before this takes place, the Son of Man must pass through great suffering and rejection from this generation.
17.26: The same things that happened in the days of Noah will take place in the days of the Son of Man.
17.27: They were eating, they were drinking, they were marrying, and they were given in marriage until the day Noah boarded the ark and the devastating flood came and swept them all away.
17.28: “The days of the Son of Man can also be compared to the days of Lot. The people of that time lived their lives as normal. They got married, raised families, built homes and businesses, yet they were totally unaware of what was coming until the day Lot departed from Sodom. The sky opened up and rained fire and burning sulfur upon them, destroying everyone and everything they had built. So it will be on the day of the unveiling of the Son of Man.
17.29: until the morning Lot left Sodom. Then fire and burning sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed them all.
17.30: Yes, it will be 'business as usual' right up to the hour when the Son of Man returns.
17.31: “On that day, if one is outside, he won’t even have time to go back into the house to gather his belongings. And those toiling in their fields won’t have time to run back home.
17.32: Don’t forget the example of Lot’s wife and what happened to her when she turned back.
17.33: All who are obsessed with being secure in life will lose it all—including their lives. But those who let go of their lives and surrender them to me will discover true life.
17.34: For in that night there will be two lying in their bed; one will be suddenly swept away while the other will be left alive.
17.35: There will be two women working together at household duties; one will be suddenly swept away while the other will be left alive.”
17.37: His apostles asked, “Lord, where will this judgment happen?” Jesus responded, “ It will be obvious, for wherever there are those spiritually dead, there you will find the eagles circling.”

18.1: One day Jesus taught the apostles to keep praying and never stop or lose hope. He shared with them this illustration:
18.2: “In a certain town there was a judge, a thick-skinned and godless man who had no fear of others’ opinions.
18.3: And in the same town there was a poor widow who kept pleading with the judge, ‘Grant me justice and protect me from my oppressor!’
18.4: “He ignored her pleas for quite some time, but she kept asking. Eventually he said to himself, ‘This widow keeps annoying me, demanding her rights, and I’m tired of listening to her. Even though I’m not a religious man, and I don’t care about the opinions of others, I’ll get her off my back by answering her claims for justice and I’ll rule in her favor. Then she’ll leave me alone.’ ”
18.5: 'but this woman is driving me crazy. I'm going to see that she gets justice, because she is wearing me out with her constant requests!'"
18.6: Jesus continued, “Did you hear what the godless judge said—that he would answer her persistent request?
18.7: Don’t you know that God, the true judge, will grant justice to all his chosen ones who cry out to him night and day? He will pour out his Spirit upon them. He will not delay to answer you and give you what you ask for.
18.8: God will give swift justice to those who don’t give up. So be ever praying, ever expecting, in the same way as the widow. Even so, when the Son of Man comes back, will he find this kind of undying faith on earth?”
18.9: Jesus taught this parable to those who were convinced they were morally upright and to those who trusted in their own virtue yet looked down on others with disgust:
18.10: “Two men who went into the temple to pray. One was a proud religious leader, the other a despised tax collector.
18.11: The religious leader stood apart from the others and prayed, ‘How I thank you, O God, that I’m not wicked like everyone else. They’re cheaters, swindlers, and crooks—like that tax collector over there. God, you know that I never cheat or commit adultery; I fast from food twice a week and I give you a tenth of all I earn.’
18.12: I fast twice a week, and I give you a tenth of my income.'
18.13: “The tax collector stood alone in a corner, away from the Holy Place, and covered his face in his hands, feeling that he was unworthy even to look up to God. Beating his breast, he sobbed with brokenness and tears saying, ‘God, please, in your mercy and because of the blood sacrifice, forgive me, for I am nothing but the most miserable of all sinners!’
18.14: “Which one of them left for home that day reconciled to God? The humble tax collector, not the religious leader! For everyone who praises himself will one day be publicly humiliated, and everyone who humbles himself will one day be publicly honored and lifted up.”
18.15: The people brought their babies and small children to Jesus so that he might lay his hands on them to bless them. When the disciples saw this, they scolded the parents and told them to stop troubling the Master.
18.16: Seeing what was happening, Jesus called for the parents, the children, and his disciples to come and listen to him. Then he told them, “Never hinder a child from coming to me but let them all come, for God’s kingdom belongs to them as much as it does to anyone else. These children demonstrate to you what faith is all about.
18.17: Learn this well: unless you receive the revelation of the kingdom the same way a little child receives it, you will never be able to enter in.”
18.18: One day a wealthy Jewish nobleman of high standing posed this question to Jesus: “Wonderful Teacher, what must I do to receive eternal life?”
18.19: Jesus answered, “Why would you call me wonderful when there is only one who is wonderful—and that is God alone?
18.20: You already know what is right and what the commandments teach: ‘Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not lie, and honor your father and your mother.’ ”
18.21: The wealthy leader replied, “These are the very things I’ve been doing for as long as I can remember.”
18.22: “Ah,” Jesus said, “there’s still one thing you’re missing in your life.” “What is that?” asked the man. “You must go and sell everything you own and give all the proceeds to the poor so you will have eternal treasures. Then come and follow me.”
18.23: These words devastated the rich leader, for he was extremely wealthy.
18.24: Jesus saw his disappointment, and looking right at him said, “It is next to impossible for those who have everything to enter into God’s kingdom.
18.25: Nothing could be harder! You could compare it to trying to stuff a rope through the eye of a needle.”
18.26: Those who heard this said, “Then who can be saved?”
18.27: Jesus responded, “What appears humanly impossible is more than possible with God. For God can do what man cannot.”
18.28: Peter said, “Master, see how we’ve left all that we have, our houses and our careers, to follow you.”
18.29: Jesus replied, “Listen to my words: anyone who leaves his home behind and chooses God’s kingdom over wife, children, parents, and family, it will come back to him many more times in this lifetime. And in the age to come, he will inherit even more than that—he will inherit eternal life!”
18.30: will be repaid many times over in this life, as well as receiving eternal life in the world to come."
18.31: Jesus took the Twelve aside and told them in private, “We are going to Jerusalem so that everything prophesied about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.
18.32: They will betray him and hand him over to the people, and they will mock him, insult him, and spit in his face.
18.33: And after they have abused and flogged the Son of Man, they will kill him. But in three days he will rise again.”
18.34: The disciples had no clue what he was saying, for his words were a mystery that was hidden from them.
18.35: As Jesus and his followers arrived at Jericho, a blind beggar was sitting by the roadside.
18.36: When he heard the crowd approaching, he asked, “What’s all this commotion about?”
18.37: “It’s Jesus!” they said. “Jesus the Nazarene is passing by.”
18.38: The blind beggar shouted, “Jesus, Son of David, have pity and show me mercy!”
18.39: Those in the front of the crowd scolded him and warned him to be quiet, but the blind beggar screamed out even louder, “Jesus, Son of David, show me mercy!”
18.40: Suddenly Jesus stopped and directed those nearby, “Bring the man over to me.” When they brought him before Jesus, he asked the man,
18.41: “What do you want me to do for you?” “Master,” he said, “please, I want to see.”
18.42: Jesus said, “Now you will see. Receive your sight this moment, for your faith in me has given you sight and new life.”
18.43: Instantly he could see again. His eyes popped open, and he saw Jesus standing in front of him! He shouted loud praises to God and he followed Jesus. And when the crowd saw what happened, they too erupted with shouts of praise to God.

19.1: On his way to Jerusalem, Jesus had to pass through Jericho.
19.2: There lived a very wealthy man named Zacchaeus, who supervised all the tax collectors.
19.3: He was very eager to see Jesus and kept trying to get a look at him through the massive crowd. Since Zacchaeus was a short man and couldn’t see over the heads of the people,
19.4: he ran on ahead of everyone and climbed up a blossoming fig tree to get a glimpse of Jesus as he passed by.
19.5: When Jesus got to that place, he looked up into the tree and said, “Zacchaeus, hurry on down, for I must stay at your house today!”
19.6: So he scurried down the tree and found himself face-to-face with Jesus.
19.7: As Jesus left to go with Zacchaeus, many in the crowd complained, “Look at this! Of all the people to have dinner with, he’s going to eat in the house of a crook.”
19.8: Zacchaeus was amazed over his gracious visit to his home and joyously welcomed Jesus. Zacchaeus stood in front of the Lord and said, “Half of all that I own I will give to the poor. And Lord, if I have cheated anyone, I promise to pay them back four times as much as I stole.”
19.9: Jesus said to him, “Your repentance shows that today life has come to you and your household, and that you are a true son of Abraham.
19.10: The Son of Man has come to seek out and to give life to those who are lost.”
19.11: At this time Jesus was getting close to entering Jerusalem. The crowds that followed him were convinced that God’s kingdom would fully manifest when Jesus established it in Jerusalem.
19.12: So he told them this story to change their perspective: “Once a wealthy prince left his province to travel to a distant land, where he would be crowned king and then return.
19.13: Before he departed he summoned his ten servants together and charged them, ‘I am entrusting each of you with fifty thousand dollars to invest while I am away. Trade with it and put the money to work until I return.’
19.14: “Some of his countrymen despised the prince and sent a delegation after him to declare before the royals, ‘We refuse to let this man rule over us! He will not be our king!’
19.15: “Nevertheless, he was crowned king and returned to his land. Then he summoned his ten servants to see how much each one had earned and what their profits came to.
19.16: “The first one came forward and said, ‘Master, I took what you gave me and invested it, and it multiplied ten times.’
19.17: “ ‘Splendid! You have done well, my excellent servant. Because you have shown that I can trust you in this small matter, I now grant you authority to rule over ten cities.’
19.18: “The second came and said, ‘Master, what you left with me has multiplied five times.’
19.19: “His master said, ‘I also grant you authority in my kingdom over five cities.’
19.20: “Another came before the king and said, ‘Master, here is the money you entrusted to me. I hid it for safekeeping.
19.21: You see, I live in fear of you, for everyone knows you are a strict master and impossible to please. You push us for a high return on all that you own, and you always want to gain from someone else’s efforts.’
19.22: “The king said, ‘You wicked servant! I will judge you using your own words. If what you said about me is true, that I am a harsh man, pushing you for a high return and wanting gain from others’ efforts,
19.23: why didn’t you at least put my money in the bank to earn some interest on it?’
19.24: “The king said to his other servants, ‘Take the money he has and give it to the faithful servant who multiplied my money ten times over.’
19.25: “ ‘But master,’ the other servants objected, ‘why give it to him? He already has so much!’
19.26: “ ‘Yes,’ replied the king. ‘But to all who have been faithful, I will give even more to them. And for the ones who have nothing, even the little they seem to have I will take from them.
19.27: Now, bring all those rebellious enemies of mine who rejected me as their king—bring them here before me and execute them!’ ”
19.28: After saying all of this, Jesus headed straight for Jerusalem.
19.29: When he arrived at the stables of Annia near the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples ahead, saying,
19.30: “When you enter the next village, you will find tethered there a donkey’s young colt that has never been ridden. Untie it and bring it to me.
19.31: And if anyone stops you and asks, ‘What are you doing?’ just tell them this: ‘It is needed for the Lord.’ ”
19.32: The two disciples entered the village and found the colt exactly like Jesus had said.
19.33: While they were untying it, the owners confronted them and asked, “What are you doing?”
19.34: The disciples replied, “We need this donkey for the Lord.”
19.35: After they brought the colt to Jesus, they placed their prayer shawls on its back, and Jesus rode it as he descended the Mount of Olives toward Jerusalem. As he rode toward the city, people spontaneously threw their prayer shawls like a carpet on the path in front of him.
19.36: Then the crowds spread out their coats on the road ahead of Jesus.
19.37: As soon as he got to the bottom of the Mount of Olives, the crowd of his followers shouted with a loud outburst of ecstatic joy over all the mighty wonders of power they had witnessed.
19.38: They shouted over and over, “Highest praises to God for the one who comes as King in the name of the Lord! Heaven’s peace and glory from the highest realm now comes to us!”
19.39: Some Jewish religious leaders who stood off from the procession said to Jesus, “Teacher, order your followers at once to stop saying these things!”
19.40: Jesus responded, “Listen to me. If my followers were silenced, the very stones would break forth with praises!”
19.41: When Jesus caught sight of the city, he burst into tears with uncontrollable weeping over Jerusalem,
19.42: saying, “If only you could recognize that this day peace is within your reach! But you cannot see it.
19.43: For the day is soon coming when your enemies will surround you, hem you in on every side, and lay siege to you.
19.44: They will crush you to pieces, and your children too! And they will leave your city totally destroyed. Since you would not recognize God’s day of visitation, you will see your day of devastation!”
19.45: Jesus entered the temple area and forcibly threw out all the merchants from their stalls.
19.46: He rebuked them, saying, “The Scriptures declare, ‘My Father’s house is to be filled with prayer—a house of prayer, not a cave of bandits!’ ”
19.47: From then on Jesus continued teaching in the temple area, but the high priests, the experts of the law, and the prominent men of the city kept trying to find a strategy to accuse Jesus, for they wanted him dead.
19.48: They could find no reason to accuse him, for he was a hero to the people and the crowds were awestruck by every word he spoke.

20.1: One day Jesus was teaching in the temple courts and sharing with the people the wonderful news of salvation. The high priest, the experts of the law, and the prominent men of the city confronted Jesus and asked him,
20.2: “We want to know right now by what authority are you teaching here in the temple? And who gave you the authority to teach these things?”
20.3: Jesus responded, “First, let me ask you a question and you tell me right now.
20.4: Did John baptize because he had a commission from heaven or merely from men?”
20.5: His interrogators pulled themselves aside to consider how to respond to Jesus. “What should we say? If we say that John’s mandate was from heaven, he will ask us, ‘Then why didn’t you believe him and be baptized?’
20.6: But if we say, ‘John’s mandate was merely from men,’ then all the people around him will stone us, for they believe John was a prophet of God.”
20.7: So unable to devise an answer they said to Jesus, “We cannot tell where John’s authority came from.”
20.8: Jesus said, “Then neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
20.9: Jesus taught the people using this story: “A man once planted a vineyard, then leased it out to tenants. Then he left to go abroad and was away for a long time.
20.10: At harvest time, the owner sent one of his servants to the tenants to collect the landowner’s share of the harvest, but the tenants sent him away, beaten and empty-handed.
20.11: So the owner dispatched another one of his servants to collect his portion, but the tenants treated him the same way. They cursed him, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.
20.12: Then the owner sent a third servant, but they brutalized him also with the same treatment.
20.13: Finally the owner of the vineyard said to his son, ‘Perhaps if I send you, my own cherished son, they will be ashamed of what they’ve done.’
20.14: “But when the tenants saw the son coming, they schemed among themselves. ‘This is the heir of the vineyard! If we kill him, the inheritance will be ours.’
20.15: So they threw the son off the property and killed him. “I ask you, what do you think the owner of the vineyard will do to his son’s murderers?
20.16: He will come back and destroy them and give his vineyard to another.” When the people heard this story, they all agreed, “This should never happen!”
20.17: Jesus looked straight at the people and their leaders and said, “What do you think this verse means? ‘The worthless, rejected stone has become the cornerstone, the most important stone of all.’
20.18: Everyone who falls in humility upon that stone will be broken. But if that stone falls on you, it will grind you to pieces!”
20.19: When the high priests and experts of the law realized that this story was about them, they wanted to have Jesus arrested that very moment, but they were afraid of all the people.
20.20: Later, they sent spies who pretended to be honest seekers, but who wanted an opportunity to entangle Jesus by his words. Their plan was to catch him saying something against the government, so they could hand him over to the jurisdiction of the Roman authorities who would execute him for sedition.
20.21: At the right time they asked him this question: “Teacher, we know that all you say is straightforward and what you teach us is right. You give us the true ways of God. You’re one who shows no favoritism to anyone’s status. So we ask you—
20.22: is it proper or not to pay taxes to a corrupt government?”
20.23: Jesus saw right through their cunning ploy and said, “Why are you testing me?
20.24: Show me one of the Roman coins. Whose head is on the coin? Whose title is stamped on it?” They answered, “Why, it’s Caesar’s.”
20.25: Jesus said, “Precisely. The coin bears the image of the Emperor Caesar, and you should give back to Caesar all that belongs to him. But you bear the image of God. So give back to God all that belongs to him.”
20.26: The imposters were left speechless and amazed in the presence of all the people, unable to trap Jesus with his words.
20.27: Some of the Sadducees (a religious group that denies there is a resurrection of the dead) came to ask Jesus this question:
20.28: “Teacher, the law of Moses teaches that if a man dies before he has children, his brother should marry the widow and raise up children for his brother’s family line.
20.29: Now suppose there was a family with seven brothers, and the oldest married and died without children.
20.30: Then his brother married the widow, and he too died with no children. And it continued to happen, one brother after another brother, until each of the seven had married the widow and died childless.
20.31: And so it went, one after the other, until each of the seven had married her and died, leaving no children.
20.32: Then finally, the widow died too. So here’s our dilemma:
20.33: Whose wife will the woman be when she’s resurrected from the dead? Which of the brothers will be her husband, since all seven were once married to her?”
20.34: Jesus replied, “Marriage is meant for this world only.
20.35: Those who are worthy of the resurrection from the dead into glory become immortal, like the angels, who never die nor marry. When the dead come to life again, they will be children of God—the children of the resurrection.
20.36: And they will never die again. In these respects they are like angels. They are children of God raised up to new life.
20.37: Even Moses taught the resurrection of the dead when he wrote of the Lord God who was at the burning bush and said ‘I am the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.’
20.38: Don’t you agree that God is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living? For in his eyes, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are alive forevermore. He is the God who raises the dead.”
20.39: The experts of the law chimed in, “Yes, Teacher, you speak the truth beautifully.”
20.40: From then on, the religious Sadducees never dared ask Jesus a question again.
20.41: Jesus then posed this question to the people: “How can the experts of the law say that Messiah is David’s son?
20.42: Haven’t you read in the Psalms where David himself wrote: The Lord Yahweh said to my Lord, ‘Sit near me in the place of authority
20.43: until I subdue all your enemies under Your feet!’ ”
20.44: Jesus explained, “If David calls this one ‘my Lord,’ how can he be his son?”
20.45: Within earshot of all the people, Jesus warned his disciples,
20.46: “Don’t follow the example of these pretentious experts of the law! They love to parade around in their religious garments so that people honor them wherever they go. They like to sit right up front in every meeting and push their way to the head table at every banquet.
20.47: And for an offering they will pray long religious prayers at the homes of widows, cheating them out of their very livelihood. Beware of them all, because one day the Judge will strip them of honor, and judge them severely.”

21.1: Jesus observed all the wealthy coming into the temple courts wanting to be noticed as they came with their offerings.
21.2: He noticed a very poor widow who dropped two small copper coins in the offering box.
21.3: “Listen to me,” he said. “This poor widow has given a larger offering than any of the wealthy.
21.4: For the rich only gave out of their surplus, but she sacrificed out of her poverty and gave to God all that she had to live on.”
21.5: Some of the disciples remarked about the beauty of the temple. They pointed out all the lovely adornments and how it was built with excellence from the gifts given to God. Jesus said,
21.6: “The day of utter destruction will come to everything you admire here. It will all become a heap of rubble!”
21.7: “Master, tell us,” they asked, “when exactly will this happen? Can you tell us what warning sign to look for when it is about to take place?”
21.8: Jesus responded, “Deception will run rampant and many will appear on the scene, saying I have sent them, or saying about themselves, ‘I am the Messiah!’ These doomsday deceivers will say, ‘The end of the age is now here!’ But listen to me. Don’t let any of these imposters fool you.
21.9: “There will also be many wars and revolutions on every side, with rumors of more wars to come. Don’t panic or give in to your fears, for these things are bound to happen. This is still not the end yet.”
21.10: Jesus continued, “ There will be upheavals of every kind. Nations will go to war against each other, and kingdom against kingdom.
21.11: There will be terrible earthquakes and seismic events of epic proportion that result in famines in one place after another. There will be horrible plagues and epidemics, cataclysmic storms on the earth, and astonishing signs and cosmic disturbances in the heavens. But before all of this happens, you will be hunted down and arrested, persecuted by both civil and religious authorities, and thrown into prison.
21.12: And because you follow me, you will be on trial before kings and governmental leaders as an opportunity to testify to them in my name.
21.13: This will be your opportunity to tell them about me.
21.14: Yet determine in your hearts not to prepare for your own defense. Simply speak with the words of wisdom that I will give you that moment, and none of your persecutors will be able to withstand the grace and wisdom that comes from your mouths.
21.15: for I will give you the right words and such wisdom that none of your opponents will be able to reply!
21.16: “You can expect betrayal even by your parents, your brothers, your relatives and friends—and yes, some of you will die as martyrs.
21.17: You will be hated by all because of my life in you.
21.18: But don’t worry. My grace will never desert you or depart from your life.
21.19: Stand firm with patient endurance and you will find your souls’ deliverance.”
21.20: “When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, you will know for sure that its devastation is imminent.
21.21: At that time all who are living in Judea must flee to the mountains. Those who live inside the city gates, leave and flee, and those who live outside the city must not enter it seeking refuge.
21.22: For these will be the days of God’s vengeance to fulfill what has been written against Jerusalem.
21.23: It will be extremely difficult for pregnant women and for those nursing little ones in that day, for great persecution and wrath will rise against this nation.
21.24: Many will be cut down by the sword or scattered as prisoners to many countries. And Jerusalem shall be trampled down by nations until the days of world empires come to an end.”
21.25: “Expect to witness amazing and perplexing signs with the sun, the moon, and the stars. The raging of the sea will bring desperation and turmoil to many nations.
21.26: Earthquakes will bring panic and disaster. What men see coming to the earth will cause the fear of doom to grip their hearts, for they will even see the powers of the heavenly realm shaken!
21.27: “And at last, when you see how the Son of Man comes—surrounded with a cloud, with great power and miracles, in the radiance of his splendor, and with great glory and praises —it will make you jump for joy! For the time of your full transformation has arrived.”
21.28: So when all these things begin to happen, stand straight and look up, for your salvation is near!"
21.29: Jesus gave his disciples this parable: “Haven’t you observed that when the fig tree, or any tree, buds and blooms, the season is changing and summer is near?
21.30: When the leaves come out, you know without being told that summer is near.
21.31: In the same way, when you see these prophetic signs occurring, you realize the earth is yielding to the fullness of God’s kingdom.
21.32: I assure you, the end of this age will not come until all I have spoken has come to pass.
21.33: Earth and sky will wear out and fade away before one word I speak loses its power or fails to accomplish its purpose.”
21.34: “Be careful that you never allow your hearts to grow cold. Be careful that you are not caught off guard, or your hearts will be weighed down with carousing, drunkenness, and the worries of this life, and that day will come upon you suddenly like a trap. Don’t let me come and find you drunk or living carelessly like everyone else.
21.35: For that day will come as a shocking surprise to all.
21.36: Keep a constant watch over your soul, and pray for the courage and grace to prevail over these things that are destined to occur and that you will stand before the presence of the Son of Man with a clear conscience.”
21.37: Each day, Jesus taught in the temple and spent his nights on the Mount of Olives.
21.38: And all the people came early to the temple courts to listen to the words he taught.

22.1: As the celebration of the Passover Lamb was approaching, the Jewish religious leaders and scholars of the law continually schemed to find a way to murder Jesus without starting a riot—for they feared the crowds.
22.2: The leading priests and teachers of religious law were actively plotting Jesus' murder. But they wanted to kill him without starting a riot, a possibility they greatly feared.
22.3: At that time Satan himself entered into Judas the locksmith, who was one of the twelve apostles.
22.4: He secretly went to the religious hierarchy and the captains of the temple guards to discuss with them how he could betray Jesus and turn him over to their hands.
22.5: The religious hierarchy was elated over Judas’ treachery, and they agreed to give him a sum of money in exchange for Jesus’ betrayal.
22.6: Judas vowed that he would find them a suitable opportunity to betray Jesus when he was away from the crowds.
22.7: On the day the Passover lambs were to be sacrificed, Jesus sent for Peter and John and instructed them, “Go and prepare the Passover supper so we can eat it together.”
22.8: Jesus sent Peter and John ahead and said, "Go and prepare the Passover meal, so we can eat it together."
22.9: They asked him, “Where do we make the preparations to eat the meal?”
22.10: Jesus gave them this sign: “When you enter the city, you will find a man carrying a jug of water. Follow him home
22.11: and say to the owner of the house, ‘The Teacher told us to ask you, “Where is the room I may use to have the Passover meal with my disciples?” ’
22.12: He will then take you to a large, fully furnished upstairs room. Make the preparations for us there.”
22.13: They went and found everything to be exactly like Jesus had prophesied, and they prepared the Passover meal.
22.14: When Jesus arrived at the upper room, he took his place at the table along with all the apostles.
22.15: Then he told them, “I have longed with passion and desire to eat this Passover lamb with you before I endure my sufferings.
22.16: I promise you that the next time we eat this, we will be together in the feast of God’s kingdom.”
22.17: Then he raised a cup and gave thanks to God and said to them, “Take this and pass it on to one another and drink.
22.18: I promise you that the next time we drink this wine, we will be together in the feast of God’s kingdom.”
22.19: Then he lifted up a loaf, and after praying a prayer of thanksgiving to God, he gave each of his apostles a piece of bread, saying, “This loaf is my body, which is now being offered to you. Always eat it to remember me.”
22.20: After supper was over, he lifted the cup again and said, “This cup is my blood of the new covenant I make with you, and it will be poured out soon for all of you.
22.21: But I want you to know that the hands of the one who delivers me to be the sacrifice are with mine on the table this very moment.
22.22: The Son of Man must now go where he will be sacrificed. But there will be great and unending doom for the man who betrays me.”
22.23: The apostles questioned among themselves which one of them was about to do this.
22.24: The disciples bickered over which one of them would be considered the greatest in the kingdom.
22.25: Jesus interrupted their argument, saying, “The kings and men of authority in this world rule oppressively over their subjects, claiming that they do it for the good of the people. They are obsessed with how others see them.
22.26: But this is not your calling. You will lead by a different model. The greatest one among you will live as one called to serve others without honor. The greatest honor and authority is reserved for the one who has a servant heart.
22.27: The leaders who are served are the most important in your eyes, but in the kingdom, it is the servants who lead. Am I not here with you as one who serves?
22.28: “Because you have stood with me through all my trials and ordeals,
22.29: I am promising you the kingdom that the Father has promised me.
22.30: We will celebrate in this kingdom and you will feast with me at my table. And each of you will be given a throne, twelve thrones in all, and you will be made rulers on thrones to judge the tribes of Israel.”
22.31: “Peter, my dear friend, listen to what I’m about to tell you. Satan has obtained permission to come and sift you all like wheat and test your faith.
22.32: But I have prayed for you, Peter, that you would stay faithful to me no matter what comes. Remember this: after you have turned back to me and have been restored, make it your life mission to strengthen the faith of your brothers.”
22.33: “But Lord,” Peter replied, “I am ready to stand with you to the very end, even if it means prison or death!”
22.34: Jesus looked at him and prophesied, “Before the rooster crows in the morning, you will deny three times that you even know me.”
22.35: Then he said to all of them, “When I sent you out empty-handed, did you lack anything?” “Not a thing,” they answered. “God provided all we needed.” Jesus said, “But now I say to you: Take what you need.
22.36: If you have money, take it —and a knapsack and a sword. Danger is imminent.
22.37: For the prophetic Scripture about me ‘He will be accused of being a criminal’ will now come to pass. All that was prophesied of me will be fulfilled.”
22.38: The disciples told him, “Lord, we already have two swords!” “You still don’t understand,” Jesus responded.
22.39: Jesus left the upper room with his disciples and, as was his habit, went to the Mount of Olives, his place of secret prayer.
22.40: There he told the apostles, “Keep praying for strength to be spared from the severe test of your faith that is about to come.”
22.41: Then he withdrew from them a short distance to be alone. Kneeling down, he prayed,
22.42: “Father, if you are willing, take this cup of agony away from me. But no matter what, your will must be mine.”
22.43: Jesus called for an angel of glory to strengthen him, and the angel appeared.
22.44: He prayed even more passionately, like one being sacrificed, until he was in such intense agony of spirit that his sweat became drops of blood, dripping onto the ground.
22.45: When Jesus finished praying, he got up and went to his disciples and found them all asleep, for they were exhausted and overwhelmed with sorrow.
22.46: “Why are you sleeping?” he asked them. “You need to be alert and pray for the strength to endure the great temptation.”
22.47: No sooner had he finished speaking when suddenly a mob approached, and in front of the mob was his disciple Judas. He walked up close to Jesus and greeted him with a kiss. For he had agreed to give the religious leaders a sign, saying, “The one I kiss is the one to seize.”
22.48: Jesus looked at him with sorrow and said, “A kiss, Judas? Are you really going to betray the Son of Man with a kiss?”
22.49: When the other disciples understood what was happening, they asked, “Lord, shall we fight them with our swords?”
22.50: Just then, one of the disciples swung his sword at the high priest’s servant and slashed off his right ear.
22.51: Jesus stopped the incident from escalating any further by saying, “Enough of this!” Then he touched the right side of the injured man’s head and the ear grew back —he was healed!
22.52: Jesus turned to those who had come to seize him—the ruling priests, the officers of the temple police, and the religious leaders—and said, “Am I a criminal that you come to capture me with clubs and swords? Wasn’t I with you day after day, teaching in the temple courts?
22.53: You could have seized me at any time. But in the darkness of night you have now found your time, for it belongs to you and to the prince of darkness.”
22.54: The religious leaders seized Jesus and led him away, but Peter followed from a safe distance. They brought him to the home of the high priest, where people were already gathered out in the courtyard.
22.55: Someone had built a fire, so Peter inched closer and sat down among them to stay warm.
22.56: A girl noticed Peter sitting in the firelight. Staring at him, she pointed him out and said, “This man is one of Jesus’ disciples!”
22.57: Peter flatly denied it, saying, “What are you talking about, girl? I don’t know him!”
22.58: A little while later, someone else spotted Peter and said, “I recognize you. You’re one of his, I know it!” Peter again said, “I’m not one of his disciples.”
22.59: About an hour later, someone else identified Peter and insisted he was a disciple of Jesus, saying, “Look at him! He’s from Galilee, just like Jesus. I know he’s one of them.”
22.60: But Peter was adamant. “Listen, I don’t know what you’re talking about. Don’t you understand? I don’t even know him.” While the words were still in his mouth, the rooster crowed.
22.61: At that moment, the Lord, who was being led through the courtyard by his captors, turned around and gazed at Peter. All at once Peter remembered the words Jesus had prophesied over him, “Before the rooster crows in the morning, you will deny three times that you even know me.”
22.62: Peter burst into tears, ran off from the crowd, and wept bitterly.
22.63: Those who were guarding Jesus mocked and beat him severely.
22.64: They also made fun of him, blindfolding him and slapping his face and saying, “Prove that you are a prophet and tell us which one of us hit you!”
22.65: They blasphemed and heaped insult after insult upon him.
22.66: At daybreak the high priests, the experts of the law, and the top religious leaders convened and had Jesus brought before their council.
22.67: They asked him point blank, “Tell us, are you the Christ, the Messiah, or not?” Jesus responded, “If I tell you the truth, you won’t believe me.
22.68: And if I question you, you will not answer me or release me.
22.69: But from today on, the Son of Man will be enthroned in the place of honor, power, and authority with Almighty God.”
22.70: They all shouted, “Then you do claim to be the Son of God?” He said to them, “You are the ones who say I am.”
22.71: They all shouted, “We’ve heard it from his very lips! What further proof do we need?”

23.1: The entire council stood at once and took Jesus to Pilate, the Roman governor.
23.2: They accused him of false testimony, saying, “This man tells us not to pay our taxes to Caesar. And he proclaims himself to be Christ the King and Messiah. He’s a deceiver of our nation.”
23.3: Pilate asked Jesus, “Is this true? Are you their king and Messiah?” Jesus answered, “It is true.”
23.4: Pilate turned to the high priests and to the gathered crowd and said, “This man has committed no crime. I find nothing wrong with him.”
23.5: But they yelled and demanded that Pilate do something, saying, “He has stirred up our nation, misleading people from the moment he began teaching in Galilee until he has come here to Jerusalem!”
23.6: When Pilate heard the word Galilee, he asked if Jesus was a Galilean, and when they told him “yes,” Pilate saw a way out of his problem. He knew that Antipas, son of Herod, ruled over Galilee, and he happened to be in Jerusalem at that time, so Pilate sent Jesus to Antipas.
23.7: When they answered that he was, Pilate sent him to Herod Antipas, because Galilee was under Herod's jurisdiction, and Herod happened to be in Jerusalem at the time.
23.8: When he saw Jesus, he was elated, for he had heard a great deal about his ministry and wanted Jesus to perform a miracle in front of him.
23.9: Antipas questioned him at length, but Jesus wouldn’t even answer him.
23.10: All the while the high priests and religious leaders stood by, accusing Jesus of wrongdoing, so that Antipas and his soldiers treated him with scorn and mocking. Antipas put an elegant purple robe on Jesus and sent him back to Pilate.
23.11: Now Herod and his soldiers began mocking and ridiculing Jesus. Then they put a royal robe on him and sent him back to Pilate.
23.12: That day, Antipas and Pilate healed their long-standing feud and they became good friends.
23.13: Pilate gathered together the people, the high priests, and all the religious leaders of the nation. He told them, “You have presented this man to me and charged him with stirring a rebellion among the people. I have examined him here in your presence and have put him on trial. My verdict is that none of your charges against him are true. I find no fault in him.
23.14: and he announced his verdict. "You brought this man to me, accusing him of leading a revolt. I have examined him thoroughly on this point in your presence and find him innocent.
23.15: Then I sent him to Antipas, son of Herod, who questioned him and found him not guilty. Since he has done nothing deserving of death, I have decided to punish him with a severe flogging and release him.”
23.16: So I will have him flogged, but then I will release him."
23.17: For it was Pilate’s custom to honor the Jewish holiday by releasing a prisoner.
23.18: When the crowd heard this, they went wild. Erupting with anger, they cried out, “No! Take this one away and release Barabbas!”
23.19: For Barabbas had been thrown in prison for robbery and murder.
23.20: Pilate, wanting to release Jesus, tried to convince them it was best to let Jesus go,
23.21: but they screamed out over and over, “Crucify him! Crucify him!”
23.22: A third time, Pilate asked the crowd, “What evil crime has this man committed that I should have him crucified? I haven’t found one thing that warrants a death sentence! I will have him flogged severely and then release him.”
23.23: But the people and the high priests, shouting like a mob, screamed out at the top of their lungs, “No! Crucify him! Crucify him!” Finally their shouts and screams succeeded.
23.24: Pilate caved in to the crowd and ordered that the will of the people be done.
23.25: Then he released the guilty murderer Barabbas, as they had insisted, and handed Jesus over to be crucified.
23.26: As the guards led Jesus to be crucified, there was an African man in the crowd named Simon, from Libya. He had just arrived from a rural village to keep the Feast of the Passover. The guards laid Jesus’ cross on Simon’s shoulders and forced him to walk behind Jesus, carrying his cross.
23.27: Massive crowds gathered to follow Jesus, including a number of women, who were wailing with sorrow over him.
23.28: Jesus turned to them and said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me. You should be weeping for yourselves and your children.
23.29: The day is coming when it will not be the women with children who are blessed but those who are childless. Then you will say, ‘The barren women are the most fortunate! Those who have never given birth and never nursed a child— they are more fortunate than we, for they will never see their children put to death!’
23.30: And the people will cry out for the mountains and hills to fall on top of them to hide them from all that is to come.
23.31: For if this is what they do to the living Branch, what will they do with the dead ones?”
23.32: The guards led away two criminals with Jesus, to execute all three at the same time.
23.33: When they came to the place that is known as The Skull, the guards crucified Jesus, nailing him on the center cross between the two criminals.
23.34: While they were nailing Jesus to the cross, he prayed over and over, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they’re doing.” The soldiers, after they crucified him, gambled over his clothing.
23.35: A great crowd gathered to watch what was happening. The religious leaders sneered at Jesus and mocked him, saying, “Look at this man! What kind of ‘chosen Messiah’ is this? He pretended to save others, but he can’t even save himself!”
23.36: The soldiers joined in the mockery, offering Jesus a drink of vinegar.
23.37: Over Jesus’ head on the cross was written an inscription in Greek, Latin, and Aramaic: “This man is the king of all the Jews.” And all the soldiers laughed and scoffed at him, saying, “Hey! If you’re the king of Jews, why don’t you save yourself?”
23.38: A signboard was nailed to the cross above him with these words: "This is the King of the Jews."
23.39: One of the criminals hanging on the cross next to Jesus kept ridiculing him, saying, “What kind of Messiah are you? Save yourself and save us from this death!”
23.40: The criminal hanging on the other cross rebuked the man, saying, “Don’t you fear God? You’re about to die!
23.41: We deserve to be condemned. We’re just being repaid for what we’ve done. But this man—he’s done nothing wrong!”
23.42: Then he said, “I beg of you, Jesus, show me grace and take me with you into your everlasting kingdom!”
23.43: Jesus responded, “I promise you—this very day you will enter paradise with me.”
23.44: It was now only midday, yet the whole world became dark for three hours as the light of the sun faded away.
23.45: And suddenly in the temple the thick veil hanging in the Holy Place was ripped in two!
23.46: Then Jesus cried out with a loud voice, “Father, I surrender my Spirit into your hands.” And he took his last breath and died.
23.47: When the Roman captain overseeing the crucifixion witnessed all that took place, he was awestruck and glorified God. Acknowledging what they had done, he said, “I have no doubt; we just killed the righteous one.”
23.48: The crowds that had gathered to observe this spectacle went back to their homes, overcome with deep sorrow and devastated by what they had witnessed.
23.49: But standing off at a distance were some who truly knew Jesus, and the women who had followed him all the way from Galilee were keeping vigil.
23.50: There was also a member of the Jewish council named Joseph, from the village of Ramah, a good-hearted, honorable man who was eager for God’s kingdom to appear. He had strongly disagreed with the decision of the council to crucify Jesus.
23.51: but he had not agreed with the decision and actions of the other religious leaders. He was from the town of Arimathea in Judea, and he had been waiting for the Kingdom of God to come.
23.52: He came before Pilate and asked permission to take the body of Jesus for a proper burial, and Pilate granted his request.
23.53: So he took the body from the cross, wrapped it in a winding sheet of linen, and placed it in a new, unused tomb chiseled out of solid rock.
23.54: It was Preparation Day, and the Sabbath was fast approaching.
23.55: The women who had been companions of Jesus from the beginning saw all this take place and carefully contemplated how the body was laid in the tomb.
23.56: Afterward they returned home and prepared fragrant spices and ointments and were planning to anoint his body after the Sabbath was completed, according to the commandments of the law.

24.1: Very early that Sunday morning, the women made their way to the tomb, carrying the spices they had prepared. (10) Among them were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Jesus’ mother Mary.
24.2: Arriving at the tomb they discovered that the huge stone covering the entrance had been rolled aside,
24.3: so they went in to look. But the tomb was empty. The body of Jesus was gone!
24.4: They stood there, stunned and perplexed. Suddenly, two men appeared above them in dazzling white robes shining like lightning.
24.5: Terrified, the women fell to the ground on their faces. The men in white said to them, “Why would you look for the Living One in a tomb? He is not here, for he has risen!
24.6: Have you forgotten what he said to you while he was still in Galilee:
24.7: ‘The destiny of the Son of Man is to be handed over to sinful men, to be nailed to a cross, and on the third day to rise again’?”
24.8: All at once they remembered his words.
24.9: Leaving the tomb, they went to break the news to the Eleven and to all the others of what they had seen and heard.
24.10: The women who went to the tomb were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and several others. They told the apostles what had happened,
24.11: When the disciples heard the testimony of the women, it made no sense, and they were unable to believe what they heard.
24.12: But Peter jumped up and ran the entire distance to the tomb to see for himself. Stooping down, he looked inside and discovered it was empty! There was only the linen sheet lying there. Staggered by this, he walked away, wondering what it meant.
24.13: Later that same day, two of Jesus’ disciples were walking from Jerusalem to Emmaus, a journey of about seventeen miles.
24.14: They were in the midst of a discussion about all the events of the last few days when Jesus walked up and accompanied them in their journey.
24.15: Suddenly, Jesus himself came along and joined them and began walking beside them.
24.16: They were unaware that it was actually Jesus walking alongside them, for God prevented them from recognizing him.
24.17: Jesus said to them, “You seem to be in a deep discussion about something. What are you talking about, so sad and gloomy?” They stopped, and the one named Cleopas answered, “Haven’t you heard? Are you the only one in Jerusalem unaware of the things that have happened over the last few days?”
24.18: Then one of them, Cleopas, replied, "You must be the only person in Jerusalem who hasn't heard about all the things that have happened there the last few days."
24.19: Jesus asked, “What things?” “The things about Jesus, the man from Nazareth,” they replied. “He was a mighty prophet of God who performed miracles and wonders. His words were powerful and he had great favor with God and the people.
24.20: But three days ago the high priest and the rulers of the people sentenced him to death and had him crucified. We had all hoped that he was the one who would redeem and rescue Israel.
24.21: We had thought he was the Messiah who had come to rescue Israel. That all happened three days ago.
24.22: Early this morning, some of the women informed us of something amazing.
24.23: They said they went to the tomb and found it empty. They claimed two angels appeared and told them that Jesus is now alive.
24.24: Some of us went to see for ourselves and found the tomb exactly as the women had said. But no one has seen him.”
24.25: Jesus said to them, “Why are you so thick-headed? Why do you find it so hard to believe every word the prophets have spoken?
24.26: Wasn’t it necessary for the Messiah to experience all these sufferings and afterward to enter into his glory?”
24.27: And beginning with Moses and all the prophets he carefully unveiled to them the revelation of himself throughout the Scriptures.
24.28: As they approached the village, Jesus walked on ahead, telling them he was going on to a distant place.
24.29: They urged him to remain there with them and pleaded, “Stay with us. It will be dark soon.” So Jesus went with them into the village.
24.30: Joining them at the table for supper, he took bread and blessed it and broke it, then gave it to them.
24.31: All at once their eyes were opened and they realized he was Jesus! Then suddenly, in a flash, Jesus vanished from before their eyes!
24.32: Stunned, they looked at each other and said, “Why didn’t we recognize him? Didn’t our hearts burn with the flames of holy passion while we walked beside him? He unveiled for us such profound revelation from the Scriptures!”
24.33: They left at once and hurried back to Jerusalem to tell the other disciples. When they found the Eleven and the other disciples all together,
24.34: they overheard them saying, “It’s really true! The Lord has risen from the dead. He even appeared to Peter!”
24.35: Then the two disciples told the others what had happened to them on the road to Emmaus and how Jesus had unveiled himself in the breaking of bread.
24.36: While they were still discussing all of this, Jesus suddenly appeared right in front of their eyes! Startled and terrified, the disciples were convinced they were seeing a ghost. Standing there among them he said, “Be at peace. I am the living God. Don’t be afraid.
24.37: But the whole group was terribly frightened, thinking they were seeing a ghost!
24.38: Why are you so frightened? Don’t let doubt enter your hearts.
24.39: See my pierced hands and feet. See for yourselves, it is I, standing here alive. Touch me and know that my wounds are real. A spirit does not have a body of flesh and bone as you see that I have.”
24.40: Then he showed them his pierced hands and feet and let them touch his wounds.
24.41: The disciples were ecstatic, yet dumbfounded, unable to fully comprehend it. Knowing that they were still wondering if he was real, Jesus said, “Here, let me show you. Give me something to eat.”
24.42: They handed him a piece of broiled fish and some honeycomb. And they watched him eat.
24.43: and he ate it as they watched.
24.44: Then he said to them, “Don’t you remember the words that I spoke to you when I was still with you? I told you that I would fulfill everything written about me, including all the prophecies from the law of Moses through the Psalms and the writings of the prophets.”
24.45: He supernaturally unlocked their understanding to receive the revelation of the Scriptures,
24.46: and said to them, “Everything that has happened fulfills what the Scriptures prophesied of me. The Messiah was destined to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day.
24.47: Now you must go into all the nations and preach repentance and forgiveness of sins so that they will turn to me. Start right here in Jerusalem,
24.48: for you are my witnesses and have seen for yourselves all that has transpired.
24.49: I will send the fulfillment of the Father’s promise to you, so stay here in the city until you are clothed with the mighty power of heaven.”
24.50: Jesus led his disciples out to Bethany. He lifted his hands over them and blessed them in his love.
24.51: While he was still speaking words of love and blessing, he floated off the ground into the sky, ascending into heaven before their very eyes!
24.52: And all they could do was worship him. Overwhelmed and ecstatic with joy, they made their way back to Jerusalem.
24.53: Every day they went to the temple, to praise and worship God.

1.1: In the beginning the Living Expression was already there. And the Living Expression was with God, yet fully God.
1.2: They were together— face-to-face, in the very beginning.
1.3: And through his creative inspiration this Living Expression made all things, for nothing has existence apart from him!
1.4: A fountain of life was in him, for his life is light for all humanity.
1.5: And this Light never fails to shine through darkness— Light that darkness could not overcome!
1.6: Suddenly a man appeared who was sent from God, a messenger named John.
1.7: For he came as a witness, to point the way to the Light of Life, and to help everyone believe.
1.8: John was not that Light but he came to show who is. For he was merely a messenger to speak the truth about the Light.
1.9: For the perfect Light of Truth was coming into the world and shine upon everyone.
1.10: He entered into the world he created, yet the world was unaware.
1.11: He came to the people he created — to those who should have received him, but they did not recognize him.
1.12: But those who embraced him and took hold of his name he gave authority to become the children of God!
1.13: He was not born by the joining of human parents or from natural means, or by a man’s desire, but he was born of God.
1.14: And so the Living Expression became a man and lived among us! We gazed upon his glory, the glory of the One and Only who came from the Father overflowing with tender mercy and truth!
1.15: John announced the truth about him when he taught the people, “He’s the One! He’s the One I’ve been telling you would come after me, even though he ranks far above me, because he existed before I was even born.”
1.16: And from the overflow of his fullness we received grace heaped upon more grace!
1.17: Moses gave us the Law, but Jesus, the Anointed One, unveils truth wrapped in tender mercy.
1.18: No one ever before gazed upon the full splendor of God except his uniquely beloved Son, who is cherished by the Father and held close to his heart. Now that he has come to us, he has unfolded the full explanation of who God truly is!
1.19: Now this was John’s testimony when some of the Jewish leaders sent an entourage of priests and temple servants from Jerusalem to interrogate him. “Who are you?” they asked him.
1.20: John answered them directly, saying, “I am not the Messiah!”
1.21: “Then who are you?” they asked. “Are you Elijah?” “No,” John replied. So they pressed him further, “Are you the prophet Moses said was coming, the one we’re expecting?” “No,” he replied.
1.22: “Then who are you?” they demanded. “We need an answer for those who sent us. Tell us something about yourself—anything!”
1.23: John answered them, “I am an urgent, thunderous voice crying out in the desert—clear the way and prepare your hearts for the coming of the Lord Yahweh!”
1.24: Then some members of the religious sect known as the Pharisees questioned John,
1.25: “Why do you baptize the people if you are neither the Messiah, Elijah, nor the Prophet?”
1.26: John answered them, “I baptize the people in this river, but the One who will take my place is to be more honored than I, but even when he stands among you, you will not recognize or embrace him! I am not worthy enough to stoop down in front of him and untie his sandals!”
1.27: who will soon begin his ministry. I am not even worthy to be his slave. "
1.28: All these events took place at Bethany, where John was baptizing at the place of the crossing of the Jordan River.
1.29: The very next day, John saw Jesus coming to him to be baptized, and John cried out, “Look! There he is—God’s Lamb! He takes away the sin of the entire world!
1.30: I told you that a Mighty One would come who is far greater than I am, because he existed long before I was born!
1.31: My baptism was for the preparation of his appearing to Israel, even though I didn’t recognize him.”
1.32: Then, as he baptized Jesus, he proclaimed these words: “I see the Spirit of God appear like a dove descending from the heavenly realm and landing upon him—and it remained on him!
1.33: Before this I didn’t know who he was. But the one who sent me to baptize with water had told me, ‘You will see the Spirit come down and stay on someone. He will be the One I have sent to baptize with the Holy Spirit.’
1.34: Now I have seen this happen and I can tell you for sure that this man is the Son of God.”
1.35: The next day, Jesus walked right past where John and two of his disciples were standing. John, gazing upon Jesus, pointed to him and prophesied, “Look! There’s God’s sacrificial Lamb!”
1.36: As Jesus walked by, John looked at him and then declared, "Look! There is the Lamb of God!"
1.37: And as soon as John’s two disciples heard this, they immediately left John and began to follow a short distance behind Jesus.
1.38: Jesus turned around and saw they were following him and asked, “What do you want?” They responded, “Rabbi (which means, Master Teacher), where are you staying?”
1.39: Jesus answered, “Come and discover for yourselves.” So they went with him and saw where he was staying, and since it was late in the afternoon, they spent the rest of the day with Jesus.
1.40: One of the two disciples who heard John’s words and began to follow Jesus was a man named Andrew. He first found his brother, Simon Peter, and told him, “We have found the Anointed One!” (Which is translated, the Christ.)
1.41: The first thing Andrew did was to find his brother, Simon, and tell him, "We have found the Messiah" (which means the Christ).
1.42: Then Andrew brought Simon to meet Jesus. When he gazed upon Andrew’s brother, he prophesied to him, “You are Simon and your father’s name is John. But from now on, everyone will call you Cephas” (which means, Peter the Rock).
1.43: The next day, Jesus decided to go to Galilee, where he found Philip. Jesus said to him, “Come and follow me.”
1.44: (Now Philip, Andrew, and Peter had all grown up together in the village of Bethsaida.)
1.45: Philip went to look for his friend, Nathanael, and told him, “We’ve found him! We’ve found the One we’ve been waiting for! It’s Jesus, son of Joseph from Nazareth! He’s the One whom Moses and the prophets prophesied would come!”
1.46: Nathanael sneered, “Nazareth! What good thing could ever come from Nazareth?” Philip answered, “Come and let’s find out!”
1.47: When Jesus saw Nathanael approaching, he said, “Here comes a true son of Israel—an honest man with no hidden motive!”
1.48: Nathanael was stunned and said, “But you’ve never met me—how do you know anything about me?” Jesus answered, “Nathanael, right before Philip came to you, I saw you sitting under the shade of a fig tree.”
1.49: Nathanael blurted out, “Teacher, you are truly the Son of God and the King of Israel!”
1.50: Jesus answered, “Do you believe simply because I told you I saw you sitting under a fig tree? You will experience even more impressive things than that!
1.51: I prophesy to you eternal truth: From now on, you all will see an open heaven and gaze upon the Son of Man like a stairway reaching into the sky with the messengers of God climbing up and down upon him!”

2.1: Now on the third day, Jesus’ mother went to a wedding feast in the Galilean village of Cana.
2.2: Jesus and his disciples were all invited to the banquet, but with so many guests, they ran out of wine. And when Mary realized it, she came to Jesus and asked, “They have no wine; can’t you do something about it?”
2.3: The wine supply ran out during the festivities, so Jesus' mother spoke to him about the problem. "They have no more wine," she told him.
2.4: Jesus replied, “My dear one, don’t you understand that if I do this, it will change nothing for you, but it will change everything for me! My hour of unveiling my power has not yet come.”
2.5: Mary then went to the servers and told them, “Whatever Jesus tells you, do it!”
2.6: Nearby stood six stone water pots meant to be used for the Jewish washing rituals. Each one could hold about twenty gallons or more.
2.7: Jesus came to the servers and instructed them, “Fill the pots with water, right up to the very brim. ”
2.8: Then he said, “Now fill your pitchers and take them to the master of ceremonies.”
2.9: And when they poured out their pitchers for the master of ceremonies to sample, the water had become wine! When he tasted the water that had become wine, the master of ceremonies was impressed with its quality. (Although he didn’t know where the wine had come from, only the servers knew.) He called the bridegroom over
2.10: and said to him, “Every host serves his best wine first, until everyone has had a cup or two, then he serves the cheaper wine. But you, my friend, you’ve reserved the most exquisite wine until now!”
2.11: This miracle in Cana was the first of the many extraordinary miracles Jesus performed in Galilee that revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.
2.12: After the wedding, Jesus, his mother and brothers, and his disciples traveled to Capernaum and stayed there for a few days.
2.13: When the time was close for the Jewish Passover to begin, Jesus walked to Jerusalem.
2.14: As he went into the temple courtyard, he noticed it was filled with merchants selling oxen, lambs, and doves for exorbitant prices, while others were overcharging as they exchanged currency behind their counters.
2.15: So Jesus found some cords and made them into a whip. Then he drove out every one of them and their animals from the courtyard of the temple, and he kicked over their tables filled with money, scattering it everywhere!
2.16: And he told the merchants, “Get these things out of here! Don’t you dare commercialize my Father’s house!”
2.17: That’s when his disciples remembered the Scripture: “I am consumed with a fiery passion to keep your house pure!”
2.18: Then the Jewish religious leaders challenged Jesus, “What authority do you have to do this sort of thing and what supernatural sign will you show us to prove it?”
2.19: Jesus answered, “Destroy this temple, and I will raise it up again in three days.”
2.20: Then the Jewish leaders sneered at Jesus’ answer, “This temple took forty-six years to build, and you mean to tell us that you will raise it up in three days?”
2.21: But they failed to understand that Jesus was speaking of the “temple” of his body.
